UI-camera-qml.summary: I checked each finding in the code at cinemate-port (UI 7ea9afc, Core 01f170c) and compared it with upstream-1.6.0. Stands: F1, F2, F3, F5, F6, F9, F10. Corrected: F4 (deliberate and Core-driven, now a nit), F7 (commit da2a9b5 does state the HDMI change, so deliberate is yes and it is now a nit) and F8 (dropped the move into ApertarControlBridge, because the steps live in SettingsBridge and the hand-paired copy is the upstream pattern). Added F11, found while checking F4: the UI offers ISO Auto in all lossless modes, but port Core keeps auto ISO only on the IMX585 and silently turns it off on other sensors. None of the findings were dropped.

abstraction_verdicts.name: valueSteps / cappedValueEntries / fpsOptionEntries / fpsCeiling / shutterAngleEntries
abstraction_verdicts.reason: Hand-written CameraPage helpers next to upstream availableFpsOptions; same style. Comments need fixing (F1, F2), and the fpsCeiling fallback needs fixing (F3).

abstraction_verdicts.name: Option object {value, enabled, cameraSet} in TopDropdownStat
abstraction_verdicts.reason: Plain strings still work; it is the smallest widening of the generic upstream component.

abstraction_verdicts.name: cameraSet / italic convention
abstraction_verdicts.reason: New ground, and weighed: green tried in f1edf96, replaced by italics in 35b31f6. Document it once for the original developer.

abstraction_verdicts.name: bufferFlushing / pillRecordingActive
abstraction_verdicts.reason: Use one takeActive property per window, everywhere (F6).

abstraction_verdicts.name: Buffer bar Item+Rectangle x2
abstraction_verdicts.reason: Make it one shared component, as DroppedFrameWarning is (F5).

abstraction_verdicts.name: ControlsWarning.qml
abstraction_verdicts.reason: Same shape as DroppedFrameWarning.qml. Drop the T45 comment and add the file to qml.qrc.

findings.title: Ticket numbers, names and dates in code comments
findings.port_way: The comments contain 'T33', 'T45', 'Request 24', 'request 25', '(Patrik, 2026-10-28)' and '(HDMI 50 min, Core 37 min, 2026-10-27)'.
findings.apertar_way: Comments say what the code does and carry no ids, e.g. qml/CameraPage.qml:2563@upstream-1.6.0. Upstream qml/ has no ids or dates anywhere.
findings.why_it_matters: The ids mean nothing to the original developer. The dated notes tell history instead of describing the code.
findings.rework: Delete the ids, names and dates and keep the one-line 'what'. For :710, keep '16-bit = 2 bytes a pixel'.

findings.title: Stale 'green' comments; the convention is italics
findings.port_way: The comments say camera-set values are green. The code renders them in italics (TopDropdownStat.qml:39 valueItalic, :114 font.italic: optionCameraSet), since commit 35b31f6.
findings.apertar_way: no precedent
findings.why_it_matters: The comments contradict the rendering.
findings.rework: Replace 'green' with 'italic' in the four comments. Leave the safety-stop 'READY green' comments alone; they describe real colours.

findings.title: Lossless ISO and IMX585 lossless FPS caps lost against a Core without iso_max/fps_max
findings.port_way: const maximum = root.controlBridge ? root.controlBridge.isoMax : (root.losslessIsoLimitedMode ? 1600 : 0). controlBridge is always set (Main.qml:500), so the fallback never runs and isoMax=0 means no cap. fpsCeiling() has an empty 'if (root.losslessImx585Mode) { }' in the fallback path.
findings.apertar_way: qml/CameraPage.qml:511-513@upstream-1.6.0 offers [100,200,400,800] with no Auto in lossless. :815 has 'if (root.losslessImx585Mode) max = Math.min(max, 30.0)'. Core clamps silently at src/camera/CameraController.cpp:2483-2490@upstream-1.6.0.
findings.why_it_matters: With the port UI on an un-updated Core in IMX585 lossless cDNG, the UI offers Auto, ISO 1600-51200 and 50/60 fps, and Core silently corrects the selection.
findings.rework: isoOptions: use controlBridge.isoMax only when it is > 0, else (losslessIsoLimitedMode ? 800 : 0), and drop Auto while that fallback applies. fpsCeiling(): restore 'max = Math.min(max, 30.0)' for losslessImx585Mode in the fallback branch, which runs only when fpsMax is 0.
findings.deliberate_evidence: b4591dc set the fallback to 1600 'as Core' without noticing that the fallback cannot run.

findings.title: ISO Auto in IMX585 lossless; lossless ISO ceiling 800 -> 1600
findings.port_way: The UI drops Auto only in Clear HDR. The lossless ceiling follows Core's iso_max, which is 1600.
findings.apertar_way: Upstream allows no Auto and a maximum of 800 in lossless: qml/CameraPage.qml:511-513@upstream-1.6.0, src/web/WebControlPage.cpp:5025@upstream-1.6.0, src/camera/CameraController.cpp:2483-2484@upstream-1.6.0.
findings.why_it_matters: This changes a limit the original developer set in three places. The decision sits in Core; the UI only follows iso_max, which is the right pattern.
findings.rework: No UI change beyond F3 and F11. Keep it together with the Core change (CC unit), and state the measured reason in the commit and the handoff, without names or dates.
findings.deliberate_evidence: UI 682a186 'Core keeps auto ISO in IMX585 lossless now'; b4591dc 'Core's lossless ISO cap is 1600 now'; Core comment at CameraController.cpp:3098.

findings.title: Buffer bar written twice (StatusChip and HDMI pill)
findings.port_way: Both files hold the same code: a clipped Item with an inner Rectangle copy of the pill shape, the drainOnly colour rule, 0.85 opacity and a 150 ms animation. The two copies differ only in the id they size against.
findings.apertar_way: A pill decoration shown on both screens is one small component used twice: DroppedFrameWarning at qml/CameraPage.qml:2569@upstream-1.6.0 and qml/ExternalMonitorWindow.qml:1103@upstream-1.6.0.
findings.why_it_matters: The two copies will drift apart.
findings.rework: Add qml/StatusPillBufferBar.qml (props fill, drain, inset, pillRadius) and use it inside StatusChip and the EMW pill. Register it in CMakeLists.txt and qml.qrc. Keep the EMW pill itself inline, as upstream does.

findings.title: Safety-stop flush: pill says READY while the frame, red timecode and audio outline still show recording
findings.port_way: bufferFlushing and pillRecordingActive gate only the pill and the record button (CameraPage.qml:2694,3953; EMW:157). The frame, timecode and outline use root.recording or recordingActive. After its own record_stop, Core keeps recording true while it drains (src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:11094-11110@cinemate-port).
findings.apertar_way: no precedent
findings.why_it_matters: In a buffer safety stop with Recording Frame on, the pill shows green READY, but the red frame and red timecode stay until Core clears recording.
findings.rework: Add one 'readonly property bool takeActive: root.recording && !root.bufferFlushing' to CameraPage and rename EMW pillRecordingActive to takeActive. Use it for the pill, button, frame, timecode and audio outline.

findings.title: HDMI timecode turns red while recording by default
findings.port_way: color: root.recordingActive && (!settingsBridge || settingsBridge.recordingRedTimecodeEnabled) ? "#ff4d4d" : "white". The switch defaults to true.
findings.apertar_way: qml/ExternalMonitorWindow.qml:1129@upstream-1.6.0 has color: "white". Only the touch timecode turns red (qml/CameraPage.qml:3747@upstream-1.6.0).
findings.why_it_matters: A default on the client monitor changed from white to red while recording.
findings.rework: Keep it; the commit already states it. List it in the handoff notes as a default change on the HDMI monitor.
findings.deliberate_evidence: da2a9b5 message: 'the red timecode as an option (default on, as before on the touch screen; HDMI now follows it too)'.

findings.title: isoOnAddedCap, built-in ISO list and raw-format test copied into the HDMI window with drift
findings.port_way: EMW repeats isoOnAddedCap with an inline ISO list and without the valueSteps filter. EMW rawRecordFormat tests for ProRes and 'H.264' instead of using its own processedVideoRecordFormat (:137). The pre-roll fps uses toFixed(3) instead of formatFpsValue.
findings.apertar_way: Upstream pairs the CameraPage and EMW label code by hand (ui-map section 4, 'CameraPage vs ExternalMonitorWindow labels'). The copy follows the upstream pattern; the drift does not.
findings.why_it_matters: After a one-sided edit, the two windows show different values.
findings.rework: Make the EMW copies match CameraPage: the same valueSteps-style filter, processedVideoRecordFormat, and the same fps formatting. Add these rows to ui-map section 4. Do not move the logic into ApertarControlBridge; the steps live in SettingsBridge.

findings.title: Empty if-block with a comment in fpsCeiling()
findings.port_way: if (root.losslessImx585Mode) { // Core's fps_max carries ... } else if ...
findings.apertar_way: qml/CameraPage.qml:815@upstream-1.6.0 has 'if (root.losslessImx585Mode) max = Math.min(max, 30.0)'.
findings.why_it_matters: The empty block reads like dead code.
findings.rework: Folded into F3: restore the upstream line.

findings.title: ControlsWarning.qml is in CMakeLists.txt but not in qml.qrc
findings.port_way: The new file is added only to the CMake list. Non-AOT builds compile qml.qrc (CMakeLists.txt:200-203), and AOT is off by default for cross builds (:59-63).
findings.apertar_way: Upstream has the same trap: DroppedFrameWarning.qml and InlineChoice.qml are in CMakeLists.txt@upstream-1.6.0 but not in qml.qrc (ui-map section 4).
findings.why_it_matters: A cross (non-AOT) build probably cannot resolve ControlsWarning in CameraPage. Not confirmed by a non-AOT build.
findings.rework: Add ControlsWarning.qml to qml.qrc, and add the two upstream files in a separate commit. Or keep it as upstream does and record it.

findings.title: ISO Auto offered in non-IMX585 lossless modes, where Core still turns it off
findings.port_way: The UI drops Auto only in Clear HDR (682a186). Port Core keeps auto ISO in lossless only on the IMX585: 'if (sensorFamily != SensorFamily::Imx585) settings.isoAuto = false;'.
findings.apertar_way: In upstream the picker and Core agree: no Auto in any lossless mode (qml/CameraPage.qml:511-513@upstream-1.6.0, src/camera/CameraController.cpp:2484@upstream-1.6.0).
findings.why_it_matters: In lossless 4K/2K cDNG on IMX477 or IMX283, the operator can pick Auto, and Core silently switches to manual ISO.
findings.rework: In isoOptions, also return entries without Auto when (root.losslessFourKMode || root.losslessTwoKMode) && !root.imx585Detected. Alternatively, Core publishes a scalar iso_auto_allowed that the UI reads, as it does isoMax.
findings.deliberate_evidence: 682a186 justifies only the IMX585 ('Core keeps auto ISO in IMX585 lossless now'); the UI change applies more widely.

UI-settings-qml.summary: Skeptic pass over 13 findings. 12 survive and 1 is dropped. Stands: F1, F2, F4, F5, F7, F9, F10, F12. Corrected: F3 (upstream does have long-press drag in the reorder and sidebar popups at SettingsPage.qml:6111-6297, so the port's hand-placed ghost is a second drag idiom, not a first one), F6 ("12 frames" is a fixed Core constant, maxQueuedFrames_ = 12, so that part is removed), F8 (the QML and Core token lists match today, so the loss is only possible in future; severity cut to nit), F11 (the #9aa5b1 12 px helper texts copy upstream's Format card; only the white 14 px sub-labels and the missing compact/medium pill sizes remain). Dropped: F13 (upstream itself inlines its hotspotEditTarget popup conditionals, and F2's rework deletes the timecode duplication). No new findings. Main items: radio-style ActionTiles (F1), the timecode split that breaks upstream "Mode" (F2), and the oversized drag composer in ClipNameCard (F3).

findings.title: ActionTiles with a flipping accent tone used as radio buttons
findings.port_way: tone: apertarControlBridge.bufferSetting === "frames" ? "accent" : "default"; the selected value is drawn as an accent ActionTile
findings.apertar_way: Booleans: title+description+TogglePill (qml/SettingsPage.qml:3562 gyroRecordToggle, :4885 dateTimeOverlayToggle @upstream-1.6.0). Value choice: InlineDropdownField with value/label options (Compression :3250). ActionTile is a verb with constant tone (:3640/:3650/:3712/:3723 default, :5416 accent Standby, danger elsewhere); no conditional tone in any upstream qml/*.qml
findings.why_it_matters: The original developer reads an accent ActionTile as the primary action. Four places introduce a third widget idiom for a choice
findings.rework: Write Buffer -> InlineDropdownField {label "Write Buffer", options frames/ram, onValueSelected applyBufferMode(v)} in the Bit Depth/Compression row; Log -> TogglePill row (or dropdown Off/On); Automatic pre-roll -> TogglePill row like gyroRecordToggle; clip-name presets -> InlineDropdownField "Pattern" with displayValue "Custom" when none matches. Keep ActionTile only for the Storage Pre-roll verb. Keep the #9aa5b1 status texts
findings.deliberate_evidence: Commit 841d0ed calls them 'Frames / RAM buttons', 'Log buttons'; no reasoning about widget choice

findings.title: Timecode card: upstream Mode no longer sets file timecode; Free Run / Rec Run renamed
findings.port_way: First dropdown relabelled 'UI timecode' and calls applyTimecodeMode(v, "ui"); new 'File timecode' dropdown calls applyTimecodeMode(v, "files"); options shown as 'Time of Day' / 'Clip' via timecodeChoices
findings.apertar_way: One dropdown label "Mode", options ["Free Run", "Rec Run"], apertarControlBridge.applyTimecodeMode(v) (qml/SettingsPage.qml:3753-3782 @upstream-1.6.0); bridge sends set_timecode_mode value only (src/ApertarControlBridge.cpp:622-635); Core sets camera and UI.conf together (core-upstream src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:9424-9435)
findings.why_it_matters: An operator who picks Rec Run in the first dropdown, as in upstream, gets Rec Run on screen and Free Run in the files. The original developer's terms disappear from Settings
findings.rework: Restore the upstream dropdown verbatim (label Mode, Free Run/Rec Run, applyTimecodeMode(v) with no target). If a separate file timecode stays, add a second dropdown 'Files' whose first option 'Same as Mode' sends nothing, so the default equals upstream. Delete timecodeChoices and timecodeDisplayName; put clearer wording in description. Revert the CameraPage tap to toggle both (unit UI-camera-qml)
findings.deliberate_evidence: Commits 7029db1 and 08cefcf explain the split and the renaming ('Rec Run normally continues from the previous clip, so the name was wrong')
findings.rework_risk: Port Core keeps target=both as default (ApertarCoreApp.cpp:13279-13299@cinemate-port), so dropping the target is safe with both Cores

findings.title: ClipNameCard: drag-and-drop composer with its own drag layer, untested on touch
findings.port_way: 601+115 lines: ListModel parser/serialiser, 350 ms preview and 1000 ms save timers, ghost Rectangle with Drag.Internal placed by hand through mapToItem, DropArea, insertion marker, indexAt, begin/move/endDrag, long-press that sets preventStealing = true plus a 0 ms reset Timer, new colours #123d59/#3fd0ff/#e2f6ff
findings.apertar_way: No precedent for a composer. Upstream drag exists only in the reorder and sidebar popups (qml/SettingsPage.qml:6111-6211 reorderDelegate, :6282-6297 sidebar @upstream-1.6.0): held flag, drag.target on the content item, Drag.active: held, pressAndHoldInterval 260, preventStealing false, DelegateModel moves. Fields apply on selection without timers
findings.why_it_matters: Largest new QML in the unit, never run on a touch screen (fork-log 841d0ed row 'untested by hand'; drop-frames README:102, :158). The selection tiles (move left/right, Edit text, Remove) already do what drag does, so the drag layer is a second route in a second drag idiom
findings.rework: Simplify: keep the preset dropdown (F1), the pill row as a Flow of tappable chips, palette tap to append, the selection tiles, the Next clip line. Delete ghost, DropArea, marker, indexAt, beginDrag/moveDrag/endDrag, drag signals and long-press code in ClipNamePill, drag* properties. Save on each edit instead of the two timers if preview can follow the save. About 200 lines less. If drag is kept, rebuild it on the reorderDelegate pattern (drag.target, held), not a hand-positioned ghost
findings.deliberate_evidence: KB working/drop-frames/README.md:102 documents the feature ('QML Drag / DropArea with tap fallbacks') and the WebUI twin; no note weighs a simpler touch UI

findings.title: recordItemVisible() hides the Clip Names card
findings.port_way: Record Repeater Loader gets visible: root.recordItemVisible(modelData); clipNames hidden until Core reports a template
findings.apertar_way: Section Loaders have no visible hook (qml/SettingsPage.qml:7017-7024 @upstream-1.6.0); unavailable features keep the card and explain in description (:3039 sound recorder, :3071 exposure compensation)
findings.why_it_matters: A new per-item hook in the section machinery; the reorder popup still lists the hidden item
findings.rework: Delete recordItemVisible and the Loader line; in recordClipNamesComponent set description to 'Not available with this Core version' when !clipNameKnown and hide/disable the ClipNameCard inside the card

findings.title: Storage pre-roll placed inside the Media Speed card
findings.port_way: Tile, Automatic On/Off block and three Texts appended to systemMediaSpeedComponent (description 'Measure sequential write performance'); the manual tile has no Core-support guard
findings.apertar_way: One card per feature, registered in defaultPowerOrder, favoriteCandidateOrder, sectionItemTitle, powerComponentForId (qml/SettingsPage.qml:798-802, :838-878, :2336 @upstream-1.6.0)
findings.why_it_matters: A separate feature with its own setting hidden in another card, not reorderable or favouritable; with an original Core the tile sends storage_preroll and gets 'Unknown command: storage_preroll' (core-upstream src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:10820)

findings.title: UI text states Core settings as fixed values
findings.port_way: 'Records 2 seconds ... Also runs when a card is inserted or formatted.' (always shown, outside the Automatic block); 'WebUI: http://<ip>:8000, Settings, Controls'
findings.apertar_way: Core lets the operator change these: [media] preroll_seconds=1..10 (Apertar-Core src/util/StoragePreroll.hpp:17-23@cinemate-port), --web-port PORT (core-upstream src/main.cpp:35,68; ApertarCoreApp.hpp:36 @upstream-1.6.0). Upstream UI nowhere prints the WebUI port

findings.title: New items skip icon and favourite registration
findings.port_way: 4 Monitoring rows: no titleIconSource, no favoriteEnabled, ids not in favoriteCandidateOrder; clipNames: no favourite, not in favoriteCandidateOrder; controls: no icon

findings.port_way: saveNow returns when !editable; on recording stop onRecordingChanged stops the timers and syncFromBridge(true) reloads Core's template
findings.apertar_way: no precedent (upstream applies settings at once)

findings.title: set_timecode_mode target ignored by an original Core
findings.port_way: Adds a target=ui|files argument; port Core default 'both' (Apertar-Core ApertarCoreApp.cpp:13279-13299) keeps the original UI working

findings.port_way: Text { color: "white"; font.pixelSize: 14 } without font.family as sub-headings ('Write Buffer', 'Log', 'Automatic pre-roll', 'Pattern') and for 'Next clip'; pill height/font only for large/standard layouts

findings.apertar_way: Duplicating Core lists in QML has precedent (per-sensor resolution tables, ui-map section 4); the token list is also in Core src/util/ClipName.hpp:29-34 and WebControlPage.cpp:14456-14472. Today both lists hold the same 19 tokens

findings.apertar_way: no ticket tags in upstream comments

UI-control-bridge.summary:
Skeptic pass, checked at UI 7ea9afc / Core 01f170c against upstream-1.6.0. Of the 10 findings, 5 stand (F2, F4, F5, F6, F8), 4 are corrected (F1, F3, F9, F10) and 1 is dropped (F7).
- F1: the rework had the wire wrong. Core's set_storage_preroll and set_cdng_log read `value`, and so does the WebUI. Sending `enabled` therefore needs Core and WebUI changes too. applyCdngLog is added to the renames.
- F3: downgraded to nit. Upstream also sets a member after a successful send (applyH264Resolution). Only applyClipNameState(reply) is a real double apply.
- F9: only storagePrerollAutoKnown has its own signal, and one line number was wrong.
- F10: the std::clamp-vs-qBound point was dropped, because upstream uses std::clamp in AudioMeterBridge. Only the missing <algorithm> include remains.
- F7 dropped: Core's Lock reads the measured gain under the controller mutex at that moment. The proposed UI-side set_iso(isoInUse) would use a value up to 1 s old and lose that. The enabled=true/false spelling is upstream's, and a mixed UI/Core version does not occur once both ship together.

findings.title: Six new invokables return void; bool args sent as value=on/off and auto/off; names not in the upstream form
findings.port_way: Q_INVOKABLE void applyBufferMode/applyStoragePreroll/applyStoragePrerollAuto(bool on)/applyClipNameTemplate/requestClipNamePreview/applyCdngLog(bool on). set_storage_preroll sends value=on|off, set_cdng_log sends value=auto|off.
findings.apertar_way: Every command invokable returns bool; thin variants 'return sendCoreCommand(...)'; booleans as enabled="true"/"false" with apply<Thing>Enabled(bool enabled): src/ApertarControlBridge.cpp:736-741@upstream-1.6.0; Core reads command.string("enabled") (src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:9482,9514@upstream-1.6.0). Only notifyUserActivity/refresh are void (ApertarControlBridge.hpp:100,110@upstream-1.6.0). Actions are verbs (capturePhoto, calibrateGyro).
findings.why_it_matters: QML cannot tell success from refusal. The original developer reads void apply* as fire-and-forget, which upstream never does. on/off and auto/off are extra boolean spellings on the wire.
findings.rework: Make all six bool (return false after setLastError or failed send, true at the end, or 'return sendCoreCommand(...)'). Rename applyStoragePreroll -> startStoragePreroll(). Replace applyStoragePrerollAuto(bool on) with applyStoragePrerollAutoEnabled(bool enabled) and applyCdngLog(bool on) with applyCdngLogEnabled(bool enabled), both sending enabled="true"/"false". Core set_storage_preroll and set_cdng_log read 'enabled' (they read 'value' today, src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:12901,13080@cinemate-port). The WebUI senders (WebControlPage.cpp:15451,15843@cinemate-port) switch in the same change. QML ignores the results; only the renamed calls change.
findings.rework_risk: Core and WebUI change together with the UI; a one-release fallback to 'value' in Core avoids a mixed-version break.
findings.deliberate_evidence: 841d0ed and 606f137 do not discuss the return type or the argument spelling.

findings.title: Second state path: dedicated buffer/controls/media event branches and a key-name-parameterised setter
findings.port_way: applyCoreMessage has branches: controls -> setControlsStatus(message,"errors","warnings"); media -> setCoreMediaState(state, mounted); buffer -> applyBufferState + applyRecordingDroppedFrames. applyCoreState calls the same mappers with the spellings controls_errors/controls_warnings and media_state/media_alive. Core spells each value two ways (src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:12346-12348 vs :9458-9459; :10826-10828 vs :9555-9556@cinemate-port).
findings.apertar_way: Events whose fields are state keys go whole to applyCoreState: 'if (event == "standby" || ... || event == "media_write_state") { applyCoreState(message); return; }' src/ApertarControlBridge.cpp:1191-1195@upstream-1.6.0; recording_health likewise :1213-1216. No setter takes key names. Rule UI-S4.
findings.why_it_matters: State reaches properties through two paths with two key spellings. A maintainer who adds a key to applyCoreState misses the event path, or the other way round.
findings.rework: Core: the controls event emits controls_errors/controls_warnings and the media event emits media_state/media_alive (keep the old names only if another reader needs them). UI: add controls, media and buffer to the upstream applyCoreState event list. applyCoreState already runs applyBufferState and applyRecordingDroppedFrames (ApertarControlBridge.cpp:1457,1732@cinemate-port). Delete the three branches. Delete setControlsStatus and inline compare/assign/emit for controls_errors/controls_warnings in applyCoreState, in the form of recording_has_dropped_frames (ApertarControlBridge.cpp:1270-1276@upstream-1.6.0).
findings.rework_risk: The buffer event now runs all of applyCoreState; same cost class as recording_health upstream.
findings.deliberate_evidence: The ea44bd7, 160898c and 841d0ed messages describe what is read, not why there is a separate path.

findings.title: applyTimecodeMode gained a required target: upstream one-arg call gone, camera tap no longer sets file timecode
findings.port_way: bool applyTimecodeMode(displayValue, target), target ui|files|both, no default. The camera tap and the UI timecode dropdown send "ui". QML writes settingsState.timecodeMode, which persists UI.conf (SettingsBridge.cpp:1223-1233@cinemate-port). The bridge writes UI.conf timecodeMode again, and Core writes it a third time (src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:13293-13298@cinemate-port).
findings.apertar_way: bool applyTimecodeMode(const QString &displayValue) sets the camera mode and UI.conf (src/ApertarControlBridge.cpp:622-636@upstream-1.6.0; src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:9424-9437@upstream-1.6.0). The camera tap changes both (qml/CameraPage.qml:1709-1715@upstream-1.6.0). The UI-side value is SettingsBridge.timecodeMode, READ/WRITE (rule UI-S5).
findings.why_it_matters: A one-argument caller fails with 'Insufficient arguments'. The operator's tap no longer changes the timecode written into clips, which the original developer would not expect. A string 'target' selector on an apply* has no precedent.
findings.rework: Restore the one-argument applyTimecodeMode(displayValue): Core treats no target as both. Add bool applyFileTimecodeMode(displayValue), sending target="files" and setting fileTimecodeMode. A UI-only change is settingsState.timecodeMode = v with no Core call. Delete the target parameter and its validation. The camera tap returns to upstream behaviour unless the owner keeps the split tap; if so, document it for the original developer. QML side: rev-UI-settings-qml.md F2.
findings.rework_risk: Owner decision on the camera-tap behaviour. Core no longer hears UI-only timecode changes, so check the WebUI's UI-timecode display.
findings.deliberate_evidence: 7029db1: 'the tap on the camera screen toggles the UI timecode only'; fork-log 909aaa5.

findings.title: 1 s full get_state poll while auto ISO/WB; updateRefreshTimer on every state pass
findings.port_way: kLiveValuePollIntervalMs = 1000. The steady interval is 1 s while m_isoAuto || m_whiteBalanceAuto. updateRefreshTimer() is called at the end of the camera-set block in applyCoreState.
findings.apertar_way: Two tiers: 1 s while disconnected, 30 s steady (src/ApertarControlBridge.cpp:17-18,875-882@upstream-1.6.0). Core pushes a live value as its own event, mapped in one line: audio_level (ApertarControlBridge.cpp:1196-1199@upstream-1.6.0).
findings.why_it_matters: While auto ISO or WB is on, the GUI thread parses the whole state and runs all of applyCoreState every second, 30x upstream's cadence. The settings event carries iso_actual (CameraController.cpp:175@cinemate-port) but fires only on settings changes, so the poll is the only feed.
findings.rework: Core publishes a small rate-limited event only on change, e.g. {"event":"exposure_measured","iso_actual":..,"wb_actual_kelvin":..,"wb_measured":..}, as it does for audio_level. The UI adds it to the applyCoreState event list (F2). Delete kLiveValuePollIntervalMs, the ternary at :1016 and the call at :1621.
findings.rework_risk: Needs a Core-side change-detection point for the measured gain and WB.
findings.deliberate_evidence: f1edf96: 'While auto ISO or WB runs the bridge asks for the state every second (30 s otherwise)'.

findings.title: String-or-number tolerant parsing justified by 'KB trap 7'; Core emits typed JSON
findings.port_way: '// Core's flat JSON delivers scalars as strings (KB trap 7); accept numbers too.' This is followed by string-or-number and string-or-bool branches six times, plus an asBool lambda in applyCdngLogState.
findings.apertar_way: Typed accessors with a default: state.value("iso_auto").toBool(m_isoAuto) src/ApertarControlBridge.cpp:1321@upstream-1.6.0. Core emits these fields typed: src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:257-263,306@cinemate-port; src/camera/CameraController.cpp:207-210@cinemate-port.
findings.why_it_matters: About 40 lines of dead generality. The comment cites an internal KB trap about Core's request parser, not its output.
findings.rework: Use .toDouble()/.toInt()/.toBool() with the member as the default. Delete the lambda and the comment.

findings.title: shutterSetByCamera reads m_recording before setRecordingState in the same pass
findings.port_way: shutterSet = m_recording && m_fpsSpeedRamp && m_fpsSpeedRampKeepExposure, in the unconditional camera-set block. The recording event calls applyCoreState(message) first and setRecordingState(active) after. setRecordingState neither recomputes it nor emits cameraSetValuesChanged.
findings.apertar_way: no precedent
findings.why_it_matters: In a speed-ramp take with the Exposure policy, the shutter's camera-set mark lags one state pass at the start of the take. After stop it stays until the next pass, which is the 30 s poll if auto ISO/WB is off. Not seen on screen yet: this needs the Pi, and ramp fps changes probably bring settings events sooner.
findings.rework: Recompute m_shutterSetByCamera in setRecordingState and emit cameraSetValuesChanged there, or move the camera-set block below the recording key handling.

findings.title: Presence latches storagePrerollAutoKnown / clipNameKnown for 'older Core'
findings.port_way: Two extra properties go true once Core has sent the key; for clipNameKnown the template must also be non-empty. QML hides the controls until then. storagePrerollAutoKnown has its own signal; clipNameKnown rides on clipNameChanged.
findings.apertar_way: Feature presence comes from flags Core sends: recording_capabilities, wb_available, exposure_compensation_available (src/ApertarControlBridge.cpp:1286-1304,1331,1360-1366@upstream-1.6.0). No 'key was absent' latch.
findings.why_it_matters: After the merge UI and Core ship together, so the latches only matter for mixed versions. They add two properties and one signal for little benefit.
findings.rework: Drop the *Known properties and show the controls. If mixed versions must work, Core sends one capability flag inside recording_capabilities.

findings.title: Ticket ids, other product name, stale comments; missing <algorithm> include; setter among members
findings.port_way: Comments carry '(T31)', 'T45:', '(KB trap 7)', 'CineMate Log', 'shown green' (QML shows italics since 35b31f6) and 'older Core'. std::clamp<qint64> is used without #include <algorithm> and compiles through transitive includes. setControlsStatus is declared among the data members.
findings.apertar_way: Comments are rare, one or two lines, and say why (conv-ui-cpp section 11; e.g. ApertarControlBridge.cpp:861-862@upstream-1.6.0). std::clamp is also upstream style (src/AudioMeterBridge.cpp:179@upstream-1.6.0).
findings.why_it_matters: Internal ticket numbers and another product's name mean nothing to the original developer, and the stale colour comment misdescribes the UI.
findings.rework: Rewrite the comments in plain terms ('speed ramp', 'hardware file check'); drop the ids and 'CineMate'. Add #include <algorithm>. setControlsStatus goes away with F2.

findings.title: Clip-name reply applied twice in applyClipNameTemplate
findings.port_way: applyClipNameTemplate calls applyClipNameState(reply) after sendCoreCommand, which already fed the reply through applyCoreMessage -> applyCoreState -> applyClipNameState (ApertarControlBridge.cpp:1210,1411-1412,1734@cinemate-port). applyBufferMode and applyCdngLog set m_bufferSetting / m_cdngLogOn directly after the send (:697-700, :723-726), bypassing a setter.
findings.apertar_way: Thin variants rely on the reply: applyCaptureMode 'return sendCoreCommand(...)' (src/ApertarControlBridge.cpp:731-734@upstream-1.6.0). Older camera-setting invokables set the value through a setter after the send (applyH264Resolution, :616-618@upstream-1.6.0). So the post-send set in applyBufferMode/applyCdngLog is itself an upstream form.
findings.why_it_matters: The double apply suggests the reply is not applied automatically, which misleads the next maintainer.
findings.rework: Delete applyClipNameState(reply) and the reply object; with F1 the body becomes 'return sendCoreCommand(...)'. Optional: drop the buffer/cdng post-send assignments as F1 thins those bodies, or route them through a setter.

UI-bridges.summary: Skeptic pass: all 11 findings survive. 6 stand (F1, F3, F4, F8, F9, F11) and 5 are corrected (F2, F5, F6, F7, F10). F2's rework is changed: putting the UI writer back would clash with the port Core's own "replaced by the touch UI template" check (Core 014fa22). Instead Core writes the file from its template when the file is missing, and the template gets chip=auto. F5 is cut to five apply* methods; requestClipNamePreview is a query, like refresh(). F6 gains ApertarControlBridge.cpp:275 and lists the QML sites. F7 drops the argument about an unmodified original Core, because port Core defaults target to both; severity goes to nit. F10 now says that upstream also acts on single samples, but its unmount is not lazy and can be refused. F1 stays a blocker: with F2, every fresh port install starts in HDMI-only mode with the touch window hidden.

findings.title: Display fallback changed from 720x720 touch panel to HDMI-only 1080p (touch window hidden)
findings.port_way: kDefaultUiWidth=1920, kDefaultUiHeight=1080, m_uiLayout=landscape_large, m_hdmiExternalOnly=true, missing-key fallback true. The Core template mirrors it (7af9f13).
findings.apertar_way: src/DisplayConfigBridge.cpp:14-15@upstream-1.6.0 720/720, :579 square, :584 false, :646-649 fallback false. Upstream templates write hdmi_external_only=false (UI :323, Core ApertarCoreApp.cpp:4320-4329@upstream-1.6.0).
findings.why_it_matters: main.cpp:432-433 hides the main window when hdmiExternalOnly is set. A missing file, or an older file without the key, shows no touch UI on a touch-panel camera. Because of F2 a fresh install has no file, so every fresh port install starts HDMI-only.
findings.rework: Revert UI 7c41a27: constants, start values, hpp member defaults and the missing-key fallback go back to 720/720/square/false. Revert the [display] block in Core defaultHardwareConfigTemplate() (7af9f13). The rig sets ui_width=1920 ui_height=1080 ui_layout=landscape_large hdmi_external_only=true in its own apertar-hardware.conf.
findings.deliberate_evidence: 7c41a27: a test restart with the file moved away showed 720x720 on the rig's HDMI. Touch-panel cameras were not considered.

findings.title: Nothing creates the default apertar-hardware.conf at first start any more
findings.port_way: Both ensureDefaultHardwareConfigFile() writers and their calls are deleted (c9d841f). Core's store returns the template text when the file is missing but does not write it. Only the WebUI editor shows it. Core 014fa22 flags a missing file, or one that starts like the touch UI's default template, and offers a restore.
findings.apertar_way: src/DisplayConfigBridge.cpp:41-326,:587@upstream-1.6.0 writes /home/pi/apertar-hardware.conf from a full commented template when it is missing. The template has chip=auto under [gpio_buttons]/[gpio_encoders] (:161,:172) and gpiochip=auto under the outputs (:110,:123). A second copy is in Ina219Bridge.cpp:69-342,:497. Upstream Core only shows its template.
findings.why_it_matters: A fresh image has no documented file to edit, and because of F1 it starts HDMI-only. The Core template has no chip= line for [gpio]/[gpio_encoders], the same kind of loss as the GPIO-chip setting the owner had restored. The INA219 log names a file that does not exist.
findings.rework: Do not restore the UI writer. It would bring back the hazard c9d841f removed and trip Core's own replaced-by-UI-template check. Instead, Core writes the file from defaultHardwareConfigTemplate() at start when the file is missing and no hardware-last-written.conf exists. When that copy exists, keep the current missing/restore path. Add chip=auto under [gpio] and [gpio_encoders] in the Core template. Keep the Ina219Bridge copy removed. Document 'Core is the single writer of apertar-hardware.conf' as considered new architecture.
findings.deliberate_evidence: c9d841f: a moved file came back as the template and undid the NeoRotary fix; 'Core now owns the file and offers to restore it' (Core 014fa22). Tested at the desk only.
findings.rework_risk: Core must not write the template over a file the user moved away on purpose. Gate it on the absence of hardware-last-written.conf.

findings.title: Preview cap drops frames before frameArrived, so the Rec Run UI timecode slows or stops
findings.port_way: With APERTAR_UI_PREVIEW_RECORDING_FPS set, frames over the cap return before emit frameArrived().
findings.apertar_way: No precedent. Upstream emits frameArrived for every frame and counts it the same way (qml/CameraPage.qml:1901-1908@upstream-1.6.0).
findings.why_it_matters: The Rec Run timecode counts frameArrived while recording. With env=0, a 10 s take shows 00:00:00:00. With env=12 on a 25 fps take, the timecode runs at about half speed. This only happens when the env var is set.
findings.rework: Remove the knob (F4). If it stays on a test branch, count the frame for timecode before dropping it.
findings.deliberate_evidence: No KB or commit note covers the timecode interaction.

findings.title: APERTAR_UI_PREVIEW_RECORDING_FPS experiment knob left in the merge branch
findings.port_way: The constructor reads the env var (comment: 'A/B knob like Core's APERTAR_WEB_PREVIEW_RECORDING_FPS'). setRecording is wired from recordingChanged, and handlePreviewFrame throttles frames. Off by default.
findings.apertar_way: Upstream env knobs only select a render path: APERTAR_PREVIEW_FORCE_{CPU,PLANAR,EGL} (src/PreviewWindowRenderer.cpp:296-301@upstream-1.6.0). Upstream has no experiment throttles.
findings.why_it_matters: A test instrument with a known bug (F3) reads as a product feature to the original developer.
findings.rework: Drop setRecording, the four members, the env read and the main.cpp connect from the merge branch. Keep them on a test branch.
findings.deliberate_evidence: c234d77 calls it 'an A/B knob'. It was used on the rig with =12 and =0 (lessons/hardware-log.md:992-993). KB sweep-knobs.md:153 rates it developer-only, 'never a default'.

findings.title: Five new apply* invokables return void instead of bool
findings.port_way: Q_INVOKABLE void applyBufferMode, applyStoragePreroll, applyStoragePrerollAuto, applyClipNameTemplate, applyCdngLog.
findings.apertar_way: Every apply* returns bool and sets lastError on failure (src/ApertarControlBridge.hpp:111-141@upstream-1.6.0). Only refresh() and notifyUserActivity() are void. requestClipNamePreview is a query, like refresh(), and may stay void.
findings.why_it_matters: It breaks a one-line rule a maintainer relies on. QML cannot react to a refused command.
findings.rework: Change the five to bool. Return the sendCoreCommand result, or false, on the existing early returns, and true at the end. QML may ignore the result.
findings.deliberate_evidence: No commit or KB note.

findings.title: Ticket tags and Cinemate names in code comments
findings.apertar_way: Comments are one or two lines on why, with no ticket ids (conv-ui-cpp section 11, e.g. src/ApertarControlBridge.cpp:861-862@upstream-1.6.0).
findings.why_it_matters: The ids mean nothing to the original developer. 'CineMate' names another project.
findings.rework: Delete the T-tags. Rename 'CineMate Log' to 'cDNG log encoding'. Drop the 'A/B knob' comment with F4.

findings.title: The camera-screen timecode tap no longer changes clip timecode
findings.port_way: applyTimecodeMode(displayValue, target) has no default, and the CameraPage tap sends target=ui. Port Core treats a missing target as both, so the protocol stays compatible.
findings.apertar_way: src/ApertarControlBridge.cpp:622-636@upstream-1.6.0: one call sends set_timecode_mode and writes UI.conf timecodeMode, and Core changes the clip timecode too.
findings.why_it_matters: An upstream operator gesture changes meaning: the tap now changes only the timecode the screens show. This is a product decision, not architecture.
findings.rework: Give the invokable target = QStringLiteral("both") as its default, so the upstream one-argument call keeps its meaning. Record the tap change in the handoff. Owned by unit UI-control-bridge.
findings.deliberate_evidence: Commit 7029db1 'UI timecode and file timecode are set apart'.

findings.title: ControlsWarning.qml missing from qml.qrc (non-AOT builds)
findings.port_way: Added to APERTAR_QML_FILES only. The same branch did add ClipNameCard.qml and ClipNamePill.qml to qml.qrc.
findings.apertar_way: The two lists mirror each other (CMakeLists.txt:19-52, qml.qrc:3-33@upstream-1.6.0). Upstream has the same gap for DroppedFrameWarning.qml.
findings.why_it_matters: With APERTAR_QML_AOT=OFF (the default when cross-compiling, CMakeLists.txt:59-64), the build adds qml.qrc (:202) and main.cpp:401 loads qrc:/qml/Main.qml. CameraPage's ControlsWarning {} then does not resolve.
findings.rework: Add qml/ControlsWarning.qml and qml/DroppedFrameWarning.qml to qml.qrc in CMakeLists order.

findings.title: Core media override in MediaStatusBridge is never cleared when Core goes away
findings.port_way: updateStatus returns early with mediaMounted=false while the last Core state is removed/error and not alive. setConnected(false) does not reset it, and empty states are ignored.
findings.apertar_way: No precedent. Upstream uses QStorageInfo only (MediaStatusBridge.cpp:1232-1234@upstream-1.6.0).
findings.why_it_matters: Pull the card (Core sends removed), stop Core, then re-insert the card and let the automounter mount it: the touch UI shows no media until Core returns. statusText stays 'MEDIA REMOVED' after a later state.
findings.rework: On disconnect, ApertarControlBridge clears m_coreMediaState and emits coreMediaStateChanged("", true). MediaStatusBridge::setCoreMediaState clears m_coreMediaKnown on an empty state and resets statusText.

findings.title: Surprise card removal acts on one undebounced I2C sample, with an unrefusable unmount
findings.port_way: One read with the insert bit newly set while mounted calls handleSurpriseRemoval: umount2(MNT_DETACH) plus PCIe device remove.
findings.apertar_way: Upstream also acts on single samples (eject release -> unmountPcie(), src/CfeAutomounter.cpp:549-550@upstream-1.6.0). Its unmount is umount2(path, 0) (:704), which fails on a busy mount during a take. Failed reads return nullopt (:410-416), so only a wrong byte read cleanly triggers either path.
findings.why_it_matters: Probable: one corrupt I2C byte during a take detaches the recording card and removes its PCIe device. The upstream path would refuse while files are open.
findings.rework: Require the insert bit on two consecutive 100 ms polls before calling handleSurpriseRemoval.

findings.title: Fan mode change from the touch UI now needs a running Core
findings.port_way: applyFanMode sends Core's set_fan_mode over a private synchronous QLocalSocket (id 42002, 1 s connect, 8 s reply).
findings.apertar_way: Upstream UI wrote config.txt itself with sudo -n install (src/SystemActionBridge.cpp:431-476@upstream-1.6.0), duplicating Core's applyFanMode (Core ApertarCoreApp.cpp:3127-3175@upstream-1.6.0). Upstream Core already has set_fan_mode. The private socket client copies upstream MediaStatusBridge.cpp:15-35 (id 42001).
findings.why_it_matters: The fan mode cannot be changed while Core is down; the operator gets a clear message. The change removes a duplicate writer.
findings.rework: Keep. Mention in the handoff.
findings.deliberate_evidence: 41ff827: Core owns config.txt with a lock, and the UI's write could race a Boot Config save.

Playback.summary: I checked all 15 reviewer findings against the code on both sides. 14 survive and 1 is dropped. 7 stand as written: F1, F2, F5, F7, F8, F9, F12, F15 (F15 makes 8). 6 are corrected: F3, F4, F6, F10, F13, F14. F11 is dropped because upstream's own APERTAR_LOSSYDNG_WRITER_BYTES is the same kind of undocumented environment setting. F3: errorReplyBody is not upstream code; the port added it in f5a61b8. The page only reads the 409/503 status and body.gone. F4 goes from major to minor: the page shows a 'Playback held' line, and the browser button is greyed during a take on purpose (owner decision Q5). F6: sizeText is identical to formatBytesHuman and should go, but durationCardText copies the touch UI on purpose, so the rework must pick one duration rule for the whole list. F10: upstream does send X-Accel-Buffering, but no diagnostic headers. F13: a slot holds about 39 MiB, not 46, because the slot's rgb buffer is never filled. F14: there are three identical clocks, trimNowMs included. Still major: F1 (tutorial and critic IDs in every playback header) and F2 (one tjhandle leaked per decoded frame, because each connection gets its own one-request detached thread; upstream's RAII TurboJpegCompressor is the fix).

findings.title: Comments narrate tutorial and critic history across all playback files
findings.port_way: Every playback file opens with a header essay of several paragraphs. They cite 'design sketch v2 (not in any repository)' and 'reference for the tutorial; not in any repository until you type it'. They also use critic IDs M1/M5/M8/M9/m14, operator P1, T47/T48/T50, Q23, 'design §2.7/§4.x' and 'KB rule M5', and point to test paths in the KB.
findings.apertar_way: Comments are rare: one sentence stating a hazard or a reason (C1-I14). Upstream src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp@upstream-1.6.0 has about a dozen // lines in 13k lines and no ticket IDs.
findings.why_it_matters: The original developer cannot look up these IDs. The subsystem reads like a tutorial transcript, not like Apertar code.
findings.rework: Remove the IDs and the history from src/playback/* and from the App/AppH playback lines, and delete the essays. Keep a one-sentence hazard in four places. 1) The yield window is lock-free because the camera mutex is held during the stop drain. 2) The facts cache is keyed on mtime because readdir on exFAT is slow. 3) Why POSIX_FADV_DONTNEED is used. 4) Playback uses the frame-number clock, not the file position. Also state that RawRender is a named copy of the UI cdngimageprovider.cpp preview: name the function and drop 'critic' and 'KB rule'.
findings.deliberate_evidence: The owner's intent in BRIEF.md says the port must read as original Apertar. Nothing in the KB keeps these IDs on purpose.

findings.title: tjhandle leaks once per decoded frame
findings.port_way: PlaybackFrames.cpp:92 creates 'thread_local tjhandle handle = tjInitCompress();' and never calls tjDestroy on it. The decode runs on the web connection thread. WebServer.cpp:279-290 starts one detached thread per connection, and clientLoop (:298) serves one request with Connection: close (:136). So every frame that is decoded rather than served from cache leaks one handle and its libjpeg state.
findings.apertar_way: src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:4108-4121@upstream-1.6.0 defines struct TurboJpegCompressor, whose destructor calls tjDestroy(handle) if the handle is set. It is used as 'thread_local TurboJpegCompressor compressor;' (:4134). The port still has this at App:4807.
findings.why_it_matters: Core's memory grows with every scrub and play session.
findings.rework: Move TurboJpegCompressor, unchanged, into a small shared header, or expose encodeRgbToJpeg next to encodeYuv420ToJpeg in App. Playback calls it. Delete the raw handle.
findings.rework_risk: Low. Same output, and the encoder settings stay as they are.

findings.title: Playback routes hand-write JSON error bodies
findings.port_way: The routes build bodies by hand: response.body = "{\"ok\":false,\"error\":\"Playback held: " + hold + ...; {"ok":false,"busy":true} with no sentence; and {"ok":false,"error":"This clip was removed.","gone":true}. The hold check is repeated in five routes.
findings.apertar_way: Upstream web routes set the body only through errorReply(-1, sentence) or okReply, e.g. src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:7204,7218@upstream-1.6.0. Upstream App has no response.body = "{ literal. errorReplyBody is not upstream: the port added it in f5a61b8 (Controls unit).
findings.why_it_matters: The replies are built in a way foreign to Apertar, and the busy reply carries no sentence for the operator.
findings.rework: For hold and busy, use errorReply(-1, sentence). The page reads only the 409/503 status (WCP:12355-12358), so the hold and busy keys can go. For gone, the page needs body.gone (WCP:12361): answer 410 through errorReply, or keep the one extra key through errorReplyBody if that helper survives the Controls review. Put the repeated hold check in one local lambda in handleWebRequest (C1-I17).

findings.title: In a hold, /api/media drops items without cached facts
findings.port_way: 'if (held && !haveFacts) continue;' applies during a take, a write drain, standby, a media test or a yield window. In that time H.264/ProRes container folders, every Timelapse_* folder and every take not yet probed disappear from the list, while Photos/ is still read from the card. The page shows 'Playback held: ... Pictures return when it ends.' (WCP:11939-11941), which promises thumbnails back, not missing items. The browser button is greyed during a take (WCP:12022-12024, owner Q5), so this happens when the browser is already open as a take starts.
findings.apertar_way: discoverMediaLibraryItems (src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:6282@upstream-1.6.0) lists every folder whenever media is mounted.
findings.why_it_matters: Items disappear from an open list during a take. The hold's own goal, no card reads, is not met for Photos/ either.
findings.rework: In a hold, list the bare entry for folders without facts: name, kind, category from the folder name, size '--', and no recursive scan. The comment at App:7488 already promises this ('or the bare entry'). Alternatively skip Photos/ as well and say in the status line that the list is partial.
findings.deliberate_evidence: decisions.md Q4 'hold everything' (thumbnails) and Q5 'greyed' button. The vanishing list entries are not discussed.

findings.title: Downloads refused in every hold, also standby
findings.port_way: Downloads get 409 for the recording, writing, media_test, standby and media holds. A running download stops within one 64 KiB chunk, and the zip child gets SIGTERM.
findings.apertar_way: /api/media/download (src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:7197-7330@upstream-1.6.0) has no recording gate.
findings.why_it_matters: Upstream behaviour is narrowed. The original developer must find it documented.
findings.rework: Keep the behaviour. Add one line to the README's WebUI section. Reply through errorReply (see F3).
findings.deliberate_evidence: working/playback/decisions.md Q21 (takes: refuse new downloads, stop running ones) and Q20 (hold in standby). The writing and media_test cases extend Q21.

findings.title: Clip text helpers duplicate App formatters
findings.port_way: sizeText produces the same text as formatBytesHuman (App:4595@cinemate-port). durationCardText produces '01:02:03'/'00:00'; it copies the touch UI card text (comment at ClipProbe.hpp:29). Other list items use durationTextForFrameCount, which produces '1:02:03'/'--'. fps text comes from %g.
findings.apertar_way: formatBytesHuman (src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:3922@upstream-1.6.0), durationTextForFrameCount (:5747), durationTextForSeconds (:5767), and compactNumber(fps) + " FPS" in discoverMediaLibraryItems.
findings.why_it_matters: One list follows two formatting rules, and the rules are maintained in two places.
findings.rework: Delete sizeText and use formatBytesHuman. Let ClipFacts carry numbers only (bytes, fps, span seconds) and let App format them. For duration, choose one rule for the whole WebUI list (touch-UI parity or App's helper) and apply it to every item kind.
findings.deliberate_evidence: The comment states touch-UI parity (design §4.2). The clash with Core's own formatters is not discussed.

findings.title: Dead code and hooks for tests kept outside the repo
findings.port_way: DecodeSlot::rgb is never filled: renderPreview allocates its own Rgb8Image per request, so the 'rgb 7 MiB per slot' comment is false. DecodeSlots::bytesHeld() (the total), ClipFactsCache::probes(), FrameList::numberAtTime and DngInfo::tailBytesRead have no caller in the repo. The header cites the KB file working/tools/playback/frames_test.cpp.
findings.apertar_way: Upstream Core has no tests and no tools/ directory, and no test hooks in src.
findings.why_it_matters: The reader trips over unused API and a wrong claim about memory.
findings.rework: Either render into slot->rgb (pass the buffer to renderPreview) or delete the member and fix the comment. Delete the unused API, or move the KB test into tools/ next to dng_limits_test.cpp so the hooks have a caller.

findings.title: Hold rule built twice; name string parsed back into enum
findings.port_way: HoldSignals is filled by hand twice: in buildWebStateJson and in playbackHoldReason. The watcher maps the returned string back to playback::Hold with an if-chain. It also calls playbackHoldReason(false) twice per cycle, and each call reads the camera mutex 4 times. The comment at :9362 says the builder avoids a second camera read, but :9364 calls camera_.isRecording() again.
findings.apertar_way: Upstream gates inline: if (camera_.isRecording() || soundRecordingActive() || camera_.timelapseActive()) (src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:7514,7586@upstream-1.6.0).
findings.why_it_matters: More indirection than the job needs, and a comment that the next line contradicts.
findings.rework: playbackHoldReason returns playback::Hold. Call holdName() only where JSON is written. Make one call per watcher cycle and reuse it for both the yield and the trim. Fix or drop the stale comment.

findings.title: FORMAT row guesses the lossy ratio from the clip name
findings.port_way: A clip counts as lossy 3:1 only if its folder name contains cDNG_3to1 or lossy3, and as 5:1 only if it contains cDNG_5to1 or lossy5. Lossy DNGs are written as compression 7 plus LinearizationTable (src/lossydng/LossyDngEncoder.cpp:537,544@cinemate-port), the same tags as lossless companded files.
findings.apertar_way: no precedent
findings.why_it_matters: The token picker allows custom clip-name templates without {format} or {comp}. A clip named with {date}_{clip} and recorded lossy 3:1 shows FORMAT 'Clear HDR 12-bit companded · lossless'.
findings.rework: Derive the ratio from something Core writes (a tag or the ImageDescription, set at write time), or drop the lossless/lossy suffix when the name does not say.

findings.title: Playback RAM on 1-2 GB boards; JPEG caches never trimmed
findings.port_way: Each slot holds about 39 MiB at IMX283 size (samples 38 MiB + scratch 1.3 MiB); the comment's 46 MiB counts the unused rgb buffer. There are 2 slots by default and up to 4, plus about 7 MiB per render in flight. The JPEG LRU caches (8 + 24 MiB) have no way to be cleared. Slots are trimmed after 30 s idle or in a hold; the caches never are.
findings.apertar_way: Upstream Core holds no decode memory.
findings.why_it_matters: Up to 32 MiB of JPEG cache stays resident through takes on a Pi 4 2 GB or CM4 1 GB. Not confirmed on a Pi; to check, run free -m during a 4-tab scrub and then during a take.
findings.rework: Clear both JPEG caches in trimIdleFrameSlots when hold is true. Fix the slot comment. Note the peak memory in the README.
findings.deliberate_evidence: The comments cost out slot memory. Cache trimming is not discussed.

findings.title: Diagnostic response headers no page reads
findings.port_way: The frame route sends X-Frame-Count, X-Frame-Source and X-Decode-Ms. WCP:12368-12370 reads only X-Frame-Number, X-Frame-Index and X-Histogram, and no UI code reads them.
findings.apertar_way: Upstream sends one functional header (X-Accel-Buffering, src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:7114@upstream-1.6.0) and no diagnostic headers.
findings.why_it_matters: Debug leftovers.
findings.rework: Drop the three headers and FrameOut::fromCache/decodeMs.

findings.title: liblj92 README describes the UI's use
findings.port_way: The file is a byte-identical copy of the UI's (diff -r against ui-upstream is empty). It says 'Used to decode lossless JPEG tiles in the UI and independently verify the Apertar encoder.'
findings.apertar_way: That sentence belongs to ui-upstream third_party/liblj92/README.apertar.md.
findings.why_it_matters: It misleads about how Core uses the library.
findings.rework: State Core's use (src/playback/DngFrameReader.hpp, WebUI playback). Keep the provenance and local-fix lines.

findings.title: Three identical millisecond steady clocks
findings.port_way: steadyMs(), playbackNowMs() and trimNowMs() (port commit d44b177) are the same expression.
findings.apertar_way: Upstream writes the steady_clock expression inline where it is needed (src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:7036,8617@upstream-1.6.0).
findings.why_it_matters: Small duplication.
findings.rework: Keep one: playbackNowMs in PlaybackHold.hpp, or inline the expression as upstream does. Delete the others.

findings.title: UI helper namespace style
findings.port_way: namespace apertar::clipframes
findings.apertar_way: ui-upstream helper namespaces are VideoPlayback (src/VideoPlayback.hpp:13), lowPower and standbyUsb. No apertar:: namespace appears in ui-upstream src.
findings.why_it_matters: Small style drift in the UI.
findings.rework: Rename to namespace ClipFrameFiles, so the namespace matches the file name, as VideoPlayback does.

Driver-imx585.summary: Skeptic pass on the 13 findings: 8 stand and 5 are corrected (F1, F4, F7, F8, F12). None dropped. Corrections: F1, 1.6.0 Core also allows auto fallback for a mono sensor, so the 1920x1038 configure failure affects the colour sensor only; Core commit 900d282 is added as evidence that the rename was deliberate. F4, the count was wrong: 42 entries at 960/1024 wide, 44 under 1280 including binned 1080x1080. F7, the per-mode hmax_table pointer and the two update loops are Will Whang's own design (70bdb26), so they were removed from the finding; what remains is the unused min_vmax_default hook and 2 wrong literals, now a nit. F8, Core already probes each table row at start but drops rows the driver refuses without logging; the rework is narrowed to logging them. F12, 9 experimental: subjects plus about 7 fix-ups, not 22, and WP ids in 13 subjects. Hint answers: 18 of the 20 sizes 1.6.0 Core requests are still there; 3840x2076 and 1920x1038 are gone. No existing control changed its default. Colour 12-bit CCMP Clear HDR is now offered without the ccmp param.
conforms: Every other size 1.6.0 Core requests is still advertised under the same name (18 of 20), APERTAR.md:155-157@cinemate-port
The Clear HDR HMAX floor and the per-mode HMAX tables follow Will Whang's c0f5404/70bdb26 structure, imx585.c:3271-3346@cinemate-port

findings.title: 1.85:1 sizes renamed (3840x2076->3840x2072, 1920x1038->1920x1036); unmodified 1.6.0 Core cannot configure 1920x1038 on a colour sensor
findings.port_way: Centred 1.85:1 windows of 2072 sensor rows at crop top 44 (VST 56), advertised as 3840x2072 and 1920x1036 in both the 12-bit and 10-bit tables. The port Core migrates the old sizes (migratedImx585CropResolution, Apertar-Core CameraController.cpp:441-453@cinemate-port).
findings.apertar_way: The baseline advertises 3840x2076 and 1920x1038 with IMX585_WIN_CROP_REGS(54, 2076) (base imx585.c:586-591, 667-672, 817@apertar). Core 1.6.0 requests both (core-upstream CameraController.cpp:366-396@upstream-1.6.0), and the WebUI (WebControlPage.cpp:5120,5254,5268@upstream-1.6.0) and touch UI (ApertarControlBridge.cpp:1842,1912@upstream-1.6.0) offer them. Core tries an explicit sensorConfig first (:6010, :6115-6118@upstream-1.6.0). Auto fallback exists only for mono, IMX294/577 and isImx585Raw12CropResolution (:5993-5996@upstream-1.6.0). libcamera returns Invalid on a sensor size mismatch (pipeline_base.cpp:226-238@libcamera apertar).
findings.why_it_matters: A 1.6.0 image that updates only the driver loses 2K 1.85:1 on the colour sensor: configure fails for 1920x1038 because it has no fallback. 4K 1.85:1 probably records 3840x2072 through the auto fallback (unconfirmed; the Core 'sensorConfig=auto' log line on a Pi settles it). Mono falls back to auto for both sizes. Driver and Core must merge in lockstep, and both 1.6.0 UIs list sizes the driver no longer has.
findings.rework: Keep the old advertised sizes. Add IMX585_MODE_CROP_3840X2076 and IMX585_MODE_CROP_BIN_1920X1038 to supported_modes[] and supported_10bit_modes[] with crop {0, 40, 3840, 2076}: VST 52 and height 2076 both pass imx585_program_window(), at two rows off centre. Then delete Core's migratedImx585CropResolution/migrateImx585LadderRungs and the WebUI alias entries (WebControlPage.cpp:9078-9085@cinemate-port). This also removes the 3840x2072 duplicate warning (F6). Fallback option: keep 2072/1036 and state in the merge notes that driver and Core release together.
findings.deliberate_evidence: APERTAR.md 'Sizes that changed'; the Core comment at CameraController.cpp:441-445@cinemate-port gives the VST-54 alignment reason; Core commit 900d282 (fork-log row d44b177).
findings.rework_risk: Not run on hardware: VST 52 needs one take at each size on the Pi.

findings.title: Mode table carries work-package history, 'Experimental' labels on shipping modes, references to absent files and stale comments
findings.port_way: 54 WP-585 references and 65 'experimental' comment lines. A history block of about 90 lines sits above the enum. It cites INVESTIGATION.md, RESULTS.md, ASPECT-RATIOS.md, WORK-PACKAGES.md, D1, DEC-1, DEC-2 and G1-G4, none of which is in the repo. Stale comments: :2950 cites a '1280x760' mode that does not exist; :2120-2124 says everything below 1440 moved to the 1x1 window, yet 2x2 960/1024 entries follow; the mono Y10 comment at :3026 says '4K 10-bit' but the branch returns all 62 modes.
findings.apertar_way: The baseline uses one-line per-mode comments ('1.85:1 2x2 binned, full-width RAW12 crop', base imx585.c:815@apertar) and short routing comments in get_mode_table (base imx585.c:1384-1387@apertar). The driver author's longer comments in 70bdb26 explain hardware, not process.
findings.why_it_matters: The original developer cannot follow ticket ids or absent documents. Shipping modes labelled 'Experimental' read as unfinished, and the stale comments mislead.
findings.rework: Replace the history with an invariant block of about 20 lines: table order, the three ranges get_mode_table hands out, the RAW16 OB-row rule and crop in sensor coordinates. Give each entry one comment line with its ratio and binning. Strip all WP/D/DEC/G ids and the names of absent files. Fix the three stale comments. Move the hardware findings (windowed 2x2 RAW16 = pedestal, mono binned HDR = pedestal) to APERTAR.md 'Validation'.
findings.deliberate_evidence: The comments narrate the work-package process; nothing records a decision to keep them.

findings.title: 1440x1080 has a different field of view in 12-bit (1x1 1440 window) and 10-bit (2x2 of a 2880 window)
findings.port_way: In the 12-bit table, supported_modes[28] is a 1x1 crop {1200, 540, 1440, 1080}. In the 10-bit table, supported_10bit_modes[2] is 2x2 over {480, 0, 2880, 2160}.
findings.apertar_way: no precedent (the baseline had no 1440x1080 and no 10-bit table)
findings.why_it_matters: Failing case: select 1440x1080 and switch from 12-bit to 10-bit. The size stays the same, but the framing changes by 2x (centre tele crop vs 4:3 full height).
findings.rework: Give both tables the same geometry: either a 1x1 1440 window in the 10-bit table, or a 2x2 windowed 1440x1080 in the 12-bit table kept outside the HDR range. Or name the difference in APERTAR.md.
findings.deliberate_evidence: WP-585-5 comments on both entries explain why each table kept its own variant.

findings.title: 42 entries at 960/1024 wide (44 under 1280) are advertised but hidden by Apertar Core by default
findings.port_way: Each SDR table has 11 crops at 960 wide and 10 at 1024 wide: 2x2 crops of the 1920/2048 windows from commit 18c1eb2, checked on the host only. With binned 1080x1080, each table has 22 entries under 1280. Core hides widths below 1280 unless APERTAR_IMX585_MIN_MODE_WIDTH is set.
findings.apertar_way: no precedent
findings.why_it_matters: The driver carries data and validation debt for modes Apertar does not offer, and Core gains an env-var knob to hide them.
findings.rework: Pick one. Either drop the 960/1024 families from the Apertar branch and remove the Core env knob, or offer them in Core and remove the knob.
findings.deliberate_evidence: Commit 18c1eb2 (WP-585-10); Imx585Modes.hpp:15-16 'hidden as in cinemate'.

findings.title: The clearhdr_windowed_binning module parameter and the tools/clearhdr-gate kit depend on CineMate and have no recorded run
findings.port_way: A bool module parameter (0444) widens the 12-bit HDR range to the windowed 2x2 crops for a hardware test. The kit requires CineMate settings.jsonc and cinepi-raw.
findings.apertar_way: no precedent (the baseline driver has no module params and no tools dir)
findings.why_it_matters: This is a test switch and a CineMate procedure in the Apertar driver, and APERTAR.md has to tell users not to set it.
findings.rework: Keep the range end at IMX585_MODE_CROP_1440X1080_HDR12 and its static_assert. Remove the module parameter, its probe warning and tools/clearhdr-gate/ from the Apertar branch. A later validated change is a one-line range edit.
findings.deliberate_evidence: The comment above the param (imx585.c:1025-1037) gives the reason for using a module param instead of DT.

findings.title: The probe-time table audit prints a known warning on every boot, and the window predicate exists four times
findings.port_way: imx585_check_mode_table() runs at every probe. Its duplicate-size check is table-wide, so 3840x2072 at supported_modes[5] (SDR 1.85:1) and [67] (RAW16 1.89:1) warns on every boot, although the two never share a get_mode_table range. The alignment predicate is copied into imx585_program_window(), the audit and two Python tools ('must stay identical').
findings.apertar_way: no precedent (the baseline has no audit)
findings.why_it_matters: A permanent harmless warning in dmesg, plus four copies of one predicate kept in sync by hand.
findings.rework: Add static bool imx585_window_ok(const struct imx585_mode *) and use it in imx585_program_window(). Either drop the probe audit (the tables are static and the host tool covers them) or check duplicates per get_mode_table range. Merge the two Python tools into one.
findings.deliberate_evidence: Commits 74b9b73 and aa6c723; commit 8f508fb accepts the collision.

findings.title: Unused min_vmax_default override and two wrong min_vmax literals
findings.port_way: min_vmax_default is 0 on every windowed entry, which is the only place it is read. It is set to IMX585_VMAX_DEFAULT on 6 non-windowed entries, where it is ignored. The audit checks this unused override. The runtime-overwritten min_vmax literals are consistent except one per table (10-bit 1440x1080: 1150, derived 2230).
findings.apertar_way: The driver author's imx585_mode has min_hmax/min_vmax 'computed at runtime' and no override (70bdb26 imx585.c:371-373, 1210-1248). The per-mode hmax_table pointer and the separate 10-bit loop with its 1039 MHz rule are his design and stay.
findings.why_it_matters: An override hook nobody uses, plus misleading numbers. Small, but it is more to read.
findings.rework: Delete min_vmax_default from struct imx585_mode, its 158 initialisers, the ternaries in imx585_update_hmax and the audit's override check. Fix or zero the two wrong literals.
findings.deliberate_evidence: Commit 5901dc8 'experimental: add per-mode VMAX default field', no user.

findings.title: Core's Imx585Modes.hpp hand-copies the four driver tables; rows that do not match the driver are dropped without a log line
findings.port_way: Core keeps four constexpr arrays 'as the driver lists it'. At start it configures each row and skips rows the driver refuses with a silent continue. Rows that only the driver has are never offered.
findings.apertar_way: Upstream Core also hard-codes IMX585 sizes (core-upstream CameraController.cpp:360-396@upstream-1.6.0), on a smaller scale. Fork main probes sensor modes at start (core-main f60e301).
findings.why_it_matters: Any driver table edit needs a matching Core edit. A mismatch disappears without a log line.
findings.rework: In the Core unit, keep Imx585Modes.hpp for policy (H16 OB rows, hiding). Log each table row the probe drops, and each driver size (formats.sizes()) that no table row covers. Optionally add a host test that parses imx585.c like tools/replay_mode_table_audit.py.
findings.deliberate_evidence: Imx585Modes.hpp:3 names the driver branch it mirrors.

findings.title: Docs: the README CineMate section, the fork clone URL and the branch name cinemate-port
findings.port_way: The README clone line is 'git clone -b cinemate-port https://github.com/Tiramisioux/...'. A 120-line 'CineMate branch (cinemate-7modes)' section has a CineMate CLI/settings/Redis layer table and a seven-mode matrix that no longer describes the tables. APERTAR.md says to use cinemate-port.
findings.apertar_way: The baseline README and 70bdb26 point the clone at will127534 and cover only driver install, overlay and link rates.
findings.why_it_matters: After a merge, the docs point at the fork and at another product's layers.
findings.rework: Remove the CineMate layer table and the seven-mode matrix. Keep the blend-menu table, the HMAX floor and the link-rate notes. Set the URL and branch name to the merge target.

findings.title: Colour 12-bit CCMP Clear HDR is default-on, overriding the driver author's opt-in ccmp gate
findings.port_way: clearhdr_ccmp = !mono || sony,clearhdr-ccmp, so the ccmp param has no effect on colour.
findings.apertar_way: Will Whang's 70bdb26 (Apertar-Studio driver main) requires the ccmp overlay param for 12-bit CCMP on both variants. The 1.6.0 image driver offered 4K 12-bit HDR unconditionally (base imx585.c:1392-1394, 1429-1432@apertar).
findings.why_it_matters: The behaviour departs from the driver author's own design. Mono now needs ccmp, which comes from 70bdb26 and is not the port's change. Unmodified 1.6.0 Core does not use Clear HDR, so it sees no runtime effect.
findings.rework: No code change. Name the departure in the merge notes and APERTAR.md, and agree it with the driver author.
findings.deliberate_evidence: The b6a6f5b commit message explains why colour should not need the param.

findings.title: 12-bit Clear HDR is offered on 27 1x1 windowed crops with no recorded hardware validation, while the 2x2 crops are gated for the same reason
findings.port_way: The HDR-12 range is supported_modes[0..28]: binned 1080p, 4K and every 1x1 crop, including the 1920/2048 windows (18c1eb2, host-only). Hardware evidence exists only for 16-bit 1x1 crops (fdd767a) and the seven full-field modes.
findings.apertar_way: The baseline offered 12-bit HDR at 4K only (base imx585.c:1392-1394, 1429-1432@apertar).
findings.why_it_matters: The risk policy is inconsistent, and users may get invalid HDR frames at a crop. Unconfirmed.
findings.rework: Record one 12-bit HDR take at a 3840 crop and one at a 1920-window crop on the Pi. If they fail, end the HDR-12 range after the 4K entry plus the validated crops.

findings.title: 55 commits, with 9 'experimental:' subjects, about 7 fix-ups of earlier commits and WP numbers in 13 subjects
findings.port_way: On 2026-09-19 there are nine 'experimental:' commits (b050b7c..4949b06) and fix-ups such as 7061c74 'Fix IMX585 mode enum and array ordering', 27c7cb4 'Restore IMX585 12-bit mode table ordering' and a09ac49 'experimental: fix mode table after low-res removal'. WP-585-n appears in 13 subjects. The 55 include 4 Will Whang commits and 2 merges.
findings.apertar_way: The driver author's commits are one feature per commit with a plain subject (3680bf4, c0f5404, 11178c8, 70bdb26).
findings.why_it_matters: The history is hard to review or bisect for the original developer.
findings.rework: Keep the four Will Whang commits. Squash Patrik's into about 6 feature commits: mode families and window programming, RAW10 families, binned Clear HDR, crop reporting and geometry controls, logging, docs.

findings.title: The read-only geometry controls (+10..+14) have no Apertar consumer
findings.port_way: Mode Binning and Mode Crop Left/Top/Width/Height are custom read-only controls. Their consumer is cinepi-raw (cinepi_raw.cpp:177-217).
findings.apertar_way: Apertar Core reads only base+0/+1/+5 (CameraController.cpp:7034-7037@cinemate-port). The standard V4L2_SEL_TGT_CROP carries the same data.
findings.why_it_matters: These are extra custom controls; a maintainer may wonder who reads them.
findings.rework: Keep them, and say in APERTAR.md that Cinemate reads them and Apertar uses the selection API.
findings.deliberate_evidence: Commit b703f46.

Driver-imx283.summary: Skeptic pass on 14 findings: 9 stand, 5 corrected, 0 dropped. F1: reference lines are 37, not 43. F3: three more stale comments added. F8: downgraded to nit, because upstream Core also hand-codes sensor sizes and the probe cannot replace the table. F11: the "Your Name", --force and REMAKE_INITRD commits are Will Whang's origin/6.12.y history, not the port's. F14: reduced to the lost final newline. The top issues are F2 (crop_vmax defaults on with unmeasured VMAX floors) and F1 (comment mass and internal vocabulary).

findings.title: Comment mass and internal vocabulary (WP/DEC/REBUILD/ROUND2/GAP/development refs)
findings.port_way: 1116 comment lines (base 198). Long HISTORY blocks with DNG file names and dates. 37 lines carry WP-283-n, DEC-4, REBUILD.md, ROUND2 Defect C4, GAP.md or development/... references, and development/ is not in the repo. MODULE_PARM_DESC(crop_vmax) points to development/imx283-crop-fps/.
findings.apertar_way: imx585 origin/apertar crops carry one-line comments ('Full-width RAW12 aspect crops. VST is centered inside the 2160 active area.', imx585.c:585@apertar). Base imx283 has 198 comment lines.
findings.why_it_matters: The original developer cannot tell current behaviour from narrated history and cannot follow the references.
findings.rework: Cut each block to what it does plus one non-obvious why. Move the measurement history (2704 vs 2736 columns, 236/924, 784/852) to KB lessons/hardware-log.md. Delete every WP/DEC/REBUILD/ROUND2/GAP/development reference, including the one in MODULE_PARM_DESC(crop_vmax).
findings.deliberate_evidence: Comments narrate agent rebuild rounds (REBUILD, ROUND2 Defect C4)

findings.title: crop_vmax defaults to 1 (unmeasured per-crop VMAX floors on) while Apertar requires 0
findings.port_way: static bool crop_vmax = true; described as 'experimental, UNMEASURED'. APERTAR.md tells Apertar users to create /etc/modprobe.d/imx283.conf with crop_vmax=0. Core's table cap is the crop_vmax=0 floor (Core CameraController.cpp:3332-3337, Imx283Modes.hpp:9-10).
findings.apertar_way: No precedent in Apertar 1.6.0. The same driver makes its other unvalidated feature opt-in: experimental_modes defaults to off (imx283.c:269).
findings.why_it_matters: setup.sh and dkms.postinst install no modprobe.d file. So a user who follows the README runs any libcamera app on unmeasured VMAX floors, for example about 35 fps on the 2.55:1 Mode-0 row. Apertar caps at the crop_vmax=0 floor anyway, so the parameter brings Apertar nothing.
findings.rework: Delete crop_vmax, the crop_min_VMAX field and the _crop_vmax macro argument until the floors are measured (at minimum, default it to false). Drop the crop_vmax modprobe.d instruction from APERTAR.md.
findings.deliberate_evidence: 94eb7e2 'imx283: enable experimental crop VMAX by default'; the comment at imx283.c:271-276 justifies it for an experiment

findings.title: Residue of the reverted active-only experiment: identity wrappers, hand-rolled nearest-size, stale comments
findings.port_way: imx283_output_width/height/crop return mode fields unchanged (31 call sites). They were added by 4350e3e, 4123dd2 and efe2463 and kept after revert a852cfe. imx283_find_nearest_mode replaces v4l2_find_nearest_size. Three stale comments: 'the driver now emits an active-only frame' (2506-2509); '2x2-binned modes ... overclaims by 32 columns' (58-62), which the HISTORY at 420-444 contradicts; and v4l2_find_nearest_size cited at 1463 and 1504, though the code no longer calls it.
findings.apertar_way: The base driver used mode->width/height/crop directly and called v4l2_find_nearest_size (base imx283.c:1121@origin/master).
findings.why_it_matters: Indirection with no function, and comments that describe behaviour that was reverted or disproved.
findings.rework: Delete the three wrappers and use the mode fields. Restore v4l2_find_nearest_size. Delete or fix the three stale comments. Tie-breaking differs: the kernel stops at the first exact match and keeps the last of equal non-exact distances, while the port keeps the first. So add a host check that each table has no duplicate transport sizes.
findings.deliberate_evidence: git log -S imx283_output_width finds only 4350e3e, 4123dd2 and efe2463, all part of the experiment that a852cfe reverted

findings.title: Dead macros IMX283_CROP_1X1 / IMX283_CROPPED_1X1_MODE and compile-time WINDOW_LEFT switch
findings.port_way: IMX283_CROP_1X1 has no caller, and IMX283_CROPPED_1X1_MODE is used only by it ('kept correct rather than deleted'). Three macros select between 236 and 924.
findings.apertar_way: No precedent. The base had a single imx283_UHD_area rectangle (base imx283.c:223@origin/master).
findings.why_it_matters: Dead code and an A/B switch read as unfinished work.
findings.rework: Delete both crop macros. Write .left = 924 with a one-line derivation. Move the 236 history to the KB.
findings.deliberate_evidence: The comment at imx283.c:732-737 says the macros are kept on purpose

findings.title: Function-local statics shared by all driver instances
findings.port_way: get_mode_table builds static filtered tables lazily, without a lock. __imx283_get_pad_crop returns a pointer to static struct v4l2_rect output_crop.
findings.apertar_way: The base returned the const tables and &imx283->mode->crop (base imx283.c:717-735, 1143-1155@origin/master).
findings.why_it_matters: With two IMX283 sensors (CM5 cam0 + cam1), concurrent G_SELECTION calls on the two subdevs hold different mutexes and write the same static, so one sensor can return the other's crop. Probable, not run. Apertar runs one camera, so exposure is low, and the fix is one line.
findings.rework: return &imx283->mode->crop. Keep the const tables and skip .experimental entries while walking them (enum_frame_size, nearest size), or build filtered copies per instance in probe.

findings.title: IMX283_ASPECT_MODE takes 15 positional arguments; parent timing repeated in 51 rows
findings.apertar_way: imx585 origin/apertar uses small macros over the numbers that vary, IMX585_WIN_CROP_REGS(vst, vwidth) (imx585.c:563-572@apertar). The port's own IMX283_ASPECT_MODE_1C(_w,_h) (imx283.c:862) already has that shape.
