findings.why_it_matters: The rows are unreadable, and a change to a parent's timing must be repeated in every row.
findings.rework: Write one (_w, _h) wrapper per family (MODE_0/2/2A/3/1/1A) over the generic macro, like _1C, and keep the CENTERED_RECTANGLE derivation. Do this after F2: removing crop_vmax removes the last per-row timing argument.
findings.deliberate_evidence: The macro comment explains why the left/top arguments were removed (REBUILD)

findings.title: Probe-time imx283_check_mode_table audits static data every boot
findings.port_way: An audit of about 150 lines with six checks, dev_warn only, run in every probe.
findings.apertar_way: No precedent in the base driver or in imx585 origin/apertar.
findings.why_it_matters: Boot-time kernel code that checks compile-time data.
findings.rework: Move it to a host check (a small script or test in the driver repo). If it stays in the driver, keep only the crop-inside-active and binning-non-zero checks.
findings.deliberate_evidence: The comment at imx283.c:1757-1776 explains the choice

findings.title: Core Imx283Modes.hpp hand-copies the 57 driver rows; provenance is a branch name
findings.port_way: A separate header holds the 57 active sizes and the crop_vmax=0 floors, host-tested by tools/imx283_modes_test.cpp. The header cites 'Tiramisioux/imx283-v4l2-driver, branch cinemate-port'.
findings.apertar_way: Upstream also hand-codes sensor sizes in Core, inline (isImx585FullHdCropResolution, CameraController.cpp:366-377@upstream-1.6.0), so a hand table is the upstream pattern at a larger scale. The probe cannot replace it: it gives only transport sizes, the OB offset depends on binning, libcamera does not expose the driver's Mode controls, and the floors are still needed.
findings.why_it_matters: An edit to the driver table drifts silently from Core, and the branch name will not exist after the merge.
findings.rework: Keep the table. Replace the branch name with the driver commit it matches. Add one line to the driver's APERTAR.md saying that Core's Imx283Modes.hpp must change together with the mode tables.
findings.deliberate_evidence: The header comment states the experimental_modes=0 / crop_vmax=0 contract

findings.title: MODE_1C window .top = 852 not centred on the corrected active area (784); .left 924 OB unchecked on raw
findings.port_way: .top = 852 is centred against the old, swapped active.top = 108 and is programmed into VWINPOS (comment 828-833). At .left 924, columns 0..95 were checked only on an ISP preview frame.
findings.apertar_way: No precedent.
findings.why_it_matters: The UHD window is 68 rows off-centre, and the DNG ActiveArea may be wrong if columns 0..95 at 924 are not optical black.
findings.rework: Take one raw 3936x2176 frame at .left 924 with .top 784 and another with .top 852, then keep one value with a one-line comment.
findings.deliberate_evidence: Listed under APERTAR.md Open questions; the comment at imx283.c:810-833 says .top 852 stays until 784 is tested

findings.title: Docs: stale EXPERIMENTAL_CROPS.md shipped; APERTAR.md and README name the fork branch and CineMate
findings.port_way: A doc marked STALE is kept. APERTAR.md has a lineage paragraph about cinemate-modes/CineMate. README says git clone -b cinemate-port of the fork.
findings.apertar_way: The Core README says drivers are installed separately and names no fork branch (core-upstream README.md:87@upstream-1.6.0).
findings.why_it_matters: The stale doc and the Cinemate lineage confuse the reader.
findings.rework: Delete EXPERIMENTAL_CROPS.md and the places that mention it (APERTAR.md:7-8, MODULE_PARM_DESC(experimental_modes), imx283.c:257). Trim APERTAR.md to install, config.txt, modprobe, modes and open questions. Set the branch name at merge.
findings.deliberate_evidence: 53ae581 marked the file stale instead of deleting it

findings.title: Port history: reverted 11-commit experiment, WP numbers in subjects
findings.port_way: 93 commits in the range. 6 of them are from origin/6.12.y (Will Whang and 'Your Name': the upstream author's history, not the port); about 87 are port commits. The history is step by step, with an experiment and its revert, and 7 subjects carry WP-283-n numbers.
findings.apertar_way: See conv-style-commits.md and the squash plan in sweep-commits-ui-drivers.md:185.
findings.why_it_matters: From the steps, the reader cannot tell whether 236 or 924 is current, or which table is.
findings.rework: Use origin/6.12.y as the baseline. Squash the port into one mode-set commit plus 4a1662e, d810aa7, d6ec1c7, 4064e88 and one docs commit (257c9cf is already on 6.12.y).

findings.title: Nine read-only Mode * geometry controls have no Apertar consumer
findings.port_way: Custom controls at V4L2_CID_USER_BASE+0x2100, read by name by cinepi-raw (core/driver_mode_metadata.hpp, cinepi/cinepi_raw.cpp). Nothing in Apertar-Core/src reads them.
findings.apertar_way: No precedent in 1.6.0. The imx585 port uses the same names.
findings.why_it_matters: API surface whose only consumer is Cinemate's recorder.
findings.rework: Drop the controls together with the active_width/active_height fields, unless an Apertar consumer is planned. If they stay, document them in APERTAR.md as a Cinemate interface.

findings.title: Base sizes 2784x1548 (MODE_2A) and 5568x3094 (MODE_1A) removed
findings.port_way: The full MODE_2A entry is replaced by ten 2736-wide rows (1.78:1 is 2784x1544). The MODE_1A height goes from 3078 to 3076 (transport 5568x3092).
findings.apertar_way: Apertar 1.6.0 never requested these sizes (it has no IMX283). The baseline is Will Whang's driver; 2A itself was added by Patrik in 95183c8.
findings.why_it_matters: Third-party apps that ask for the old sizes get the nearest row. No Apertar regression.
findings.rework: None; add one line to the driver doc.
findings.deliberate_evidence: Commit text gives the reason as an even Bayer origin; see the comment at imx283.c:1459-1462

findings.title: Lost final newline after MODULE_LICENSE
findings.port_way: The file ends without a newline; origin/master and origin/6.12.y both end with one. dkms install --force and the REMAKE_INITRD removal are Will Whang's fea3d35 and e8e3d4a on origin/6.12.y, not the port's.
findings.apertar_way: No precedent (driver install is outside Apertar).
findings.why_it_matters: Noise in the diff.
findings.rework: Restore the final newline.

WCP-06.summary: Skeptic pass: all 13 findings survive. Nine stand as written. Four are corrected. F1 now notes that the port keeps some upstream media* names next to the pb* ones, so one feature uses two naming schemes. F3: playclock.js does exist, but in the KB and not in the code repo. F4: single Download from the viewer works for every format, and the per-row Delete is also gone. F2 gets more precise scrim locations. Verified bugs: F5 (stale badges for non-cDNG items), F6 (a clip opened during a hold stays blank), F7 (freeze when the WAV is short; probable), F8 (a failed remove closes the viewer).

findings.title: Upstream media state and function names replaced by nested state.pb and pb*/pbv* families
findings.port_way: All Playback state in a nested state.pb object; 70 pb/pbv-prefixed functions, many renames of upstream jobs (renderMediaLibrary->pbRender, sortedMediaItems->pbSorted, selectedMediaItems->pbSelectedItems, toggleMediaSelection->pbToggle, setMediaBrowserFilter->pbSetFilter, downloadSelectedMediaItems->pbDownloadSelected, deleteSelectedMediaItems->pbRemoveSelected). Some upstream names stay (fetchMediaLibrary, setMediaBrowserOpen, mediaSelectionKey, mediaSelectionQuery, state.mediaBrowserOpen P:6714), so the feature mixes two schemes.
findings.apertar_way: Flat state literal with media prefix, src/web/WebControlPage.cpp:4233-4246@upstream-1.6.0; no nested objects in state. Verb-first or full-noun function names; media functions at src/web/WebControlPage.cpp:7511-7700, 10361-10460@upstream-1.6.0.
findings.why_it_matters: The diff reads as a rewrite of the whole media feature, though much of it is the same job renamed. The original developer must relearn his own feature, and pb/pbv is an abbreviation no other part of the page uses.
findings.rework: Restore upstream names (renderMediaLibrary, sortedMediaItems, selectedMediaItems, toggleMediaSelection, setMediaBrowserFilter, setMediaBrowserSort, downloadSelectedMediaItems, deleteSelectedMediaItems, pruneMediaSelection, selectAllVisibleMedia). Flatten the browser state to state.mediaLibraryPayload/mediaLibrary/mediaSelection/mediaBrowserFilter/mediaBrowserSort/mediaFetchInFlight, plus new flat media* fields (mediaFetchQueued, mediaSelecting, mediaThumbCache, mediaThumbQueue, mediaThumbsInFlight, mediaThumbObserver, mediaHold, mediaSnapshotHold, mediaError, mediaRemoving, mediaHistoryPushed, mediaLastOpenedKey, mediaBrowserPage). Keep the viewer object as state.clipViewer (createClipViewerState). Give new functions verb-first names: buildMediaCard, queueMediaThumbnail, openClipViewer, closeClipViewer, playClip, pauseClip, stepClipFrame, seekClip, fetchClipFrame, drawClipFrame, applyClipHold, installClipViewerInteractions, clipTimeline, clipNumberAtTime, clipFrameInHole. Mechanical, no behaviour change.
findings.deliberate_evidence: bc12c0a/4629de2 describe features only; nothing on naming or the state layout.

findings.title: Custom remove scrim dialog where the WebUI convention is window.confirm
findings.port_way: pbOpenRemoveDialog fills a custom #pbRemoveScrim (title, count, name, more, confirm/cancel, focus, Escape branch, keydown guard). The viewer's Download in the same feature uses window.confirm (P:12914).
findings.apertar_way: Every destructive action uses window.confirm: src/web/WebControlPage.cpp:10434@upstream-1.6.0, also 10307, 10385, 10672, 11266, 11278, 11325, 11337. Upstream WebUI has no scrim or modal; the scrim is the touch UI's dialog (Apertar-UI qml/ClipBrowserPage.qml@upstream-1.6.0).
findings.why_it_matters: Two dialog styles in one page, and extra HTML, CSS, focus and Escape handling for one confirm.
findings.rework: Use window.confirm("Remove " + label + "? This cannot be undone.") in deleteSelectedMediaItems. Delete the #pbRemoveScrim markup/CSS, pbOpenRemoveDialog, state.pb.removeTargets, the scrim branch in pbEscape, the scrim lines at P:10137 and P:20634, and the keydown guard. Viewer Remove calls the same function with [item].
findings.deliberate_evidence: bc12c0a: 'Remove Selected (dialog)' in 'the touch UI's shape'.

findings.title: Tracker ids and history narration in Playback comments
findings.port_way: Comments carry T49, T50, T51, O1, O4, R2, P2, Q2, CLM:559-568, 'design §2.6' and 'the sketch's playclock.js (node-tested, 16 checks)'. playclock.js and playclock_test.js exist only in the KB (apertar-kb/working/tools/playback/page/), not in Apertar-Core.
findings.apertar_way: Upstream WebUI JS comments carry no tracker ids (0 hits in src/web/WebControlPage.cpp@upstream-1.6.0 apart from 'P3-D60').
findings.why_it_matters: The ids mean nothing to the original developer, and the test claim points outside the repository.
findings.rework: Delete the ids and history phrases and keep the rule sentences. Either port the clock checks as a host test under tools/ (from the KB's playclock_test.js) or drop the reference.

findings.title: Clip cards lost size, fps, frame count and per-row Download/Delete; non-cDNG items show them nowhere
findings.port_way: The card shows duration, DROP, name, format label, shot date and TC. Size, fps and frames appear only in the viewer Info panel, which is filled only for cDNG. Single Download is only in the viewer (works for every format, behind window.confirm); single delete is only the viewer's Remove.
findings.apertar_way: The upstream media row showed frame count, Duration, fps_text, size_text and 'Updated ...', plus per-row Download and Delete, src/web/WebControlPage.cpp:7735-7790@upstream-1.6.0 (mediaFrameCountLabel :7571, mediaFpsLabel :7584). Core still sends size_text and fps_text (ApertarCoreApp.cpp:9276-9280@cinemate-port).
findings.why_it_matters: For ProRes, H.264, MLV, stills and audio the WebUI no longer shows size, fps or frame count anywhere.
findings.rework: Add size_text and fps_text (mediaFpsLabel) to the card foot, or fill the Info rows from the /api/media item for non-cDNG items. Note in the handoff that per-item actions moved into the viewer.
findings.deliberate_evidence: The card copies the touch UI; bc12c0a does not mention dropping the WebUI-only columns.

findings.title: Viewer keeps previous clip's FPS/DROP badges, time and Info rows when a non-cDNG item opens
findings.port_way: For format !== 'cdng', pbvOpen sets only pbvInfo, pbvFrame and the note, then returns. pbvFps, #pbvDrop, pbvTime, pbvTc and #pbvMetaGrid keep the previous clip's content.
findings.apertar_way: no precedent
findings.why_it_matters: Open a cDNG clip with drops, then Next onto a ProRes clip: DROP N, the cDNG fps badge and the cDNG metadata appear under the ProRes name.
findings.rework: Before the format branch, clear pbvFps/pbvTime/pbvTc, hide #pbvDrop and clear #pbvMetaGrid (or fill it from the list item, F4).

findings.title: Clip opened during a hold stays blank after the hold ends
findings.port_way: On a 409, pbvOpen applies the hold and returns with v.tl null. pbvApplyHold('') redraws only if v.tl is set, pbvPlay returns on !v.tl, and pbSnapshotChanged does not reload the viewer.
findings.apertar_way: no precedent
findings.why_it_matters: A take starts from the touch UI, the operator taps a card in the WebUI, the take ends: the hold card goes, the stage stays black and Play does nothing until Back and reopen.
findings.rework: In pbvApplyHold(''): if (wasHeld && !v.tl) void pbvReload();

findings.title: Playback freezes at the end when the WAV is shorter than the frame span (probable)
findings.port_way: With sound on, t comes from audio only while !audio.ended; otherwise t = v.t. The loop fires only at t >= (last-first+1)/fps. There is no 'ended' listener. The WAV is served raw (ApertarCoreApp.cpp:7387, 8551@cinemate-port).
findings.apertar_way: no precedent
findings.why_it_matters: When the WAV ends before the frame span, the picture stands while the badge says PLAYING. The 5 s fallback does not fire because audioLive is already true. Probable; settle with such a take.
findings.rework: In pbvTick's waiting branch, when audio.ended, switch to the wall clock from v.t (audioOn=false, clockBase=v.t, clockStart=now) and turn audio back on after the loop.

findings.title: Failed remove from the viewer closes the viewer
findings.port_way: The catch only shows a toast. The same item is still at the index and in the removed list, so pbvClose() runs.
findings.apertar_way: no precedent
findings.why_it_matters: If Core refuses the remove (busy), the error toast shows and the viewer closes although the clip still exists.
findings.rework: Track success; on failure leave the viewer open.

findings.title: pbvTimecodeAt and pbvClock re-implement formatTimecode and pad2
findings.port_way: Local pad lambdas and their own h:m:s:f arithmetic.
findings.apertar_way: pad2 src/web/WebControlPage.cpp:4635@upstream-1.6.0 and formatTimecode :4678@upstream-1.6.0, both still in the port (P:7117, P:7160).
findings.why_it_matters: Two timecode formatters in one page drift apart.
findings.rework: pbvTimecodeAt: parse the start to frames, add number - tl.first, return formatTimecode(frames % (nominal*86400), nominal) to keep the 24 h wrap. pbvClock: use pad2.

findings.title: Snapshot merge uses typeof === 'number' instead of isFiniteNumber; env-knob field reaches the page
findings.port_way: typeof === 'number' checks for cdng_log_bits, buffer_stop_percent and storage_preroll_fps. storage_preroll_auto_env is copied to the snapshot (read at P:15839).
findings.apertar_way: isFiniteNumber(source.x) + Number() in the upstream merge, src/web/WebControlPage.cpp:8640-8676@upstream-1.6.0; no typeof-number checks.
findings.why_it_matters: A small inconsistency inside one function, and the field exposes an experiment knob.
findings.rework: Use isFiniteNumber + Number() for the three fields. Decide storage_preroll_auto_env in the knob sweep.

findings.title: Dead indirection and unused parameters
findings.port_way: pbOpenClip only calls pbvOpen (one caller, P:11915). pbvEls().hist is never used. tl is unused in pbvLookAhead and pbvFillMeta.
findings.apertar_way: no precedent
findings.why_it_matters: Noise for a reader.
findings.rework: Remove pbOpenClip, drop hist from pbvEls and remove the unused tl parameters.

findings.title: state.previewPausedForPlayback not declared in the state literal
findings.port_way: The field is created on first assignment in pbPauseLive.
findings.apertar_way: Every state field is declared in the literal, e.g. previewStreamStarted: false, src/web/WebControlPage.cpp:4227@upstream-1.6.0.
findings.why_it_matters: A reader cannot see the field in the state list.
findings.rework: Add previewPausedForPlayback: false next to previewStreamStarted (P:6708).

findings.title: Player pacing (0.35 s look-ahead, two lanes at 640 w) measured on Pi 5 only
findings.port_way: Constants tuned against Pi 5 decode times (4fa0432: 180 ms lossless).
findings.apertar_way: no precedent
findings.why_it_matters: On Pi 4/CM4 Core decodes slower; the page should degrade to 'PLAYING · N FPS' rather than fail. Unconfirmed; settle on a Pi 4.
findings.rework: No change now; record the measured behaviour on Pi 4 in the Pi-model stage.
findings.deliberate_evidence: The 4fa0432 message gives the Pi 5 measurements.

WCP-04.summary: All 15 findings survive and none were dropped. 9 stand and 6 are corrected. F1: deliberate changed to yes (commit 66b324d). F3: only the first fetch exists because of F1. F4: the same hook is also in createFavoritePillGrid, and the rework is now a generic onDisabledClick so locked pills keep their grey look. F5: QML is not involved, so the rules live in JS and Core only. Core has no quality sort or default maxes, and JS already disagrees with Core on "never used" (JS refuses, Core warns), so the rework moves sort and defaults into ModeLadder.hpp. F9: inline SVG is used across the port page (13 places), so it needs one decision for the whole page. F12: the driver dependency is confirmed (baseline driver has 2076, port driver has 2072), and the alias stays because Core migrates the same way.

findings.title: IMX585 resolution pills read the Mode Ladder reply (state.ladderServer.pool)
findings.port_way: imx585ClassRows takes sizes from state.ladderServer.pool (filled only by get_mode_ladder via applyModeLadder), else JS class tables; main Recording resolution pills, crop row and imx585BaseCommands depend on it.
findings.apertar_way: Hand-written per-sensor JS arrays as the one source: src/web/WebControlPage.cpp:5112-5121, 5249-5290@upstream-1.6.0. Merge target has list_sensor_modes (src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:9231@main; port App:12724) with width, height, bit_depth, clear_hdr, binning.
findings.why_it_matters: Two features coupled through a private JS cache; changing the ladder reply breaks the resolution pills; four sources of the same facts (Core tables, JS tables, pool, fps_max).
findings.rework: Delete the pool read in imx585ClassRows and imx585LadderFamily. Keep JS tables only (upstream pattern), or fetch list_sensor_modes once via sendCommand into state.sensorModes and read that (mono sensor keeps working). get_mode_ladder carries only the ladder.
findings.deliberate_evidence: commit 66b324d: 'The Mode Ladder's pool decides what exists; the class tables are the fallback until it arrives'

findings.title: Mode Ladder editor re-implements and extends Core's ladder rules in JS
findings.port_way: About 45 JS functions: ladderArranged (quality sort, default maxes 25/33/50/+25), normalizeLadderDraft, ladderDraftProblem, ladderOrderProblem, ladderRowStates, ladderSpans, ladderWithMode; auto-save 200 ms after each edit. set_mode_ladder dry_run (App:14095-14107) is never called from JS. Core validate (src/camera/ModeLadder.hpp:206-256) has no sort and no default maxes; JS refuses 'never used' while Core only warns (ModeLadder.hpp:243 vs WCP:7859-7860).
findings.apertar_way: No precedent of this size. Nearest is the favourites editor src/web/WebControlPage.cpp:7315-7400@upstream-1.6.0 (list from state, add/remove, one command with a joined string, no client rule engine). C1-N01: Core is the single source of truth. The port WebUI itself uses dry_run elsewhere (set_controls WCP:18795, boot config WCP:20246).
findings.why_it_matters: Ladder rules live in JS and Core and already differ; a maintainer must change both. QML is not affected (only reads ladderActive).
findings.rework: Keep card, rows, crop picture, pool tiles. Move quality order and default maxes into ModeLadder.hpp (Core fills an empty threshold by place). On each edit send set_mode_ladder resolutions=... dry_run=true and show Core's errors[]/warnings[] per row; save without dry_run. Delete ladderArranged, ladderDefaultMax, normalizeLadderDraft, ladderDraftProblem, ladderOrderProblem, ladderSpans, ladderWithMode (~250 lines); ladderRowStates reads Core's from/ceiling per resolution.
findings.deliberate_evidence: fork-log l.97 'approved design'; commits 1ef94fe, e472b1b, b8ee23f, 392e812; first editor 920beb0 showed Core's dry-run messages, later dropped
findings.rework_risk: Needs a Core change in ModeLadder.hpp for default maxes and sort; touch UI unaffected.

findings.title: ladderRequest duplicates sendCommand's fetch path
findings.port_way: Own fetch('/api/command') and error throw; comment says get_mode_ladder and dry runs skip sendCommand's snapshot patching.
findings.apertar_way: Read-only queries go through sendCommand: refreshAudioCaptureCapabilities 'const reply = await sendCommand({cmd: "audio_capabilities", device});' src/web/WebControlPage.cpp:11100-11113@upstream-1.6.0; applyCommandSnapshotPatch (8678) ignores unknown commands.
findings.why_it_matters: Second call path for the same route; no dry run is sent from JS, so the stated reason is void.
findings.rework: fetchModeLadder calls sendCommand({cmd:'get_mode_ladder'}); delete ladderRequest.
findings.deliberate_evidence: comment at P:8004

findings.title: Ladder fetched from inside renderModeLadder on every poll
findings.port_way: renderModeLadder (called per snapshot, P:16028) starts fetchModeLadder: first fetch, 5 s retry, refetch on ladder_active change. Port also fetches on panel open.
findings.apertar_way: Side data fetched when a panel opens: setSettingsPanel 'if (normalized === "presets") fetchPresetLibrary(true);' src/web/WebControlPage.cpp:6162-6167@upstream-1.6.0, in-flight flag (10305).
findings.why_it_matters: Network side effect in a render function. First fetch and retry exist because of F1; the ladder_active refetch has its own reason (ceilings change).
findings.rework: After F1 keep only the panel-open fetch; move the ladder_active-change refetch to the state poll handler, only while the Modes panel is open.

findings.title: Generic pill builders know the Mode Ladder (option.locked -> showLadderLockWarning)
findings.port_way: buildOptionButtonsInto and createFavoritePillGrid: 'button.disabled = !option.enabled && !option.locked; ... if (option.locked) { showLadderLockWarning(false); return; }'; normalizeChoiceOptions carries locked.
findings.apertar_way: buildOptionButtons is generic, {value,label,enabled}: src/web/WebControlPage.cpp:9146-9166@upstream-1.6.0.
findings.why_it_matters: Two shared widgets depend on one feature.
findings.rework: Replace locked with a generic optional onDisabledClick argument on buildOptionButtonsInto / createFavoritePillGrid (a disabled pill stays clickable only when given one); ladderLockedOptions sets enabled:false; ladder call sites (P:11161, 15978, 15990) pass () => showLadderLockWarning(false). Keep system (CSS class) and the element-taking variant.
findings.deliberate_evidence: commit 392e812 adds the warning, says nothing about the placement

findings.title: Crop diagram and ladder names assume IMX585 3840x2160 readout for all sensors
findings.port_way: ladderCropArea fixed 3840x2160; windows clipped to it; non-IMX585 names call any 3840-wide mode '4K SDR' and any 1920-wide '2K SDR binned'.
findings.apertar_way: no precedent
findings.why_it_matters: IMX283 3840x2160 10-bit crop (window_w 3840 of 5472) shows 'Whole sensor area, no crop'; 5.5K window clipped to 3840; same for IMX477 4056. Probable, needs a pool on those sensors.
findings.rework: Readout area from the largest pool window, or show the crop picture only on IMX585; name other sensors' modes by size.

findings.title: Stale, contradictory and orphan comments; section banners
findings.port_way: Comment says the editor 'asks Core about the draft (dry_run) and saves it with Save ladder' (no dry_run, no Save button, auto-save at P:8083); 'no Auto under a ceiling' while code blocks Auto only in Clear HDR (P:8665); orphan ISO comments; '// ---- Mode Ladder (T34) ---' banner.
findings.apertar_way: C1-I14: comments rare, state a hazard or reason; no banners, no ticket numbers (App:10827-10828@upstream-1.6.0).
findings.why_it_matters: Misleads the next reader about how saving and ISO Auto work.

F3 is corrected. The comment rule is C3-I7, not C3-I9. The block has 11 comment lines, not 9, plus 2 more inside renderSnapshot. The header comment at 16416-16418 is out of date: it says the buffer is polled only while the option is on, but c5db8b2 made it poll with the option off too.

findings.port_way: const frameBufferBar = {...} with 14 fields; window.setInterval(pollFrameBufferBar, 250). The poll writes state.snapshot.storage_preroll_* directly, and applyPrerollPill / applyFrameBufferPillClasses toggle .preroll/.recording/.writing/.buffer-drain and the #recordingStatus text. 1000 ms freshness guards decide whether the poll or the 1 Hz render wins. frameBufferBar is read from 5 other places (WCP:14381, 15389, 15757-15759, 15917, 19201).
findings.apertar_way: One store: const state = { WCP:4204@upstream-1.6.0, with timers as state.<x>Timer (C3-I2). One poll: window.setInterval(() => fetchState(true), 1000) WCP:11609@upstream-1.6.0 (C3-I3, C3-N8). Pill classes are set only in renderSnapshot, WCP:9794-9802@upstream-1.6.0. Fresher values go sendCommand -> applyCommandSnapshotPatch -> renderSnapshot (WCP:9109-9145@upstream-1.6.0).
findings.why_it_matters: The pill has two writers that race, and timing guards settle which one wins. The original developer has to read about 170 lines to learn why the pill shows READY while recording is true, and every later pill change must be made in both paths.
findings.rework: Move the fields into state (bufferPollTimer, bufferPollInFlight, bufferPolledAtMs, prerollPollUntilMs, bufferDiscardSeen) and delete frameBufferBar. Rename pollFrameBufferBar to fetchBufferState and keep the lock-free route. On each reply, call applyBufferSnapshotPatch(payload), which merges the flat buffer/preroll keys into state.snapshot. The reply's recording value goes in as buffer_recording and never over snapshot.recording, because /api/buffer reports false during a safety stop (App:8424@cinemate-port). Extract the pill block of renderSnapshot (WCP:15752-15771) into renderRecordingStatus(snapshot) and call it from renderSnapshot and fetchBufferState. Delete applyPrerollPill, applyFrameBufferPillClasses and the READY/PRE-ROLL label rewrites. Fire the toasts from a previous-vs-new comparison of buffer_safety_stop and buffer_flush_discarded, like the recording_error toast (WCP:9331-9333@upstream-1.6.0). Start and stop the timer in one function that decides from the snapshot. Point the 5 outside readers at state.snapshot fields.
findings.rework_risk: C3-N7 says renderSnapshot should not be split unasked. Extracting only the pill block is a small, justified split. Safety stop, flush-discard and the pre-roll pill must be tested again on the Pi.

WCP-10.summary:
I checked all 13 findings against both code trees. None were dropped and none were added. Six findings stand as written (F2, F5, F6, F8, F9, F11, F13 with line refs fixed). Six were corrected:
- F1: deliberate is now "unknown", because commit 2955ef8 says it copied /api/config. The fan-mode command (set_fan_mode) is a closer upstream precedent. The rework now keeps the revision guard.
- F3: upstream does touch config.txt, but only through the fan-mode select. That backs the "simplify" verdict.
- F4: the guard is weaker than reported. On /api/command, set_boot_config passes browser=false, so any client writes without a revision. Upstream does write root-owned system state, but only through fixed actions, never text sent in by the caller.
- F7: there is one store and two transports, not two validation paths. The "h" fallback always gets a stale reply.
- F10: lowered to nit. It only depends on rev-WCP-08.
- F12: upstream line ref fixed.
The "## Skeptic" and "## Final findings" sections are appended to the report.

findings.title: Boot Config posts to its own route instead of /api/command
findings.port_way: bootConfigPost does fetch("/api/boot-config", POST, JSON.stringify(body)) with JSON booleans and numbers. Core inserts "cmd":"set_boot_config" into the body string and calls parseControlCommand. set_boot_config already exists in handleCommand (App:14589) and takes revision as a field. result.httpStatus is set (WCP:20011) and never read. The card branches on result.code (WCP:20329).
findings.apertar_way: Every camera action goes through POST /api/command -> handleCommand (src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:7637-7642@upstream-1.6.0). The upstream config.txt writer is a command too: sendCommand({cmd:"set_fan_mode", value}) (src/web/WebControlPage.cpp:11093@upstream-1.6.0, src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:10568@upstream-1.6.0). Booleans travel as "true"/"false" (src/web/WebControlPage.cpp:10111@upstream-1.6.0, C3-S7, C3-I5).
findings.why_it_matters: The original developer sees a second command entry point that builds JSON by inserting into a string, for a command the normal path already accepts.
findings.rework: Make bootConfigPost a sendCommand/controlsCall-style POST to /api/command: {cmd:"set_boot_config", camN_sensor, camN_link_frequency, i2c:"true"/"false", ..., dry_run:"true", confirm_display, revision}. Delete the POST /api/boot-config branch (App:9170-9196). In Core, make set_boot_config require revision for every write that is not a dry run. Today App:14589 passes browser=false and skips the check. Keep GET /api/boot-config and /api/boot-config/parse.
findings.deliberate_evidence: 2955ef8 models the POST on /api/config ('409 when stale, as /api/config'). It gives no reason for not using /api/command.

findings.port_way: const bootConfig = { payload, form, loading, saving, waiting, savedPendingReboot, review, text, previewState, editorMarks, editorTimer }, wired by a separate installBootConfigInteractions(). It has the same shape as controlsState, frameBufferBar and settingsSearch.
findings.apertar_way: One global state object with flat fields, <thing>InFlight busy flags and state.<thing>Timer timers (src/web/WebControlPage.cpp:4204-4266@upstream-1.6.0). All listeners sit inline in installInteractions (11348-11610@upstream-1.6.0). C3-I2.
findings.why_it_matters: A fourth parallel store makes the page read as several small apps instead of one page driven by state.
findings.rework: Move the fields to state.bootConfigPayload, bootConfigForm, bootConfigFetchInFlight, bootConfigSaveInFlight, bootConfigRebootWaiting, bootConfigReview (bootConfigText/EditorTimer go away with F3). Move the listeners of installBootConfigInteractions into installInteractions, next to restartSystemButton.

findings.title: Boot Config card over-built: Edit file, live managed-line marks, legend, own-lines hint
findings.port_way: About 800 lines: controls, dry-run review, Save Only and Save and Reboot, View, Download, Upload, and Edit file with its own gutter. Edit file shows italic managed-line marks, re-read through POST /api/boot-config/parse 500 ms after each keystroke. Also a legend of runs, an own-lines hint, Use This Text and a reboot wait.
findings.apertar_way: Upstream touches config.txt only through one control: the fan-mode select rewrites one managed block (set_fan_mode, src/web/WebControlPage.cpp:11093@upstream-1.6.0; writer App:3042-3178@upstream-1.6.0). A typical upstream feature is 20-40 lines in 3-5 places (C3 section 0). The one upstream text editor is a plain textarea with Reload/Save (src/web/WebControlPage.cpp:10304-10359@upstream-1.6.0).
findings.why_it_matters: The card's size and its live re-parse are far beyond the scale of the rest of the code. The text path is the only client of the whole-file root write (F4).
findings.rework: Simplify. Keep the controls, the dry-run review, Save, View file and Download. Delete BOOT_CONFIG_MANAGED, bootConfigManagedMap/Summary, bootConfigOwnLinesHint, bootConfigEditorEdited and showBootConfigEditorMarks (2a4266e), plus Core state.managed. Delete Edit file / Use This Text (3b87d99) and Core's text= field.
findings.deliberate_evidence: 3b87d99: 'the card only reached the lines it has controls for; anything else in config.txt still needed ssh or a card reader'. 2a4266e gives a reason for the marks. Neither weighs the size against Apertar's scale.

findings.title: Edit file sends whole config.txt to a root write; set_boot_config has no revision guard on /api/command
findings.port_way: body.text = bootConfig.text. Core writes /boot/firmware/config.txt as root via scripts/apertar-boot-config. A missing revision is refused only when browser is true. /api/boot-config sets browser from whether an Origin header is present (App:9193). /api/command always passes false (App:14589). So curl, a LAN script, or any POST to /api/command can write any text with no guard.
findings.apertar_way: Upstream changes root-owned system state from the WebUI only through fixed actions: the config.txt fan block from a select, date/time, format media. It never writes text sent in by the caller into a system file. README:130@upstream-1.6.0: the WebUI is not an authenticated internet-facing service.
findings.why_it_matters: Anyone on the LAN can make the Pi unbootable with one request. Already reported in sweep-protocol-security.md (new root paths, item a); this slice is the client.
findings.rework: Drop Edit file (F3). Then remove text= from set_boot_config, so only the card's fields can be written. Require a revision for every set_boot_config write that is not a dry run, on every path (F1). Keep config.txt.apertar.bak, because the controls alone can still write an overlay that does not boot.
findings.deliberate_evidence: The text write is deliberate (3b87d99). The missing guard on /api/command is not discussed anywhere.

findings.title: Display-change checkbox gate instead of window.confirm
findings.port_way: gate = document.createElement("input"); gate.type = "checkbox"; ' Change the display anyway'. Both Save buttons stay disabled until it is ticked (syncGate).
findings.apertar_way: There is no checkbox anywhere in upstream (C3-I6). System-level actions ask with window.confirm: if (!window.confirm("Restart the Apertar system now?")) (src/web/WebControlPage.cpp:11325@upstream-1.6.0, C3-N4).
findings.why_it_matters: A new widget and a new way of confirming, for one case.
findings.rework: Delete the checkbox and syncGate. In saveBootConfig, when review.display_changed is set, call window.confirm("Change the display and reboot? <DPI consequence sentence>"). Keep the diff-note lines.
findings.deliberate_evidence: 8a56545: 'a display change needs a tick that names what it costs'

findings.title: Reboot wait polls /api/buffer; the 60 s never-down rule misreports a slow shutdown
findings.port_way: Every 2.5 s for up to 240 s it fetches /api/buffer, a route the port added. If no failed fetch is seen within 60 s, it says 'The camera kept answering, so it did not reboot.' and stops waiting.
findings.apertar_way: requestRestartSystem sends restart_system and toasts 'Restart requested.' (src/web/WebControlPage.cpp:11324-11334@upstream-1.6.0). Reconnection is handled by the 1 s fetchState poll plus the loading overlay (C3-N5).
findings.why_it_matters: Core's shutdown stops camera_ before webServer_ (src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:8185-8190@cinemate-port), so the page keeps getting answers while a take drains. Probable failing input: Save and Reboot during a take with a full RAM buffer. A drain over 60 s gives a false 'did not reboot' message, and then the reboot happens anyway. To settle it on a Pi: record 4K, fill the buffer, then Save and Reboot.
findings.rework: Poll /api/state (the upstream route) or reuse fetchState. Drop the never-down branch, because the restart_system reply already confirms the request.

findings.title: Config Check and Save use two transports; Check falls back to base "h" and then always fails
findings.port_way: Check: controlsCall({cmd:"set_controls", base: state.configRevision || "h", text, dry_run:"true"}) on /api/command. Save: POST /api/config with an X-Apertar-Revision header. Both end in HardwareConfigStore::replace (App:12763, App:8644). "h" is not a revision; the absent-file revision is h0000000000000000 (HardwareConfigText.hpp:315). The store compares base even on a dry run and answers stale (HardwareConfigStore.cpp:282-295), so Check fails if it runs before the file has loaded.
findings.apertar_way: One path per file: GET/POST /api/config (src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:7168/7175@upstream-1.6.0). Route options come from the query string via queryParameterValue (C3-S7).
findings.why_it_matters: One file has two transports into the same store call, plus a magic value that can never succeed.
findings.rework: Check posts to /api/config?dry_run=1 with the same header and body as Save; Core reads the flag with queryParameterValue and sets flags.dryRun. Disable Check until state.configRevision is set. Delete the "h" fallback.

findings.title: Two diff renderers; bootConfigOption re-implements ensureSelectEntries
findings.port_way: showConfigDiff, reviewBootConfig/bootConfigDiffLine and toggleBootConfigFile each build their own diff box and a row of buttons created in JS. Selects are rebuilt with innerHTML="" plus bootConfigOption, only to get a disabled flag.
findings.apertar_way: Selects are filled through ensureSelectOptions / normalizeSelectEntries / ensureSelectEntries (src/web/WebControlPage.cpp:6191, 6210, 6221@upstream-1.6.0). Disabled choices are passed as enabled:false (normalizeChoiceOptions 6317@upstream-1.6.0).
findings.why_it_matters: The same behaviour lives in two or three places.
findings.rework: Add one renderDiffBox(boxId, lines, actions). Extend normalizeSelectEntries with enabled. Call ensureSelectEntries from renderBootConfigPort and the display select, and delete bootConfigOption.

findings.title: Remote controls loader runs its own untracked 5 s setTimeout loop
findings.port_way: const loadRemoteControls = () => { if (controlsState.model) return; void loadControls(true); setTimeout(loadRemoteControls, 5000); }. The timer is never stored or cleared.
findings.apertar_way: One poll loop, window.setInterval(() => fetchState(true), 1000) (src/web/WebControlPage.cpp:11609@upstream-1.6.0). A retry uses a stored timer: state.previewRetryTimer = window.setTimeout(loadPreviewStream, 1500) (8578@upstream-1.6.0). C3-I2.
findings.why_it_matters: A second poll loop that nothing tracks.
findings.rework: In fetchState, after a good snapshot: if (!controlsState.model && !controlsState.loading) void loadControls(true). Delete the loop. The smaller fix is to store the timer as state.controlsRetryTimer.
findings.deliberate_evidence: 1319967 and the code comment: the main page needs the controls before Settings opens.

findings.title: toggleRecord decides 'flushing' from page-side frameBufferBar
findings.port_way: const flushing = frameBufferBar.safetyStop === true && !state.snapshot.timelapse_active. This skips the media_writes_pending guard and the record_stop branch, so a press during the flush starts a new take.
findings.apertar_way: The guard reads state.snapshot fields only (src/web/WebControlPage.cpp:10690-10695@upstream-1.6.0, C3-N2).
findings.why_it_matters: The behaviour is an owner decision and stays. Only the input is foreign: it comes from the store that rev-WCP-08 reworks.
findings.rework: Keep the behaviour. Read state.snapshot.buffer_safety_stop once rev-WCP-08 merges frameBufferBar into the snapshot. This is a dependency note, not separate work.
findings.deliberate_evidence: c5db8b2; owner decision 2026-11-01 (fork-log)

F10 is dropped because upstream reaches into builder output the same way (card.lastChild.children[1].disabled = true at @upstream-1.6.0 :7116); the F1 rework removes the line anyway. F1 is corrected: the ladder lock also sits in a second generic builder (buildOptionButtonsInto :15038-15045), and the rework now keeps the wanted greyed-but-clickable behaviour through a generic flag plus caller onSelect guards. F5 goes from minor to nit: the 'only history state' claim was wrong (the viewer pushes too, :12777/:12869) and the finding asks for no change here. F7 and F9 are widened to port-wide sweeps: 32 lines use '·' and 23 comment lines carry ticket tokens. F8 adds a second hasMedia copy (:15255). Many line numbers were corrected. F2 and F3 stand, with their UI commits (08cefcf, 7029db1) added.

findings.title: Mode Ladder lock wired into the generic pill builders; two lock mechanisms
findings.port_way: Options gain `locked`. Both generic pill builders (createPillGrid, buildOptionButtonsInto) keep locked pills enabled and call the feature toast showLadderLockWarning(false) themselves. Select fields use a second mechanism: dataset.ladderLock plus a document-level click delegate. The favourites Bit Depth block is greyed through bitDepthBlock.lastChild.
findings.apertar_way: The generic builders are generic: `button.disabled = !option.enabled;` and nothing else (src/web/WebControlPage.cpp:6608 createPillGrid, :9158 buildOptionButtons @upstream-1.6.0). The caller gives the refusal reason in its onSelect, e.g. Sound Recorder `if (!audioOptions.hasInputDevices) { showToast("No audio input device detected.", true); return; }` (src/web/WebControlPage.cpp:6992-6995@upstream-1.6.0).
findings.why_it_matters: A feature toast hard-wired into two shared builders, next to a parallel mechanism for selects, is coupling the original developer has to undo when the next 'greyed, but say why' case arrives.
findings.rework: Rename `locked` to a generic flag (e.g. `blocked`: looks disabled, stays clickable). Handle it the same way in createPillGrid and buildOptionButtonsInto: add the 'disabled' class, keep the button enabled and call onSelect. Each ladder-locked caller (Resolution and Crop pills :15978/:15990, favourites Bit Depth :11161) starts its onSelect with `if (state.snapshot && state.snapshot.ladder_active === true) { showLadderLockWarning(false); return; }`, as upstream does for Sound Recorder. Selects keep one mechanism (the data-ladder-lock delegate). Pass the ladder-locked class through createFavoriteSelectBlock instead of reaching into bitDepthBlock.lastChild.
findings.deliberate_evidence: Commit 392e812 'a locked control answers with the red warning; the selected one goes grey too': the behaviour is wanted, but putting it in the builders is not argued.
findings.rework_risk: Low. The greyed-but-clickable behaviour is kept; the guard must read the live snapshot, not a captured one.

findings.title: Upstream timecode labels Free Run / Rec Run shown as Time of Day / Clip
findings.port_way: The stored values stay 'Free Run' / 'Rec Run'. Every label shown in the WebUI and in the touch UI Settings is 'Time of Day' / 'Clip' (timecodeDisplayName, timecodeChoices).
findings.apertar_way: timecodeModeLabel returns 'Rec Run' / 'Free Run' and is shown as is (src/web/WebControlPage.cpp:5852, favourite :7042@upstream-1.6.0). The touch UI uses the same words (ui-upstream qml/CameraPage.qml:1693-1710@upstream-1.6.0).
findings.why_it_matters: Upstream names that operators see change in both UIs, and the original developer may not share the naming argument.
findings.rework: Keep the upstream labels in the merge. Offer the rename upstream as a separate proposal. Core 2c259b9 and UI 08cefcf are isolated commits and can be held back.
findings.deliberate_evidence: Commits 2c259b9 (Core) and 08cefcf (UI): Rec Run normally continues across clips, while Apertar restarts the count for each clip.
findings.rework_risk: Low; only the labels change.

findings.title: One timecode setting split into UI and file timecode; the favourite became two blocks
findings.port_way: set_timecode_mode takes target=ui|files|both (no target = both). Favourites show separate 'UI Timecode' and 'File Timecode' blocks. The touch UI is split too (UI commit 7029db1).
findings.apertar_way: One set_timecode_mode sets the camera and UI.conf timecodeMode together (src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:9424-9437@upstream-1.6.0). There is one 'Timecode Mode' favourite (src/web/WebControlPage.cpp:7042@upstream-1.6.0).
findings.why_it_matters: The protocol change is additive and keeps the old default, but the quick-access favourite now shows a power-user split to every operator.
findings.rework: Keep `target` in Core and on the Timecode card. Make the favourite one 'Timecode Mode' block again, sending target=both, with its value text from timecodeSummaryLabel so a split state stays visible.
findings.deliberate_evidence: Commit 909aaa5 Why/What, and UI commit 7029db1.
findings.rework_risk: Low.

findings.title: Settings search with a MutationObserver and runtime DOM insertion
findings.port_way: applySettingsSearch inserts a .settings-search-label in each panel and #settingsSearchEmpty at runtime. While a query is active, a MutationObserver (childList, subtree, characterData) on .settings-panels re-runs the filter 250 ms after any change (:10272-10279).
findings.apertar_way: Upstream has no search, so the feature itself has no precedent. Upstream uses no Mutation, Intersection or Resize Observer anywhere (0 hits), refreshes the page from one renderSnapshot (src/web/WebControlPage.cpp:9327@upstream-1.6.0), and keeps static elements in the HTML string.
findings.why_it_matters: The observer is a refresh path the original developer will not expect next to renderSnapshot. Elements that exist only after a search are not in the HTML he reads.
findings.rework: Put the per-panel label and the empty-state div in the static HTML, hidden by class. Drop the observer. Call `if (settingsSearch.active) applySettingsSearch();` at the end of renderSnapshot (:15214) and after the async card loaders in setSettingsPanel. Keep the class-only show/hide. Move the feature into its own commit (it is now inside squash d44b177).
findings.deliberate_evidence: Commit d44b177: 'a search box like CineMate's (filters cards on every page)', bundled in a squash of 19 features.
findings.rework_risk: Cards rebuilt by async loaders outside renderSnapshot need an explicit re-filter call each.

findings.title: History API for phone Back in the media overlay (pointer to the Playback unit)
findings.port_way: history.pushState when the overlay opens (and again for the viewer), history.go(-steps) on close, and a popstate listener with state.pb.ignorePop.
findings.apertar_way: setMediaBrowserOpen toggles a class and #mediaBrowserOverlay and fetches the library (src/web/WebControlPage.cpp:6139-6147@upstream-1.6.0). The file has no history use.
findings.why_it_matters: The code is small and meets a real need, but it is a second navigation model the original developer has to know about.
findings.rework: No change in this slice. Document it in the Playback handoff and judge it in the Playback unit.
findings.deliberate_evidence: Commit bc12c0a: 'the phone's Back closes it'.

findings.title: imx585Selected predicate next to inline indexOf for the other sensors

findings.why_it_matters: Two styles for the same dispatch in one function.
findings.rework: Inline `sensorNameLower(snapshot).indexOf("imx585") !== -1`, drop imx585Selected and keep the early returns.
findings.deliberate_evidence: Commit 66b324d states the early return in each dispatcher; the predicate itself is not discussed.

findings.title: Port labels use the ' · ' separator; upstream uses ' • '
findings.port_way: ' · Log', 'UI x · Files y', '2.39:1 · 3840x1608', plus the ladder, Controls and playback meta lines: 32 lines across the port.
findings.apertar_way: Summaries join with ' • ' (30 uses, 0 uses of '·'), e.g. the favourites summary `recordFormatText + " • " + ...` (src/web/WebControlPage.cpp ~6440@upstream-1.6.0).

findings.title: 'Older Core' fallbacks in a page served by the same Core binary
findings.port_way: hasMedia is computed twice as `snapshot.media_alive !== undefined ? snapshot.media_alive : snapshot.media_mounted`, and a comment calls the value-list constants 'the fallback for an older Core'.
findings.apertar_way: `const hasMedia = !!(snapshot && snapshot.media_mounted);` (src/web/WebControlPage.cpp:6766,9358@upstream-1.6.0). The page and Core ship as one binary.
findings.why_it_matters: The fallback branch is dead: Core always emits both media fields (src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:9554,9556@cinemate-port) and always emits the ui.*_steps arrays (:1966-1969). The comment invents a compatibility need that does not exist.
findings.rework: Use `const hasMedia = !!(snapshot && snapshot.media_alive);` in both places. Reword the comment to 'the constants are the default lists'.

WCP-07.summary: Skeptic pass: all 12 findings survive, none dropped. 3 stand as written (F2, F8, F9). 9 are corrected: wrong line numbers in F10, F11 and F12. F3's rework now sits in Core: Core emits bufferSettingMembers twice, flat in settingsBody and nested under system in /api/state. Upstream never patches snapshot.system, so "patch systemState" would be new ground. F4 is softer and more precise: the page falls back to the raw note, the fraction and queue depth are configurable, and buffer_stop_percent is the per-take value. F5 is deliberate and was tested by the owner. F6 is deliberate (438a342). Its --simulate point is weaker than claimed because upstream also guards on media_mounted. The real defect is the media_alive/media_mounted split and the mediaGateError sentence that the operator never sees. F7 is recategorised as a mismatch, because upstream does have env knobs but never surfaces them. F1 adds the twin QML composer (ClipNameCard.qml, 601 lines), which has to be reworked together with the WebUI one.

Touch UI twin ClipNameCard.qml is 601 lines with its own drag.
findings.apertar_way: No drag and drop in upstream WCP (dragstart, draggable, setPointerCapture, vibrate = 0). Choices are buildOptionButtons pill grids (WebControlPage.cpp:9147-9167@upstream-1.6.0); free values settings-input + Apply.
findings.why_it_matters: The original developer would maintain a mini drag framework, twice (JS and QML), for a setting changed rarely; an order of magnitude beyond any upstream card.
findings.rework: Keep presets (buildOptionButtons clipNamePresets), a token palette inserting {token} at the caret, and the preview line. Replace the pill row with one settings-input holding the template + Apply (set_clip_name_template); preview on input via preview_clip_name. Delete clipPointerDrag, clipAttachPill, clipBindRow, clipDropIndex, clipOverRow, clipShowMarker, clipApplyDrop, the text-pill editor and ghost/marker CSS (~570 -> ~80 lines). Same shape in ClipNameCard.qml (TextField + token buttons). src/util/ClipName.hpp and the two commands unchanged.
findings.deliberate_evidence: 014a2bf body: 'a drag-and-drop pill composer'; UI 606f137 (fork-log: untested by hand).

findings.title: Buffer/pre-roll setting fields published twice by Core; page copies system.* to the top level
findings.port_way: bufferSettingMembers() is flat in settingsBody and events but nested under system in /api/state via bufferMembers. renderSnapshot loops Object.keys(snapshot.system) and copies buffer_*/storage_preroll_* to the top level; the same slice reads systemState.clip_merge_* / frames_per_folder directly.

WCP-01.summary: Skeptic pass on the CSS slice (P:22-1879). All 12 findings survive. None was dropped, 9 were corrected and 3 stand as written; no new finding. Corrections: the comment lines in F1 (the review cited P:88-89 and P:583; the actual lines are P:196 and P:587). F2's rework keeps the "Allow speed ramping" label and Off/On buttons that UI-DESIGN.md:71 asks for. In F4, Activate becomes primary-button, not secondary-button, because the port's button is white-filled. In F5, the .ladder-row-controls rules were taken off the dead list; deleting createLadderIconButton also leaves ladderIcons.up and .remove unread. F6 overstated "identical" (padding and remove-button sizes differ). F8 has 134 pb- lines, not 116. F9's 16:9 was a deliberate IMX585 choice (6707b08); IMX283 came later and the constant was not revisited, so it is still a probable bug. F10 is deliberate: designed in both UIs (README:102, 606f137). In F11 the crop and amber colours come from the approved design (UI-DESIGN.md:88-90), so the rework puts them in :root tokens instead of replacing them. The "--info/--ok as rgba" point was dropped because upstream tints --ok the same way (U:833). F11's line numbers were fixed. Side note for the HTML unit: the port's Timecode card dropped upstream's online-pill#settingsTimecodeValue (U:3016).

findings.why_it_matters: There are up to four chip vocabularies for one visual element.
findings.rework: Use one .chip base and one .chip-remove button. Make .chip.token/.text/.sep and .chip.flicker-free modifiers. Put the drag-only properties (cursor: grab, touch-action) on the composer's modifier.

findings.title: 741 lines split the .pill-button group; mid-file 560px media block; variants before base
findings.port_way: Mode Ladder, Value list and Clip name CSS sit between .pill-button.active (P:843) and .pill-button.disabled (P:1591). There is a second @media (max-width: 560px) block. .online-pill.off and .section-head .online-pill come before the base .online-pill (P:1632).
findings.apertar_way: .pill-button rules are kept together at src/web/WebControlPage.cpp:763-803@upstream-1.6.0. One block per breakpoint sits at the end of the stylesheet: 2034, 2062, 2190, 2319 (560px), 2391@upstream-1.6.0 (conv-webui I10).
findings.why_it_matters: A reader of the pill states finds 741 lines of unrelated card CSS in between. Responsive rules are no longer all in one place.
findings.rework: Keep the .pill-button.* modifiers next to .pill-button.active. Move the ladder, value-list and clip-name blocks after the settings-card and .preset-row rules. Move the .online-pill.* variants after the base rule. Merge the 560px rules into the end block. The later mid-file media blocks (P:2452-4364) are the same issue in other slices.

findings.title: body.media-browser-open renamed to the abbreviation body.pb-open, declared twice
findings.port_way: body.settings-open, body.pb-open { overflow: hidden }, and again body.pb-open { overflow: hidden } (both from bc12c0a). It is toggled from the same state.mediaBrowserOpen as upstream.
findings.apertar_way: body.settings-open, body.media-browser-open at src/web/WebControlPage.cpp:65-68@upstream-1.6.0, toggled at 6143@upstream-1.6.0. Class names are full words (conv-webui I7).

findings.title: Crop thumbnail hard-wired to a 16:9 3840x2160 sensor area
findings.port_way: .crop-frame has fixed sizes 78x44/160x90/64x36, and const ladderCropArea = { width: 3840, height: 2160 } clamps every window
findings.apertar_way: Geometry is passed from script through a custom property: --preview-aspect-ratio at src/web/WebControlPage.cpp:266, set at 5447@upstream-1.6.0
findings.why_it_matters: On IMX283 (5472x3648, 3:2; carried by the port since a47dc28) the full sensor is clamped into a 16:9 frame, and the 'Crop in' and percent texts are wrong. Probable: read from code, not run. To settle it, run get_mode_ladder on an IMX283.
findings.rework: Take the full readout area per sensor (the largest window_w/h in the get_mode_ladder pool, or a sensor field). Set --crop-aspect on the frame, use aspect-ratio instead of fixed heights, and delete ladderCropArea. Keep the IMX585 rule from UI-DESIGN.md:92 (3840x2200 is drawn as 3840x2160).
findings.rework_risk: Must keep 16-bit Clear HDR from looking letterboxed on IMX585
findings.deliberate_evidence: 6707b08 (fork-log) chose 16:9 thumbnails for IMX585. UI-DESIGN.md:89 asks for 'the full readout area'. IMX283 (a47dc28) came later and the constant was not revisited.

findings.title: Clip names drag-and-drop composer where upstream reorders with buttons

findings.title: One-line rules, duplicate selector, untokenised colour literals, third monospace stack

findings.title: Settings search (.searching, .search-hidden): keep

WCP-09.summary: Skeptic pass on WCP-09 (Controls/Hardware/Remote controls JS). 17 findings checked on both sides: 9 stand, 8 corrected, none dropped. Corrections: F2 has 15 call sites, and Listen must not use sendCommand because it schedules a /api/state refresh on each call; background polls keep a plain fetch (precedent U:11509). F3: the owner chose to keep Remote controls (fork-log:163-164), so the rework moves it into the Controls panel instead of deleting it. F7: Scan stays stuck until the page is reloaded, and Undo has no busy flag. F8: the rework no longer routes through sendCommand. F10 drops to nit, because upstream has persistent status lines. F11 becomes a bug, since Core still reads enabled and line independently. F12 adds the Check dry_run text path at P:18795. F13: Core's validator has the same 0-27 rule (HardwareConfigText.hpp:869), so the rework starts in Core. F16: the bool-as-select point is dropped because upstream uses selects for on/off (U:3791).

findings.title: Second client store controlsState plus module-level mutable state
findings.port_way: const controlsState = { loading, saving, revision, model, peripherals, catalog, edits, buttons, removed, added, settingEdits, buses, scans, dpiLines, apply, history, listening }; besides it controlsChipLines, controlsSeparateTurns, controlsReplaced, let controlsListenTimer/controlsListenSeq, and 13 const tables.
findings.apertar_way: One const state = { src/web/WebControlPage.cpp:4204-4266@upstream-1.6.0; timers state.<x>Timer, busy state.<x>InFlight; config editor state.configDirty/configFetchInFlight/configSaveInFlight (:10265-10359@upstream-1.6.0). C3-I2.
findings.why_it_matters: The original developer looks for page state in state and finds a second store (four with WCP-06 pb and WCP-08 frameBufferBar).
findings.rework: Flat fields on state: controlsModel, controlsRevision, controlsCatalog, controlsPeripherals, controlsEdits, controlsButtons, controlsRemoved, controlsAdded, hardwareEdits, controlsLoadInFlight, controlsSaveInFlight, controlsListenTimer, controlsChipLines, controlsSeparateTurns, controlsReplaced. Delete controlsState. Label tables move to the option-list block at the top of the script (C3-S6, U:4039-4127).
findings.deliberate_evidence: No commit discusses the store; the port itself keeps config-text state on state (P:18716, 18720).
findings.rework_risk: Mechanical rename across ~300 references.

findings.title: Second fetch wrapper controlsCall; hand-checked ok, missing try/catch
findings.port_way: async function controlsCall(payload) posts to /api/command and returns the JSON; 15 call sites test result.ok by hand; 7 have no try/catch.
findings.apertar_way: sendCommand src/web/WebControlPage.cpp:9109-9145@upstream-1.6.0 is the door for actions and throws new Error(result.error || "Command failed."); handlers try/catch with showToast(error.message, true) (C3-S3, C3-I4). A plain fire-and-forget fetch exists only for background traffic (user_activity, :11509-11513@upstream-1.6.0).
findings.why_it_matters: Two command paths with different error semantics; failures at unguarded sites become unhandled rejections (F7).
findings.rework: In sendCommand: const error = new Error(result.error || "Command failed."); error.result = result; throw error; (same as the port's /api/config save, P:18930-18931). User-action calls (save, undo, scan, test, history, get_controls, list_actions) use sendCommand in try/catch; save paths read error.result.issues/.code. The Listen poll stays a plain fetch (sendCommand would schedule a /api/state refresh per poll and move deferFetchUntilMs) in try/catch with an in-flight flag on state. Delete controlsCall.
findings.deliberate_evidence: Probable reason: set_controls failures carry issues/code that sendCommand drops; not stated in any commit.
findings.rework_risk: Routing a 300 ms poll through sendCommand would add ~3 /api/state fetches per second.

findings.title: Remote controls card on the main page with hold-to-repeat pills
findings.port_way: A 'Remote controls' card under Camera settings in the main grid; pills call test_input; knob arrows repeat while held (pointer capture, 450 ms delay, 140 ms interval); bootstrap retries get_controls every 5 s until Core answers.
findings.apertar_way: Main grid holds only preview, Camera settings, System, Current capture (src/web/WebControlPage.cpp:2456-2726@upstream-1.6.0; C3-S2). No hold-to-repeat anywhere upstream. Panel data loads in setSettingsPanel (:6164-6166@upstream-1.6.0).
findings.why_it_matters: Changes the camera-critical main page; duplicates the Try buttons on every Controls line; adds a load-time request loop.
findings.rework: Keep the feature (owner restored it 2026-11-04, fork-log.md:163-164) but move it off the main page: a settings-card in the Controls panel, pills built with buildOptionButtons, one command per click, data loaded from setSettingsPanel("controls"). Delete the main-page card and the bootstrap retry loop. Hold-to-repeat goes, or stays as the one documented new-ground widget.
findings.deliberate_evidence: 1319967: 'The main page gets a Remote controls card under Camera settings, laid out like it'; fork-log.md:163-164 owner chose to keep Remote controls.
findings.rework_risk: Operators lose one-tap access from the main page; check with owner.

findings.title: 2100-line structured hardware editor with extras; size and shape foreign
findings.port_way: 74 functions: per-device cards, gesture dropdowns, chips, Turn-adjusts pairing by _up/_down id and label regex, a pin claim that removes another control after a confirm, a review in words that re-derives moved rows, Listen, Undo, history, Scan, Test.
findings.apertar_way: No precedent for a structured editor; upstream edits apertar-hardware.conf as text via POST /api/config (src/web/WebControlPage.cpp:10330-10359@upstream-1.6.0); a typical WebUI feature is 20-40 lines in 3-5 places (conv-webui section 0).
findings.why_it_matters: The original developer must maintain a client application larger than any upstream feature, with pin-ownership rules duplicated from Core's validator.
findings.rework: Simplify. Keep rows, action dropdown from list_actions, gesture dropdown, add/remove, pin dropdowns with disabled 'used by' options, revision-checked set_controls save, Hardware card fields. Drop the chip editor (F9), the main-page card (F3), the moved-row re-derivation in renderControlsReview, the controlsClaimPin cascade (a disabled option is the upstream rule C3-I11), the one-entry function dropdown (F17); keep Turn adjusts only if Core's catalog sends the pair. Document what stays as new ground.
findings.deliberate_evidence: d282de9 Why; extras in fa3a798, 8be1ab5 (T40-T43), 1319967; working/controls/decisions.md:47.
findings.rework_risk: Owner-visible feature reduction; needs owner sign-off per extra.

findings.title: Saving Controls or Hardware silently drops the other card's unsaved edits
findings.port_way: saveHardware and saveControls call loadControls(true) (no discard flag, so no confirm), which resets settingEdits, edits, added, removed, buttons; each save sends only its own card's edits. The text-editor save guards with if (!controlsDirty() && !hardwareDirty()) (P:18938).
findings.apertar_way: No precedent for two editors; upstream asks before discarding edits: window.confirm("Reload Apertar config and discard unsaved edits?") src/web/WebControlPage.cpp:10307@upstream-1.6.0 (C3-N3).
findings.why_it_matters: Change GPIO 6 Press on Controls (unsaved), change a NeoRotary setting on Config, press Save Hardware: the GPIO 6 change is gone without a prompt.
findings.rework: After a save, reload the model only if the other card is clean; otherwise update the revision and keep the other card's key-level edits, or ask with window.confirm.

findings.title: Pins recovered by regex from Core's display text
findings.port_way: controlsRowPinInfo parses row.title /^GPIO (\d+)(?: \+ (\d+))?$/ and row.detail /^A (\d+), B (\d+), push (\d+|none)$/; controlsPcfPinsInUse takes the PCF pin from the title's trailing digits. Core builds those strings for display, with value_or("?").
findings.apertar_way: Render reads data fields from the snapshot (state.snapshot src/web/WebControlPage.cpp:9334@upstream-1.6.0; C3-I3); no label parsing.
findings.why_it_matters: encoder0_b missing gives detail 'A 5, B ?, push none', the regex fails, the encoder gets no pin dropdowns and its pins are absent from controlsPinOwners, so GPIO 5 is offered unmarked to another control (Core refuses on save; probable).
findings.rework: Core adds "pins":"5,6,13" (one string) per row next to "pin" (ControlsModel.hpp:353); controlsRowPinInfo splits it; delete the regexes.

findings.title: Unhandled rejections: Scan sticks at Scanning..., Listen overlaps, Undo unguarded
findings.port_way: Scan sets scans[bus]={loading:true} then awaits controlsCall with no catch; a network error or non-JSON reply leaves Scan disabled and 'Scanning...' until the page is reloaded (loadControls never clears scans). Listen setInterval(async, 300) has no in-flight guard. Undo awaits two calls without try/catch and without a busy flag.
findings.apertar_way: Every fetch in try/catch/finally with state.<x>InFlight guards (fetchConfigFile src/web/WebControlPage.cpp:10304-10327@upstream-1.6.0).
findings.why_it_matters: Stuck UI after one failed request; a slow Core receives stacked Listen requests; Save can run during an Undo.
findings.rework: With F2: sendCommand in try/catch, loading cleared in finally; state.controlsListenInFlight for the poll; Undo sets state.controlsSaveInFlight.

findings.title: Listen is a second network poll loop (300 ms) with its timer outside state
findings.port_way: setInterval 300 ms on controls_last_input, auto-off after 120 s or when the panel is hidden; timer and seq in module-level let.
findings.apertar_way: One network poll: window.setInterval(() => fetchState(true), 1000) src/web/WebControlPage.cpp:11609@upstream-1.6.0 (C3-I3, C3-N8); timers on state.
findings.why_it_matters: With WCP-08's /api/buffer poll the page has three loops; timing state is scattered.
findings.rework: Either keep the short user-started poll with timer, seq and in-flight flag on state, as a plain fetch in try/catch (not sendCommand, see F2); or add controls_last_input_seq/section/key to /api/state and highlight from renderSnapshot (1 s latency, no new loop).
findings.deliberate_evidence: 8be1ab5 'Listen lights the row of the control you press'; working/controls/decisions.md:24.

findings.title: Chip editor: duck-typed fake select with drag and drop
findings.port_way: A div that defines value and disabled via Object.defineProperty, dispatches a synthetic change, draggable chips with x buttons, a '__several__' sentinel option.
findings.apertar_way: No precedent; no draggable or defineProperty anywhere upstream; choices are pill grids or native selects (C3-I5, violation example 'custom dropdown components'). The port's own buildControlsSelect already shows an unknown value as '(as written in the file)' (P:16785-16790).
findings.why_it_matters: A widget behaviour no other control on the page has; hard to maintain.
findings.rework: Drop the chip box; multi-action lines show '(as written in the file)' and are edited in Config text. If kept, a plain settings-input holding 'iso200,fps24'.
findings.deliberate_evidence: 8be1ab5 'a line can hold several actions as chips you drag to reorder' (T41).

findings.title: Inline success message duplicates the toast
findings.port_way: A save writes 'Saved. Core applies it now.' into controlsMessage/hardwareMessage and toasts 'Controls saved.'/'Hardware settings saved.'.
findings.apertar_way: One toast, showToast src/web/WebControlPage.cpp:7804-7813@upstream-1.6.0; saveConfigFile toasts only (:10351@upstream-1.6.0); C3-N4 ('inline success banners'). Persistent status lines do exist upstream (settingsImuCalibrationStatus :3007, :9572@upstream-1.6.0).
findings.why_it_matters: Two feedback channels for one event.
findings.rework: Success and 'applies after the take' go into the toast text; keep the issue list (line numbers) and the pending note as status lines.
findings.deliberate_evidence: 8be1ab5 'Saves say Core applies them now, or after the take'.

findings.title: Tally card cannot switch off with wiring kept: None/Remove erases the pin
findings.port_way: enabled field hidden; syncTallyEnabled writes enabled from 'pin set'; pin None and Remove write line=-1, pcf_pin=-1; a file with enabled=false shows its pin as None.
findings.apertar_way: Core reads enabled (src/hardware/RecordingIndicatorOutput.cpp:339@upstream-1.6.0) and line (:349) independently, so the LED can be off with its wiring kept.
findings.why_it_matters: Switching the tally off from Controls erases its pin; turning it on again needs the pin re-entered.
findings.rework: Show enabled as an On/Off control over toggleOptions; leave line/pcf_pin untouched; delete tallyFileEnabled, syncTallyEnabled and the special cases in tallyShown and Remove.
findings.deliberate_evidence: Comment P:17617-17618 'The Tally LED has no On field: it is on exactly when the chosen wiring has a pin'.

findings.title: Whole-file text through a command while upstream's door is /api/config
findings.port_way: Undo sends the whole history text via set_controls text=; Check sends the editor text via set_controls text= dry_run=true; the text editor saves through POST /api/config.
findings.apertar_way: Whole-file work is a route: POST /api/config src/web/WebControlPage.cpp:10336-10340@upstream-1.6.0, App:7175-7195@upstream-1.6.0 (C3-S9). Key-level command writes have precedent (set_imu_*, conv-hardware-config 7).
findings.why_it_matters: Two doors with different checks for the same file (set_controls text= skips the /api/config empty/size/NUL checks, rev-HW-config-text-store F5).
findings.rework: Undo posts the history text through POST /api/config; Check uses a dry-run on the same route (header or query flag); set_controls drops text. Key-level set_controls stays.
findings.deliberate_evidence: 8be1ab5 'Undo last save puts back the version the last save replaced'.

findings.title: Any DPI line greys GPIO 0-27, in the page and in Core's validator
findings.port_way: if (dpiLines.length > 0) for (pin = 0; pin <= 27; ++pin) taken.add(pin); Core's validator refuses any gpio <= 27 when a DPI line exists; the note says 'it holds GPIO 0 to 27'.
findings.apertar_way: no precedent
findings.why_it_matters: Probable: 16/18-bit DPI modes leave upper GPIO free; those pins become unusable for buttons. Settle by reading the overlays in use and their pin maps.
findings.rework: Core computes the pins each detected overlay holds and sends them (dpi_pins); validator and page use that set; the page drops its own 0-27 loops.
findings.deliberate_evidence: 9b5ea14 'With a DPI line in config.txt, GPIO 0-27 are greyed'; DPI greying tested desk only.

findings.title: Issue box x3, Test handler x2, kind-name map x3, pin sets x2
findings.port_way: showControlsMessage/showHardwareMessage/showConfigIssues have the same body; test_output click handler twice; kind names in controlsKindNames and two literal maps; controlsPinsTaken and controlsPinOwners compute nearly the same set.
findings.apertar_way: Shared helpers by role: setText, setFormValue, buildOptionButtons, showToast (src/web/WebControlPage.cpp:6172-6189, 9147-9167, 7804@upstream-1.6.0); request<Action> naming (C3-I6).

findings.rework: One showIssueBox(id, title, issues, isInfo); one requestTestOutput(peripheral); controlsKindNames everywhere; controlsPinsTaken = keys of controlsPinOwners.

findings.title: 127 comment lines incl. T39-T42 ticket ids and 'as in Cinemate'
findings.port_way: 95 full-line and 32 trailing // comments; T41 x3, T42 x4, T40, T39; 'as in Cinemate'.
findings.apertar_way: 2 JS comment lines in the whole upstream script (src/web/WebControlPage.cpp:8474-8475@upstream-1.6.0); C3-I7.
findings.why_it_matters: Ticket ids and Cinemate references mean nothing to the original developer.
findings.rework: Delete ticket ids, Cinemate references and narration; keep at most one-line reasons where a rule is not obvious.

findings.title: Inline grid style, 'GPIO in' vs 'GPIO buttons', loadControls naming
findings.port_way: grid.style.gridTemplateColumns set inline; the GPIO card retitled 'GPIO in' on Controls only; loadControls.
findings.apertar_way: Column classes toggled on the pill grid (three-col, src/web/WebControlPage.cpp:9150@upstream-1.6.0, CSS :755); fetch<X> for loaders (:10207, 10246, 10304, 10361@upstream-1.6.0) (C3-I6). Bool selects are fine: upstream uses selects for on/off (:3791-3794, createFavoriteSelectBlock with toggleOptions :6850).

findings.title: One-entry Function dropdown for outputs
findings.port_way: const controlsOutputFunctions = [["tally", "Tally light"]] with comment 'Tally light for now; add more'; a select with one fixed option.
findings.apertar_way: no precedent
