findings.title: [storage] parsed twice; live buffer state shared through header singletons and a global hook
findings.port_way: App's refreshBufferRequest parses [storage] from hardware::configStore() twice per call. It stores the results in header-level inline function-static atomics (framesPerFolderRequest, clipMergeRequest, prerollState), which only App reads. CC parses [storage] again by itself at take start, with its own path search (loadBufferConf, CC:4297, :5505). App and CC also share live state through more header singletons: safetyStopState, bufferSettingStorage, flushAbortFunction, and safetyStopHook, a global std::function that App sets (App:7988) and CC calls (CC:5018).
findings.apertar_way: C1-S07: each apertar-hardware.conf key has one owner, the class that parses its section. C1-S19: parts reach App through std::function callbacks passed in the constructor (App:6783-6785@upstream-1.6.0), not through globals. Upstream process-wide state sits in the owning class's .cpp behind static members (Mpu6050RecordingSession.hpp:77-82@upstream-1.6.0). No mutable state lives in headers.
findings.why_it_matters: The two parsers of one section can disagree: after a save, App's state can show one value while CC records with another. The original developer cannot find who owns frames_per_folder or where the safety stop is signalled.
findings.rework: CameraController owns [storage]: one loadBufferConf, read at start and again through camera_.reloadStorageOptions(), which replaces App's 7 refreshBufferRequest calls. App reads camera_.storageOptions() and camera_.bufferSettingStatus() for state and for the merge worker. The safety-stop flags become std::atomic members of CC behind a getter. safetyStopHook becomes a constructor callback like eventCallback_. abortSafetyStopFlush becomes camera_.abortSafetyStopFlush(), taking only the queue's own mutex. Delete the singletons in BufferBudget.hpp and StoragePreroll.hpp; the pure parse and plan functions stay.
findings.rework_risk: The abort must stay callable without commandMutex_ (see F13).

findings.title: Env-var knobs in the command plane, overriding hardware.conf keys and exposed as *_env state
findings.port_way: App reads APERTAR_WEB_PREVIEW_RECORDING_FPS, APERTAR_CDNG_BUFFER, APERTAR_STORAGE_PREROLL, APERTAR_CDNG_FRAMES_PER_FOLDER, APERTAR_CLIP_MERGE and APERTAR_BOOT_CONFIG. The env value beats the hardware-file key that the WebUI edits (BufferBudget.hpp:303-330). storage_preroll_auto_env, frames_per_folder_env and clip_merge_env_off are sent to clients.
findings.apertar_way: C1-S24: App reads only APERTAR_HARDWARE_CONFIG (App:4254@upstream-1.6.0). 'An environment variable switch in the command plane' is a listed violation. C2-R5 step 4: bench knobs stay out of apertar-hardware.conf, the socket API and the README, and are read where used in CC or the encoders (C2 5.11).
findings.why_it_matters: A variable in the systemd unit silently beats the operator's WebUI choice, and the UI needs *_env flags to explain why. Experiment knobs are left in shipping code.
findings.rework: Operator values: hardware-file key only. Drop the four env reads, their CC twin at CC:4293 and the three *_env fields. APERTAR_WEB_PREVIEW_RECORDING_FPS: delete it, or make it a C2-R5 knob beside the preview code with no state field. APERTAR_BOOT_CONFIG: replace with a path parameter on the writer for the host test; Core keeps kBootConfigPath.

findings.title: Boot Config field command has a second HTTP entry with its own lock, header protocol and 403/409 codes
findings.port_way: POST /api/boot-config inserts "cmd":"set_boot_config" into the body and reads X-Apertar-Revision. It treats a request with an Origin header as 'browser' and refuses it without a revision. It calls bootConfigSet without commandMutex_. BootConfigReply{status, body} returns 200/400/403/409/500. The same function also answers the socket command inside handleCommand. Writes are serialised by bootConfigMutex().
findings.apertar_way: C1-S09: field changes go through POST /api/command (App:7637-7641@upstream-1.6.0). C1-S02/S03: a flat if-chain in handleCommand under one commandMutex_. Whole-file save routes are precedented: POST /api/config (App:7175-7195@upstream-1.6.0) returns status 400 with errorReply(-1, ...), with no revision header and no 409. Upstream set_fan_mode writes config.txt from inside handleCommand (App:10568@upstream-1.6.0).
findings.why_it_matters: A second command path with its own lock and status vocabulary. The original developer's rule that the socket, the touch UI and the WebUI share one dispatcher no longer holds.
findings.rework: The WebUI sends get_boot_config and set_boot_config through sendCommand; both stay ordinary handleCommand blocks returning okReply/errorReply. Delete BootConfigReply, POST /api/boot-config, the Origin test and bootConfigMutex, so the fan mode and Boot Config both run under commandMutex_. revision becomes a plain field. GET /api/boot-config may stay as a read route. /api/boot-config/parse folds into set_boot_config with dry_run and text, or stays as a file-work route shaped like POST /api/config.
findings.deliberate_evidence: The 2955ef8 message describes the route, the X-Apertar-Revision header and the 409. Its 'as /api/config' refers to the port's own /api/config change, not to upstream.

findings.title: errorReplyBody adds machine error codes and extra members to error replies
findings.port_way: A third reply builder. 14 call sites (Boot Config, set_controls, /api/config, set_buffer_mode, set_frames_per_folder, set_storage_preroll) send "code":"invalid|unreadable|old_page|stale|refused|confirm_display|permission|write_failed", plus revision, drm and issue lists, with ok:false.
findings.apertar_way: C1-I06: replies come only from okReply and errorReply(id, sentence) (App:108-128@upstream-1.6.0). C1-I07 lists 'Error codes' as a violation. C1-N02: the refusal sentence is shown as written. Upstream has no "code" key in any reply.
findings.why_it_matters: Clients branch on codes instead of showing the sentence, and a second error vocabulary grows beside the sentence families.
findings.rework: Delete errorReplyBody. Stale revision: refuse with a sentence; the client re-reads with get_boot_config. Display guard: answer ok with "display_changed":true,"written":false, as dry_run does, and let the card resend with confirm_display. Hardware-config issues: a sentence, with the details from the existing GET /api/config.
findings.deliberate_evidence: f5a61b8 introduces it for set_controls ('refusals carry their code, issues and conflicts through the new errorReplyBody'). Boot Config uses it throughout.

findings.title: apertar::bootconf: 1355-line header-only config.txt editor with free-text edit
findings.port_way: A header-only module: parser, board rules, sensor and link frequency per port, dtparams, RP1 clock, DPI display, a line diff and JSON output. Around it: a review step, a revision check, a display guard and whole-file text editing. It edits the existing lines of config.txt in place (f19b245).
findings.apertar_way: No precedent. Upstream touches config.txt only through a managed fan block (fanModeBlock App:3042, stripManagedFanBlock App:3084, applyFanMode App:3127@upstream-1.6.0). Code with I/O is a .hpp/.cpp pair (hardware/GpioInput.{hpp,cpp}@upstream-1.6.0). Upstream header-only modules hold pure logic of about 200 lines at most (DefaultTuningSelection.hpp 207, ButtonActionList.hpp 121) or data tables.
findings.why_it_matters: The largest new subsystem in the slice. Much of it (the diff, the review step, the revision check) exists only because arbitrary lines are edited.
findings.rework: Drop the free-text edit, or make it a whole-file save shaped like POST /api/config. Write dtparams, RP1 clock and link frequency as one Apertar-managed block that is stripped and rewritten like the fan block. Sensor overlays keep a narrow in-place comment/uncomment of the existing dtoverlay=imx... lines and camera_auto_detect. Split the module into src/hardware/BootConfig.{hpp,cpp}.
findings.rework_risk: A block appended at the end cannot switch off an earlier sensor overlay or camera_auto_detect=1, because every overlay line loads. The in-place part for sensors must stay.
findings.deliberate_evidence: Nine commits (f19b245 .. 2a4266e), host test tools/boot_config_test.cpp (427 lines, 73 checks), and the 'Why' paragraph of 3b87d99.

findings.title: LAN client can write arbitrary config.txt text as root
findings.port_way: set_boot_config with text (from the socket, /api/command or POST /api/boot-config) goes to a NOPASSWD root helper. The helper checks only size, NUL bytes and a [pi5]/[pi4]/[all] line, so any LAN client can set overlays, kernel, initramfs or os_prefix.
findings.apertar_way: C1-N10: the WebUI is for a trusted LAN and uses fixed helper command lines. App:1543@upstream-1.6.0: 'Fixed executable and arguments only; never accept paths from WebUI/config.' Upstream sudoers rules pin their arguments (Apertar-UI/systemd/apertar-standby-usb.sudoers@upstream-1.6.0), and the fan route writes only a generated block. Upstream's one free-text editor (POST /api/config) writes a file that is neither root-owned nor needed to boot.
findings.why_it_matters: One bad or hostile save leaves the Pi unbootable until the card is fixed on another machine.
findings.rework: Together with F6: only generated lines from validated fields reach the file. Remove the free-text edit, or require confirmation on the touch screen. Keep the argument-pinned helper.
findings.deliberate_evidence: The helper's header documents its checks; 3b87d99 adds text editing on purpose.

findings.title: Boot Config error sentences carry install commands and wire field names
findings.port_way: "Writing config.txt needs root. Install the helper: sudo install -m 0755 ... ~/ApertarCore/scripts/..."; "... Send confirm_display=true to save anyway."; "<port>_link_frequency must be ... or null ...". The fan mode keeps the upstream sentence (App:3645-3647).
findings.apertar_way: C1-I07: one sentence for the operator, no developer detail. Upstream: 'Changing the fan mode needs sudo permission.' (App:3164@upstream-1.6.0).
findings.why_it_matters: Toasts shown to the operator contain shell commands and protocol field names.
findings.rework: Use 'Writing config.txt needs the apertar-boot-config helper.' and add a README install section. Remove wire names from the sentences.

findings.title: Nested Boot Config replies
findings.port_way: Replies hold boot_config{...,state{...},drm[...],text}, plus changes[], state{} and drm[].
findings.apertar_way: C1 5.5: replies are flat, with a short fixed list of nested values. One object per topic is precedented (imuStatusBody "imu":{...}, App:130@upstream-1.6.0).
findings.why_it_matters: It lengthens the list of nested replies and makes them harder for flat clients to read.
findings.rework: After F6: one flat "boot_config":{...} object like imu. changes becomes a joined string or is dropped; drm becomes a count of connected connectors.
findings.deliberate_evidence: The 2955ef8 message lists the reply shape.

findings.title: Three write routes for config.txt, one of them a second atomic-write implementation
findings.port_way: First, a direct write when Core may write the file (as root, or to the APERTAR_BOOT_CONFIG copy), using its own fsyncPath and a temp/fsync/rename/directory-fsync sequence. Else the root helper. Else sudo -n install, plus an extra sudo -n install of the backup (App:3595).
findings.apertar_way: One route: sudo -n install -m 644 <tmp> /boot/firmware/config.txt (App:3155-3158@upstream-1.6.0). Atomic writes go through settingsFile::atomicWrite (src/util/SettingsFile.hpp:36-55@upstream-1.6.0).
findings.why_it_matters: Three branches to reason about, and a second atomic-write implementation beside SettingsFile.hpp.
findings.rework: Keep the helper, then the upstream sudo -n install route. Drop the direct route and fsyncPath together with F3's APERTAR_BOOT_CONFIG. The host test passes a path to a writer that uses settingsFile::atomicWrite.
findings.deliberate_evidence: 2955ef8 message: 'direct when allowed, else the apertar-boot-config helper, else sudo -n install as before'.

findings.title: With the helper installed, fan mode fails on a config.txt without [pi5]/[pi4]/[all]
findings.port_way: The helper exits 2 when there is no [pi5]/[pi4]/[all] line, and fanModeBlock adds none. Core returns the helper's output as the error and does not fall back to another route.
findings.apertar_way: applyFanMode writes any config.txt (App:3127-3178@upstream-1.6.0).
findings.why_it_matters: A config.txt with only [cm4]/[cm5] sections, or no sections (hand-made or older images), fails. Fan mode worked on these files upstream and is now refused with a helper message.
findings.rework: Drop the section check, or accept any non-empty text that contains the managed block.

findings.title: abortSafetyStopFlushForRecord runs before the command lock
findings.port_way: A lock-free abort runs before commandMutex_ and hardwareActionMutex_ are taken, because the safety-stop thread holds commandMutex_ while it drains.
findings.apertar_way: C1-S03 lists 'a command body that runs before the lock' as a violation. C1-S20: slow work that must not hold the lock is its own worker with its own state group.
findings.why_it_matters: It is an exception to the one-lock rule. The root cause is that the drain holds commandMutex_.
findings.rework: Keep it for now. When the safety-stop drain stops holding commandMutex_ (a later slice, C1-S20), move the abort into the record_start block. Judge it together with the other code that runs before the lock at App:12562-12565 (handleReadOnlyHardwareCommand, test_input, both from f5a61b8).
findings.deliberate_evidence: Explanatory comments at both call sites.

findings.title: Eject-intent flag file has no reader in Apertar
findings.port_way: writeEjectIntent runs before an eject. clearEjectIntent runs after a mount and on a removal. The flag is /run/apertar-media/eject/<dev>, and its directory comes from a tmpfiles.d install step. A comment cites Cinemate f01b6cd.
findings.apertar_way: The upstream automounters are Apertar-UI/src/CfeAutomounter.cpp and Core's embedded Python watcher (App:3391+@upstream-1.6.0). Neither uses such a flag, and no reader exists in Core src or UI src at the port.
findings.why_it_matters: A write path that nothing reads, plus an install step with no consumer.
findings.rework: Either make CfeAutomounter and the Python watcher honour the flag in the same change, or delete MediaIntent.hpp, the three calls and the eject line of the tmpfiles file. The tune line stays.
findings.deliberate_evidence: 438a342 ports Cinemate f01b6cd on purpose.

findings.title: FPS/ISO step lists now end on the mode's odd ceiling
findings.port_way: selectableValueSteps appends the cap whenever a listed value lies above it.
findings.apertar_way: App:1150-1167@upstream-1.6.0: presets <= max are kept, and max is added only `if (filtered.empty())`.
findings.why_it_matters: The IMX477 4144x2176 dial was 24, 25, 30 upstream and is now 24, 25, 30, 41.08. This changes button and encoder behaviour without an option.
findings.rework: Restore the upstream rule (add the cap only when the list is empty), or make 'add ceiling' an explicit value-list option. State the choice in the handoff.
findings.deliberate_evidence: Comment 'T33 (request 24)' at App:1272.

findings.title: Tutorial numbers, KB paths, Cinemate history, banner and run-on comments
findings.port_way: 'kb working/dng-chain, V/H4', 'T33 (request 24)', 'Free stepping (T33)', 'Cinemate's two versions ... both are off', '(Cinemate f01b6cd)', a `// ---- Boot config card ... ----` banner, and one comment line of about 250 characters.
findings.apertar_way: C1-I14: comments are rare, each one sentence giving a hazard or a reason; no banners, no ticket numbers. Upstream App has 10 comment lines; the port's App has 307.
findings.why_it_matters: The internal references mean nothing to the original developer, and the comments read as a narrated history.
findings.rework: Delete the ticket, KB and Cinemate references and the banner. Cut each note to its one hazard sentence.

findings.title: State fields with no reader
findings.port_way: conform_fps, ladder_override, buffer_used, buffer_capacity, buffer_unit, sensor_binning, sensor_binning_source and sensor_crop appear only in their serialisers (App, CC). git grep over both repos finds no reader in WCP, the touch UI, tools, scripts or the README.
findings.apertar_way: C1-S13: each camera field costs a line in three serialisers. Every upstream field has a reader (C1-R4 readers list).
findings.why_it_matters: Protocol fields that nothing reads, maintained in three places.
findings.rework: Drop them unless a client in this merge reads them. Before dropping sensor_binning*, ask the owner whether socket tooling outside the repos uses them (unconfirmed).

findings.title: boolFieldValue: a second boolean parser accepting on/yes/off/no
findings.port_way: Accepts true/1/on/yes and false/0/off/no, case-insensitive. Three Boot Config callers.
findings.apertar_way: C1-I05: `*enabled == "true" || *enabled == "1"` tested by hand. parseUiSettingsBool (App:350-357@upstream-1.6.0) accepts true/1/false/0 only.
findings.why_it_matters: The accepted boolean words differ from command to command.
findings.rework: Use the upstream hand test. Keep the existing '<field> must be true or false.' refusal for any other text.

findings.title: IMX585 Clear HDR fallback fps cap and its comment disagree with Core's table
findings.port_way: The fallback, used while fps_max is 0, caps only 16-bit Clear HDR at 25, with the comment 'as in Core's tableMaximumFpsForResolution()'. CC's table caps any Clear HDR at 25 when the sensor limit is unknown, and has had no 16-bit cap since 31d5418.
findings.apertar_way: Upstream keeps App's per-sensor fallback (maximumPcfFpsForSettings, used by App:1150-1167@upstream-1.6.0) equal to CC's table. C1-I14: a comment states a reason that is true.
findings.why_it_matters: While fps_max is 0, the dial can offer 30 fps in 12-bit Clear HDR where Core's table says 25 (probable; fallback path only). The comment points the reader at a rule that no longer exists.
findings.rework: Change the condition to `settings.clearHdr ? 25.0 : 30.0`, matching CC's unknown-limit row, and reword or delete the comment.

findings.title: Second include block after the JPEG #if; util/ headers ahead of public headers
findings.port_way: util/ includes come before <apertar/core/...>. <csignal>, <functional> and the playback/ and cdng/ headers sit in a separate block after the JPEG #if.
findings.apertar_way: App:1-55@upstream-1.6.0: own header, public headers, project headers, std, system, then the #if blocks.
findings.why_it_matters: It is the first thing the original developer sees in the file, and it reads as bolted on.
findings.rework: Move each include into its upstream group.

App-3.summary: Skeptic pass on App-3. 13 findings in: 3 stand (F5, F7, F12), 9 corrected (F1, F2, F3, F4, F6, F8, F9, F10, F11), 1 dropped (F13). 12 survive. F13 is dropped because the wrapper keeps the upstream function name and call site, so removing it is churn. Main corrections: (1) F1. Upstream also writes a config file from a route outside handleCommand (POST /api/config, App:7175@upstream-1.6.0), so a file route is not a mismatch in itself. The two doors with different rules and the JSON body splice are. Severity goes to minor. (2) F2. Upstream already treats timelapse as a take, and holding downloads during the speed test is reasonable. The real loss is downloads in Standby. Severity goes to minor. (3) F3. A README row already exists, and the knob is one of about ten port env knobs. Severity goes to minor. (4) F4. The rule that a request with an Origin header comes from a browser is upstream's own (WebServer.cpp:160-161@upstream-1.6.0). (5) F6. The WebUI never shows these strings, so it drops to nit. (6) F8. Effort goes to S, because the streams already take a callable. (7) F9. The proposed reorder does not close the race. The fix is to take commandMutex_ around the checks and the scope construction. (8) F10. The key is added in the route (App:8424), not in bufferMembers. (9) F11. The rename does not match upstream naming, so only the leading-comma fix stays. No new findings.

findings.title: POST /api/boot-config is a second door for set_boot_config; splices "cmd" into the body
findings.port_way: The route finds the first '{' in the body, inserts "cmd":"set_boot_config", runs parseControlCommand and calls bootConfigSet(parsed.command, revision, request.headers.count("origin") > 0) outside handleCommand/commandMutex_ (under bootConfigMutex()). The socket command calls the same function with browser=false. One write, two doors, different rules (old_page only on the route, revision from header or field).
findings.apertar_way: A file writer is either a route (POST /api/config, src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:7175-7195@upstream-1.6.0) or a command (set_fan_mode, :10568, via POST /api/command -> handleWebCommand -> handleCommand, :7085-7091, :7637-7641). Each has one door. No route rewrites a JSON body into a command.
findings.why_it_matters: The text splice is a hack the original developer would refuse. Two doors with different refusal rules for one file is the spaghetti the owner wants removed.
findings.rework: Delete the POST /api/boot-config route. In WCP bootConfigPost, send {"cmd":"set_boot_config",...,"revision":r} to /api/command. The command already reads revision as a field, and the card branches only on result.code (result.httpStatus is set at WCP:20011 and read nowhere). Drop the browser parameter from bootConfigSet (see F4). GET /api/boot-config stays as the read twin of GET /api/config. POST /api/boot-config/parse stays as a raw-body file route, like presets/import. With one caller left, BootConfigReply can become a plain reply string.
findings.deliberate_evidence: Commit 2955ef8 and KB architecture/config.md section 7.1 describe both doors but never weigh /api/command.

findings.title: Downloads refused in Standby (and without media), not only during a take
findings.port_way: Both download routes return 409 whenever playbackHoldReason() is non-empty. That rule was written for playback. It covers recording, sound, timelapse, the yield window, pending writes, the speed test, Standby and media not usable.
findings.apertar_way: GET /api/media/download (src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:7197@upstream-1.6.0) and download-selected (:7318) have no guard, so downloads work in Standby. Upstream counts timelapse as a take (:7514), so holding downloads for recording, sound, timelapse, writes and the speed test is consistent with the commit's stated reason.
findings.why_it_matters: An operator who offloads clips from a sleeping camera gets 409 'Playback held: standby. Downloads wait.' The WebUI starts downloads with an anchor click (WCP:12089, :12917), so the refusal shows only as a failed browser download, right after the toast 'Preparing ... for download.'
findings.rework: Give the download routes their own rule, downloadHoldReason(): recording, sound, timelapse, yield window, pending writes and speed test. Hold in Standby only when standbyUsbPoweredOff_ is true. Drop the 'media' hold, since the route's own 404 covers missing media. Keep the stream stop callback. Add one README sentence on the take rule.
findings.deliberate_evidence: Commit a37a902 and its fork-log row justify the hold during a take only ('a big read from the card a take writes to'). Standby is not mentioned.

findings.title: APERTAR_WEB_PREVIEW_RECORDING_FPS env knob left from an experiment
findings.port_way: std::getenv in a static lambda. The comment calls it 'the A/B knob' and cites KB research ids. The default of 30 equals the old fixed rate. It is one of about ten APERTAR_* env reads the port added to App (App:266-285, :6402, :11335, :11379, :11402). State also exposes media_trim_env_off and clip_merge_env_off. It has a README row.
findings.apertar_way: constexpr double kWebPreviewMaxFps = 30.0 (src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:62@upstream-1.6.0), used at :8105. Core reads one env var of its own, APERTAR_HARDWARE_CONFIG (:4254). Process options are Options plus main flags (C1-S24).
findings.why_it_matters: The knob comes from an experiment, changes nothing by default and was never run on the Pi (commit fb557e9: 'Not run on the Pi'). The upstream code base has no env knobs like it.
findings.rework: Run the two-take test. If the knob is not needed, delete webPreviewRecordingFps(), the rawTakeActive branch and the README row. If it is needed, use a fixed reduced rate during raw takes, or an Options field with a --flag and a usage line. Handle the *_env_off state members in the port-wide knob sweep.
findings.deliberate_evidence: Commit fb557e9 calls it a knob whose need a Pi test still has to decide.

findings.title: Revision in an X-Apertar-Revision header, plus an old_page refusal
findings.port_way: A custom request header carries the revision. A request with an Origin header and no revision gets 409 old_page. A request without Origin keeps last-writer-wins.
findings.apertar_way: Route parameters travel in the query string (queryParameterValue(request.query, "name"), src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:7440@upstream-1.6.0). The rule that an Origin header means a browser is upstream's own (src/web/WebServer.cpp:160-161@upstream-1.6.0, 'Native clients/CLI have no Origin.'). Core and page ship together, and upstream has no page-version concept (C1-N11).
findings.why_it_matters: The revision check is worth keeping. The header is a second parameter channel next to the query string, and old_page is a page-version concept upstream does not have.
findings.rework: Use POST /api/config?revision=r (and, with F1, a revision field in set_boot_config). A stale revision returns 409 stale. Keep old_page only if the owner wants the stale-tab guard; it can keep using upstream's Origin rule. Drop the header reads in App and WCP.
findings.deliberate_evidence: Commit 5395fa4 explains the stale-tab case.

findings.title: 409 hold replies hand-built at five sites; sibling routes differ; busy and gone replies without error key
findings.port_way: "{\"ok\":false,\"error\":\"Playback held: " + hold + ..." is string-built at five sites. The /api/media/clip 409 (:8460) uses errorReply and has no hold member. Busy {"ok":false,"busy":true} and gone {...,"gone":true} are hand-built too.
findings.apertar_way: Replies come only from okReply/errorReply, reused with id -1 in HTTP routes (src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:7188, :7647@upstream-1.6.0; C1-I06). The port already has errorReplyBody for extra members (App:173@cinemate-port).
findings.why_it_matters: The reply text is duplicated and the shapes are inconsistent. A client that shows result.error gets nothing for busy.
findings.rework: Add a free function playbackHoldReply(hold) that returns errorReplyBody(-1, holdSentence(hold), "\"hold\":\""+hold+"\""). Use it at all six hold sites, /api/media/clip included. Build busy and gone with errorReplyBody: an operator sentence plus "busy":true or "gone":true.

findings.title: Hold sentences carry internal hold tokens
findings.port_way: 'Playback held: media_test. Downloads wait.'; 'Recording. Downloads wait until the take ends.'
findings.apertar_way: An error is one operator sentence: 'Stop recording before deleting media.' (src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:7514@upstream-1.6.0), 'Wait for the media speed test to finish first.' (:9110), 'Wake the camera before capturing.' (:9211). C1-I07, C1-N02.
findings.why_it_matters: The impact is small. The WebUI never shows these strings: the Clip Viewer maps the token itself (pbvHoldText, WCP:12156-12162), and downloads are anchor clicks. Only scripts and a raw JSON page show the internal identifiers.
findings.rework: Add holdSentence(hold) next to the F5 helper, using upstream's sentence families. recording: 'Stop recording before downloading media.' writing: 'Wait for the current capture to finish writing to media.' media_test: 'Wait for the media speed test to finish first.' standby: 'Wake the camera first.' media: 'Mount media first.'

findings.title: Ticket numbers and history narration in comments
findings.port_way: Comments carry T48, T51, T39, T47, T20 Step 4, T34, 'request 13', KB research ids, 'design sketch v2 (not in any repository)', 'critic M8' and line numbers into other files. App has 46 T<nn> matches.
findings.apertar_way: The 11 025-line upstream App has 10 full-line comments. Each states a hazard or a reason, and none has a ticket number (C1-I14; e.g. src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:8103-8104@upstream-1.6.0).
findings.why_it_matters: These references mean nothing to the original developer, and the line numbers go stale.
findings.rework: Delete the tags and references. Where a comment states a hazard, keep one sentence: hold before read, no lock on the completion thread, and why the yield window exists.

findings.title: Playback yield window is a file-scope singleton
findings.port_way: static PlaybackYield in playbackYield(), plus free functions playbackYieldActive() and playbackNowMs(). handleCommand (App:12582) and the media watcher (:10915, :10976, :11264) write it; stream writers and state builders read it. The stated reason is to avoid header rebuilds.
findings.apertar_way: Cross-thread control flags are std::atomic members of App in ApertarCoreApp.hpp (C1-S18). Parts receive std::function callbacks from App (src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:6783-6792@upstream-1.6.0; C1-S19). Upstream uses function-local statics only for caches (:2269-2272, :2788-2790), which is what clipFactsCache() is.
findings.why_it_matters: Control state hides outside the App object, unlike every other state group.
findings.rework: Add playback::PlaybackYield playbackYield_ as a member in ApertarCoreApp.hpp (PlaybackHold.hpp pulls in only <atomic> and <cstdint>). The streams already take a callable (App:8522, :8608, :8742, :8767, :8799, :8856); pass [this]{ return playbackYield_.active(playbackNowMs()); }. clipFactsCache() stays a function-local static.
findings.deliberate_evidence: Comment at App:6335-6336: 'File scope, so the header does not pull in the readers'.

findings.title: Delete gate is not atomic with record_start
findings.port_way: The delete routes check isRecording, sound, timelapse and mediaWritesPending, then construct MediaDeleteScope. handleCommand refuses record_start with 'Deleting media. One moment.' only if the flag is already set when it reaches App:12587. The routes do not take commandMutex_.
findings.apertar_way: Upstream had no flag and the same race (src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:7514@upstream-1.6.0), so this is a hole in the port's new guarantee, not a regression. Upstream serialises with commandMutex_, which handleCommand holds for the whole command.
findings.why_it_matters: record_start passes the flag check. The route then checks isRecording before the start has set it, sees false, and deletes during the start of the take. Constructing the scope first does not close this window.
findings.rework: In both delete routes, hold a std::lock_guard on commandMutex_ around the recording and pending-writes checks and the MediaDeleteScope construction. Keep the scope in a std::optional declared before the lock block, and release the lock before the delete itself. A running record_start has then either finished (recording is true, so the route refuses) or not yet reached its check (it sees the flag).

findings.title: /api/buffer 'recording' differs from /api/state 'recording'
findings.port_way: The /api/buffer route appends recording = buffer.recording && !safetyStopState().active. /api/state sends recording = camera_.isRecording() || soundRecording.
findings.apertar_way: One key has one meaning across state copies (C1-S13; /api/state recording at src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:7841@upstream-1.6.0).
findings.why_it_matters: A page that reads both routes sees the same key disagree, for example in a sound-only take or a safety stop.
findings.rework: Rename the key in the /api/buffer route (App:8424) to buffer_recording (or buffer_active), and update the reader at WCP:16514. Keep the 4 Hz route.

findings.title: State fragment helpers return a leading comma
findings.port_way: mediaTrimStateJson() and clipMergeStateJson() return text that starts with ','. In the same chain, bufferMembers is used as "," << bufferMembers(...).
findings.apertar_way: Fragments carry no separator; the caller writes it: "," << exposureMeteringJson(settings) (src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:7867@upstream-1.6.0), "," << imuStatusBody(true) (:8028). Upstream names fragments both *Json and *Body, so the names can stay.
findings.why_it_matters: Two conventions inside one << chain.
findings.rework: Drop the leading comma in both functions, and write << "," << mediaTrimStateJson() and << "," << clipMergeStateJson() at their callers.

findings.title: Constant "play_reason":"" read by nobody
findings.port_way: Every list item and every clip info carries an empty play_reason. Neither WebControlPage.cpp nor Apertar-UI reads it; only the KB design page working/playback/design-playback.md:588 plans a reader.
findings.apertar_way: no precedent
findings.why_it_matters: Dead protocol field.
findings.rework: Delete it at both sites.

App-5.summary: Skeptic pass on App-5: 9 findings checked, 0 dropped, 4 corrected, 5 stand as written, none added. F1 corrected: original Apertar does let operator commands write single hardware-file keys. set_imu_driver calls the owning module, Mpu6050RecordingSession::setConfiguredDriver, which calls writeHardwareConfigValue (App:9646, Mpu6050RecordingSession.cpp:604,1300@upstream-1.6.0). So the mismatch is how the code is shaped, not which file the keys go in: the store edit is written out three times, with the flags.trusted bypass, worker wakes and array replies. The rework is now one owner function plus C1-I01 blocks. The keys stay in the hardware file, because buffer sits next to buffer_ram_*/buffer_stop_percent. F2 narrowed: original Apertar already uses parseUiSettingsBool and a bool lambda in apply_preset. What still stands is set_storage_preroll value=on|off and the switches named without _enabled. F5 corrected: the ranges are duplicated in the snapshot reader (App:2160) as well, and set_favorites_order's array reply is the precedent for a list in a reply. F8 corrected: the closest original name is storage_preroll_start (matches record_start/timelapse_start). F3, F4, F6, F7, F9 stand.
conforms: set_controls restore= uses parseBooleanToken, which is an upstream helper (App:2936@upstream-1.6.0), with a refusal sentence
set_mode_ladder's boolField lambda and set_value_steps' parseUiSettingsBool follow upstream apply_preset's addBoolUpdate lambda (App:10231-10237@upstream-1.6.0)
set_media_trim, set_preview_tdn, set_fps_phase_lock, set_conform_fps: C1-I01 setter blocks replying settingsBody (App:13194-13240@cinemate-port)
set_timecode_mode and set_iso_auto: an absent new field gives the upstream behaviour (C1-N11)

abstraction_verdicts.name: hardware::HardwareConfigStore use for storage switches
abstraction_verdicts.reason: Keep the store, but move the edit into one owner function (e.g. bufferbudget::saveStorageKey), following upstream Mpu6050RecordingSession::setConfiguredDriver + writeHardwareConfigValue. That leaves App with C1-I01 blocks and keeps flags.trusted out of handleCommand.

abstraction_verdicts.name: apertar::clipname::parse in App
abstraction_verdicts.reason: Parse once, in CC (F4).

abstraction_verdicts.name: set_value_steps ListKeys table
abstraction_verdicts.reason: Make it a free function in the anonymous namespace, shared with the snapshot reader at App:2160 (F5).

findings.title: Storage switches inline the hardware-store edit three times in handleCommand
findings.port_way: set_buffer_mode, set_frames_per_folder/set_clip_merge (one block), set_storage_preroll each build StoreFlags{backup, trusted=true}, call hardware::configStore().edit(base-or-current, {{Set,"storage"|"media",key,value}}, by, flags, hardwareConfigFacts()), return errorReplyBody with code/revision/issues array, update controlsErrors_/controlsWarnings_, wakeControlsWorker(), refreshBufferRequest(), reply revision/written/apply + bufferSettingMembers(). flags.trusted bypasses the store's text-mode-only rule for [storage]/[media].
findings.apertar_way: An operator command that persists one hardware-file key calls the owning module's setter from a C1-I01 block: `if (!Mpu6050RecordingSession::setConfiguredDriver(*value, &errorMessage)) return errorReply(command.id, errorMessage); return okReply(command.id, imuStatusBody(false));` (src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:9646-9655@upstream-1.6.0); the owner writes the key with writeHardwareConfigValue(config.configPath, "imu", "driver", ...) (src/hardware/Mpu6050RecordingSession.cpp:604, :1295-1300@upstream-1.6.0). Whole-file saves go through the WebUI editor (App:7178@upstream-1.6.0).
findings.why_it_matters: Three copies of store plumbing (revisions, error codes, worker wakes, a bypass flag, array replies) sit inside four ordinary switches. Where the original developer expects a four-line setter call he finds the set_controls machinery.
findings.rework: Add one owner function next to the buffer/storage code, e.g. bufferbudget::saveStorageKey(section, key, value, std::string *error). It does the store edit with trusted (kept inside, with its comment), the controls counts and the worker wake. Each App block becomes C1-I01: check the value, `if (!saveStorageKey("storage","buffer",*value,&error)) return errorReply(command.id, error); refreshBufferRequest(); return okReply(command.id, bufferSettingMembers());`, plus clipMerge("switch") when merge is switched on. Drop revision/written/issues from these replies, or keep revision only if WCP reads it (check WCP:14027-14031). The keys stay in the hardware file, because buffer belongs with buffer_ram_fraction/floor_mb/max_fraction, buffer_stop_percent and the env overrides (KB architecture/config.md:115). Moving them to camera_settings.conf is not recommended. Same direction as the App-2 rework.
findings.deliberate_evidence: Comment App:12827-12828 says 'through the store like set_controls (revision, history, stale and lock refusals)', so the store was chosen on purpose. Nothing shows the three inline copies were weighed.
findings.rework_risk: WCP or the touch bridge may read revision/written from the reply; grep before removing them.

findings.title: set_storage_preroll takes value=on|off with its own parse; camera switches lack _enabled
findings.port_way: set_storage_preroll lower-cases value and accepts on/off/true/false/1/0. It is the only on/off command that takes value= instead of enabled=. set_media_trim, set_preview_tdn, set_fps_phase_lock and set_fps_speed_ramp take enabled= but are not named *_enabled.
findings.apertar_way: C1-I05: `const bool value = (*enabled == "true" || *enabled == "1");` (src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:9482-9486@upstream-1.6.0), with the strict form where a wrong value must be refused (App:9130-9133@upstream-1.6.0). The argument is named enabled and the command set_<thing>_enabled. parseUiSettingsBool on command arguments and a local bool lambda have upstream precedent in apply_preset (App:10231-10237, 10282@upstream-1.6.0), so set_value_steps, set_mode_ladder and set_controls restore= are not part of this finding.
findings.why_it_matters: One command breaks the on/off argument shape every client otherwise uses.
findings.rework: set_storage_preroll becomes set_storage_preroll_enabled enabled= with the strict C1-I05 test. Delete the tolower loop. Update Apertar-UI ApertarControlBridge.cpp:627 and WCP:14030, :15843. Optional: rename the four camera switches to *_enabled (a protocol change for both clients).

findings.title: get_state writes media_state twice from two snapshots
findings.port_way: Line 12944 streams "media_state" from a fresh mediaSnapshot(). Line 12961 streams the same key again from mediaState, the snapshot taken at 12935.
findings.apertar_way: C1-R4: one key per status field, the same key in get_state and /api/state (src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:9223-9237 and 7836-7856@upstream-1.6.0). The port's web state writes it once (App:9555@cinemate-port).
findings.why_it_matters: {"cmd":"get_state"} sent while a card is pulled can carry two different values. Which one wins depends on the client's JSON parser.
findings.rework: Delete line 12944.

findings.title: Clip name template parsed in App and again in CC; unused out-parameter
findings.port_way: set_clip_name_template calls apertar::clipname::parse in App, then camera_.setClipNameTemplate, which parses again. `std::string stored` is passed but never read. preview_clip_name calls camera_.previewClipName (which parses) and then parses again in App to get normalized/corrected.
findings.apertar_way: C1-I12: App checks that the argument is present; the CC setter validates and reports through lastError() (src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:9251-9258@upstream-1.6.0; src/camera/CameraController.cpp:7835-7849@upstream-1.6.0).
findings.why_it_matters: The two validation points can drift apart. The error order differs: App's parse error comes before CC's 'while recording' refusal. The out-parameter is dead.
findings.rework: App only checks presence and calls camera_.setClipNameTemplate(*value). corrected = (settings.clipNameTemplate != *value). previewClipName returns the normalized template and the corrected flag together with the example. Remove the stored parameter from the signature; App is its only caller.

findings.title: set_value_steps: range table inside the branch, nested ui reply
findings.port_way: One command with a name= selector writes up to six UI.conf keys. A static constexpr ListKeys table with ranges sits inside the branch. The UI.conf snapshot reader repeats the ranges (parseValueStepsList(value, 50.0, 51200.0) at :2160). The reply is "ui":{valueStepsJson(...)}.
findings.apertar_way: UI.conf commands echo flat keys: set_sleep_mode replies "sleep_mode":... (App:10206-10216@upstream-1.6.0), set_favorites_order replies "favorites_order":[...] (App:10227@upstream-1.6.0). Tables of allowed values are free functions in the anonymous namespace (C1-S06, favoriteCandidateOrder() App:727-763@upstream-1.6.0). A nested ui group exists only in /api/state.
findings.why_it_matters: The reply duplicates the state's ui group, and the ranges live in two places that can drift.
findings.rework: Move the table to a free valueStepsKeys(name) beside parseValueStepsList and use it in the snapshot reader too. Reply with flat keys for the chosen list, or a plain okReply (the WebUI polls at 1 Hz). Keep one command for the four lists. Remove T33 (F6).
findings.deliberate_evidence: Commit b0e90ad lays out the design: UI.conf keys, one command, 'the lists and settings in the web state's ui object and in the reply'.

findings.title: Tutorial codes and history narration in handleCommand comments
findings.port_way: Comments carry '// T42:', '// T39:', '// T34:', '// T33:', '// T34 (Q10):' and 'no target: both, as before'.
findings.apertar_way: C1-I14: comments are rare and state a hazard or a reason. Upstream src@upstream-1.6.0 has no ticket ids.
findings.why_it_matters: The codes mean nothing to the original developer. 'as before' refers to a history he never saw.
findings.rework: Delete the codes and keep the sentences. Change 'as before' to 'no target: both'.

findings.title: set_timecode_mode target= sets the UI timecode and the file timecode apart; not run on a Pi
findings.port_way: Optional target=both|ui|files, with both as the default. The preset key cameraTimecodeMode sets the file copy. The legacy timecodeMode key sets both only when the new key is absent.
findings.apertar_way: No precedent. Upstream writes the camera value and UI.conf together (src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:9424-9436@upstream-1.6.0), C1-I18. An unmodified client sends no target and gets the old behaviour (C1-N11).
findings.why_it_matters: UI.conf timecodeMode and camera timecode_mode can now differ, which C1-I18 otherwise rules out. Commit 909aaa5 says: 'Tested: desk (page loads, labels); Pi build pending'.
findings.rework: Keep the shape: an optional field with the old default is the least foreign form. Run it on a Pi before the merge and document the exception to C1-I18 for the original developer.
findings.deliberate_evidence: Commit 909aaa5 explains why the two are set apart and keeps old presets compatible.

findings.title: record_stop also ends a storage pre-roll; manual command named storage_preroll
findings.port_way: While a pre-roll runs, record_stop sets storagePrerollStop_ and replies recording:false, storage_preroll_stopped:true. The manual action is the bare noun storage_preroll.
findings.apertar_way: record_stop already stops whatever runs: first the sound take, then the camera take (src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:10783-10794@upstream-1.6.0). Action names carry a verb: record_start, timelapse_start/timelapse_stop, run_media_speed_test (C1-I04).
findings.why_it_matters: Only the name is foreign. The record_stop branch matches upstream's one-stop-button idea.
findings.rework: Keep the record_stop branch. Rename storage_preroll to storage_preroll_start, which pairs with record_stop the way timelapse_start/timelapse_stop do; run_storage_preroll is the alternative. Update the head gate App:12591, help, Apertar-UI ApertarControlBridge.cpp:621 and WCP.
findings.deliberate_evidence: The comment at App:14833 states the intent, and the head gate lists the command.

findings.title: set_iso_auto gains an enabled field (false = lock at measured gain)
findings.port_way: An optional enabled= field. false switches auto off at the gain measured inside CC.
findings.apertar_way: The auto variants take no fields (src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:9269, 9293, 9308@upstream-1.6.0), C1-I04. A client could send set_iso value=<iso_actual>, but that value may be one poll stale.
findings.why_it_matters: A small protocol extension. With no field the command still means auto on.
findings.rework: Keep it. Reading the gain under CC's mutex is the sound place to do it.
findings.deliberate_evidence: Commit 646a194 weighs set_iso value=N against the lock.

HW-config-text-store.summary:
All 15 findings survive, none dropped and none added. 7 stand as written and 8 are corrected. The corrections:
- F1: four of the error rules really guard upstream's Python configparser NVMe helper (App:3437@upstream). Upstream still saved such files, so the finding stays.
- F6: the partial /home/pi file hides /boot from every reader, not only the IMU. Upstream's IMU did write /boot in that case.
- F9: WCP branches on code in three places, not one.
- F11: dpiCommands, i2cArm and dpiOverlays are dead code.
- F12: no new fix is needed. BootConfigText::filterApplies is already board-aware, so the fix is F11.
- F13: narrowed to the port-frame narration, plus the T39 comments.
- F14: the claimed drift was wrong. The real split is the two refreshBufferRequest policies. Per C1-I17 the shape belongs in a local lambda.
- F15: the proposed sleep rework was backwards. The fix is to drop the sleep.

findings.title: The Config page's text save is refused on new validator errors, and the WebUI has no override
findings.port_way: saveLocked validates the current text and the next text and refuses when newErrors is non-empty unless flags.force is set. POST /api/config never sets force, and the page has no 'save anyway'. Error rules include cases the C++ readers tolerate: duplicate_key (the later line wins), unknown_action, gpio_twice, address_range, header_text. Some rules (junk, key_above, duplicate_section, duplicate_key) guard the Python NVMe helper.
findings.apertar_way: saveHardwareConfigFile saves any text that is non-empty, at most 256 KiB and NUL-free (src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:5323-5385@upstream-1.6.0), even though upstream's own NVMe helper (App:3437-3447@upstream-1.6.0, configparser, catches only OSError) would stop on some of them. HW-N7: be lenient with the operator's file. HW-N3: the raw textarea is the operator's surface.
findings.why_it_matters: The original developer's Config textarea can no longer save files the readers accept. Example: a button on a pin that is already claimed. The reply is 400, nothing is saved, and the browser offers no way round it.
findings.rework: In HardwareConfigStore::saveLocked, the text path (replace) never blocks on validation: write the file, then return the issues. The page already shows issues after a successful save (WCP:18938-18940). Keep the warnings that name the NVMe helper. Keep the newErrors block only for key edits (edit(), easy mode).
findings.deliberate_evidence: design-controls.md:562 and :857; fork-log 'Save blocked on new errors only, force overrides'

findings.title: The browser cannot change [run_script] paths, and the same check blocks Undo and restore
findings.port_way: Any save whose non-empty [run_script] path* keys differ from the current file is refused with 'Script paths are changed over ssh, not here.' The check also runs for Undo (set_controls text=<history version>) and for restore=true.
findings.apertar_way: The WebUI writes the whole file, [run_script] included (src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:7175-7193@upstream-1.6.0). C1-N10: the WebUI is for a trusted LAN. HW-N3 lists the scripts among the file's operator keys.
findings.why_it_matters: An upstream capability is gone. The check also breaks the port's own recovery. Undo is refused after any ssh path edit made since the last Core save. Restore is refused after a default file dropped the paths.
findings.rework: Delete scriptPaths() and the check in saveLocked (the upstream trust model). If the owner keeps decision Q2, exempt Undo and restore and document the rule in the README.
findings.deliberate_evidence: working/controls/decisions.md:10 Q2 '[run_script] paths: ssh only'

findings.title: hwconf is a second, table-driven model of every reader in one 1141-line header, and it has already drifted
findings.port_way: kSections[] holds per-section alias strings, a ValueRule, a default bus and on-defaults. canonicalSection, canonicalKey and canonicalEncoderKey form one shared alias map. Global lines map channel/i2c_bus/bus_number/pcf_bus to bus and addr/pcf_address to address for every section. All of it is inline in one header.
findings.apertar_way: HW-S2: there is no shared parser. HW-I1: aliases are flat key == chains in each reader (src/hardware/Pcf8574Input.cpp:366-371@upstream-1.6.0). pcf_bus/pcf_address exist only in TriggerOutput.cpp:320-323 and RecordingIndicatorOutput.cpp:359-362@upstream-1.6.0. C1-S06: only small header-only files sit next to their owner.
findings.why_it_matters: Every reader's rules exist twice, and they have drifted. Pcf8574Input.cpp:273@cinemate-port takes only bus/channel/i2c_bus, so for [pcf8574] pcf_bus=10 the validator checks bus 10 while the reader uses bus 1. Mpu6050RecordingSession.cpp:762@cinemate-port takes only bus/bus_number, so for [mpu6050] channel=3 the validator checks bus 3 while the reader ignores the key. Every alias needs two edits.
findings.rework: Split the header into HardwareConfigText.hpp (types) and a .cpp registered in CMakeLists (HW-S9). Make canonicalKey per section only: each branch is a flat key == chain with a comment citing the reader line it mirrors. Delete the global lines 169-170. Keep parse, join, applyEdit, diff and validate. The validator stays advisory for text saves (F1).
findings.deliberate_evidence: design-controls.md T37 'a validator built from what each reader really does'; risk R14 named

findings.title: A key edit on a duplicated section writes the copy the readers ignore
findings.port_way: applyEdit Set replaces the key only inside the first copy of the section and stops at the second header. The readers use the later line. checkEdits refuses duplicates, but trusted writes skip checkEdits: IMU calibration and orientation, set_buffer_mode, set_frames_per_folder, set_clip_merge and set_storage_preroll.
findings.apertar_way: writeHardwareConfigValue re-enters the target section at every header of that name and rewrites the key in each copy (src/hardware/Mpu6050RecordingSession.cpp:628-668@upstream-1.6.0).
findings.why_it_matters: Take a file with [mpu6050] twice, the second copy holding gyro_bias_x=12. calibrate_gyro replies ok and writes the new bias into the first copy, but the reader keeps 12. The same happens with [storage] twice and set_buffer_mode. Upstream did not have this bug.
findings.rework: In applyEdit Set, replace the key in every copy of the section, as upstream did. Insert a new line only when no copy has the key.

findings.title: set_controls text= skips the upstream empty, size and NUL checks
findings.port_way: checkHardwareConfigText runs only in POST /api/config. set_controls passes text= straight to store.replace.
findings.apertar_way: The three checks guard the one whole-file write (src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:5325-5343@upstream-1.6.0).
findings.why_it_matters: {"cmd":"set_controls","base":"<current>","text":""} writes an empty file. Every reader then falls back to its defaults.
findings.rework: Move the three checks into HardwareConfigStore::replace so every caller gets them, and delete checkHardwareConfigText.

findings.title: An IMU write on a /boot-only rig creates a partial /home/pi file that hides the /boot file from every reader
findings.port_way: IMU writes always go to configStore().path(). When that file is absent, the store starts from empty text (refreshLocked clears text_).
findings.apertar_way: The IMU writes config.configPath, the file the loader read, which can be the /boot file (src/hardware/Mpu6050RecordingSession.cpp:610, :1148, :1300, loader :854-860@upstream-1.6.0). Every reader takes the first candidate that exists.
findings.why_it_matters: Take a rig where only /boot/firmware/apertar-hardware.conf exists, holding [imu], the buttons and so on. calibrate_gyro creates /home/pi/apertar-hardware.conf with only the bias keys. On the next start every reader (Pcf8574Input.cpp:230-232@cinemate-port, the IMU, GPIO and others) opens that file and loses the /boot sections. The Config page shows the partial file instead of boot_copy.
findings.rework: In saveLocked, when the editable file does not exist and a /boot copy does, start current from the /boot copy. buildHardwareConfigFileJson already applies this rule (App:6187-6200). The write still goes only to the editable path (HW-S10).
findings.deliberate_evidence: comment at Mpu6050RecordingSession.cpp:605-606@cinemate-port; inventory section 7

findings.title: The text merge-review path has no in-tree caller
findings.port_way: A stale text save that changed only values becomes key edits (textToEdits) and comes back with needsReview. Writing it needs confirm_merge. No client in the tree sends confirm_merge: 0 hits in WCP, the UI and tools. POST /api/config turns needsReview into 409 merge_review, which the page treats like stale (WCP:18948).
findings.apertar_way: No precedent. Upstream is last-writer-wins with a .bak.
findings.why_it_matters: About 60 lines plus flags and reply fields serve a client that is not in the tree. The original developer cannot exercise the path.
findings.rework: Delete textToEdits, StoreResult.merged/needsReview and StoreFlags.confirmMerge. A stale text save returns stale. Keep the per-key conflicts() for easy-mode key edits.
findings.deliberate_evidence: commit f5a61b8; design-controls.md T37/T38

findings.title: POST /api/config from a browser without X-Apertar-Revision gets a 409
findings.port_way: A missing header with an Origin present gives 409 with code old_page. A request without Origin keeps last-writer-wins.
findings.apertar_way: There is no header; the request is always saved when sane (src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:7175-7193@upstream-1.6.0).
findings.why_it_matters: Only tabs opened before the update, and other pages posting the file, are hit. Behaviour that depends on Origin is new and surprising.
findings.rework: A missing header means base = the current revision for every client (upstream behaviour). Check the revision only when the header is present.
findings.deliberate_evidence: commit 5395fa4; comment at App:8628-8629

findings.title: StoreResult machine codes and issue arrays in error replies
findings.port_way: Refusals carry a code (locked, being_written, stale, conflict, edits, errors, script_paths, backup, write) plus issues, new_errors and conflicts arrays of objects, all through errorReplyBody. WCP branches on code in three places to append 'stays on the page / in the box'.
findings.apertar_way: C1-I06: replies come only from okReply/errorReply. C1-I07: 'error codes' is a listed violation, and upstream App has 0 "code" members. C1-I10: a fallible helper returns bool and writes std::string *errorMessage (saveHardwareConfigFile, src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:5323@upstream-1.6.0).
findings.why_it_matters: This is a second error protocol next to the operator sentence. The code list and three WCP branches have to stay in step. It overlaps App-1 errorReplyBody.
findings.rework: saveLocked returns bool, writes std::string *errorMessage and sets a bool *stale out-flag. App maps stale to HTTP 409, puts the 'stays on the page' sentence into the message and replies with errorReply. Issues go only in ok replies and in get_controls. Drop the three WCP code branches.

findings.title: A src/hardware header includes capture-pipeline util headers
findings.port_way: The validator includes util/BufferBudget.hpp and util/StoragePreroll.hpp to check the [storage] and [media] values. BufferBudget.hpp pulls cdng/FramePath.hpp (:24) and holds the process-wide safetyStopState() (:231-233).
findings.apertar_way: HW-S8: hardware headers include only hardware and standard headers. A grep for quoted includes in src/hardware/*@upstream-1.6.0 finds hardware headers only.
findings.why_it_matters: The hardware layer gains a dependency on capture-pipeline and CinemaDNG code.
findings.rework: Delete the storage/media branches from validate(). App appends the bufferConfProblem/prerollConfProblem issues after hwconf::validate, next to refreshBufferRequest.

findings.title: A second config.txt parser, mostly dead, duplicates BootConfigText
findings.port_way: hwconf has its own parseConfigTxt, BootFacts and dpiCommands (sudo cp/sed/reboot lines). dpiCommands, BootFacts.i2cArm and BootFacts.dpiOverlays have no caller in src or tools. The only consumer is App:4976, which uses .dpiLines.
findings.apertar_way: No precedent. Upstream has no config.txt parsing in the hardware path.
findings.why_it_matters: Two copies of the firmware-filter rules already differ: BootConfigText is board-aware and hwconf is not (F12). The dead code also names a person (F13).
findings.rework: Delete parseConfigTxt, BootFacts and dpiCommands from HardwareConfigText. hardwareConfigFacts() (App:4976) takes the DPI line numbers from BootConfigText's parse, which already applies filterApplies.

findings.title: parseConfigTxt applies only [all] and [pi5] blocks
findings.port_way: applies = filter == "[all]" || filter == "[pi5]"
findings.apertar_way: HW-N4 / HW-I7: Pi 5 first, Pi 4/3 through auto-detection, and no Pi-5-only path (src/hardware/GpioInput.cpp:247-253@upstream-1.6.0). The port's own BootConfigText::filterApplies (BootConfigText.hpp:102-117@cinemate-port) already handles pi5, cm5, pi4, cm4, pi3 and the others.
findings.why_it_matters: On a CM5, a DPI overlay under [cm5] is missed. On a Pi 4 or CM4, [pi5] lines are applied and [pi4]/[cm4] lines are ignored, so the gpio_dpi errors are wrong. With F1 those false errors block saves. This is the same issue as App-2-F12.
findings.rework: None of its own: F11 replaces this parser with BootConfigText's board-aware one.

findings.title: Owner name, ticket numbers, an out-of-tree client and history narration in code and operator text
findings.port_way: 'The commands the I2C card shows for Patrik to run' (in dead code). 'Gesture suffixes (T44)'. '// T39'. core.py is named four times, and it is in neither tree. 'the text the touch UI used to write' (the upstream UI still writes it). The operator message carries '(unconfirmed on hardware)'.
findings.apertar_way: C1-I14: comments are rare sentences stating a hazard or a reason. There are no ticket numbers (0 TODO, 0 /// in src@upstream-1.6.0).
findings.why_it_matters: These references mean nothing to the original developer and point at tools he does not have.
findings.rework: Drop the name and the ticket numbers. Say 'socket clients' instead of core.py. Reword Store.cpp:62 to 'the template the touch UI writes'. Remove the hedge from the operator string.

findings.title: Three storage blocks repeat the store.edit shape, and the post-write block appears twice more
findings.port_way: set_buffer_mode, set_frames_per_folder/set_clip_merge and set_storage_preroll each build StoreFlags{backup,trusted}, call store.edit, map the refusal, update controlsErrors_/controlsWarnings_, wake the worker when written and always call refreshBufferRequest. set_controls and POST /api/config repeat the post-write block but call refreshBufferRequest only when written.
findings.apertar_way: C1-I17: a shape repeated inside one function becomes a local lambda before its first use (src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:9478@upstream-1.6.0).
findings.why_it_matters: Five copies of the post-write step, with two refresh policies, will drift.
findings.rework: In handleCommand, add one local lambda writeStorageKey(section, key, value) that returns the refusal reply or an empty string. Add one App helper afterHardwareWrite(const StoreResult &) for the post-write block, shared with the web route. Pick one refreshBufferRequest policy.

findings.title: `by` is written raw into hardware-state.conf, and a 100 ms sleep runs under the store mutex
findings.port_way: writeStateLocked writes the client-supplied by unfiltered. The constructor parses key=value lines back with the last line winning, so by="x\nwritten_revision=h0" injects a revision. settledLocked sleeps 100 ms under mutex_ when the file is over 1 s old and Core did not write it, once per outside edit.
findings.apertar_way: No precedent. History names already go through safeName (HardwareConfigStore.cpp:54-60@cinemate-port).
findings.why_it_matters: The two paths filter by differently, and one stall per outside edit lands on whichever writer comes first, the IMU included.
findings.rework: Use safeName(by) in writeStateLocked. Drop the sleep and the second stat: the age check (under 1 s refuses) already covers an editor that is mid-save.

Build-scripts-docs.summary: Skeptic pass: all 13 findings survive, none dropped. 8 stand; 5 corrected: F2 (13 rows, not 14; upstream README APERTAR_ hits = 0), F4 (README recipe split; media-tune helper is called by Core although not installed), F5 (permission error also embeds shell install commands), F6 (env var stripped by env_reset; 'disables sudo' unconfirmed; real only once installed). Verified on both sides at cinemate-port 01f170c and upstream-1.6.0.

findings.title: Media tuning file family (INI + /run override + apertar-tune + tmpfiles) beside upstream's .apertar-tuning
findings.port_way: Four layers per write-path knob (env > /run/apertar-media/media-tune.override.conf > ~/apertar-media-tune.conf > default), own key names (dontneed, writeback, sync_ms, raw_buffers, extra_raw_buffers, workers, queue, kernel_tune), per-medium INI sections, a 487-line Python editor, a tmpfiles entry.
findings.apertar_way: src/prores/ProresEncoder.cpp:771-813@upstream-1.6.0 tuningOverride(name): env wins, else NAME=VALUE from /home/pi/.apertar-tuning, same APERTAR_* names, re-read at clip open, absent in production, written for the same reason (A/B arms without restart). CAM-24, CAM-19.
findings.why_it_matters: The original developer meets a second tuning mechanism with its own dialect and a Python tool, for a job his 40-line function already does.
findings.rework: Move tuningOverride() into src/util/TuningOverride.hpp; read the write-path knobs at take start by their APERTAR_* names; per-medium defaults stay as a C++ table in MediaProfile; echo effective values in the 'ApertarCore recording clip:' line. Delete config/apertar-media-tune.conf, scripts/apertar-tune, src/util/MediaTune.hpp, config/apertar-media.tmpfiles.conf.
findings.rework_risk: Per-medium override sections are lost; owner asked for the file.
findings.deliberate_evidence: Owner asked for the file 2026-11-02 (fork-log.md:142-143, sweep-knobs.md:402); removal is his call.

findings.title: README table of env knobs and A/B instructions
findings.port_way: Section 'Write-path knobs for A/B tests': file/override instructions and a 13-row table of APERTAR_* vars with defaults, file keys and KB references.
findings.apertar_way: README tables stop at launch options (README.md:248-257@upstream-1.6.0); grep -c APERTAR_ README.md@upstream-1.6.0 = 0. STY-14, CAM-24, recipe R8 ('Not in ... README').
findings.why_it_matters: The README is for camera builders; experiment levers read like product features.
findings.rework: Delete the section. Surviving knobs keep the unsignedEnvValue/boolEnvValue form and appear in the take-start log line. Documentation, if wanted, on a KB page.
findings.deliberate_evidence: Commit c57c284: 'The README gets a table of the write-path knobs for A/B tests'.

findings.title: RT scheduling in the start script; LimitRTPRIO=80 under upstream's 'non-real-time' comment
findings.port_way: APERTAR_RT=1 prefixes exec with chrt -f 70 ionice -c2 -n0 taskset -c 1-3; drop-in gains unconditional LimitRTPRIO=80; APERTAR_RT_CAPTURE_PRIORITY puts the completion thread on SCHED_FIFO.
findings.apertar_way: Drop-in = LimitNICE=-5 under '# Permit only a bounded, non-real-time boost for the camera callback thread.' (config/apertar-core-capture-priority.conf@upstream-1.6.0); script ends exec "$CORE_BIN" --socket ... --media ... (scripts/start-apertar-core.sh:21@upstream-1.6.0). PLT-14.
findings.why_it_matters: The drop-in contradicts its own comment. Capture-thread FIFO measured 'no effect' (lessons/hardware-log.md:954); whole-process RT never measured. chrt is probed with /bin/true but taskset is not, so a bad APERTAR_RT_CPUS makes the exec fail and Core does not start (PLT-22).
findings.rework: Restore the upstream start script and drop-in; delete the APERTAR_RT_CAPTURE_PRIORITY block in CC.
findings.deliberate_evidence: c57c284 body: 'keeps it as a test, not a default'; README: 'An A/B instrument, not a recommendation'.

findings.title: Three root helpers as /bin/sh scripts, with sudoers and tmpfiles, inside the Core repo
findings.port_way: POSIX sh helpers (set -u, [ ]) in Core scripts/, sudoers in Core config/; README install recipes for boot-config and trim; media-tune and tmpfiles recipes in the config file headers. Core calls the media-tune helper although it is never installed.
findings.apertar_way: Simple privileged steps are sudo -n from App: sudo -n install -m 644 (App:3157), sudo -n mount (App:3623), sudo -n blockdev --flushbufs (App:3353), sudo -n sh -c 'echo 1 > sysfs' (App:3373) @upstream-1.6.0 (PLT-5). A real root program is Qt-free C++ in the UI repo with sudoers listing every verb (UI/systemd/apertar-standby-usb.sudoers@upstream-1.6.0), called as /usr/bin/timeout 6s /usr/bin/sudo -n /usr/local/libexec/apertar-standby-usb <verb> (App:1544) (PLT-4). No #!/bin/sh file in either upstream tree; Core has only scripts/start-apertar-core.sh. STY-16.
findings.why_it_matters: A third shape for root work, in the repo that has none. The image already relies on broad sudo -n, so the narrow rules add files without adding a boundary.
findings.rework: Trim: in the trim worker call /usr/bin/timeout 20s /usr/bin/sudo -n /usr/sbin/fstrim -v <shellQuote(media root)>; discard and mount checks in App; delete script, sudoers, tools/media_trim_test.sh. Media-tune: delete with kernel_tune and APERTAR_MEDIA_TUNE. Boot config: one route only, either upstream sudo -n install with App doing checks and backup first, or the helper rewritten as UI/src/BootConfigWriter.cpp per recipe R14 steps 5-6.
findings.deliberate_evidence: dda1713: 'Same shape as apertar-media-trim'; 26da30e: 'added but not installed ... Core's sudo -n call fails and logs'.

findings.title: Three write routes for config.txt; raw helper stderr and shell commands in operator errors
findings.port_way: writeBootConfigText tries a direct write (root, or APERTAR_BOOT_CONFIG copy), then the helper on stdin, then sudo -n install twice. A helper refusal returns helper.output (3589-3590), e.g. 'apertar-boot-config: input has no [pi5], [pi4] or [all] section: not the Apertar config.txt'. A sudo refusal returns a message holding two 'sudo install ...' command lines (3604-3607).
findings.apertar_way: One route, sudo -n install; a missing rule becomes 'Changing the fan mode needs sudo permission.' (App:3157-3170@upstream-1.6.0). PLT-5, STY-10.
findings.why_it_matters: Three routes to test for one file write; operator errors break the one-sentence style.
findings.rework: Keep one route (F4). Map helper exit codes 2 and 3 to operator sentences; one-sentence permission error. Drop the APERTAR_BOOT_CONFIG test path.
findings.deliberate_evidence: The comment above writeBootConfigText lists the order on purpose.

findings.title: apertar-media-tune keeps root state in a pi-owned /run dir; sudoers pin the path only
findings.port_way: /run/apertar-media is 0755 pi:pi and holds tune/ (root:root). As root the helper runs cat "$2" > "${STATE_DIR}/${1}", later writes those values to /proc/sys/vm/* and rm -f's them. Sudoers rules allow any arguments.
findings.apertar_way: PLT-4: root-owned /run/apertar-<name>, sudoers listing every verb (UI/systemd/apertar-standby-low-power.sudoers@upstream-1.6.0).
findings.why_it_matters: Probable, not run; real only once helper and tmpfiles are installed. pi owns the parent, so pi can rename or (after a restore) remove tune and plant ln -s /etc/sudoers.d /run/apertar-media/tune; the next sudo -n apertar-media-tune apply nvme0n1 pi-nvme exfat makes root create /etc/sudoers.d/queue_scheduler containing '[mq-deadline] none' (a sudoers parse error; whether sudo then refuses depends on the sudo version, unconfirmed). A pi-owned replacement dir lets pi choose the vm.dirty values restore writes back. APERTAR_MEDIA_RUN_DIR is stripped by sudo's default env_reset (probable; sudo -n env on the image settles it), so the env path is not the attack.
findings.rework: Remove the helper with F4. If kept: root-owned parent dir, no env var, sudoers listing the apply/restore forms.

findings.title: Ticket ids, Cinemate hashes, KB paths and history narration in code, config and README
findings.port_way: '// T50, Q23: ...', T37, T39, T42, T31, 7 x T34, '(Cinemate c8f06c9)', 'T29 measures them', 'the A/B in the kb (working/dng-chain) decides', '64 KiB used to drop the client without a word'; README 'measured 2026-11-04, probable', KB file paths, 'Apertar-UI 7ea9afc (local branch clip-split)'.
findings.apertar_way: STY-9: no ticket numbers or other projects' hashes; 0 hits in both upstream trees. STY-8: no history narration.
findings.why_it_matters: The ids mean nothing to the original developer and the text reads as lab notes.
findings.rework: Delete the ids and references. Keep a present-tense why-line only where it names a hazard (e.g. '// A set_controls text carries the whole hardware file.').

findings.title: ApertarCoreApp.hpp layout: methods among members, split member groups, commented header
findings.port_way: Method declarations among data members (runControlsWorker 179, noteInputSeen 196); media-trim members (324) split from their group by clip-merge members (323); enum class ClipMergeOutcome in the method list (145); 37 '//' comment lines.
findings.apertar_way: CMD-20: owned components first, then state groups split by blank lines, mutex first (AppH:110-124@upstream-1.6.0). Upstream header has 1 '//' line (STY-8).
findings.why_it_matters: The header no longer reads like the upstream one, and lock ownership is hard to see.
findings.rework: Move all new methods into the private method block after joinMediaSpeedTest(). Each worker one contiguous group (mutex first, thread, flag, cv, state). At most one lock-rule comment per group. handleReadOnlyHardwareCommand goes with the rev-App-4 rework.

findings.title: Host tests in tools/ outside CMake, with build lines that disagree and test lines in the operator README
findings.port_way: 15 C++ tests, 3 sh tests, 2 Python tools. Build lines mix g++ and c++, -std=c++17 and c++20, with and without warnings and -I include (buffer_budget_test, storage_buffer_conf_test omit it). MediaTune.hpp:5 names tools/media_tune_test.cpp, which does not exist.
findings.apertar_way: No precedent: upstream Core has no tests and no tools/ dir (PLT-12, section 5). Core is C++20 (PLT-15).
findings.why_it_matters: Outside CMake is the least foreign shape. The inconsistency and the README placement make it look accidental.
findings.rework: Keep, simplify. One header line form 'g++ -std=c++20 -O2 -Wall -Wextra -I src -I include tools/<name>.cpp -o /tmp/<name> && /tmp/<name>'. Take test lines out of the operator README sections; one sentence in 'For Developers'. Fix or drop the dangling media_tune_test reference (goes with F1).

findings.title: Socket request line raised from 64 KiB to 1 MiB for whole-file set_controls
findings.port_way: constexpr size_t kMaxRequestLineBytes = 1024 * 1024, because a set_controls text carries the whole hardware file.
findings.apertar_way: Socket line limited to 64 KiB (ControlServer.cpp:261@upstream-1.6.0). Whole hardware-file text travels over POST /api/config (App:7175@upstream-1.6.0) under WebServer.cpp:23 kMaxRequestSize = 1024 * 1024.
findings.why_it_matters: No break for an unmodified UI (touch UI never sends set_controls: 0 hits in Apertar-UI/src); the raise serves only external socket clients. Memory per stalled client grows 16x.
findings.rework: Follow the HW-config-text-store decision. If set_controls text gives way to /api/config, revert to the 64 KiB literal. Otherwise keep the constant with a one-line why.
findings.deliberate_evidence: Commit 5395fa4 'the socket takes 1 MiB lines' and its comment.

findings.title: Preview temporal denoise off by default
findings.port_way: bool previewTdn = false; Core hands libcamera a _notdn.json copy of the tuning file with tdn stripped.
findings.apertar_way: libcamera loads the selected tuning file unchanged, so tdn runs as the file says (scripts/start-apertar-core.sh:15-18, src/camera/DefaultTuningSelection.hpp@upstream-1.6.0).
findings.why_it_matters: After an update the operator sees a noisier preview without changing anything. The reason was measured once, on one rig and mode.
findings.rework: Owner decision. Either default to true (upstream behaviour) and switch it off on the rig, or keep false and state the reason in the commit and the handoff.
findings.deliberate_evidence: README cites the 2026-11-04 measurement.

findings.title: README growth: install recipes, socket field lists, measurements, misplaced sections
findings.port_way: +90 lines: a Boot Config section, three operator sections under 'Where Are Recordings Saved?' plus the knob table, three sudo install recipes (boot-config, trim, capture-priority drop-in), a 'Socket commands:' list of 14 fields, dated measurements.
findings.apertar_way: STY-14: camera-builder voice; tables stop at launch flags. Helpers get no install recipes: 'depend on the installed panel drivers, helpers and permissions' (UI/README.md:199@upstream-1.6.0). PLT-6, PLT-24.
findings.why_it_matters: The README becomes a lab manual.
findings.rework: One short operator paragraph per feature (Boot Config card, split clips with the import warning, trim on/off). Move install recipes, socket lists, measurements and A/B notes to the handoff or KB. Knob table deleted (F2).
findings.deliberate_evidence: c57c284 and the feature commits add the sections on purpose.

findings.title: Core's liblj92 README.apertar.md says 'in the UI'
findings.port_way: Byte-identical to UI/third_party/liblj92/README.apertar.md@upstream-1.6.0: 'Used to decode lossless JPEG tiles in the UI'.
findings.apertar_way: PLT-17: README.apertar.md names the purpose (UI/third_party/liblj92/README.apertar.md:1-11@upstream-1.6.0).
findings.why_it_matters: In Core the users are src/playback/DngFrameReader.hpp and DngTags.hpp, so the stated purpose is wrong.
findings.rework: Change the sentence to: 'Used by Core playback (src/playback/) to decode lossless JPEG tiles of recorded DNGs.'

CC-2.summary:
Skeptic pass on CC-2: 20 findings checked, 1 dropped, 10 corrected, 9 stand.
- Dropped F4: the Pi 4 failing input cannot happen. Lossless cDNG only runs on Pi 5-class boards (bcm2712) in both upstream and the port (RecordingCapabilities.hpp:26, :71-75, :87).
- F16: the shell-launch part is gone, because upstream App has its own shellQuote and a popen shell runner (App:1482, 1501-1505). Only the RF64 bug is left, now a nit.
- F5 moves from major to minor and should be documented, not made opt-in. The sync was carefully considered and measured, and opt-in would lose the pull-safety feature.
- F11 moves to nit. Upstream CdngEncoder.cpp:52-66 also reads a knob once with its own parser.
- F17 narrowed: ext4 and exFAT already match the upstream defaults. Only vfat, NTFS and Other differ.
- F2: the claim that upstream has the path list once is wrong. Upstream copies hardwareConfigCandidatePaths into 5 files. The real issue is that [storage] reaches the queue by two routes.
- F1: dropped the claim that the parser stops at the first file found, because upstream's Ina219 reader does the same.
- F7: the rework must not take the controller lock. safetyStopState is the same pattern and should be fixed with it.
- F14: the wrong menu path is now confirmed (the card is under Settings > Modes).
- F15: added that Rung already holds CdngLog as an enum.

findings.title: Camera side reads apertar-hardware.conf ([camera] Clear HDR ISO caps)
findings.port_way: struct CameraSection + loadCameraSection() parse [camera] clear_hdr_iso_max_12bit/16bit from the hardware file with an own INI dialect (strips all whitespace); cached in a function-local static; template ships the keys.
findings.apertar_way: S22: camera side never reads apertar-hardware.conf (0 hits in src/camera @upstream-1.6.0). Sensor/format limits are literals in the sanitiser: settings.iso = std::min<uint32_t>(settings.iso, 800u); CC:2483@upstream-1.6.0 (5.14). Bench overrides are env vars (N11, R5).
findings.why_it_matters: Driver facts (gain codes 57/80 of the port's imx585 driver) become operator config, and a hardware-file parser appears inside CameraController; reads as a layer violation.
findings.rework: constexpr uint32_t kClearHdrMaxIso12 = 720, kClearHdrMaxIso16 = 1585 next to kLosslessMaxIso; clearHdrIsoCap returns them. Optional bench override unsignedEnvValue("APERTAR_CLEAR_HDR_ISO_MAX_12", 720, 0, 51200) at use. Delete CameraSection, loadCameraSection, cameraSection, the [camera] template block in App and its README text.
findings.deliberate_evidence: 8175273 describes the [camera] keys as intended.
findings.rework_risk: An operator who edited the keys loses them (none recorded).

findings.title: DngRecordingQueue re-reads [storage] from disk at each take; App already publishes the same value
findings.port_way: loadBufferConf() opens the hardware file and passes it to bufferbudget::parseBufferConf at each take (frames_per_folder here, RAM plan in CC-3). The App already parses the same text from configStore() and publishes framesPerFolderRequest() (App:281-283), which the queue ignores. Candidate list inlined twice in CC.
findings.apertar_way: S22.
