Per-take options that are not camera settings go from App into startRecording as a struct: GyroRecordingOptions (Types.hpp:199, App:10633, CameraController.hpp:78 @upstream-1.6.0; 5.14). Bench knobs env-only (N11, R5). Per-file copies of hardwareConfigCandidatePaths() are upstream style (5 copies @upstream-1.6.0); the problem is the camera side reading the file at all.
findings.why_it_matters: [storage] reaches the recorder by two routes that can disagree; the camera side gains file I/O.
findings.rework: Add StorageRecordingOptions (framesPerFolder, buffer mode and fractions) to Types.hpp. App fills it from configStore() at record_start; startRecording passes it to DngRecordingQueue::startAtFolder. Delete loadBufferConf and both inline path lists. Since d7dd337 calls frames_per_folder an A/B campaign knob, consider dropping the [storage] key and set_frames_per_folder and keeping APERTAR_CDNG_FRAMES_PER_FOLDER only.
findings.deliberate_evidence: d7dd337 and d44b177: read at each take so a Config save applies.

findings.title: Upstream lossless cDNG limits changed (ISO 800->1600, auto ISO kept on IMX585, IMX585 fps 30 -> mode max)
findings.port_way: kLosslessMaxIso = 1600 'on Patrik's request'; isoAuto forced off only for non-IMX585 ('Other sensors are unchecked'); IMX585 fps = mode maximum unless APERTAR_LOSSLESS_FPS_LIMIT.
findings.apertar_way: enforceLosslessCaptureLimits CC:2470-2491@upstream-1.6.0: settings.iso = std::min<uint32_t>(settings.iso, 800u); settings.isoAuto = false; IMX585 maximumFps 30.0.
findings.why_it_matters: Three product-policy defaults of the original developer change silently inside a refactor; auto-ISO part recorded as unverified (fork-log.md:85).
findings.rework: Keep 800 / manual ISO / 30 as defaults in enforceLosslessCaptureLimits. Expose the relaxed values as R5 bench knobs (unsignedEnvValue at use), or move the change into its own commit with the measurements for the original developer to accept.
findings.deliberate_evidence: Commits 2f43ecc, b5b787e, d44b177; fork-log.md:80,85.

findings.title: Sync thread fsyncs clip frames once a second by default (deliberate departure from N10)
findings.port_way: APERTAR_MEDIA_SYNC_MS default 1000 (or media tune file); syncLoop fsyncs DNGs written in the last tick and the clip folder, run via spawnWorker; sync_ms on the clip line.
findings.apertar_way: N10: clip frames are not synced, for throughput. AtomicStillFile.hpp:31-32@upstream-1.6.0: 'Keep this out of the continuous recording path: syncing each video frame would destroy throughput.'
findings.why_it_matters: Reverses an intent upstream wrote in a comment; the original developer will ask about throughput on slower media.
findings.rework: Keep: carefully considered and measured (C0007 3 min clean, C0011 258/281 frames readable after a pull, syncfs variant rejected after 782 drops; fork-log.md:51-53). Document for the original developer as a deliberate departure from N10 with those numbers. Its file-based default goes with F6 (env only).
findings.deliberate_evidence: Commits 4ce382e, 5b68f1f, 7d9dd60; fork-log.md:51-53.
findings.rework_risk: Opt-in default would lose pull safety; not recommended.

findings.title: Media tuning file feeds per-take recorder knobs
findings.port_way: mediaTuneForConfiguredRoot() reads /home/pi/apertar-media-tune.conf and /run/apertar-media/media-tune.override.conf for sync_ms; mediaProfile_.writer (workers, queueFrames) takes file values and changes writer defaults.
findings.apertar_way: N11: internal tuning stays out of files; knobs are undocumented env vars. 5.12 lists 'a config file or config section for recorder tuning' as deliberately absent. Precedent APERTAR_CDNG_QUEUE_FRAMES CC:3329-3330@upstream-1.6.0.
findings.why_it_matters: Second tuning channel (file, override, tmpfiles, root helper) beside the env knobs upstream uses only.
findings.rework: Delete MediaTune.hpp, the override path and tmpfiles/helper wiring. Keep APERTAR_MEDIA_SYNC_MS, APERTAR_CDNG_UNCOMPRESSED_WORKERS, APERTAR_CDNG_QUEUE_FRAMES as the only overrides.
findings.deliberate_evidence: Commits 26da30e, 2edc6d0, ebdcd08.

findings.title: Process-wide flush-abort callback registered by the queue
findings.port_way: startAtFolder registers a global std::function in BufferBudget.hpp, destructor unregisters it; handleCommand calls abortSafetyStopFlush() on record_start before any lock, bypassing CameraController. safetyStopState() is a further process-wide singleton written by the queue, read by App.
findings.apertar_way: App reaches the queue only through CameraController methods. Cross-thread signals are controller-owned objects passed to the queue by pointer: RecordingDropWarning (CameraController.hpp:113, queue ctor CC:3251 @upstream-1.6.0).
findings.why_it_matters: Hidden global path from the command plane into a recorder; not findable by reading CameraController.
findings.rework: CameraController::abortFlush() that takes no controller mutex (the drain holds it, App:286-288) and sets an atomic in a controller-owned object the queue holds by pointer (like dropWarning_); the drain loop checks it. handleCommand calls that method. Delete the registry; move safetyStopState into the same controller-owned object.
findings.deliberate_evidence: c5db8b2 (record during a safety-stop flush).

findings.title: FrameBufferGauge is a hidden function-local singleton
findings.port_way: Five atomics behind frameBufferGauge() static, written by the queue and read by frameBufferStatus() without the controller mutex.
findings.apertar_way: I17: function-local statics only for process-lifetime one-offs (captureSettingsPersister CC:885-889, cachedPiSerial CC:2990-2994 @upstream-1.6.0). Per-take shared state is controller-owned and passed by pointer (RecordingDropWarning). Queue depth in the API absent upstream (5.12, N3).
findings.why_it_matters: Feature is new ground with a sound reason (mutex held during drain), but its shape hides the dependency.
findings.rework: Make FrameBufferGauge a member of CameraController and pass it to DngRecordingQueue(RecordingDropWarning*, FrameBufferGauge*); frameBufferStatus reads the member lock-free.
findings.deliberate_evidence: Comment CC:4170-4172 states the mutex reason.

findings.title: stop() joins copy workers without a bound; copy workers mkdir part folders on the medium
findings.port_way: stop() calls stopCopyWorkers() (plain join) before the bounded writer wait. Copy threads start with copyThreads_.emplace_back, not spawnWorker. enqueue() on the copy thread calls ensurePartFolder() -> ::mkdir on the medium under partMutex_.
findings.apertar_way: no precedent (upstream copies on the completion thread and joins writers unconditionally, CC:3405-3408@upstream-1.6.0)
findings.why_it_matters: Failing input: frames_per_folder=1000, card pulled while a copy worker crosses a part boundary; mkdir blocks until the NVMe timeout and stop(true) hangs in join with controller and command locks held, the hang 0b1632f set out to remove. Probable (depends on the kernel blocking mkdir); off by default (frames_per_folder=0).
findings.rework: Create part folders on a writer thread (covered by the bounded stop), or start copy threads through spawnWorker and stop them inside the bounded wait.
findings.deliberate_evidence: Copy-side mkdir placement is deliberate (d7dd337 'never a writer'); the unbounded join on a dead medium is not addressed.

findings.title: fps ceiling over-built: dead backendMaximumFps, FpsCeiling.hpp wrappers, experiment env switches
findings.port_way: backendMaximumFps returns nullopt for every input (4 call sites); applyBackendCap, resolveSensorMaxFps, losslessImx585Fps are one-line std::min wrappers in their own header with a host test. APERTAR_FPS_LIMIT=table and APERTAR_IMX283_PROBE_FPS reproduce earlier behaviour.
findings.apertar_way: Inline arithmetic: probed ? std::min(table, *probed) : table (CC:2769@main); settings.fps = std::min(settings.fps, maximumFps) CC:2490@upstream-1.6.0. S4 headers hold real pure logic.
findings.why_it_matters: Dead hooks and experiment toggles; a reader traces four layers to find one min().
findings.rework: Delete backendMaximumFps, applyBackendCap, fpsLimitTableOnly, imx283ProbeFpsOnly, FpsCeiling.hpp and tools/fps_ceiling_test.cpp. Write the probe-vs-table choice inline in maximumSupportedFpsForResolution (IMX283 keeps min with the floor table).
findings.deliberate_evidence: The 25 fps cap was removed by 31d5418 and the hook left in place.

findings.title: New env knobs in CC parsed by hand, read once, logged
findings.port_way: losslessFpsOverride (strtod parser, read-once static, stderr), fpsLimitTableOnly (string compare, read-once, stderr), APERTAR_CDNG_FRAMES_PER_FOLDER (own parser, stderr on a bad value).
findings.apertar_way: In CC, I9/R5: unsignedEnvValue/boolEnvValue at use (CC:1027-1061, use CC:3329-3330 @upstream-1.6.0); malformed value falls back silently; effective value on the take-start line. A read-once hand-parsed knob exists upstream in CdngEncoder.cpp:52-66, so this is a style gap inside CC only.
findings.why_it_matters: Each port knob has its own parse and log style inside one file.
findings.rework: Use unsignedEnvValue/boolEnvValue at use, drop the extra log lines, print effective values on the 'recording clip:' line. Mostly disappears with F10.

findings.title: Ticket numbers, names, dates, take ids and KB paths in comments
findings.apertar_way: I19: comments are rare and say why in 1-3 lines; no ticket numbers, author or date (CC:6927-6928@upstream-1.6.0).
findings.why_it_matters: References mean nothing to the original developer; comments read as a history log.
findings.rework: Rewrite each comment as the constraint only, or delete it.

findings.title: Stale comments contradict the code
findings.port_way: 'the 16-bit 25 is backendMaximumFps()' (no such cap); 'only the named back-end cap kept' (none exists); 'exFAT/NTFS get 2' (MediaProfile.hpp:142 gives exFAT 4).
findings.apertar_way: I19: comments state a current constraint.
findings.why_it_matters: The comments mislead the next reader.
findings.rework: Fix them along with F10 and F17.

findings.title: Ladder refusal texts as constexpr constants with a wrong menu path
findings.port_way: constexpr kLadderOwnsMode / kLadderOwnsCompression (7 uses in CC) tell the operator 'Settings > Record > Mode Ladder'; the WebUI card is under Settings > Modes (WCP:4750-4753, data-panel="modes" WCP:5151, title WCP:5166 @cinemate-port; confirmed).
findings.apertar_way: I1/I5: one inline sentence per setErrorLocked(...), e.g. "Resolution changes are blocked while recording." CC:7715@upstream-1.6.0. No message constants, no menu paths.
findings.why_it_matters: Foreign style, and the text sends the operator to the wrong place.
findings.rework: Inline one sentence at each setter without a path, e.g. "Turn off the Mode Ladder to choose the resolution by hand."

findings.title: Ladder compression handled as strings, not enums
findings.port_way: applyRungFormat compares ladder::effectiveCompression(rung) to "lossy_3to1", "lossy_5to1", "none". Rung::compression is a string while Rung::cdngLog is already an enum.
findings.apertar_way: Format sub-options are enums in Types.hpp with toString/fromString at the edge (R3 step 1: CdngCompression, LossyDngRatio).
findings.why_it_matters: Stringly-typed internals in CC. File input is validated (knownCompression, ModeLadder.hpp:29), but a typo in a code literal compiles and falls through to lossless.
findings.rework: ladder::Rung stores RecordingFormat, CdngCompression and LossyDngRatio. Parse the strings once where the ladder is loaded or set.

findings.title: wavSampleRate rejects RF64
findings.port_way: wavSampleRate accepts a 'RIFF' header only.
findings.apertar_way: Upstream's WAV reader accepts RIFF and RF64 (App:5806@upstream-1.6.0); Core writes RF64 above 4 GiB (AudioRecordingSession.cpp:773). (The /bin/sh launch with shellQuote has upstream precedent: App:1482 shellQuote, App:1501-1505 popen; not reported.)
findings.why_it_matters: Failing input: a speed-ramp take whose WAV passes 4 GiB gives sample rate 0, so no stretched WAV is made.
findings.rework: Accept RF64 as well as RIFF in wavSampleRate.

findings.title: Uncompressed cDNG writer count and queue depth follow the filesystem on vfat/NTFS/other
findings.port_way: normalWorkerCount = env, else min(profile workers, format count); uncompressed queue = profile queueFrames when the medium is known. ext4 and exFAT give 4/12 (same as upstream); vfat, NTFS, ntfs-fuse give 2 workers / queue 16 / +2 raw buffers; Other gives 2 workers.
findings.apertar_way: CC:3323-3330@upstream-1.6.0: max(2, min(4, threads)) workers, queue 12, env overrides only.
findings.why_it_matters: An upstream default changes on numbers the commit calls 'Cinemate's numbers, not measured here' (26da30e); exFAT already had to be reverted after drops (C0106).
findings.rework: Keep the upstream defaults and the env knobs; delete the per-filesystem table, or keep it only with Apertar measurements per filesystem.
findings.deliberate_evidence: 26da30e message.

findings.title: static bool warned inside a member function
findings.port_way: Function-local static bool inside DngRecordingQueue::startAtFolder.
findings.apertar_way: I8: one-off warnings use a bool warned..._ member (warnedMissingWhiteBalance_ CC:6858-6861@upstream-1.6.0).
findings.why_it_matters: A small style break.
findings.rework: Use a member flag, or drop the warning.

findings.title: 'CineMate Log' product name in Core log text
findings.port_way: "ApertarCore CineMate Log: ..."
findings.apertar_way: Log lines name Apertar concepts only (e.g. 'ApertarCore recording clip:' CC:3353@upstream-1.6.0).
findings.why_it_matters: A foreign product name appears in the operator journal.
findings.rework: Rename to 'cDNG Log' or 'Log'.

findings.title: Detached isoForMeasuredGain comment; optional round-trip in buildCdngLogTake
findings.port_way: The comment sits above #if/wavSampleRate while the function is at 2928. The plan is copied into locals and plan->params is wrapped in std::optional only to be dereferenced.
findings.apertar_way: no precedent
findings.why_it_matters: Leftovers from edits.
findings.rework: Move the comment and use plan-> directly.

CC-4.summary: Skeptic pass on CC-4. I opened all 12 findings in the code at both refs. None was dropped. 4 stand: F6, F10, F11, F12. 8 are corrected. F1: the shared_lock copies the completion-callback context that upstream also holds (CC:6589@upstream-1.6.0); the ProRes closure has none. F2: the helper isImx585Raw12CropResolution was deleted, so the rework has to restore it. F3: unverified counts removed; the rework now keeps pre-roll at the sensor's maximum fps by passing it through the sanitiser input. F4: the test file and one comment also need changes. F5: about 30 such lines across the file. F7: upstream does start external programs (execvp aplay); the mismatch is the shell string and the package nobody declared. F8: binning cannot come from sensorBinning_. F9: board-aware point weakened, since ProRes is not board-aware either. Skeptic verdicts and the full final findings are appended to the report.

findings.title: DNG copy worker returns requests via set-once setRequestRelease(libcamera::Request*) instead of a per-frame release closure
findings.port_way: After makeRequests the session installs recorder_.setRequestRelease([this](libcamera::Request *r){ shared_lock sessionSettingsMutex_; if(!running_) return; requeueRequest(r); }, buffers-2) and recorder_.setFrameQueued(audio observe). PendingCopy carries a libcamera::Request*; the worker calls back through the stored function.
findings.apertar_way: Per-frame std::function<void()> closures, the recorder never sees a Request: ProRes CameraController.cpp:7419-7425@upstream-1.6.0 [this, request, cachedFd]{ ... requeueRequest(request); }; H.264 :7456-7465 releaseRequest = [this, request]{ requeueRequest(request); }; job field :3937 std::function<void()> release. Audio is observed on the completion thread after enqueue (:7428-7430).
findings.why_it_matters: The original developer solved 'recorder holds the buffer and gives it back' twice, the same way. A third shape (session-wide callbacks typed on libcamera::Request*, a second set-once audio callback, a hold limit set from outside) reads as another author's framework.
findings.rework: DngRecordingQueue::enqueueCopy(PendingCopy, std::function<void()> release); PendingCopy drops request. recordRawFrame builds [this, request]{ if (!running_.load()) return; requeueRequest(request); }. Pass the hold limit to startAtFolder. Delete setRequestRelease, setFrameQueued, releaseRequest_, frameQueued_. Audio: a second per-frame closure on write-queue acceptance, or observe at hand-over as ProRes does. The shared_lock copies the completion-callback context (CC:6589@upstream-1.6.0); keep it only with a one-line reason, the ProRes closure takes none.
findings.deliberate_evidence: 351a3ee moved the copy off the completion thread (6 ms per frame at 30 fps 16-bit Clear HDR); the hand-off shape was not weighed. Desk only.
findings.rework_risk: Release ordering at stop: the closure must still no-op after running_ goes false.

findings.title: Colour IMX585 raw12 crop sizes lost the auto sensor-config fallback
findings.port_way: allowAutoSensorConfigFallback = monochromeSensor_ || Imx294 || Imx577 (IMX585 clause gone, helper isImx585Raw12CropResolution deleted). A new block rejects any colour IMX585 candidate whose raw size, bit depth or ScalerCropMaximum differs from the Imx585Modes.hpp row, for explicit and auto configs alike.
findings.apertar_way: CameraController.cpp:5993-5996@upstream-1.6.0 (same at @main:6325-6328): '|| (sensorFamily_ == SensorFamily::Imx585 && isImx585Raw12CropResolution(sanitized.resolution))'. Crop sizes take the auto config and Core crops in software.
findings.why_it_matters: Probable: on the Apertar baseline imx585 driver (origin/apertar e5b74d3) the crop sizes no longer configure, so Core works only with the port's driver. To settle: on a Pi with that driver, set_resolution 3840x1744 12-bit and read the rejection log.
findings.rework: Restore the clause (restore the helper, or derive 'raw12 crop of a native mode' from Imx585Modes.hpp). Run the exact-mode rejection only when useExplicitSensorConfig is true. Nothing changes with the port driver; the old driver keeps the fallback.
findings.deliberate_evidence: caa0153: 'Colour IMX585 configures explicitly only and refuses a mode the driver adjusted'. Desk only.

findings.title: Storage pre-roll pushes fps past the sanitiser and re-pins FrameDurationLimits on every request
findings.port_way: applyControls sanitises, then 'if (prerollFps > 0.0) sanitized.fps = prerollFps;' ('past the lossless-JPEG and ladder caps'). requeueRequest sets a second FrameDurationLimits {p,p} from prerollPinUs_ on every request (also overriding the phase-lock pin). startStoragePreroll holds mutex_ and waits up to 1 s in waitForFramePeriod.
findings.apertar_way: Limits come only from the sanitise chain and effective values are read back (CC:2707-2744, :8713-8715@upstream-1.6.0). controlsForSettings already pins video to {d, d} (CC:2022-2031@upstream-1.6.0, max = d outside photo mode). The only per-request override after the merge is for bracket shots (CC:6515-6530@upstream-1.6.0).
findings.why_it_matters: A write after the sanitiser plus a duplicate frame-duration pin; the invariant 'settings_ holds what the sanitiser allowed' breaks during a pre-roll.
findings.rework: Carry the pre-roll as an input to the sanitiser (a pre-roll flag on the settings passed to sanitizeSettingsForSensor, which then uses prerollMaximumFps as the ceiling), applied through applySettingsLocked. Suspend the phase lock during a pre-roll so controlsForSettings alone sets {d, d}. Delete prerollFpsOverride_, prerollPinUs_, setPrerollFps, the override in applyControls, the pin in requeueRequest and the reset at :7505. Keep the frame/timestamp measurement. If the owner accepts the sanitised ceiling (maximumFpsForSettings) as the target, the flag is not needed.
findings.deliberate_evidence: Code comment CC:12044-12047 states the bypass; d44b177: 'a 2 s take at the mode's highest fps'.
findings.rework_risk: Target fps is an owner decision: sensor max vs recordable max.

findings.title: Dead back-end fps cap wrapper around maximumSupportedFpsForResolution
findings.port_way: fpsceiling::applyBackendCap(maximumSupportedFpsForResolution(...), backendMaximumFps(...)); backendMaximumFps voids both args and returns nullopt, comment 'Removed (User, 2026-11-03) ... KB working/research-30fps-answer.md'.
findings.apertar_way: Plain call: CameraController.cpp:6589-6592@main 'const double maxFps = maximumSupportedFpsForResolution(sensorFamily_, effectiveSettings.resolution, effectiveSettings.rawBitDepth, effectiveSettings.clearHdr);'. No history in comments.
findings.why_it_matters: Dead indirection and a KB-citing history comment in the configure path the developer reads first.
findings.rework: Restore the plain call at :8634, :3470 and in prerollMaximumFps. Delete backendMaximumFps, fpsceiling::applyBackendCap, its two test lines in tools/fps_ceiling_test.cpp, and the 'backendMaximumFps()' comment at :3378.
findings.deliberate_evidence: The cap was removed on purpose (comment); the wrapper was left behind.

findings.title: Internal vocabulary and history in comments
findings.port_way: Comments carry 'T31', 'Cinemate kept them as live keys', 'the qbc libcamera's IMX585 helper', 'hardware-log 2026-10-26', 'as on Cinemate's libcamera', '(kb working/dng-chain, V/H15)', 'CineMate Log'. About 30 such lines file-wide (grep 'T[0-9][0-9]\b|hardware-log|kb working|KB working|Cinemate's|CineMate's').
findings.apertar_way: Comments are 1-3 lines stating a constraint, no tickets, dates or authors (CameraController.cpp:6927-6928@upstream-1.6.0).
findings.why_it_matters: The original developer has no T-numbers, KB or hardware log; the references point nowhere.
findings.rework: Keep each constraint, drop the reference. For 9063-9068: 'A range, not a single value: a single-value pin makes the IMX585 helper re-choose the line length, which steps the exposure.' Name the feature 'Log', as the cdng_log key does.

findings.title: Frame-rate phase lock: servo fits the Apertar shape; socket telemetry does not
findings.port_way: Header-only PI servo; stepFramePhaseLock per frame on the completion thread pins {d,d+1} after every merge; env gains read once; five socket fields fps_phase_lock_active/err_us/dur_us/pushes/saturated. Off by default.
findings.apertar_way: No precedent (upstream fps is a static pin in controlsForSettings). Pieces match: header-only pure logic (StillBracketing.hpp), per-request override after the merge (CC:6515-6530@upstream-1.6.0), read-once env (CdngEncoder.cpp:51-65). Upstream sends only booleans for frame health (recording_has_dropped_frames, ApertarCoreApp.cpp:7843@upstream-1.6.0).
findings.why_it_matters: The shape is acceptable; four internal fields in get_state are not.
findings.rework: Keep. Expose only fps_phase_lock_active; err/dur/pushes/saturated stay in the existing log lines. Strip comments per F5.
findings.deliberate_evidence: 80ddac1 (crystal drift vs audio clock); f4a1393 ({d,d+1} from an observed HMAX change). Desk only.

findings.title: Speed ramp: frames numbered by count, fps free during a take, shelled rubberband stretch
findings.port_way: With fpsSpeedRamp on: nextFrameIndex(ts, countOnly=true), timecode from frame count, applyControls records ramp events, stop writes fps-ramp.txt and forks a detached 'nice -n 15 rubberband ...' shell string for a stretched WAV (rubberband-cli not declared in README or packaging).
findings.apertar_way: DNG index from the sensor timestamp so a dropped frame leaves a gap (CC:3518-3526@upstream-1.6.0); setFps refused during a take, 'Stop recording before changing FPS so video and audio keep the same timeline.' (CC:7745@upstream-1.6.0). External programs started with an argv via execvp (aplay, AudioRecordingSession.cpp:287@upstream-1.6.0), not a shell string.
findings.why_it_matters: With the flag on, two stated upstream intents change, and Core gains an undeclared runtime dependency started through a shell.
findings.rework: Keep the ramp behind fps_speed_ramp (default off) and state both intent changes in the handoff. Move the stretch (launchAudioStretch, pendingAudioStretch_) out of Core into an offline script that reads fps-ramp.txt; if it must stay, start it with fork/execvp and an argv and declare the package.
findings.deliberate_evidence: faa2958 tested on the Pi (C0030-C0032); ca7b7c2 labels the stretch experimental.

findings.title: IMX585 and IMX283 exact-mode checks duplicate the depth/PISP_COMP1 logic
findings.port_way: Two blocks each call formatToRawView, each carry the 'Pi 5 turns CSI2P into PISP_COMP1, reports 16 bits' exception, each write their own rejection line.
findings.apertar_way: One readout check for three sensors with one condition: CameraController.cpp:6162-6183@upstream-1.6.0 (const bool invalidReadout = sensorFamily_ == SensorFamily::Imx294 ? ... : ...;).
findings.why_it_matters: Two copies of one Pi 5 quirk drift apart; the next sensor adds a third.
findings.rework: One block with a helper rawModeAdjustment(candidateConfig, rawStreamIndex, rawSize, sensorMode.bitDepth) returning the reason string (empty = exact), used by both sensors. The IMX585 ScalerCropMaximum test stays as the only sensor-specific line, with binning from the table row (sensorBinning_ is set later from the same properties, so it cannot serve).

findings.title: Raw buffer count evaluated three times from live media state
findings.port_way: rawCameraBufferCount(clearHdr) reads the media tune and media extra on each call (stream buffers, request count, hold limit). Default 4, 8 in Clear HDR, +2 on exFAT/NTFS; env or media tune up to 16.
findings.apertar_way: Fixed kConfiguredBufferCount = 4 (CC:1023@upstream-1.6.0) read once at :6081; H.264 picks its default by board (:1124-1128). ProRes is not board-aware either (default 12, env to 32).
findings.why_it_matters: Probable: a mount or tune change between the calls gives a different count; a smaller later count leaves buffers without requests and changes the hold limit. Unconfirmed: CMA for 8-10 x ~17 MB 4K 16-bit buffers on Pi 4/CM4; settle with Clear HDR 4K on a Pi 4.
findings.rework: Compute the count once in configureAndStart into rawBufferCount_; makeRequests and the hold limit read it. Decide the Pi 4 default after the CMA check.

findings.title: syncfs at every take stop reverses 'clip frames are not synced'
findings.port_way: After a normal stop recorder_.syncToMedium() calls syncfs on the clip folder and logs the time. A 1/s sync thread also runs during the take (other unit).
findings.apertar_way: src/util/AtomicStillFile.hpp:31-32@upstream-1.6.0 'Keep this out of the continuous recording path: syncing each video frame would destroy throughput.' Clip frames are not synced.
findings.why_it_matters: A stated intent changes. The stop-time sync is defensible (one call, after the frames); the developer must be told.
findings.rework: Keep the stop-time sync; state the intent change in the handoff. Judge the 1/s thread in its own unit.
findings.deliberate_evidence: 4ce382e: C0105 lost after a card pull (30 s dirty expiry). Built, not tested.

findings.title: Two real-time scheduling knobs for one experiment
findings.port_way: APERTAR_RT_CAPTURE_PRIORITY (SCHED_FIFO for the capture thread only) and APERTAR_RT=1 (whole process under chrt/ionice/taskset from the start script), both documented in the README.
findings.apertar_way: Per-thread nice -5 on the callback thread (CC:6589-6600@upstream-1.6.0). Upstream README documents no APERTAR_ variable.
findings.why_it_matters: Leftovers of an A/B test; the thread-only knob follows the Apertar shape, the whole-process one does not.
findings.rework: Keep APERTAR_RT_CAPTURE_PRIORITY; remove APERTAR_RT from the start script and README (other unit). Strip the kb reference from the comment (F5).
findings.deliberate_evidence: README calls APERTAR_RT 'an A/B instrument, not a recommendation'.

findings.title: Session data members declared in the public section
findings.port_way: 'mutable std::mutex activeTuningMutex_; std::string activeTuningFile_;' sit between public accessors (public: runs :7251-8220).
findings.apertar_way: CameraSession data members sit in the private block at the end of the class (from CameraController.cpp:5918@upstream-1.6.0).
findings.why_it_matters: Breaks encapsulation and reading order.
findings.rework: Move both members to the private member block.

CC-6.summary: Skeptic pass on 11 findings. 3 stand (F1, F6, F10). 7 corrected: F2 (ProRes now confirmed, not probable: makeProresIspTuning starts from the TDN-stripped copy, CC:7412). F3 (enterStandby gap added). F4 (UI anchor fixed). F5 (the getter feeds the state key recording_fault, which a rig runner reads; only the event field is dead; now a nit). F8 (no race, because session_ is never replaced; safetyStopState is an I17 static; cut down to the unlocked storagePrerollError; now a nit). F9 (deliberate evidence is commit 64bbbaa). F11 (second caller setCdngLog). 1 dropped: F7, the media trim switch in camera_settings.conf. It contradicts the final App-2-F5, which per C1-R2 moves the command-set storage switches into camera_settings.conf. The trim switch is already there.

findings.title: Clip-name example probes the media root on every settings read and settings event under mutex_
findings.port_way: settings() and emitSettingsEventLocked() call fillClipNameExampleLocked -> nextClipFolderName -> nextClipNumber. That calls std::filesystem::exists for clip 1..9999 until it finds a free name, with mutex_ held. It runs on every setter reply and every state poll (WebUI every 1 s per client, WCP:20954).
findings.apertar_way: The clip folder is looked up once, at take start: CC:5548@upstream-1.6.0 `clipFolder = DngRecordingQueue::reserveClipFolder(mediaRoot, settings);`. settings() does no I/O (CC:8566-8573@upstream-1.6.0).
findings.why_it_matters: With 400 takes on the drive and one WebUI open, that is 401 stat calls per second under mutex_, also during a take. On a hung or yanked USB mount, stat can block. Then checkRecordingFailure, record stop and every setter wait on mutex_.
findings.rework: Remove fillClipNameExampleLocked from settings() and emitSettingsEventLocked(). Compute the example into a cached member in setClipNameTemplate, after take start or stop, and on mount change. Otherwise, let the composer call preview_clip_name (CC:11857-11876), which already computes it on demand.
findings.deliberate_evidence: Commit 014a2bf does not discuss the I/O cost. The host test covers only the pure logic.
findings.rework_risk: The WebUI pill composer must refresh the example from preview_clip_name or the cached field.

findings.title: Preview TDN off by default also strips temporal denoise from recorded H.264 and ProRes
findings.port_way: previewTdn defaults to false. At session start, loadablePath loads a copy of the tuning file without the rpi.denoise tdn blocks, for every record format. There is no format check. The ProRes ISP tuning is derived from that stripped copy (makeProresIspTuning(activePath, ...) at CC:7412). H.264 records the ISP YUV output. Both are confirmed.
findings.apertar_way: Upstream loads the selected or default tuning file unchanged (CC:1113-1120@upstream-1.6.0). N8: no silent downgrade of what is recorded. N13: monitoring changes stay out of the recording.
findings.why_it_matters: After the update, every H.264 and ProRes take is recorded without the temporal denoise the tuning file asks for, and the operator is not told. The setting is named 'Preview', so the operator does not expect it to change the recording.
findings.rework: In loadablePath, strip TDN only when !isProcessedVideoFormat(settings.recordingFormat) (CC:280). Keep the full file for H.264 and ProRes, also as the base of makeProresIspTuning. Alternatively, default previewTdn = true. Both keep the RAW speed gain.
findings.deliberate_evidence: Commit e625c68: 'The recorded DNGs are raw and do not change.' Processed formats are not mentioned. Tested: desk only.
findings.rework_risk: A format switch between raw and processed must restart the pipeline. setRecordingFormat already reconfigures across that boundary.

findings.title: Storage pre-roll is a hidden second take kind; N17 exclusions split between CC and App; setTuningFile and enterStandby ungated in CC
findings.port_way: startStoragePreroll starts a raw take while recording_ stays false and state_ stays Ready. It changes settings_ with commit=false, keeps a copy in prerollSaved_, and waits up to 1 s in waitForFramePeriod with mutex_ held. The exclusions are split: CC checks prerollTake_ in startRecording, applySettingsLocked and setClipNameTemplate; App checks a list of 9 command names. setTuningFile reconfigures through session_->reconfigure (CC:11545) with no prerollTake_ check, and set_tuning_file is not in App's list. enterStandby has no pre-roll check in CC.
findings.apertar_way: N17: each capture entry in CC refuses the others with a sentence (CC:8224, 8244, 8329, 7680, 8048, 8608@upstream-1.6.0). The media test is App's runMediaSpeedTest, which runs fio on the mount and does not use the camera (App:9008-9012@upstream-1.6.0).
findings.why_it_matters: set_tuning_file during the 2 s pre-roll reconfigures the session under a running pre-roll take. finishStoragePreroll then stops a recorder that is already torn down and restores the settings onto the new pipeline. Any enterStandby caller that bypasses handleCommand stops the session under the pre-roll. The original developer looks for the exclusion in CC and does not find it complete.
findings.rework: Together with CC-4-F3 and App-4-F2: keep one state in CC that every entry checks. Either run the pre-roll as a recording_-like take, so the existing refusals cover it, or add the prerollTake_ refusal to enterStandby, capturePhoto, startTimelapse and setTuningFile and delete App's command list. The refusal text 'Storage pre-roll is running. One moment.' is already used at CC:11993. Remove the 1 s wait under mutex_ once the fps override is gone.
findings.deliberate_evidence: The design is documented in the comment above startStoragePreroll and in fork-log:138. The setTuningFile and enterStandby gaps are not mentioned anywhere.
findings.rework_risk: The pre-roll must stay invisible to the UIs (no REC, no tally).

findings.title: Early safety-stop recording event carries a stale lastError_
findings.port_way: When the buffer safety stop is active, emitRecordingEventLocked() runs before lastError_ is set from the session. A setter refused during the take leaves its sentence in lastError_ (setErrorLocked, CC:12851).
findings.apertar_way: stopRecording assigns lastError_ = session_->recordingError() before the event (CC:8510-8514@upstream-1.6.0).
findings.why_it_matters: During a take, a resolution change is refused, and then the safety stop fires. The early event carries that unrelated sentence, and the bridge emits recordingFailed with it (CB:1357-1362).
findings.rework: In the announcedEarly branch, clear lastError_ and recordingFaultName_ before emitRecordingEventLocked().

findings.title: `fault` field of the recording event has no consumer
findings.port_way: The recording event gains "fault":"<name>". A grep of App, WCP, Apertar-UI src and qml finds no reader. The getter recordingFaultName() is used: App publishes it as state recording_fault (App:9562, App:12943), which commit 438a342 names and the long-takes rig runner reads.
findings.apertar_way: The upstream recording event carries only active, recording_has_dropped_frames and error (CC:8786-8796@upstream-1.6.0).
findings.why_it_matters: An unused event field next to a state key that already carries the same value.
findings.rework: Delete the fault field from emitRecordingEventLocked. Keep recordingFaultName_, the getter and the state key recording_fault.
findings.deliberate_evidence: Commit 438a342 lists the state key recording_fault but not the event field.

findings.title: Ticket and project vocabulary, essay comment, duplicated comment
findings.port_way: '// T34: Ramp-ready changes the rung with Speed Ramp' repeats the comment on the line above. A 12-line block starting "CineMate's storage warm-up" precedes startStoragePreroll.
findings.apertar_way: I19: comments are one to three lines that say why, with no ticket numbers (CC:6927-6928, CC:8248-8250@upstream-1.6.0).
findings.why_it_matters: The original developer reads internal tutorial numbers and another project's name. CC has 22 T<nn> tags in total; fold this into the file-wide sweep.
findings.rework: Delete the T34 comment. Shorten the block to one line: 'Pre-roll take: not a take for the UIs; recording_ stays false.'

findings.title: Unlocked public storagePrerollError and the atomic CC prerollTake_ it needs
findings.port_way: storagePrerollError() is public and reads prerollTake_ and session_->recordingError() without mutex_. It is the only reason CC's prerollTake_ is std::atomic; every other use in CC is under the lock. session_ is never replaced (CC:10495), so there is no race. safetyStopState() is a function-local static (I17), and the try_lock in frameBufferStatus is deliberate (CC:12522-12524).
findings.apertar_way: I24: every public CameraController method locks mutex_ first. recordingError() does (CC:12646-12650@cinemate-port, same at upstream).
findings.why_it_matters: It adds another concurrency style to the class for a 1 Hz poll that does not need it.
findings.rework: storagePrerollError() takes mutex_ like recordingError(). prerollTake_ becomes a plain bool under mutex_; drop the .load() at CC:12877.
findings.deliberate_evidence: The comment 'no controller lock, safe while the take runs' at CC:12130 states the choice but no reason.

findings.title: recording event carries a dropped-frames count
findings.port_way: Adds "recording_dropped_frames":<n>. The port UI reads it (CB:2654@cinemate-port).
findings.apertar_way: N3: one warning per clip, and counts go to the journal (RecordingDropWarning.hpp:9, CC:3416-3423@upstream-1.6.0).
findings.why_it_matters: A considered change of an upstream product rule. It is a flat scalar, so an unmodified UI ignores it.
findings.rework: Keep it and document it for the original developer as a deliberate change to N3.
findings.deliberate_evidence: Commit 64bbbaa: 'the user wants the number'; fork-log:139.

findings.title: clipNameSensorLocked duplicates sensorName
findings.port_way: A second copy of sensorName's body that returns 'Simulated' instead of 'Simulated Sensor'.
findings.apertar_way: sensorName() (CC:8576@upstream-1.6.0) is the single place for this.
findings.why_it_matters: Two copies drift apart.
findings.rework: Add a sensorNameLocked() helper used by both. The clip-name code maps the simulated name if it must differ.

findings.title: emitLogAppliedIfChangedLocked + lastEmittedLogApplied_ for one runtime field
findings.port_way: Tracks the last emitted cdng_log_applied. If it changed, sends an extra settings event on the reconfigure-failure path and after setCdngLog.
findings.apertar_way: A failed reconfigure that ends in Error sends no settings event (CC:8692-8710@upstream-1.6.0). S21: runtime fields ride on the next ordinary settings event.
findings.why_it_matters: Extra state and a helper for one field.
findings.rework: Delete lastEmittedLogApplied_ and the helper. If the Error path must inform the UIs, call emitSettingsEventLocked() there once. On success, setCdngLog already gets its event from applySettingsLocked.
findings.deliberate_evidence: Commit d44b177. The comment at CC:12873-12874 names the event-driven UIs as the reason.

Encoders-audio.summary:
Skeptic pass on Encoders-audio: 13 of 14 findings survive. 7 stand as written (F1, F3, F5, F10, F11, F12, F13). 6 are corrected: F2, F4, F6, F8, F9, F14. F7 is dropped. Why each changed:
- F2: drop-frames README:301 is plan row 2, and README:310 says that row was dropped. So the KB does not recommend sync_ms 0. The real dependency is rev-CC-2 F5.
- F4: upstream does name QRAW and CinePi in a few places. It never uses another project's brand as a feature name or in a log line.
- F6: fork-log:138 is d44b177, not this feature. The evidence is fork-log:164. The src/camera placement is backed by App including camera/ExposureMetering.hpp upstream.
- F8: downgraded to nit. It is upstream's method and window with a better estimator.
- F9: the effect is restated. The WAV length follows the video duration. Without resampling, the data chunk is shorter than the header declares; with resampling, the missing tail is silence.
- F14: the scope is restated to the unit's own tests.
- F7 dropped: the encoder lives per worker per take, and the shared_ptr outlives it. Borrowed spans into an encoder are already upstream's own Metadata pattern.
No new findings. The Skeptic verdict table and the Final findings are appended to the report.

findings.title: DONTNEED policy read from a tuning file inside the cDNG encoder
findings.port_way: dngPageCacheDrop(): env APERTAR_DNG_DONTNEED, else mediaTuneForConfiguredRoot() (reads /home/pi/apertar-media-tune.conf and the /run override), else Sync; bad env value logged to cerr. Encoder includes util/MediaProfile.hpp whose loader prints 'ApertarCore media tune: ...' once
findings.apertar_way: Encoder knobs are env-only function-local statics with silent fallback: src/cdng/CdngEncoder.cpp:51-66@upstream-1.6.0 configuredLosslessTileRows, :68-77 detailedLosslessProfilingEnabled; src/lossydng/LossyDngEncoder.cpp:96-108@upstream-1.6.0 configuredWriterByteCap. No encoder reads a file (CAM-I9, CAM-N11, PB-I1)
findings.why_it_matters: A second config layer reached from a file-format class; the original developer would not expect an encoder to parse a tuning file. Same tune file judged rework in rev-CC-2 F6
findings.rework: Make dngPageCacheDrop() env-only with the configuredLosslessTileRows body (silent fallback); delete the mediaTuneForConfiguredRoot branch and the util/MediaProfile.hpp and <iostream> includes in CdngEncoder.cpp; drop the redundant '#include cdng/CdngEncoder.hpp // dngPageCacheDrop' in LossyDngEncoder.cpp (LossyDngEncoder.hpp:3 already includes it)
findings.deliberate_evidence: commit 2edc6d0 (tune file); drop-frames README:184 /run drop-in

findings.title: Writer-side DONTNEED default changed for cDNG and dropped for Lossy DNG
findings.port_way: fadvise(DONTNEED) in the writer only when mode is Writer; default Sync drops pages on the port's sync thread after fsync, only while APERTAR_MEDIA_SYNC_MS>0 (one warning otherwise). Lossy branch never calls noteWrittenFile, so by default Lossy pages are never dropped ('sync behaves as off', commit 766aba8)
findings.apertar_way: Unconditional '::posix_fadvise(fd, 0, 0, POSIX_FADV_DONTNEED);' after every cDNG (src/cdng/CdngEncoder.cpp:1777@upstream-1.6.0) and every Lossy DNG (src/lossydng/LossyDngEncoder.cpp:82@upstream-1.6.0); clip frames are not synced during a take (CAM-N10)
findings.why_it_matters: The cDNG default depends on a port-only sync thread that rev-CC-2 F5 proposes to make opt-in (APERTAR_MEDIA_SYNC_MS default 0); with it off, Sync means never drop. Lossy behaviour changed from upstream with no measurement (measurements are cDNG Clear HDR only). Note: the KB's own 'sync_ms default 0' plan row was dropped (drop-frames README:310)
findings.rework: Keep the enum, decide at take start: Sync without a running sync thread acts as Writer (pass a bool into the writer, not a global). Lossy keeps upstream's unconditional drop (treat Sync as Writer) unless a Lossy measurement says otherwise. If Sync stays the cDNG default, document the Clear HDR numbers in the handoff
findings.deliberate_evidence: commits 0ed07ea, adac040 (2x3 min 4K Clear HDR 16-bit 25 fps: 0 lost vs 34-153 with writer), 766aba8; drop-frames README:163-189

findings.title: Comments narrate history, dates, clip ids, tutorial numbers and Cinemate hashes
findings.port_way: 'as before 2026-11-01', 'See the kb, working/dng-chain', 'T31', 'C0011, 2026-10-26', 'Cinemate ffb61fd', 'Cinemate 5021ba3', 'the old path', 'also in apertar-kb'
findings.apertar_way: Rare one-to-three-line present-tense why notes; no ticket numbers, dates or other projects' hashes (C8-S8, C8-S9, CAM-I19; e.g. src/ipc/ControlServer.cpp:25@upstream-1.6.0)

findings.title: 'CineMate Log' product name in Core code and log lines
findings.port_way: describe() returns 'CineMate Log 16->12 ...' and is logged (CC:4041); comments say 'Same curve as cinepi-raw ... share one look'; 16 mentions in src. The user-visible label is already just 'Log' (WebControlPage.cpp:9783)
findings.apertar_way: Upstream names other projects only incidentally (QRAW env fallback LossyDngEncoder.cpp:327, QRAW comparison LossyJpeg12.cpp:505, CinePi UI.conf path ApertarCoreApp.cpp:344-347@upstream-1.6.0); never another project's brand as a feature name or in log lines. Credits in README.md:307-310@upstream-1.6.0
findings.why_it_matters: Brands another project inside Apertar code and logs, while the UI calls the feature 'Log'
findings.rework: Call it 'Log' in code and log lines (namespace cdnglog stays); one README credit line; keep at most one neutral compatibility note ('the curve matches cinepi-raw's log_lut')

findings.title: Audio writer queue unbounded, heap block per read
findings.port_way: enqueueWrite allocates a std::vector<char> per read block (and one for a whole padded gap), pushes without limit; only a one-time log above 16 MB
findings.apertar_way: The encoders' background writer is bounded and recycles buffers: configuredWriterByteCap (APERTAR_LOSSYDNG_WRITER_BYTES) and the take()/give() pool in src/lossydng/LossyDngEncoder.cpp:96-150@upstream-1.6.0; CAM-N2 queues are bounded
findings.why_it_matters: Foreign next to the bounded Lossy writer; a long stall grows RAM without limit (slowly, 0.2-0.4 MB/s)
findings.rework: Cap queuedWriteBytes_ with APERTAR_AUDIO_WRITER_BYTES read like configuredWriterByteCap; on overflow set failure_ 'Audio capture write stalled.' and stop queueing; optionally reuse a small free list of blocks
findings.deliberate_evidence: Thread itself deliberate (commit 60ce8e9; cinemate-lessons section 3); no cap discussed

findings.title: Clip name template: over-built token set, placed in src/util
findings.port_way: 19 tokens + {text:}; {cam} always 'cam0', {model} always from constant CdngEncoder::Metadata{}.model, {date_} equals {yy}_{mm}_{dd}; header in src/util used by App and CC; default template reproduces upstream names; single allocator kept
findings.apertar_way: Name built inline in the one allocator, src/camera/CameraController.cpp:3646-3673@upstream-1.6.0. Pure logic headers sit in the area that owns them even when App uses them too: src/camera/ExposureMetering.hpp included by ApertarCoreApp.cpp:4@upstream-1.6.0; src/util holds latches, the settings writer and the atomic still file (CAM-S4, CAM-S6)
findings.why_it_matters: Constant tokens are generality nobody can use; util/ placement differs from upstream's layout
findings.rework: Keep the feature and header-only shape; drop {cam}, {model}, {date_}; move to src/camera/ClipName.hpp; drop the apertar-kb reference
findings.deliberate_evidence: commit 014a2bf; fork-log:164 (not :138, which is d44b177)

findings.title: After a writer failure the WAV is built from queued bytes that were never written (probable)
findings.port_way: capturedBytes_ grows at enqueue; writer discards blocks once writeFailed_; stop(!mediumGone) finalizes on ENOSPC; availableFrames comes from capturedBytes_
findings.apertar_way: capturedBytes_ grew only after a successful rawStream_.write in readerLoop (src/audio/AudioRecordingSession.cpp:472-474@upstream-1.6.0)
findings.why_it_matters: WAV length follows the video (desiredFrames) but copyFrames is over-counted. Without resample the copy loop stops at EOF and the trailing pad assumes copyFrames were written, so the data chunk is shorter than the header declares (malformed WAV); with resample the missing tail decodes as silence. Code path confirmed, effect probable
findings.rework: Count writtenBytes_ in writerLoop and use it in finalizeWav, or skip finalisation when writeFailed_

findings.title: Drift fit still resamples anywhere in 20..2000 ppm
findings.port_way: Least-squares slope over per-block stamps (pads counted), >=100 points, applied in the same 20..2000 ppm window; endpoint figure only logged
findings.apertar_way: Endpoint ratio availableFrames*1e6/capturedDurationUs with the same window, src/audio/AudioRecordingSession.cpp:523-531@upstream-1.6.0
findings.why_it_matters: Same method and window as upstream with a better estimator; silent sample loss can still bend the slope (cinemate-lessons section 3 item 3). A correctness question for the bugs milestone, not a design mismatch
findings.rework: Keep; state in the handoff that it is upstream's method with a fitted rate; consider narrowing the window (e.g. 20..300 ppm) in the bugs milestone
findings.deliberate_evidence: commit ebdcd08; fork-log:55

findings.title: ALSA hw params set by hand; ring env knob left after the reverted 1 s experiment
findings.port_way: Explicit hw params, ring 100 ms / period 10 ms as default args for every caller (idle meter too); APERTAR_AUDIO_BUFFER_MS 100..4000
findings.apertar_way: snd_pcm_set_params(..., 0, 100000) (period about 25 ms) at src/audio/TimestampedAudioCapture.cpp:189-190@upstream-1.6.0
findings.why_it_matters: Period changes 25 -> 10 ms on all paths; otherwise sound and in the dlopen/env-knob idiom
findings.rework: Keep; trim narration (F3); mention the period change in the handoff
findings.deliberate_evidence: commits 60ce8e9, 0358fcf

findings.title: Dropped-frame running total added to RecordingDropWarning
findings.port_way: droppedFrames(), markDropped(n), setMuted; latch and one-shot changed_ kept; count polled into state
findings.apertar_way: src/util/RecordingDropWarning.hpp:9@upstream-1.6.0 'notify once, not once per frame'; README 'reported rather than hidden'; CAM-N3

findings.title: Host tests in tools/ plus a Python golden-value generator
findings.port_way: The unit's host tests are built by hand with g++, not in CMake; Python re-implementation of LogCurve.hpp prints golden values to paste into the test; the .sh is #!/bin/sh with [ ]

Media-buffer-split.summary: Skeptic pass on the Media-buffer-split unit: all 14 findings survive, none dropped. 5 stand as written (F1, F2, F4, F5, F14). F6 stands with new evidence: the pre-roll default contradicts the KB's own plan (drop-frames/README.md:341 says "default off at first"). 8 are corrected: F3 rework must re-home the pre-roll and dropped-count events. F7: the merge wait is at most 1 s and the 5000 ms argument is a worker hold-off. F8: most of the README env table belongs to other units. F9, F10: line numbers; the frame-number rule belongs in FramePath.hpp. F11: the c++17/c++20 mismatch is between the test heads; severity lowered to nit. F12: lean keep, because /api/state is the full state build. F13: upstream namespace naming is itself mixed. The four .cpp host tests compile and pass here with c++20. The main blockers are still F1 (hardware file read by the camera) and F2/F3 (global statics and polling threads instead of the RecordingDropWarning latch plus 1 Hz wait()). F4/F5 are the trim helper and its kill bug, and F6 the stock-behaviour defaults.

findings.title: Recording/storage settings kept in apertar-hardware.conf and read by CameraController
findings.port_way: These are hardware-file keys: [storage] buffer, buffer_ram_fraction, buffer_ram_floor_mb, buffer_ram_max_fraction, buffer_stop_percent, frames_per_folder, clip_merge, and [media] preroll, preroll_seconds. Two hand-written parsers read them. CameraController::loadBufferConf opens the hardware file at every take start, in two places (CC:4297 and CC:5505). Commands write the keys through hardware::configStore().edit. In the same unit, media_trim is a CaptureSettings field in camera_settings.conf.
findings.apertar_way: The camera never reads apertar-hardware.conf (S22): grep in src/camera/CameraController.cpp@upstream-1.6.0 gives 0 hits. Camera settings persist in camera_settings.conf (S20). Bench knobs are env vars read where they are used: CameraController.cpp:3328-3329@upstream-1.6.0 unsignedEnvValue("APERTAR_CDNG_QUEUE_FRAMES", ...). Per-take inputs travel as option structs built by App (Types.hpp:184-201@upstream-1.6.0). Audio options come from UI settings (ApertarCoreApp.cpp:2754@upstream-1.6.0).
findings.why_it_matters: It breaks the strict split between the hardware file, camera_settings.conf and env knobs. The camera gains a reader of the hardware file, and operator switches gain a second persistence route. media_trim and clip_merge, switches of the same kind, end up in different stores. The port also has a second CC reader of the hardware file (loadCameraSection, CC:2933-2950, another unit).
findings.rework: 1. buffer mode and frames_per_folder become CaptureSettings fields: an enum with toString, a loader branch, the three field lists and the global carry-over at CC:7945-7951@upstream. Add CC setters through applySettingsLocked; the commands reply settingsBody. 2. clip_merge and automatic preroll take the media_trim route. 3. The ram fraction, floor, max fraction, stop percent and preroll_seconds become env-only, read at the point of use, and leave the README. 4. Delete loadBufferConf, BufferConf, parseBufferConf, bufferConfProblem, PrerollConf, parsePrerollConf, prerollConfProblem and refreshBufferRequest, plus the [storage]/[media] validator rules, the base/by revision handling and the template lines. 5. Keep the state names buffer_setting, frames_per_folder, clip_merge_enabled and storage_preroll_auto.
findings.rework_risk: The Config pane loses the validated RAM-fraction editing; the operator switches move to the settings UI.
findings.deliberate_evidence: KB working/drop-frames/README.md:73 states where the keys live and does not weigh camera_settings.conf against the hardware file.

findings.title: Cross-thread state through free-function statics and a global std::function hook
findings.port_way: These are process-wide mutable statics: safetyStopState(), flushAbortMutex()/flushAbortFunction(), safetyStopHook(), bufferSettingStorage()/bufferSettingMutex(), framesPerFolderRequest(), clipMergeRequest() and prerollState(). CC registers flushAbortFunction() = [this]{ return abortSafetyFlush(); }, and App assigns the global hook in its constructor body.
findings.apertar_way: A clip-scoped latch with a callback injected through the constructor: src/util/RecordingDropWarning.hpp:10-27@upstream-1.6.0. It is a controller member (CameraController.hpp:113@upstream-1.6.0) and is passed to the queue (CameraController.cpp:3251@upstream-1.6.0 explicit DngRecordingQueue(RecordingDropWarning *warning = nullptr)). RecordingFailure is a recorder member (CameraController.cpp:3901@upstream-1.6.0). The upstream function-local statics (Mpu6050RecordingSession.cpp:80, :1228@upstream-1.6.0) are private to one function and never shared.
findings.why_it_matters: Ownership is hidden: a reader of CameraController cannot see who writes what. The controller calls into App through a global instead of a callback.
findings.rework: Add src/util/RecordingSafetyStop.hpp shaped like RecordingDropWarning, with atomics active, stopPercent, flushDiscarded and a changed callback. Make it a CC member, passed to the DngRecordingQueue constructor. Add CameraController::bufferStatus() and abortSafetyStopFlush(), which take only the queue mutex; comment why. Pre-roll active/fps/last become App atomic members. framesPerFolderRequest, clipMergeRequest and bufferSettingSnapshot go with F1. Delete the statics.
findings.deliberate_evidence: The comments name lock-freedom as the reason (BufferBudget.hpp:221, :254). A latch member is equally lock-free, and no comparison with RecordingDropWarning is recorded.

findings.title: Buffer events and safety-stop threads poll instead of the 1 Hz wait() supervision
findings.port_way: runBufferEvents loops every 250 ms or 1 s and emits buffer events, including the pre-roll active/fps/last and dropped-count changes. runBufferSafetyStop waits on a cv with a 100 ms backstop, then dispatches record_stop. That is two extra threads with about 10 members.
findings.apertar_way: Periodic supervision is the 1 Hz wait() loop: ApertarCoreApp.cpp:7021-7053@upstream-1.6.0 checks camera_.checkRecordingFailure() and dispatches enter_standby via handleCommand. Events are emitted at their source, for example the audio_level callback at ApertarCoreApp.cpp:8380-8384@upstream-1.6.0.
findings.why_it_matters: Two more threads with their own synchronisation (one is a backstop for a lost wake-up) for checks that fit next to checkRecordingFailure.
findings.rework: Check the safety latch in wait() and at handleCommand entry (next to App:12584 checkRecordingFailure), and dispatch record_stop there. Publish the buffer event from the latch's changed callback for flag flips and from wait() for the level. Emit the pre-roll changes from the pre-roll thread and the dropped count from the drop latch callback. Delete runBufferEvents, runBufferSafetyStop and their members. If the bar needs 4 Hz, see F12.
findings.rework_risk: A 1 s reaction instead of 100 ms. At 90 % of a GiB-sized budget that is still seconds of headroom; say so in the commit and test with a low stop percent.
findings.deliberate_evidence: KB drop-frames/README.md:74 describes the thread and weighs no alternative.

findings.title: Root fstrim helper as shell script in Core with path argument and path-only sudoers
findings.port_way: A POSIX sh root helper validates a mount-point argument and runs timeout 20 /usr/sbin/fstrim -v. The sudoers line pi ALL=(root) NOPASSWD: /usr/local/libexec/apertar-media-trim allows any argument. Core runs execl("/usr/bin/sudo","sudo","-n",helper,mountPoint). This is one of 4 port helper scripts in scripts/.
findings.apertar_way: Simple privileged tools are called directly with sudo -n and shellQuote: ApertarCoreApp.cpp:3609@upstream-1.6.0 runShellCommand("sudo -n mkdir -p " + shellQuote(mountPath), ...), and likewise mount, mkfs and blockdev --flushbufs. Real helpers are C++ in UI/src with literal verbs only: ApertarCoreApp.cpp:1543-1544@upstream-1.6.0 "Fixed executable and arguments only; never accept paths from WebUI/config." Core ships no helper scripts: git ls-files scripts config@upstream-1.6.0 gives 2 files.
findings.why_it_matters: It adds another way to get root: a shell script in Core that takes a data argument. The sudoers grant is wider than upstream's literal-verb rules, and the README gains a manual install of two files for one fstrim call.
findings.rework: Delete scripts/apertar-media-trim, config/apertar-media-trim.sudoers, tools/media_trim_test.sh and the README install block. In the trim worker, fork/exec /usr/bin/timeout 20s /usr/bin/sudo -n /usr/sbin/fstrim -v <mediaRoot> and keep the pid of timeout (owned by pi) for the kill. Check discard support in Core without privilege (/sys/block/<disk>/queue/discard_max_bytes). Map a missing sudo rule to "Trim needs sudo permission."
findings.deliberate_evidence: Comment App:11435 "(sudo -n, like apertar-media-tune)" copies the port's own media-tune helper, not upstream.

findings.title: Ending a running trim signals sudo/sh, fstrim keeps running into the take
findings.port_way: waitForMediaTrim sends SIGTERM and then SIGKILL to the sudo pid. sudo relays SIGTERM to sh only. The foreground child timeout 20 /usr/sbin/fstrim is not exec'd and runs in its own process group (GNU timeout calls setpgid), so it gets no signal. SIGKILL is never relayed.
findings.apertar_way: No precedent. Upstream wraps sudo in /usr/bin/timeout (ApertarCoreApp.cpp:1544@upstream-1.6.0), so the process it would signal is timeout, which forwards the signal.
findings.why_it_matters: Failing input: a trim that runs longer than 2 s (a mount trim on a slow card), then record_start. Core logs "ended a trim that ran longer than 2 s" and starts the take while fstrim holds the filesystem for up to 20 s, the stall the wait exists to prevent. Probable, not run here. To settle it on the Pi: kill -TERM the sudo pid during a trim, then pgrep -a fstrim.
findings.rework: Fixed by the F4 rework (signal the timeout process). Minimum stop-gap: exec timeout 20 /usr/sbin/fstrim -v "$MNT" in the script.

findings.title: Drive trim and automatic storage pre-roll on by default change stock behaviour
findings.port_way: media_trim defaults to true: it trims after any delete of 1 GiB or more, at every mount and after a format, so deleted takes become unrecoverable (KB drop-frames/README.md:69 "no undelete"). [media] preroll defaults to on (value_or(true)). At Core start, every card insert and every format, a 2 s raw take runs. Meanwhile record, photo, timelapse, media actions and standby are refused with "Storage pre-roll is running. One moment."
findings.apertar_way: Upstream never discards free space and never writes to the media without an operator action. It records as soon as it is Ready, and it refuses commands only for work the operator started (ApertarCoreApp.cpp:9095-9117@upstream-1.6.0).
findings.why_it_matters: Two stock behaviours change silently: deleted clips become unrecoverable, and the camera is unavailable for seconds after boot or a card insert. The KB's own plan said the pre-roll should be "a setting (storage_preroll, default off at first), never a hidden step" (drop-frames/README.md:341). The port made apertar-media-tune opt-in for a similar reason (e9dd6b2).
findings.rework: Set both defaults off: CaptureSettings{}.mediaTrimEnabled = false, mediaTrimSetting_{false}, automatic pre-roll off. Keep the WebUI switches. The README says what turning trim on costs (no undelete).
findings.deliberate_evidence: ce0bd90 says "default on" for the trim. The pre-roll default contradicts the documented plan at drop-frames/README.md:341.

findings.title: Capture and media commands wait for trim and merge under commandMutex_
findings.port_way: record_start, capture_photo, timelapse_start and the media actions call waitForMediaTrim(name, 5000) and waitForClipMerge(name, 5000) inside handleCommand. The trim wait is up to about 3.5 s (2 s + 1 s + 0.5 s) and the merge wait up to 1 s. In both calls, 5000 holds the worker off and does not block the command.
findings.apertar_way: Upstream refuses with a sentence instead of waiting on a background media job: ApertarCoreApp.cpp:9108-9110@upstream-1.6.0 "Wait for the media speed test to finish first." One lock serialises all commands.
findings.why_it_matters: While a trim winds down, every socket, WebUI and button command waits behind commandMutex_, for up to about 4.5 s.
findings.rework: Keep "record always starts" if the owner wants it. After F4 the trim ends through timeout, so the wait shortens. Keep the 5 s hold-off of both workers. Document the choice for the original developer.
findings.deliberate_evidence: KB drop-frames/README.md:69: record and media actions wait at most 2 s, then end the trim.

findings.title: Comments and README narrate history and cite KB paths, campaigns, other projects, commits
findings.port_way: Examples: "(apertar-kb working/drop-frames/nvme-campaign/probe-exfat-dir.md)", "follow cinepi-raw's DNG encoder (cinepi/dng_encoder.cpp ...)", "(the NVMe campaign does, for its A/B)", "CineMate's storage warm-up", "the rule since db17860", "measured 2026-11-08", "local branch clip-split". This unit's env rows also sit in the README table "Write-path knobs for A/B tests"; the rest of that table belongs to other units.
findings.apertar_way: No tickets or other projects' commits in source (C8-S9). Comments are rare one-line why-notes (C1-I14), e.g. ApertarCoreApp.cpp:1543@upstream-1.6.0. No env-knob tables in the README (C8-S12).
findings.why_it_matters: These references mean nothing to the original developer, and they age badly.
findings.rework: Keep one-line technical reasons, e.g. "exFAT walks every entry of the target folder on create". Drop KB paths, campaign names, dates, commit hashes and other-project references. Remove README rows 355-356; the rest of the table is for the units that own it.

findings.title: Env twin for every file key, *_env flags in state, unused speculative parameter
findings.port_way: There are env > file > default chains for buffer, frames_per_folder, clip_merge, preroll and stop percent. State exposes frames_per_folder_env, clip_merge_env_off, storage_preroll_auto_env and media_trim_env_off. decideGuard takes a Trigger it ignores, "so a future rule can differ". refreshBufferRequest parses the same text three times. And ++remaining; ++remaining;.
findings.apertar_way: Env knobs are read where they are used and not shown to clients (CameraController.cpp:3328-3329@upstream-1.6.0). Comments state a present reason (C1-I14).
findings.why_it_matters: These are experiment leftovers and generality built ahead of need. They double the precedence logic the maintainer must keep right.
findings.rework: After F1, at most one bench env var per knob, read at the point of use. Drop the *_env state members and the Trigger parameter. Parse once. Write remaining += 2.

findings.title: Frame-number rule in three copies; three copied store.edit command blocks
findings.port_way: detail::frameNumber is commented "Same rule as playback/ClipFrames.hpp frameNumberFromName". Both C++ copies are port code (src/playback does not exist upstream), and a Python copy exists too. There are three ~20-line store.edit/StoreFlags/controlsErrors_/wakeControlsWorker/refreshBufferRequest blocks.
findings.apertar_way: A shape repeated inside one function becomes a local lambda (C1-I17; ApertarCoreApp.cpp:9478, :8671@upstream-1.6.0).
findings.why_it_matters: Two C++ copies of one parsing rule can drift, and so can the copied command blocks.
findings.rework: Move the rule into cdng/FramePath.hpp, which ClipMerge.hpp and ClipFrames.hpp already include, and call it from both. That avoids a cdng-to-playback include. The Python copy is fine for a desk tool. The store.edit blocks go away with F1; otherwise use one local lambda.

findings.title: Host unit tests in tools/, outside the build
findings.port_way: Standalone g++ programs, each with its own check() and a compile line in a comment. None is in CMakeLists.txt. The compile lines disagree: frame_path and clip_merge say -std=c++17 (like the README), buffer_budget says -std=c++20. The four .cpp tests compile with c++20 and pass here. The same pattern runs through the whole port (20 files in tools/).
findings.apertar_way: No precedent: upstream Core has no tests and no tools/ directory (S24).
findings.why_it_matters: It is new ground, not a mismatch. The tests cost the build nothing and cover the only parts testable off the Pi.
findings.rework: Keep them. Drop storage_buffer_conf_test.cpp and media_trim_test.sh with F1/F4. Use one compile command (c++20, matching Core) and one README line under For Developers.
findings.deliberate_evidence: Commit messages d7dd337 and ba0658d record desk test runs.

findings.title: GET /api/buffer polled at 4 Hz beside /api/state
findings.port_way: A lock-free read-only route returns the buffer and pre-roll members. The WebUI polls it about 4 times a second while the bar or the pre-roll pill shows.
findings.apertar_way: The WebUI polls GET /api/state at 1 Hz, with no push channel (C1-S26). /api/state builds the full state through controller calls (ApertarCoreApp.cpp:7154@upstream-1.6.0 buildWebStateJson). Extra read-only GET routes exist (/api/media, /api/config, /api/presets).
findings.why_it_matters: The bar gets a second state endpoint and a second polling rate. Polling the full state at 4 Hz during a take would cost more than this small route.
findings.rework: Keep the route and state its reason in the handoff: a smooth bar during a take, without the controller lock. Drop it only if 1 Hz from /api/state is enough.

findings.title: Namespace names and src/util placement differ from upstream
findings.port_way: The port uses apertar::bufferbudget, storagepreroll, clipmerge and framepath. BufferBudget.hpp and StoragePreroll.hpp sit in src/util.
findings.apertar_way: Upstream nested names are mixed: apertar::settingsFile (src/util/SettingsFile.hpp:17@upstream-1.6.0), apertar::tuning, apertar::hardware, prores_color, prores_repair. src/util@upstream holds only AtomicStillFile, RecordingDropWarning, RecordingFailure and SettingsFile. Subsystem logic sits next to its owner (src/camera/StillBracketing.hpp).
findings.why_it_matters: Small reading frictions.
findings.rework: Move BufferBudget.hpp next to the queue (src/camera or src/cdng) and StoragePreroll.hpp next to App (src/). Optionally rename the namespaces to camelCase (bufferBudget, storagePreroll, clipMerge, framePath) to match settingsFile.

findings.title: tools/flatten_clip.py desk tool
findings.port_way: A 284-line stdlib Python script with dry run, --apply and --unflatten N. It reports timing statistics (import statistics at :27, report at :184-189).
findings.apertar_way: No precedent: Core ships no helper scripts (C1-S29), and upstream has no tools/ directory.
findings.why_it_matters: It is useful when a card leaves the camera before the merge worker has run, and nothing else covers that case on a computer.
findings.rework: Keep it. Drop the statistics report. Keep --unflatten only if a test uses it; no test calls the script now.
findings.deliberate_evidence: Commit 9ec37b5 and README:331 explain the Mac-side use.

App-2.summary:
Skeptic pass over the 15 App-2 findings. 14 survive and 1 is dropped. Stand as written: F1, F3, F6, F7, F8, F10, F15. Corrected: F2, F4, F5, F9, F11, F12, F14. Dropped: F13.
- F2: upstream Core's template was already this thin. The real loss is the UI first-run writer, so the [mpu6050] values to restore are that writer's, with bus=1.
- F4: downgraded to minor. Buffer events tick at 250 ms, so they cannot move into the 1 Hz wait() loop. Only the buffer-events and safety-stop workers need their own stopX().
- F5: storage_preroll_auto_env added to the list. Effort raised to L.
- F9: upstream Core does format *_text strings itself, so the fix is to flatten meta/extra, not to move formatting into the WebUI.
- F11: keep the store. History and adopt back the restore-a-replaced-file feature. adopt() writes the adopted file only once.
- F12: firmware [pi5] also matches CM5. On CM5 only [cm5] lines are missed.
- F14: the "adopted" suffix appears on one start only.
- F13 dropped: the trim helper's path comes from the --media-root launch option, not from config.

findings.title: Template [display] defaults are an HDMI 1080p rig, not the stock 720x720 panel
findings.port_way: defaultHardwareConfigTemplate() writes ui_width=1920, ui_height=1080, ui_layout=landscape_large, hdmi_external_only=true, and its comment names 1920x1080 as the default. UI commit 7c41a27 made the same values the touch UI's fallback when there is no file.
findings.apertar_way: src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:4313,4320-4322,4329@upstream-1.6.0 720x720, square, hdmi_external_only=false; Apertar-UI/src/DisplayConfigBridge.cpp:14-15,314,323,647-650@upstream-1.6.0
findings.why_it_matters: A stock camera with no hardware file boots the touch UI in the 1080p layout with the panel handed to HDMI. Saving the Config page writes the same values. The default describes one contributor's rig.
findings.rework: Restore the four upstream [display] lines and the upstream resolutions comment in defaultHardwareConfigTemplate(). Revert the UI fallback from 7c41a27 in the same change. An HDMI rig sets its own keys.
findings.deliberate_evidence: 7af9f13: 'the 720x720 square layout of the old Hyperpixel screen, which is not what this camera uses'; fork-log rows 7af9f13 and 7c41a27
findings.rework_risk: Cameras on HDMI 1080p rigs that have no file must set [display] explicitly.

findings.title: With the UI first-run writer gone, the only default lacks chip=auto, input tuning and [mpu6050]
findings.port_way: UI commit c9d841f removed the first-run writer. Core only shows its template and never writes it. The template has [gpio] enabled=false, [gpio_encoders] enabled=false, no chip= key and no [mpu6050]. The [gpio_switches] comment says chip is read 'like [gpio]', but GpioInput.cpp:311-336 reads only enabled and switchN_* in that section.
findings.apertar_way: Apertar-UI/src/DisplayConfigBridge.cpp:57-330@upstream-1.6.0 wrote the first-run file: [gpio_buttons] chip=auto, active_low=true, pull=up, poll_ms=12, debounce_ms=60 (:156-166); [gpio_encoders] chip=auto plus tuning (:168-183); [mpu6050] bus=1, address=0x68, sample_rate_hz, gyro_range_dps=1000, dlpf_hz, use_fifo, orientation, level reference (:206-232). Upstream Core's own template was just as thin (src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:4377-4380@upstream-1.6.0).
findings.why_it_matters: A fresh camera gets no file, and the default it is shown no longer documents chip=, the input tuning or the IMU section. The owner's GPIO-chip request needs that definition in the default.
findings.rework: Fold the upstream UI first-run sections into defaultHardwareConfigTemplate(): [gpio_buttons] (an alias of [gpio] in every reader, and the name the UI writer and the Controls code use) with chip/active_low/pull/poll_ms/debounce_ms; [gpio_encoders] with chip and its tuning; [mpu6050] with the UI writer's values and enabled=false. Change the [gpio_switches] comment to: chip, pull, active_low and debounce_ms come from [gpio_buttons].
findings.deliberate_evidence: c9d841f removed the writer on purpose (a moved file kept coming back) but did not carry its content over. 4d80a35 dropped the [imu] keys as ignored and did not move them.
findings.rework_risk: Low. The values are text in a template the readers already accept.

findings.title: Buffer safety stop wired through a process-global std::function hook
findings.port_way: The App constructor body assigns bufferbudget::safetyStopHook(), a function-static std::function in a header. The DNG write queue calls it under its own mutex, and runBufferSafetyStop waits on a condition variable. flushAbortFunction() (BufferBudget.hpp:246, set at CC:4629) uses the same idiom.
findings.apertar_way: C1-S19: src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:6783-6785@upstream-1.6.0 camera_([this](const std::string &eventJson){ publishEvent(eventJson); }, ...). CC passes callbacks to its own parts (CC:7254@cinemate-port EventCallback exposureEvent). Upstream src has no static std::function.
findings.why_it_matters: It is a hidden second wiring path between camera and App. The hook captures this, outlives App, and a second instance overwrites it. The original developer looks for camera-to-app wiring in the initialiser list.
findings.rework: Add a std::function<void(const SafetyStopHit&)> parameter to CameraController's constructor, beside the event and preview callbacks. Store it and pass it to DngRecordingQueue as a member. Delete safetyStopHook(). Keep runBufferSafetyStop, which dispatches record_stop through handleCommand. Do the same for flushAbortFunction().
findings.deliberate_evidence: Introduced in omnibus commit d44b177; no design note found.
findings.rework_risk: The queue construction path inside CC must carry the callback.

findings.title: Worker start styles differ and stopMediaWatcher() also stops five other workers
findings.port_way: Six workers start with atomic stores and three guard styles (!running&&!joinable, !joinable, none). The guards never fire because stop() joins every thread. stopMediaWatcher() calls stopStoragePreroll/stopClipMerge/stopMediaTrim and inlines the buffer-events and safety-stop joins. stop() calls stopStoragePreroll() and then calls it again through stopMediaWatcher(); this is harmless because it is idempotent.
findings.apertar_way: C1-S17: start sets the flag under the group mutex, then std::thread(&ApertarCoreApp::runX, this); each worker has one stopX() (src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:6821-6825,10988-11014@upstream-1.6.0).
findings.why_it_matters: Thread lifetimes cannot be read from start()/stop(), and the name stopMediaWatcher hides five joins.
findings.rework: Add stopBufferEvents() and stopBufferSafetyStop(). Make stopMediaWatcher() stop only the watcher. Call every stopX() from stop() once, in the C1-S25 order. Use one start style: set the flag under the group mutex, no guard. Keep all of them as threads: buffer events tick at 250 ms while busy, and the others are request-driven.
findings.rework_risk: The stop order matters for pre-roll before camera_.stop().

findings.title: Env knobs surface in state and WebUI; storage switches split over three stores; App keeps a settings copy
findings.port_way: APERTAR_MEDIA_TRIM, APERTAR_CDNG_BUFFER, APERTAR_STORAGE_PREROLL, APERTAR_CDNG_FRAMES_PER_FOLDER and APERTAR_CLIP_MERGE override settings. They surface in state as media_trim_env_off, storage_preroll_auto_env, frames_per_folder_env and clip_merge_env_off, and the WebUI greys switches from them. The trim switch is in camera_settings.conf; buffer, frames per folder and merge are in hardware [storage]; pre-roll is in [media]. Each [storage]/[media] switch is written by its set_* command through the store (App:12829-12920). mediaTrimSetting_ copies the camera setting.
findings.apertar_way: C1-S24: App reads only APERTAR_HARDWARE_CONFIG (src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:4254@upstream-1.6.0). conv-core-camera R5: a bench knob is read where it is used and never added to the socket API or the settings files (src/lossydng/LossyDngEncoder.cpp:100,325@upstream-1.6.0). C1-S08: no settings copy (src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:7715@upstream-1.6.0). C1-R2: a persisted switch set by a command goes to camera_settings.conf.
findings.why_it_matters: Experiment knobs become product surface, and five related switches live in three stores with env overrides on top. raw/sweep-knobs.md rows 3, 5, 10, 25 and 40 reach the same verdict.
findings.rework: Delete mediaTrimEnvOff(), the four *_env* state fields and the env inputs of refreshBufferRequest(). Read camera_.settings().mediaTrimEnabled where the trim decides, and delete mediaTrimSetting_. Move the storage switches set by set_media_trim, set_buffer_mode, set_frames_per_folder, set_clip_merge and set_storage_preroll into camera_settings.conf per C1-R2. The hardware file keeps mount_path and pcie_controller.
findings.rework_risk: The move touches handlers, CC readers and WCP in other units, and needs a one-time migration of existing [storage]/[media] keys.

findings.title: /api/media in a hold hides folders; cDNG size_bytes/file_count change meaning
findings.port_way: In a hold, ProRes, H.264, MLV, timelapse and uncached cDNG folders are skipped with continue. The comment promises 'the bare entry', but `else if (!held)` is always true. For cDNG, size_bytes counts frames, WAVs and fps-ramp.txt, and file_count is the frame count.
findings.apertar_way: discoverMediaLibraryItems lists every folder and runs mediaStatsForPath over all files (src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:6282-6448,5915@upstream-1.6.0).
findings.why_it_matters: Clips vanish from the WebUI list during a take, and the shown size undercounts what the download zips (for example a .gcsv sidecar).
findings.rework: In a hold, push the bare entry (id, kind, name, type, size --) instead of continue. The name comes from the root iterator, so no card read is needed. Delete the duplicate comment and the dead branch. The facts cache sums all files for size_bytes, and file_count stays a count of files.
findings.deliberate_evidence: f91fafa and ab4cc92 (T47) state the hold rule: the card must not be read during a take.
findings.rework_risk: Low.
