findings.title: audio_url is JSON-escaped, not URL-encoded
findings.port_way: "/api/media/file?kind=folder&id=" + escapeJson(id) + "&name=" + escapeJson(f.name) + ".wav"; the WebUI plays it as is (WCP:12817).
findings.apertar_way: mediaDownloadUrl uses urlEncodeComponent (src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:5971,7147-7150@cinemate-port; the same helper exists at upstream-1.6.0).
findings.why_it_matters: A folder named A&B_001 gives id=A and a 404. This is probable because clip names are composable since 014a2bf. '#', '%', '+' and space break the URL the same way.
findings.rework: escapeJson("/api/media/file?kind=folder&id=" + urlEncodeComponent(id) + "&name=" + urlEncodeComponent(f.name + ".wav"))

findings.title: Ticket tags, Cinemate names and a Cinemate tool in comments and operator text
findings.port_way: Comments carry T21/T37/T39/T42/T47/T50/T51/Q23/R1 and 'design §4.3', and some narrate history (App:5585, :8032-8033). The operator text reads 'Not finalised: audio_capture.raw is on the media (raw2wav.py makes a WAV)'. The template text says 'CineMate style' and 'CineMate's warm-up'.
findings.apertar_way: C1-I14: comments are rare, state a hazard or a reason, and carry no ticket numbers (10 comment lines in App@upstream-1.6.0). raw2wav is absent from both upstream trees. audio_capture.raw itself is upstream's file (src/audio/AudioRecordingSession.cpp:233@upstream-1.6.0).
findings.why_it_matters: Internal numbers mean nothing to the original developer, and the operator is pointed at a tool an Apertar camera does not have.
findings.rework: Delete the tags and the narration. Change the operator text to 'Audio not finalised (audio_capture.raw)'. Remove the product names from the template comments.

findings.title: clipInfoJson nests meta/extra objects that repeat top-level values
findings.port_way: A flat top level plus holes (an array of pairs), ramp ({"present":true} or null), meta{...} and extra{...}. meta.frame_rate repeats fps_badge, meta.frames repeats frame_count, and extra.sound repeats sound_text.
findings.apertar_way: Upstream replies are flat objects with fixed keys and Core-formatted *_text strings (size_text and duration_text at src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:7697,7700@upstream-1.6.0; conv C1 5.5).
findings.why_it_matters: The reply shape is foreign to the codebase, and the same fact is sent twice.
findings.rework: Flatten to top-level keys: captured_text, resolution_text, bit_depth_text, duration_text, clip_size_text, path, format_text, dropped_text. Drop meta.frame_rate, meta.frames and extra.sound. Make ramp a boolean and keep holes as the only array. Update the WCP reader at :12743.
findings.deliberate_evidence: f91fafa; the comment cites 'design §4.3' (T47).
findings.rework_risk: The WCP reader in another unit must change in the same commit.

findings.title: C++ [cfexpress_hat] reader defaults to off; upstream's reader defaults to on
findings.port_way: CfeHatConfig::enabled=false. loadCfeHatConfig() turns the HAT on only when the section header exists.
findings.apertar_way: The embedded helper is upstream's only reader of the section and defaults on: CFE_HAT_ENABLED = True (src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:3393@upstream-1.6.0), overridden by enabled (:3451). The loader's shape copies loadIna219HardwareConfig (App:4450-4506@upstream-1.6.0), which is fine.
findings.why_it_matters: With no hardware file (the UI no longer writes one), the Python helper watches the slot and the C++ watcher does not, so a pulled card goes unseen.
findings.rework: Set `bool enabled = true;` in CfeHatConfig and drop the switch that turns it on when the section exists.
findings.deliberate_evidence: Comment 'Off when no hardware config has the section.' (0b1632f).
findings.rework_risk: Cameras without a HAT poll i2c bus 10 at 0x34, which the Python helper already does.

findings.title: HardwareConfigStore replaces one save function; keep it, document it, trim merge review
findings.port_way: All writers go through a store: the Config page, the Controls page and set_buffer_mode and the like. The store has revisions, history files, adopt() (writes adopted-<rev>.conf once ever), merge review and 409 codes. Upstream's three checks remain as checkHardwareConfigText.
findings.apertar_way: saveHardwareConfigFile: checks, .bak, .tmp plus rename (src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:5323-5386@upstream-1.6.0); C1-S07.
findings.why_it_matters: It is more machinery than upstream carries. But history and adopt back the restore-a-replaced-file feature (014fa22), which is why the UI writer was dropped (c9d841f). Several writers justify one store.
findings.rework: Keep revisions, the atomic write, .bak, history and adopt. Drop the merge-review path if no caller needs it. Write one paragraph for the original developer: what the store owns, the 409 codes, and where history lives.
findings.rework_risk: Low.

findings.title: Validator parses config.txt for [all] and [pi5] only
findings.port_way: hardwareConfigFacts() passes /boot/firmware/config.txt to parseConfigTxt, which applies only [all] and [pi5].
findings.apertar_way: no precedent (upstream has no validator)
findings.why_it_matters: On Pi 4 and CM4, a DPI overlay under [pi4] or [cm4] is missed and [pi5] lines are applied. On CM5, [cm5] lines are missed; firmware [pi5] also matches CM5. In both cases the pin warnings are wrong.
findings.rework: Read /proc/device-tree/model in hardwareConfigFacts(), pass the board to the parser, and honour the matching filters ([pi4], [pi5], [cm4], [cm5], [all]).

findings.title: Success lines logged at every start
findings.port_way: Every start logs '<path> <rev>: N errors, M warnings'. The suffix 'adopted, nothing changed' is added only on the one start that writes the adopted file. Every start also logs the CFE HAT settings.
findings.apertar_way: C1-I13: App logs failures and ignored input only (src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:1863,8954@upstream-1.6.0).
findings.why_it_matters: Log noise, and a different habit from upstream App.
findings.rework: Log the summary only when there are issues or a replaced file. Log the HAT line only when it changes.

findings.title: Three now-ms helpers, second /boot list, refreshBufferRequest twice, unread boot_copy
findings.port_way: playbackNowMs, trimNowMs and clipMergeNowMs are identical. buildHardwareConfigFileJson types the /boot paths again. start() calls refreshBufferRequest() twice, with a comment about the order. boot_copy has no reader in WCP or the UI.
findings.apertar_way: hardwareConfigCandidatePaths() already lists the /boot copies (src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:4251-4259@upstream-1.6.0).
findings.why_it_matters: Small drift points.
findings.rework: Keep one now-ms helper. Iterate hardwareConfigCandidatePaths() and skip the home path. Call refreshBufferRequest() once, before the first worker. Drop boot_copy.

App-4.summary: Skeptic pass on App-4 (workers and helpers block). 20 findings checked on both sides. 8 stand (F1, F4, F8, F9, F10, F13, F15, F16, F20 - 9 incl. F20), 9 corrected (F2, F3, F5, F6, F7, F11, F12, F17, F19), 2 dropped (F14: i2c-dev transfers are serialised per adapter, residual folded into F1; F18: helper validates strictly, fstrim only discards free blocks, upstream needs wider sudo). Main corrections: F3 gate is a considered safety feature that extends upstream's own 'no media mounted' rule (speed test App:8970@upstream), so severity minor, deliberate yes, rework = Options flag not weaker gate; F5/F6 upstream does have env knobs and function-static singletons, but read-once / file-local in the owner, so the mismatch is narrowed and severity minor, playbackYield removed from F6; F2 precedent is the idle timer calling handleCommand; F7 rework needs a wake at take end; F19 bus-10/Pi-5 assumption is inherited from upstream, now nit. Skeptic table and full Final findings appended to the report.

findings.title: Second dispatcher before the command lock; get_controls/controls_history duplicate GET /api/config
findings.port_way: handleReadOnlyHardwareCommand answers get_controls, controls_history, controls_last_input, scan_i2c and list_actions before handleCommand takes commandMutex_; test_input also pre-lock. get_controls returns a deeply nested object (file text, issues, model, peripherals, i2c_buses, apply, dpi_lines). Only the WebUI calls them (WCP:18264, :18518), and the same WebUI still uses GET /api/config (WCP:18741; route kept at App:8613).
findings.apertar_way: One flat chain under one lock taken on the first line: src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:9091-9093@upstream-1.6.0 (C1-S02 'a second dispatcher function', C1-S03 'a command body that runs before the lock'). WebUI reads the hardware file lock-free through HTTP: src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:7168-7173@upstream-1.6.0 GET /api/config -> buildHardwareConfigFileJson (C1-S09, 5.7).
findings.why_it_matters: The original developer finds a second command chain, and a socket command returning the file /api/config already returns, in a third JSON shape that breaks the short list of nested reply members (C1-I09).
findings.rework: Extend buildHardwareConfigFileJson with revision, written_by, issues, replaced, model, peripherals, i2c_buses, apply, dpi_lines. Add GET /api/config/history[?name=] in handleWebRequest. Move controls_last_input, list_actions, scan_i2c into ordinary handleCommand blocks under the lock (a scan is ~117 one-byte reads; slow work under the lock has precedent). Keep test_input as the single pre-lock exception with one comment line (it re-enters handleCommand). Delete handleReadOnlyHardwareCommand. Switch WebUI controlsCall({cmd:'get_controls'}) to fetch('/api/config').
findings.deliberate_evidence: f5a61b8 message; apertar-kb/working/controls/design-controls.md:112 and :644-650 (lock weighed, /api/config not).

findings.title: Storage pre-roll worker starts and finishes a camera take outside handleCommand
findings.port_way: runStoragePrerollOnce on a worker thread takes commandMutex_ itself, runs its own guard copy (storagePrerollGuard -> storagepreroll::decideGuard) and calls camera_.startStoragePreroll; then watches the clock and calls camera_.finishStoragePreroll without any lock.
findings.apertar_way: C1-S01: every camera state change enters through handleCommand. The upstream idle timer builds ControlCommand enter_standby and calls handleCommand (src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:7041-7047@upstream-1.6.0). Timed camera work lives in CameraController (timelapseLoop, src/camera/CameraController.cpp:8447@upstream-1.6.0). The port's safety stop does it right: record_stop via dispatchHardwareInputCommand (App:11107-11109@cinemate-port).
findings.why_it_matters: A third and fourth take start/stop path besides the command chain, with a separate copy of the busy guards kept in step by hand.
findings.rework: Worker keeps request/coalesce and settle wait, then builds ControlCommand storage_preroll (trigger, seconds) and calls handleCommand as the idle timer does. The storage_preroll block relies on the head guards and checks only pre-roll-specific conditions (camera ready, not still mode, raw format), then calls camera_.startStoragePreroll. Length and finish move into CameraController (timer thread like timelapseLoop) which emits the end through the existing event callback. Delete storagePrerollGuard and the guard fields the head guards already cover.
findings.deliberate_evidence: d44b177 message and comment App:11113-11118; no comparison with handleCommand found.
findings.rework_risk: The finish must still wait for the drain and delete the clip; CameraController already owns finishStoragePreroll, so the move is internal to CC.

findings.title: Record gate refuses a --media PATH that is not a mount point; the bypass is an env variable
findings.port_way: mediaGateError returns 'No media mounted at <root>.' when /proc/mounts has no exact entry for the media root; record_start, capture_photo, timelapse_start refused. Bypasses: simulateCamera and APERTAR_MEDIA_REQUIRE_MOUNT=0.
findings.apertar_way: README.md:253@upstream-1.6.0 '--media PATH | Recording destination.' Recording to any folder works; CameraController has no mount check. But upstream already treats an unmounted root as no media for the speed test (src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:8970-8974@upstream-1.6.0 'No media is currently mounted.') and the library (App:7676@upstream-1.6.0). Launch options are Options members with a --flag in src/main.cpp:52-82@upstream-1.6.0 (C1-S24).
findings.why_it_matters: apertar-core --media /home/pi/clips refuses to record where upstream recorded. The gate itself is worth keeping: without it a take under an empty /media/RAW lands on the SD card.
findings.rework: Keep the gate. Replace APERTAR_MEDIA_REQUIRE_MOUNT with an Options member and a main.cpp flag (e.g. --media-any-folder), listed in the README options table next to --media; mediaGateBypassed() reads the member. Same in storagePrerollGuard and playbackHoldReason.
findings.deliberate_evidence: Comment App:11327-11329 names the plain-directory case and gives the env bypass; 438a342 describes the gate.

findings.title: Automatic storage pre-roll on by default: a raw take at every boot, card insert and format
findings.port_way: [media] preroll defaults to on (conf.automatic.value_or(true)). The watcher requests a pre-roll at start, on card insert and after a format. Default format is cDNG (CC:5562) so the raw-format guard does not skip it. While it runs, nine commands incl. record_start answer 'Storage pre-roll is running. One moment.'
findings.apertar_way: no precedent
findings.why_it_matters: An unmodified install gets a raw take written and deleted at every boot; record, format, eject and standby are refused for its length plus up to 2 min trim wait and 3 s settle.
findings.rework: Default [media] preroll=off (value_or(false)). Keep the manual storage_preroll command and the switch.
findings.deliberate_evidence: d44b177: 'on Core start, card insert, format and by hand (storage_preroll)'.

findings.title: APERTAR_* environment knobs override saved settings and are re-read per call in App
findings.port_way: APERTAR_MEDIA_REQUIRE_MOUNT and APERTAR_MEDIA_MIN_FREE_MB (every gate call), APERTAR_MEDIA_TUNE, APERTAR_STORAGE_PREROLL, APERTAR_MEDIA_TRIM, APERTAR_CLIP_MERGE, APERTAR_CDNG_BUFFER, APERTAR_CDNG_FRAMES_PER_FOLDER; several beat the saved [media]/[storage] setting. 17 getenv("APERTAR lines in port App vs 2 upstream.
findings.apertar_way: Upstream App reads only APERTAR_HARDWARE_CONFIG (App:4254, :4273@upstream-1.6.0). Developer knobs exist but in the owning subsystem, read once into a static const, overriding no saved setting: src/lossydng/LossyDngEncoder.cpp:98-105, :325@upstream-1.6.0. Launch options are Options members (C1-S24).
findings.why_it_matters: Hidden switches that silently override what the user saved, invisible in both UIs; left over from A/B experiments.
findings.rework: Delete env reads that override a saved setting (APERTAR_STORAGE_PREROLL, APERTAR_MEDIA_TRIM, APERTAR_CLIP_MERGE, APERTAR_CDNG_BUFFER); each switch keeps one home ([media] preroll, [storage] clip_merge, mediaTrimSetting_, [storage] buffer). APERTAR_MEDIA_MIN_FREE_MB becomes [media] min_free_mb or a constant. APERTAR_MEDIA_REQUIRE_MOUNT goes with F3, APERTAR_MEDIA_TUNE with F17. A knob that must stay for bench work is read once into a static const in its owner, as LossyDngEncoder.cpp does.
findings.deliberate_evidence: d44b177 and ba0658d messages name the env vars as features.

findings.title: Cross-part state in header-level function-static singletons
findings.port_way: safetyStopState() (written by the write queue in CC, read in App; 10 + 10 uses), configStore() (App 20 uses, Mpu6050RecordingSession.cpp 2), prerollState()/prerollActive()/setPrerollLast and clipMergeRequest() (App only) are inline function-static globals in headers reachable from any file.
findings.apertar_way: Upstream uses function-static singletons only file-local in the owner's .cpp: captureSettingsPersister() (src/camera/CameraController.cpp:885-889@upstream-1.6.0), LossyDngDiskWriter::instance() (src/lossydng/LossyDngEncoder.cpp:114-118@upstream-1.6.0). Shared state is an App member group (src/ApertarCoreApp.hpp:110-176@upstream-1.6.0, C1-S18) and crosses parts through constructor callbacks (C1-S19). The port's file-local playbackYield() (App:6342) conforms.
findings.why_it_matters: The original developer cannot see from a class which part writes the safety-stop or pre-roll state, or where the hardware store lives.
findings.rework: Safety-stop state becomes a member group of CameraController (the write queue sets it), read by App via getter or the event callback. The hardware config store becomes an App member passed by reference. Pre-roll state and the clip-merge switch become App members (or file-local in App). Keep pure functions in the headers.

findings.title: Controls worker polls the hardware file every 2 s (a file watcher in Core)
findings.port_way: runControlsWorker wakes on a save or every 2 s, compares file text with applied text, applies ssh edits. The same 2 s turn retries an apply that a take deferred.
findings.apertar_way: C1-S08 names 'a file watcher in Core' as a violation. Upstream applies by restart: src/web/WebControlPage.cpp:3869@upstream-1.6.0 'Hardware, input, display, and sensor changes may need ApertarCore or the UI restarted'.
findings.why_it_matters: A background poll upstream does not have. The KB contradicts itself: design-controls.md:93-95 says ssh hand edits are 'never applied on the side', decisions.md:47 says outside edits are polled every 2 s.
findings.rework: Keep the worker (deadlock reason sound). Wake it on set_controls, POST /api/config and at take end (where syncRecordingTracking(false) runs); drop the 2 s timeout. An ssh edit applies at the next save or restart, as upstream. Fix the design page to match.
findings.deliberate_evidence: apertar-kb/working/controls/decisions.md:47; design-controls.md:93-98.

findings.title: Ticket numbers, critic ids, KB paths, banners and about 140 comment lines in the slice
findings.port_way: Comments cite T39/T40/T42/T43/T47/T48, 'critic S11', 'critic Y11', 'design §2.7', 'kb working/dng-chain, R4', 'probe-exfat-dir.md', 'the NVMe campaign'; // ---- banners; install instructions inside a log line. 140 full-line comments in App:10860-12668 (~1800 lines).
findings.apertar_way: C1-I14: comments are rare and state a hazard or a reason; upstream App has 10 full-line comments in ~10800 lines. A ticket number or banner is the listed violation.
findings.why_it_matters: The references mean nothing to the original developer; the volume reads as narration.
findings.rework: Delete ticket, critic, KB and file references and banners. Keep one hazard sentence per worker (why a thread, why not under the lock). Move measurements to the KB, install steps to the README.

findings.title: Buffer level pushed by an App polling thread instead of emitted by the camera
findings.port_way: runBufferEvents polls camera_.frameBufferStatus() and nine global flags every 250 ms (1 s idle) and publishes 'buffer'.
findings.apertar_way: The producer emits on change through its callback: emitMediaWriteState (src/camera/CameraController.cpp:7551-7563@upstream-1.6.0, 'Serialize edges'); audio_level from the recorder's level callback (src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:8380-8384@upstream-1.6.0). C1-S12 builds events at the emit site.
findings.why_it_matters: An extra thread and poll loop where upstream emits on change.
findings.rework: The write queue emits 'buffer' on a level change through the existing camera event callback, rate-limited in the queue and never under the controller mutex (as emitMediaWriteState). Pre-roll and safety-stop flags travel in the events that change them or in get_state. Delete runBufferEvents.
findings.deliberate_evidence: Comment App:10986-10992.

findings.title: Two identical buffer events in one loop turn
findings.port_way: The first branch publishes on any setting/pre-roll/dropped-frame change without updating sentUsed/sentCapacity; the busy branch then publishes again because buffer.used != sentUsed.
findings.apertar_way: no precedent
findings.why_it_matters: During a take, a dropped frame and a level change in the same 250 ms turn send two identical events to every socket client.
findings.rework: Publish once per turn: set sentUsed/sentCapacity/open in the first branch, or merge the branches. Goes away with F9.

findings.title: Media tuning helper runs sudo -n without /usr/bin/timeout or absolute paths, on the watcher thread
findings.port_way: "sudo -n " + helper + " apply " + shellQuote(rootDisk) ... via runShellCommand, no timeout, called from the media watcher (App:10941). Runs only when kernel tuning is enabled (default off).
findings.apertar_way: Upstream's libexec root helpers: "/usr/bin/timeout 6s /usr/bin/sudo -n /usr/local/libexec/apertar-standby-usb " with 'Fixed executable and arguments only' (src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:1541-1550@upstream-1.6.0). Upstream's other sudo -n calls (hwclock, systemctl, mount) are bare, so the libexec shape is the applicable one.
findings.why_it_matters: A hung helper stops the media watcher, and yank detection with it.
findings.rework: /usr/bin/timeout 6s /usr/bin/sudo -n /usr/local/libexec/apertar-media-tune apply|restore <disk> <class> <fs>.

findings.title: Five idle predicates that drift, three identical ms clocks
findings.port_way: storagePrerollGuard, playbackHoldReason, mediaTrimMayRun, clipMergeMayRun, recordingGateActive each list a different subset of busy states (mediaTrimMayRun ignores the safety-stop flush clipMergeMayRun checks). playbackNowMs, trimNowMs, clipMergeNowMs are the same steady_clock ms function.
findings.apertar_way: Busy checks written once as || lists at the head of handleCommand (src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:9095-9110@upstream-1.6.0, C1-S04). One inline clock idiom steady_clock::now().time_since_epoch() (App:9112-9114@upstream-1.6.0).
findings.why_it_matters: The subsets drift; a new busy state must be added in five places.
findings.rework: One bool mediaIdle(std::string *why) const for trim, merge and pre-roll; playbackHoldReason and recordingGateActive keep their meaning but call it where they overlap. One ms clock helper. monotonicMicros stays (compared with systemd monotonic timestamps, App:12343).

findings.title: [cfexpress_hat] parsed by two parsers with defaults in two places; get_controls parses the file 8 times
findings.port_way: loadCfeHatConfig is a hand parser; cfeHatPeripheralJson goes through hwconf with literal defaults "10" and "0x34" (also CfeHat.hpp:20). hwconf::parse(info.text) called 8 times in one reply.
findings.apertar_way: C1-S07: one owner per section of apertar-hardware.conf.
findings.why_it_matters: Defaults can diverge; wasted work.
findings.rework: One CfeHatConfig parser used by both. Parse the document once into a local in the builder.

findings.title: record_start may wait about 4.5 s under the command lock for a trim and a rename
findings.port_way: waitForMediaTrim waits 2 s, then SIGTERM + 1 s, then SIGKILL + 0.5 s; waitForClipMerge waits up to 1 s; both under commandMutex_ before a take.
findings.apertar_way: Rough edge 18 accepts slow work under the lock (format, gyro calibration), but upstream record_start does not wait (src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:9091-9110@upstream-1.6.0).
findings.why_it_matters: The record button can lag by seconds after an idle trim started.
findings.rework: On a take command, SIGTERM the trim at once with no 2 s grace. Keep the single-rename wait.

findings.title: Media watcher runs playback chores; hold reason round-trips string to enum
findings.port_way: The watcher renews the playback yield window and calls trimIdleFrameSlots ('no new thread'). playbackHoldReason returns a string which five if (hold == "...") lines map back to an enum.
findings.apertar_way: no precedent
findings.why_it_matters: Unrelated jobs hidden in the media thread, plus a needless conversion.
findings.rework: Return playback::Hold; call holdName only at the JSON edge. Move the slot trim to the playback call sites.

findings.title: Kernel tuning switch read from a fourth config file ~/apertar-media-tune.conf
findings.port_way: applyMediaTuning reads kernel_tune via loadMediaTuneLogged from /home/pi/apertar-media-tune.conf with a /run/apertar-media/ override. The same file holds seven more write-path knobs read by CC (CC:1467, :4364) and CdngEncoder.cpp:91.
findings.apertar_way: Three stores only: camera_settings.conf, UI.conf, apertar-hardware.conf (C1-S07; BRIEF).
findings.why_it_matters: A fourth config file with a hard-coded home directory.
findings.rework: In this unit: add [media] kernel_tune to apertar-hardware.conf, parsed once by its owner, and stop reading the tune file in App. The tune file as a whole is reviewed with the write-path unit.
findings.deliberate_evidence: 2edc6d0 argues for the file ('one readable file next to the hardware conf ... test nights need an override').

findings.title: Config > Hardware shows a CFexpress hat row on boards without one
findings.port_way: cfeHatPeripheralJson probes bus 10 / 0x34 even when the file has no [cfexpress_hat] section, and Config lists every peripheral.
findings.apertar_way: Upstream also assumes the hat on bus 10 / 0x34 and the Pi 5 PCIe controller (src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:3391-3395, :4303-4306@upstream-1.6.0) but shows no status row for it.
findings.why_it_matters: On a Pi 4 or CM4 the row says 'Bus 10 does not exist on this Pi.' for an accessory the user does not have.
findings.rework: Emit the hat row only when the section exists (in_file is already computed).

findings.title: Wording and shape nits
findings.port_way: 'scan_i2c needs bus= (...)'; 'Media is not answering (errno N)'; reply body built by stripping braces with substr; stopMediaWatcher stops six threads; the 'read-only' get_controls writes controlsErrors_/controlsWarnings_.
findings.apertar_way: C1-I07: '<name> requires <field>.' ('set_iso requires value.', src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:9245@upstream-1.6.0), no developer detail in operator sentences.
findings.why_it_matters: Small departures from house style.
findings.rework: 'scan_i2c requires bus.'; drop errno from the sentence (log it); catalogJson returns members only; rename stopMediaWatcher to stopMediaWorkers; stop writing counters in get_controls.

HW-controls-model.summary: The skeptic pass checked all 16 findings on both sides. 7 stand and 9 are corrected; none were dropped. Corrections: F2 drops NeoRotary heldAtStartMask from the rework because it is a release guard that matches upstream, not an inversion. F3 corrects line refs and adds the upstream trigger 'pin' key, which is refused. The hint check found that a dN=recindicatorled row loses its output action on the page; whether the page then overwrites it is unconfirmed. F5's first choice is now the three upstream normalizeSingleAction copies restored verbatim, because upstream ButtonActionList takes the normaliser as a parameter by design. F6 also restores App's analog-target copy. F7: a save is blocked unless forced, not refused outright. F12 is cut to nit. F14 gains new locations, including T44. F16's rule reference is fixed. F1 (the chip) is fixed on work/improve 04fe197; the fixed 4..27 pin list and the output line max of 27 remain open.

findings.title: GPIO chip (and poll_ms) dropped from the Controls page
findings.port_way: peripheralSettings(gpio_buttons) lists enabled, active_low, pull, debounce_ms; comment 'poll_ms (chips without edge events) and chip stay text-only: the Pi 5's header needs neither'. Outputs have no chip row; output line max 27; free-pin list fixed 4..27. Status card read chip only from [gpio_buttons]; empty chip= showed 'No GPIO chip found.'
findings.apertar_way: GpioInput.cpp:431-432@upstream-1.6.0 chip/gpiochip/gpio_chip shared by [gpio_buttons] and [gpio_encoders]; TriggerOutput.cpp:311@upstream-1.6.0 and RecordingIndicatorOutput chip key; empty means auto (HW-N3, HW-I7)
findings.why_it_matters: Pins on another chip (MCU, I2C/USB GPIO expander, DPI rig with the header taken) cannot be set up from the page; owner asked for the chip back
findings.rework: Done on work/improve 04fe197 (fix-log C1): chip and poll_ms rows for gpio_buttons, chip for both outputs, gpioPinsInUse skips non-header chips, card uses gpioInputChip(doc). Remaining: Core's model still uses fixed free-pin list 4..27 and output line max 27; give the model the chosen chip's line count via readGpioChipInfo
findings.rework_risk: Low; page already lifts the limit in JS on improve
findings.deliberate_evidence: c140c4f 'The GPIO card's settings drop poll and chip (edge events need neither)'; KB working/controls/decisions.md:46

findings.title: A button that reads pressed at start is inverted for the whole session, overriding active_low
findings.port_way: On the first sample button.inverted = level (GPIO) and invertedMask (PCF8574); logs 'reads pressed at start; taken as inverted (a 1-0-1 button)'. Ported from Cinemate check_initial_state (cinemate src/module/gpio_input.py:310-315)
findings.apertar_way: Polarity stated by the operator per section with active_low (GpioInput.cpp:433-434, Pcf8574Input.cpp:372@upstream-1.6.0); no guessing (HW-N3, HW-N7)
findings.why_it_matters: d17=capture held while Core starts, or pressed while the controls worker restarts the GPIO group after a save: every release then fires capture until next restart; a stuck contact is silently flipped
findings.rework: Delete the start-sample inversion (haveSample/inverted in GpioInput, invertedMask in Pcf8574Input). Keep NeoRotary heldAtStartMask (NeoRotary4Input.cpp:611,626-630): it only ignores a push held at open until release, matching upstream. If per-pin normally-closed buttons are needed, add a per-pin key in the header Config and loadConfig (recipe R3), e.g. d17_active_low=false / pin3_active_low=false, plus a row field on the page
findings.rework_risk: Operators with NC buttons relying on auto-detect must set the new key
findings.deliberate_evidence: 0a98868 'inverts a button that reads pressed when it starts'; c140c4f (PCF); decisions.md T44 entry

findings.title: Upstream keys refused by set_controls or hidden from the page
findings.port_way: knownKey(gpio_encoders) accepts only enabled and encoderN_*, so set.gpio_encoders.poll_ms is refused with "'poll_ms' is not a key of [gpio_encoders] that Apertar reads". Output active_low and the trigger's generic pin key are refused the same way. open_drain, pulse_ms, events, encoder _invert/_steps_per_event, NeoRotary reset_on_start/max_events_per_poll, Grove emit_on_start and every Grove aN mapping are not on the page. A dN=recindicatorled line shows as a row with no action (overwrite risk unconfirmed)
findings.apertar_way: GpioInput.cpp:431-445@upstream-1.6.0 reads chip, active_low, pull, poll_ms, debounce_ms in [gpio_encoders]; UI template writes poll_ms=3, debounce_ms=40 there (UI/src/DisplayConfigBridge.cpp:175-176@upstream-1.6.0). TriggerOutput.cpp:316,318,331,333,337@upstream-1.6.0 read pin, open_drain, active_low, pulse_ms, events; RecordingIndicatorOutput.cpp:370@upstream-1.6.0 reads active_low; Core template writes open_drain=true (App:4382@upstream-1.6.0)
findings.why_it_matters: The page states a falsehood about the reader; operator settings HW-N3 names (trigger events, pulse length, chip, poll) are not reachable from it
findings.rework: knownKey: accept chip, active_low, pull, poll_ms, debounce_ms in [gpio_encoders], active_low in both outputs, pin in [trigger_output] (or map it in canonicalKey). Add open_drain to the outputs' peripheralSettings, pulse_ms and events to the trigger's. Either add Grove rows to controlRows or say on the page that [grove_analog] channels are edited in Config. Show output actions on a button row as read-only text
findings.rework_risk: Low

findings.title: hold_ms and double_ms accepted as known keys, read by nobody
findings.port_way: Validator lists hold_ms, double_ms for gpio_buttons, pcf8574, neorotary4; timings are constexpr in ButtonGesture; grep finds no reader
findings.apertar_way: Behaviour timing fixed in code (PowerButtonGesture.hpp@upstream-1.6.0, HW-N3); no dead keys
findings.why_it_matters: [gpio_buttons] hold_ms=1000 saves clean, but Hold still fires at 3 s
findings.rework: Remove hold_ms and double_ms from knownKey
findings.rework_risk: None

findings.title: Action aliases as a runtime CSV string table instead of flat if-chains
findings.port_way: kSpecs[] rows {id, group, label, 'a,b,c' aliases, sources, ui, Arg, token}, matched with listHas; drivers call actions::canonicalAction
findings.apertar_way: GpioInput.cpp:108-202@upstream-1.6.0 flat chain if (action == "record" || action == "capture" || ...) return "capture";, copied in Pcf8574Input.cpp:140 and NeoRotary4Input.cpp:121; ButtonActionList.hpp:80,113@upstream-1.6.0 takes the normaliser as a parameter, so per-driver copies are the design (HW-I1, HW-I5, HW-S2)
findings.why_it_matters: A reader looking for an alias finds a table and a string-split helper, not the chain they wrote; one row mixes aliases, UI labels, parameter families and source flags
findings.rework: Restore the three normalizeSingleAction bodies verbatim from upstream, adding the port's new names (clear_hdr, ev_up/ev_down etc.) to each as || chains. Fallback if the owner prefers one copy: one flat-chain normalizeSingleAction in ButtonActionList.hpp beside normalizeButtonMapping. Reduce kSpecs to {id, group, label, sources} for list_actions. Delete ActionCatalog::normalizeToken; HardwareConfigText.hpp gets a file-local copy
findings.rework_risk: Alias sets must be kept identical across copies; diff against upstream
findings.deliberate_evidence: 916c1dd 'the same action names lived in three normalizeSingleAction copies ... a new action meant editing six places'

findings.title: Trigger events and analog targets moved into the catalog with no consumer
findings.port_way: eventFromToken calls canonicalTriggerEvent (token to string id), then four ifs to the enum. Grove normalizeTarget and App's target normaliser delegate to canonicalAnalogTarget. Both lists served only in list_actions; WebUI reads only catalog.actions
findings.apertar_way: TriggerOutput.cpp:130-148@upstream-1.6.0 maps token straight to the enum, same aliases; GroveAnalogInput.cpp:125-145@upstream-1.6.0 normalizeTarget; App's own copy App:8410-8432@upstream-1.6.0
findings.why_it_matters: Churn in two upstream driver files for no gain; comment 'The Outputs card reads this list' is false
findings.rework: Restore upstream eventFromToken, Grove normalizeTarget and App's target normaliser (zero diff in TriggerOutput.cpp, GroveAnalogInput.cpp). Drop kTriggerEvents, canonicalTriggerEvent, kAnalogTargets, canonicalAnalogTarget from the catalog; if F3's trigger events row is built keep only an id/label list
findings.rework_risk: Low
findings.deliberate_evidence: 916c1dd message

findings.title: classify() is a second parser of the parametric action grammar; the validator turns it into save-blocking errors
findings.port_way: classify re-parses ev/fps/resolution/iso/shutter/wb and restates Core rules ('Core clamps ... K'). Unknown action is an error issue; a new error blocks the save unless forced. App keeps the executing parser but wraps catalog suffixAfter/numberAfter via prefixViews
findings.apertar_way: HW-I5: parametric names parsed only in the handler (App:1342-1370, 8660-8955@upstream-1.6.0). HW-N7: unknown action logged at run time (App:8954@upstream-1.6.0), never refused
findings.why_it_matters: When the two parsers drift, a mapping Core would run is refused on save (only a forced save gets through). No diverging input found yet (probable)
findings.rework: Restore hardwareActionSuffix and parseHardwareActionNumber bodies in App from upstream. Drop classify, Classified, compact, number, numberAfter, suffixAfter from the catalog. Validator flags only tokens that are neither a catalog id nor start with iso/fps/wb/ev/shutter/res, as a warning
findings.rework_risk: Loses the wb_clamp warning; acceptable
findings.deliberate_evidence: 916c1dd 'a typo in the file was silent'

findings.title: list_actions serves fields nobody reads; its gestures list is wrong
findings.port_way: Reply adds values (six option lists from sensor and UI.conf), values_for, gestures {button:[press]}, analog_targets, trigger_events, max_per_mapping. WebUI caches the first reply and reads only actions/ok/error (row gestures come from get_controls); touch UI never sends list_actions
findings.apertar_way: Replies carry what a client uses (C1-I08 hand-written JSON); no precedent for unused reply fields
findings.why_it_matters: Dead protocol surface computed on every call; gestures says buttons only have press, false since 0a98868
findings.rework: Reply with "actions" only (plus max_per_mapping if the page enforces it); delete values, values_for and gestures
findings.rework_risk: None

findings.title: JSON built in the hardware header with string concatenation and its own escaper
findings.port_way: hwconf::jsonEscape; modelJson and peripheralSettingsJson build JSON with std::string +; header relies on transitive includes for snprintf, std::find, isdigit
findings.apertar_way: C1-I08: JSON hand-written with std::ostringstream and escapeJson in App (App:167-215@upstream-1.6.0); the port's own gpioPeripheralJson (App:11993) already does this
findings.why_it_matters: A second escaper and a second JSON style next to App's
findings.rework: Keep ControlsModel.hpp data only (controlRows, gpioPinsInUse, peripheralSettings). Move modelJson, peripheralSettingsJson, catalogJson into App's anonymous namespace beside gpioPeripheralJson using ostringstream and escapeJson. Delete hwconf::jsonEscape
findings.rework_risk: Low

findings.title: The settings spec repeats each reader's defaults
findings.port_way: SettingSpec fallback strings: debounce 60, poll 30/40/80, addresses 0x49/0x20/0x04, deadband 32, trigger line 17
findings.apertar_way: HW-I2: defaults are in-class initialisers of the header Config (GpioInput.hpp:45-57, Pcf8574Input.hpp:28-38, TriggerOutput.hpp:46-51@upstream-1.6.0)
findings.why_it_matters: A default changed in the reader is not seen by the page (all equal today)
findings.rework: Make each reader's Config struct public and build the fallbacks from GpioInput::Config{}, Pcf8574Input::Config{} etc. in App during serialisation (with F9)
findings.rework_risk: Touches reader headers (one access change each)

findings.title: Remote-only buttons stored as remote<N> in [gpio_buttons], a section GpioInput owns
findings.port_way: remote0..15 keys sit in [gpio_buttons]; GpioInput skips them; App runs them through test_input without the section-on check
findings.apertar_way: No precedent. C1-S07: a key is owned by the class that parses its section; HW-N3/HW-S11: the hardware file holds wiring. An App-parsed section has precedent ([ina219], App:4450@upstream-1.6.0)
findings.why_it_matters: GpioInput's section holds keys it must ignore; with test_input this lets a LAN client run scripts (X-protocol-security-2)
findings.rework: Give remote buttons their own section read by App (e.g. [remote_buttons] b0=, b0_single= ...), registered in kSections. Refuse script actions in testInputReply (X-2 fix)
findings.rework_risk: Existing remote<N> keys need a one-time move
findings.deliberate_evidence: 9b5ea14

findings.title: gpioChipScore moved out of one of its three copies
findings.port_way: GpioInput uses the shared copy in GpioChipInfo.cpp; TriggerOutput and RecordingIndicatorOutput keep local copies (weights identical)
findings.apertar_way: HW-I7: every GPIO user carries its own gpioChipScore (GpioInput.cpp:238, TriggerOutput.cpp:201, RecordingIndicatorOutput.cpp:198@upstream-1.6.0)
findings.why_it_matters: Half-shared code is harder to follow; GpioInput diff grows for no gain
findings.rework: Restore GpioInput's local gpioChipScore verbatim from upstream; keep the GpioChipInfo.cpp copy for the status card and headerGpioChipPath
findings.rework_risk: None

findings.title: GPIO input waits for kernel edge events instead of polling
findings.port_way: Lines requested with both edges; thread sleeps in poll() until an edge or ButtonGesture::nextWakeMs; falls back to poll_ms on chips without edge events (:744,856)
findings.apertar_way: HW-I4 (usually) sleep_for(pollMs) loop (GpioInput.cpp:740@upstream-1.6.0); precedent for poll() on a device fd in StandbyPowerButtonInput.cpp:51-56@upstream-1.6.0
findings.why_it_matters: Rewrites an upstream loop; desk-tested plus Pi build, edges confirmed on GPIO 6 and 10
findings.rework: Keep. Mention it in the handoff; keep the poll_ms row (F1) for chips without edge events
findings.rework_risk: None
findings.deliberate_evidence: KB decisions.md:41; 0c49601

findings.title: Comments carry Cinemate references, ticket numbers, history and stale statements
findings.port_way: 'the way Cinemate's SmartButton counts them (cinemate src/module/gpio_input.py)', 'Like Cinemate', 'T40', 'T42/T43', 'T44', 'every spelling the old normalizers accept', 'Call on every poll' (stale after 0c49601), 'The Outputs card reads this list' (nothing reads it)
findings.apertar_way: C1-I14: comments are rare sentences stating a hazard or reason; no ticket numbers
findings.why_it_matters: The original developer does not know Cinemate or the ticket numbers; stale comments mislead
findings.rework: Describe the timing in Apertar terms ('Press fires at once; releases within 500 ms count as clicks; held 3 s is Hold'); delete references, ticket numbers and history; fix the two stale comments
findings.rework_risk: None

findings.title: Status probes and scan_i2c read chips that the UI process polls (probable)
findings.port_way: cfeHatPeripheralJson probes bus 10 0x34 on every get_controls; scan_i2c holds only neorotary4/pcf8574/grove and reads every other address, including INA219 on bus 4
findings.apertar_way: HW-N5: the UI's Ina219Bridge (1 s timer) and CfeAutomounter poll these chips from another process, no lock; upstream Core never probes them
findings.why_it_matters: A one-byte read between another reader's register-pointer write and its read can return the wrong register; the header's own promise ignores UI drivers
findings.rework: Add the [ina219] and [cfexpress_hat] addresses to scan_i2c's held set as 'ui'. Report the hat from the automounter's state instead of probing it. No lock (HW-N5)
findings.rework_risk: Low

findings.title: get_controls parses the hardware file eight times per call
findings.port_way: hwconf::parse(info.text) called once per peripheral
findings.apertar_way: Plain local reuse; no precedent needed (C1-I17 is about local lambdas and does not apply)
findings.why_it_matters: Wasted work on a command the page polls
findings.rework: Parse once into const hwconf::Document doc and pass it to each peripheral
findings.rework_risk: None

HW-input-classes.summary: Skeptic pass: all 11 findings survive. 5 stand unchanged (F1, F4, F5, F8, F10); 6 are corrected (F2, F3, F6, F7, F9, F11). F1 (a wake press in Standby still triggers click and Hold actions) remains the only major. F2 is lowered to minor because it needs a button held at the moment of a read failure. Checking turned up one new fact: every Controls save that touches the GPIO/PCF group stops and restarts GpioInput (App:12302-12319). That re-applies switch positions, so a switch mapped to a toggle action (for example zebra) flips its setting on each save. This is added to F6. F7 is lowered to nit, because upstream itself uses setters on an internal CameraController class. F9 is lowered to nit and its rework changed: upstream App already writes WebUI saves to the editable path, so the only real hazard is the store creating a /home/pi file with only the IMU keys. F11 is corrected because the NeoRotary suffix array differs from the other two.

findings.title: Standby wake press seeds click/Hold gestures; upstream consumes the wake press
findings.port_way: ButtonGesture counts every press, including the one App swallowed to wake from Standby. emitAction is void, so the input class never learns of the wake. Single/Double/Triple/Hold fire later, with the camera awake, and run.
findings.apertar_way: StandbyPowerButtonInput.cpp:66-71@upstream-1.6.0 'gesture.consume(); // A wake press cannot seed another sleep.', callback std::function<bool(bool)> (StandbyPowerButtonInput.hpp:8,14). Upstream GpioInput fires Press only (GpioInput.cpp:691-710@upstream-1.6.0), so a wake press had no follow-up; App:4360@upstream-1.6.0 'a button press wakes only'.
findings.why_it_matters: d17=record_toggle, d17_hold=standby: holding d17 3 s in Standby wakes the camera and puts it back to sleep. d17_double=photo: a double click in Standby wakes and takes a photo.
findings.rework: Add ButtonGesture::consume() (clear clicks_, set longPress_ and holdFired_ while down). handleHardwareInputAction returns bool (true when it dispatched wake). Button ActionCallback in GpioInput, Pcf8574Input, NeoRotary4Input becomes std::function<bool(const std::string&)>; emitAction returns its result (false for an empty action); on true call gesture.consume(). Rotation callback stays void.
findings.deliberate_evidence: decisions.md gesture entries and commits 0a98868, c140c4f never mention Standby.
findings.rework_risk: With no Press mapped, the first gesture (Single/Hold) is the wake; consume must cover that path too.

findings.title: 1-0-1 inversion and switch start-apply re-run on every device reopen
findings.port_way: haveSample (PCF) and the rebuilt RuntimeButton/RuntimeSwitch vectors (GPIO) are reset on every reopen after a read or poll failure; invertedMask, RuntimeButton.inverted and switch stable=-2 are decided again. A button held then becomes inverted, a held 1-0-1 button loses its inversion, and every GPIO switch fires its position action again.
findings.apertar_way: Upstream reopen only re-seeds observed/stable state and keeps no polarity state (GpioInput.cpp:643-679,690-697@upstream-1.6.0; Pcf8574Input.cpp:479-505@upstream-1.6.0). decisions.md:39 limits the caveat to 'held down while Core starts'.
findings.why_it_matters: Shared I2C bus (INA219, CFE hat) gives read errors; a held record button then stays inverted until restart and each release toggles recording. Rare: needs a held button at the failing read.
findings.rework: Keep polarity and 'switch applied' in run-scope state outside the reopen block (per pin / per button index), decided on the first sample after start() only; reopen re-seeds observed/stable as upstream does.
findings.deliberate_evidence: Decision text says 'at Core start' only.

findings.title: Edge-event loop stops via a 250 ms idle wake, not an eventfd as upstream's poll() input does
findings.port_way: poll() with timeout at most 250 ms so stop() is noticed; a full readLineValues after every wake; every event in a batch stamped steady_clock::now().
findings.apertar_way: StandbyPowerButtonInput.cpp:16-31,50-56@upstream-1.6.0: eventfd stopFd_ polled next to the device with timeout -1; PowerButtonGesture.hpp:4@upstream-1.6.0 uses evdev timestamps. Upstream GpioInput itself sleeps pollMs (GpioInput.cpp:741@upstream-1.6.0).
findings.why_it_matters: The commit's aim (no periodic wake) is half met: the idle thread wakes 4 times a second. stop() can lag 250 ms, paid on every Controls save that restarts GPIO. Timestamps matter less: order is kept within a batch.
findings.rework: Add stopFd_ (eventfd) as in StandbyPowerButtonInput; stop() writes it; run() polls both fds with timeout = next debounce/gesture deadline or -1. Optionally use gpio_v2_line_event::timestamp_ns (CLOCK_MONOTONIC) as nowMs per edge.
findings.deliberate_evidence: decisions.md:41 and commit 0c49601 chose edge events; the stop and timestamp shape is not discussed.

findings.title: GpioInput::run() rebuilt around large capturing lambdas
findings.port_way: A capturing lambda of about 95 lines (process) and two smaller ones (sleepMs, toMs) inside run().
findings.apertar_way: GpioInput.cpp:621-745@upstream-1.6.0 is one straight loop with only a 4-line addOffset lambda; helpers are private members (readLineValues, emitAction, setLastError).
findings.why_it_matters: Reads as foreign and is harder to step through; the original developer expects member functions.
findings.rework: Private members, e.g. void processLevels(uint64_t levels, steady_clock::time_point now) and int wakeTimeoutMs(int64_t nowMs) const, with buttons/encoders/switches in a run-state struct or as members.

findings.title: Edge drain applies stale queued edges on top of a fresh full-level read
findings.port_way: Each wake reads at most 16 events, then always does a full readLineValues + process. Events 17..N, read on the next loop, set their bits absolutely onto a state that already holds the newer level.
findings.apertar_way: no precedent (upstream polls levels only)
findings.why_it_matters: Probable: on a fast encoder spin with more than 16 queued edges, old quadrature states are replayed, which gives spurious reverse steps. Not run on hardware.
findings.rework: Drain until read returns fewer than 16 events (poll timeout 0 or non-blocking read); do the catch-up full read only when the wake had no events.

findings.title: Switch positions apply toggle actions at start and on every Controls save; position and state drift
findings.port_way: [gpio_switches] applies the position action at each GpioInput start and on each change. GpioInput is restarted on every save that touches the GPIO/PCF group. The monitoring vocabulary consists of toggles (zebra, focus_peaking ... -> toggleSharedUiBoolAction).
findings.apertar_way: no precedent; upstream inputs fire on press edges only (GpioInput.cpp:691-710@upstream-1.6.0). Absolute settings exist only as parametric tokens (iso800, fps24, wb5600).
findings.why_it_matters: switch0_on=zebra, switch0_off=zebra, zebra saved on, switch in the on position: zebra turns off at Core start and flips again on every Controls save of the GPIO group.
findings.rework: Keep the switches. Enforce in the validator and the Controls page that switch positions take absolute actions only; if on/off are wanted, add *_on/*_off handlers in App that end in dispatch. Apply the start position only at Core start, not on Controls-worker restarts.
findings.deliberate_evidence: decisions.md:37,42 and commit c34f844 ('as in Cinemate'); the save-restart re-apply is not discussed.

findings.title: Seen callback injected by setter, not constructor
findings.port_way: setSeenCallback(ActionCallback) on three classes, called in App::start() before each start(), with comment '// T42 Listen'.
findings.apertar_way: Public hardware inputs take callbacks in the ctor (GpioInput.hpp:17@upstream-1.6.0; App:6785-6792@upstream-1.6.0 member-init list). Setters exist only on an internal class (CameraController.cpp:5020-5021@upstream-1.6.0).
findings.why_it_matters: It is a second wiring style. The unsynchronised member is safe only because it is set before start().
findings.rework: Add a ctor parameter ActionCallback seenCallback = {} to the three classes; pass [this](const std::string &k){ noteInputSeen(k); } in App's member-init list; delete the setters and the T42 comment.

findings.title: gpioChipScore half-shared: one moved, two private copies remain
findings.port_way: GpioInput calls hardware::gpioChipScore in GpioChipInfo.cpp; Trigger and LED keep their own copies.
findings.apertar_way: Each GPIO user carries its own gpioChipScore: GpioInput.cpp:238, TriggerOutput.cpp:201, RecordingIndicatorOutput.cpp:198@upstream-1.6.0.
findings.why_it_matters: It follows neither convention: a scoring change has to be made in three places, one of them in a new file.
findings.rework: Since GpioChipInfo stays for the Controls chip view (user request), make all three users call hardware::gpioChipScore and delete both output copies in one commit. Smaller alternative: restore the private copy in GpioInput.cpp and comment GpioChipInfo's copy as the page's mirror.
findings.deliberate_evidence: Commit 166cc4d moves the scoring so that GpioInput and the page pick the same chip; the outputs were not addressed.

findings.title: IMU writes can create a sparse ~/apertar-hardware.conf that shadows /boot/firmware
findings.port_way: writeHardwareConfigValues -> configStore().edit(...); the store path is env or /home/pi/apertar-hardware.conf; a missing file is treated as empty and created with only the IMU keys.
findings.apertar_way: The upstream IMU code wrote the loader's file, falling back to defaultHardwareConfigPath() (Mpu6050RecordingSession.cpp:1297-1300,1360-1362@upstream-1.6.0). Upstream App already writes WebUI saves to editableHardwareConfigPath() (App:4271-4276,5343@upstream-1.6.0), so the editable-path rule itself is upstream's.
findings.why_it_matters: Probable, rare: when the only file is /boot/firmware/apertar-hardware.conf, one calibration creates a /home/pi file holding only the [mpu6050] keys. The loaders read the first existing file, so every other setting is lost on the next start. The UI first-run template usually creates /home/pi first.
findings.rework: Keep the store. When the store file does not exist and the loader found another candidate, seed the store file from that file's text before the edit, or refuse with an error that names both paths.
findings.deliberate_evidence: Commit c509e9f: 'The store always writes the editable path, not whichever file the loader found.'

findings.title: Comments narrate Cinemate provenance and WebUI features inside src/hardware
findings.port_way: Comments such as 'Like Cinemate', 'cinemate src/module/gpio_input.py', "the WebUI's Listen", "the WebUI's Test button".
findings.apertar_way: Upstream hardware comments state behaviour only (PowerButtonGesture.hpp:4,26@upstream-1.6.0); no upstream src/hardware file mentions the WebUI.
findings.why_it_matters: The original developer does not know Cinemate. UI feature names in hardware headers leak app knowledge into src/hardware.
findings.rework: Rewrite each comment to state the behaviour and the reason; drop project and UI feature names.

findings.title: Seen-key suffixes chosen by static_cast of the gesture enum into parallel arrays, three copies
findings.port_way: static const char *const suffixes[] indexed by static_cast<size_t>(event), written three times; the NeoRotary copy starts with '_press', and GPIO replaces index 0 with pressSuffix.
findings.apertar_way: no precedent
findings.why_it_matters: If ButtonGesture::Event is reordered, Listen silently shows the wrong key.
findings.rework: Add one inline const char *gestureSuffix(ButtonGesture::Event) switch in ButtonGesture.hpp that returns '' for Press; callers add their own press suffix.

Boot-config.summary: I checked all 15 findings against the port and against upstream 1.6.0. None was dropped: 11 stand and 4 are corrected. F1: upstream already has a separate file-writing route that returns HTTP 400 (POST /api/config, App:7175-7195@upstream-1.6.0), so having a route of its own is not the mismatch. The mismatch is splicing "cmd" into the request body, the revision header, the 403/409 codes, the old-page rule keyed on the Origin header, and one setter reachable two ways. F8: lowered to nit, because every Pi OS config.txt has an [all] section. F9: I dropped the two-path claim, since /proc/device-tree is a symlink. F12: I dropped the "no wire names" part, because upstream socket errors name fields too ("set_fan_mode requires value."). F3 now notes that upstream already trusts the LAN for destructive actions, but never with free text written by root. F4 notes that HardwareConfigText.hpp has the same header-only shape across the port. Six commits are authored Claude, not three as the hint says. The Skeptic and Final findings sections are appended to the report.
conforms: Fan mode still uses fanModeBlock/stripManagedFanBlock unchanged and returns 'Changing the fan mode needs sudo permission.' (src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:3614-3649@cinemate-port)
bootConfigMutex() is a function-local static mutex, the same pattern as cacheMutex (src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:2269@upstream-1.6.0)
The engine edits config.txt in place and keeps every other byte, which matches upstream's own fan-block approach
The UI fan client uses the same synchronous QLocalSocket bridge shape as MediaStatusBridge (Apertar-UI src/MediaStatusBridge.cpp:20-42@upstream-1.6.0)

findings.title: Own POST /api/boot-config with cmd splice, revision header, 403/409 and an Origin-presence rule; one setter, two entry points
findings.port_way: The route splices "cmd":"set_boot_config" into the body and calls parseControlCommand. It takes the revision from the x-apertar-revision header, and browser = request.headers.count("origin") > 0 decides the old_page 409. bootConfigSet() runs under bootConfigMutex() and returns BootConfigReply{status, body} with 200/400/403/409/500. The socket set_boot_config command calls the same setter and drops the status. The page calls fetch("/api/boot-config") with its own header.
findings.apertar_way: A file-writing route of its own is precedented: POST /api/config -> saveHardwareConfigFile(request.body, ...), 400 on failure, okReply(-1, ...) (src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:7175-7195@upstream-1.6.0). Commands go handleWebCommand -> parseControlCommand -> handleCommand (src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:7085-7091@upstream-1.6.0). The page's fan mode is sendCommand({cmd:"set_fan_mode", value}) (src/web/WebControlPage.cpp:11093@upstream-1.6.0), handled inside handleCommand (src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:10568-10577@upstream-1.6.0). The origin policy is server-wide in allowedBrowserOrigin (src/web/WebServer.cpp:156-171@upstream-1.6.0). No upstream route reads custom headers or returns 403/409.
findings.why_it_matters: It is a parallel command plane for one card: body rewriting, a header protocol, a second error channel and an old-page rule that the original developer has nowhere else.
findings.rework: Delete POST /api/boot-config, BootConfigReply, the Origin test, the header and the 403/409 codes. get_boot_config and set_boot_config become ordinary handleCommand blocks with okReply/errorReply. commandMutex_ then serialises them with set_fan_mode, and bootConfigMutex() can go. revision, dry_run and confirm_display stay flat fields. WCP bootConfigPost -> sendCommand({cmd:"set_boot_config", ...}). A GET read route like GET /api/config may stay. Same as rev-App-1 F4 and rev-WCP-10 F1.
findings.deliberate_evidence: Comment at App:9178 'the command parser wants a name, so it gets one'; KB architecture/config.md 7.1 describes the 409/revision design; commit 2955ef8.
findings.rework_risk: The page loses HTTP-status handling and must read ok/error plus a code field from the reply.

findings.title: Root helper of a new shape plus three write routes, where upstream has one sudo -n install
findings.port_way: writeBootConfigText has three branches. First a direct write when access(W_OK) succeeds (own temp file + fsyncPath + rename). Else `sudo -n /usr/local/libexec/apertar-boot-config < staged`: a POSIX sh helper in Core scripts/ that takes the content on stdin, with sudoers `pi ALL=(root) NOPASSWD: ... ""` in Core config/ and no timeout. Else a sudo -n install fallback.
findings.apertar_way: Fan mode makes one call: `"sudo -n install -m 644 " + shellQuote(tempPath) + " " + shellQuote(kBootConfigPath)` (src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:3155-3158@upstream-1.6.0). Upstream root helpers take a fixed verb in their sudoers rule and live with the UI (systemd/apertar-standby-usb.sudoers and apertar-standby-low-power.sudoers in Apertar-UI@upstream-1.6.0). They are called as `/usr/bin/timeout 6s /usr/bin/sudo -n /usr/local/libexec/apertar-standby-usb <verb>` (src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:1544-1549@upstream-1.6.0). Upstream Core scripts/ holds only start-apertar-core.sh.
findings.why_it_matters: The README itself calls the helper optional ('Without it, Core falls back to sudo -n install, as the fan mode always has'). It adds install steps, a root interface that carries content (F3) and three paths to reason about.
findings.rework: writeBootConfigText = stage a temp file, `sudo -n install -m 644 <dest> <dest>.apertar.bak`, `sudo -n install -m 644 <tmp> <dest>`, and 'Writing config.txt needs sudo permission.' on denial. Delete scripts/apertar-boot-config, config/apertar-boot-config.sudoers, tools/boot_config_helper_test.sh, the direct branch (except a plain writeTextFileRaw for the APERTAR_BOOT_CONFIG test path), fsyncPath, kBootConfigHelper and the README install block. A future narrow helper follows the upstream helper shape: UI-side, a fixed verb in sudoers, timeout.
findings.deliberate_evidence: Commit dda1713 and helper header l.4-15; README l.199-207.
findings.rework_risk: Loses the fsync+rename atomicity on FAT; upstream install has the same property.

findings.title: set_boot_config text field writes any config.txt as root from any LAN client
findings.port_way: command.string("text") -> applyRequest(edited, ...) -> writeBootConfigText as root. The only checks are: non-empty, <= 64 KiB, no NUL, and one [pi5]/[pi4]/[all] line. kernel=, os_prefix=, initramfs and any overlay pass.
findings.apertar_way: 'Fixed executable and arguments only; never accept paths from WebUI/config.' (src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:1543@upstream-1.6.0). Upstream's root write of config.txt carries only the generated fan block (fanModeBlock, src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:3042@upstream-1.6.0). The free-text editor upstream is for apertar-hardware.conf, written as pi (saveHardwareConfigFile, src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:5323-5385@upstream-1.6.0). Upstream does trust the LAN for destructive acts (format_media, [run_script] paths), but never with free text written by root.
findings.why_it_matters: An unauthenticated LAN request can make the camera unbootable or boot another kernel.
findings.rework: Drop the text field, and with it Edit file / Use This Text, lineChanges, displayDiffers, textProblem and POST /api/boot-config/parse. Only lines generated from validated fields reach the file. View file and Download stay, read-only. Same as rev-App-1 F7 and rev-WCP-10 F3.
findings.deliberate_evidence: Commit 3b87d99 (Patrik Eriksson) adds the text field on purpose; README l.196.
findings.rework_risk: Removes a feature the owner added himself; needs his decision.

findings.title: 1355-line header-only engine; scope beyond what the card needs
findings.port_way: apertar::bootconf is header-only. It holds the board model, sensor and link tables with Mbps and 4K fps labels, Document/Editor, a 315-line applyRequest with read-back, an LCS lineChanges, stateJson/changesJson/jsonString and an FNV-1a revisionOf. On top come about 195 App lines and about 730 WCP JS lines.
findings.apertar_way: Upstream has no config.txt code beyond the fan block (fanModeBlock/stripManagedFanBlock/detectManagedFanMode, src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:3042-3117@upstream-1.6.0). Header-only modules upstream are small (src/hardware/ButtonActionList.hpp, 121 lines, and PowerButtonGesture.hpp@upstream-1.6.0). Larger hardware logic is a .hpp/.cpp pair listed in add_executable.
findings.why_it_matters: The original developer must review and maintain a small text-editing framework for one card. Most of the size serves the free-text editor and decoration, not the safe edits.
findings.rework: Keep the in-place approach: BCT l.8-13 weighs it against Cinemate's fenced block, and a managed block would still have to comment out the image's [pi5] sensor lines. Keep parse, readState, and applyRequest with read-back for sensor/link/toggles/RP1/display. Drop lineChanges, displayDiffers, textProblem and managed (with F3), and mbpsPerLane/fps4k/linkOptionLabel (keep a list of Hz values only). Move JSON to App (F6). Make it src/hardware/BootConfig.{hpp,cpp} with the .cpp in CMakeLists.txt; decide this together with the port's HardwareConfigText.hpp (1141 lines, same shape). Target about 600-700 lines.
findings.deliberate_evidence: BCT header l.2-28; KB architecture/config.md 7.1; working/handoff-boot-config.md.
findings.rework_risk: The host test must then link the .cpp; the read-back safety must survive the cut.

findings.title: include camera-selection.txt is invisible; the image's sensor mechanism is bypassed
findings.port_way: lineFrom returns no key for a line without '=', so `include camera-selection.txt` never counts. The card writes dtoverlay sensor lines in config.txt itself. The fixture keeps the image comment 'remove the "include camera-selection.txt" line' with the include already removed.
findings.apertar_way: 'Apertar's camera-selection file is authoritative ...' scanBinaryFileForSensorToken("/boot/firmware/camera-selection.txt", 4096) (Apertar-UI src/DeviceInfoBridge.cpp:213-215@upstream-1.6.0).
findings.why_it_matters: Probable on a fresh image (the stock image is not in this container). The card shows no sensor. Saving IMX585 uncomments a second overlay while the included file still loads one, and the read-back passes because it does not see the include.
findings.rework: In readState, an uncommented include line that applies to this board makes the camera rows read-only, with one sentence ('config.txt includes camera-selection.txt: the sensor comes from that file.') in the same shape as state.problem. Settle it with `grep -n '^include' /boot/firmware/config.txt` on a fresh Apertar-Beta 1.6.0 image. Same as sweep-board-support X-3.
findings.deliberate_evidence: No KB note weighs the include.

findings.title: Engine in src/hardware writes wire JSON with its own jsonString
findings.port_way: jsonString re-implements escapeJson. stateJson nests board{}, cameras{}, toggles{}, rp1{}, display{overlays[],lines[]}, candidates{}, sensors[{link{options[]}}], displays[], warnings[] and managed[]. App adds drm[] and changes[].
findings.apertar_way: Replies are built in App with std::ostringstream and escapeJson (declared in src/ipc/ControlProtocol.hpp:25, used at src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:108-128@upstream-1.6.0). No upstream src/hardware/ file writes reply JSON. One nested object per topic is precedented (imuStatusBody, src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:130@upstream-1.6.0), and arrays appear in web-route bodies (/api/media).
findings.why_it_matters: A second JSON writer, and knowledge of the wire format inside a hardware module.
findings.rework: Move serialisation into App as bootConfigBody(state) using escapeJson. One "boot_config":{...} object, with scalars plus the fixed option lists. Labels go on the page. drm[] -> a count of connected DPI connectors. rev-App-1 F9.

findings.title: Touch UI fan mode now fails when Core is not running
findings.port_way: UI 41ff827 deletes fanModeBlock, stripManagedFanBlock and the install write. It sends set_fan_mode over a private QLocalSocket (id 42002, 8 s timeout). With the socket down: 'Connect to Apertar Core before changing the fan mode.'
findings.apertar_way: Each process carries its own fan writer (src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:3042-3165 vs Apertar-UI src/SystemActionBridge.cpp:64-100@upstream-1.6.0). The touch UI changes the fan mode without Core.
findings.why_it_matters: A behaviour change the original developer must know of. It is justified only while Core edits other lines of the same file: a UI write outside Core's lock can overwrite a Boot Config save.
findings.rework: Keep it if the owner accepts the dependency, and document it in the handoff. The client follows upstream's synchronous QLocalSocket bridge pattern (MediaStatusBridge.cpp:20-42@upstream-1.6.0). Verify on the Pi; the commit says 'build only'.
findings.deliberate_evidence: Commit 41ff827 body: 'a fan change could race a Boot Config save'.

findings.title: Helper refuses a config.txt without [pi5]/[pi4]/[all], fan mode included
findings.port_way: The helper exits 2 without one of the three headers. Core returns its text and does not fall through, and applyFanMode uses this writer.
findings.apertar_way: applyFanMode writes any non-empty config.txt (src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:3127-3165@upstream-1.6.0).
findings.why_it_matters: A regression on paper only: every Raspberry Pi OS / Apertar config.txt has [all].
findings.rework: Goes away with F2. If the helper stays, drop the section check. rev-App-1 F12, sweep-board-support X-11.

findings.title: Board model: unknown board read as Pi 5, Zero 2 W counted as pi3, link list trimmed only on Pi 4
findings.port_way: `if (!board.detected) board.family = "pi5";`. Family pi3 is used for every bcm2837/2710, so [pi3] lines count on a Zero 2 W. linkOptionsFor trims only for pi4, so a Pi 3 gets the Pi 5 list.
findings.apertar_way: pipelineFromCompatible returns Unknown for an unknown board (src/camera/DefaultTuningSelection.hpp:18-31@upstream-1.6.0).
findings.why_it_matters: The card can edit the wrong section, or offer a link rate the stock driver may refuse, giving no camera after reboot. Probable: the firmware filter docs and kernel source are not in this container.
findings.rework: Unknown board -> editable=false with a sentence (the Pi 5 reading only for the test path). [pi3] does not apply on a Zero 2 W. The link list is offered only for the pi5 family, the default rate otherwise. sweep-board-support X-4, X-6.

findings.title: Two config.txt readers with two filter rules; second boolean parser
findings.port_way: The Controls validator uses hwconf::parseConfigTxt, which applies [all]/[pi5] only. bootconf::isDpiOverlay copies its name rule ('Same rule as HardwareConfigText's parseConfigTxt') but uses board-aware filters. boolFieldValue accepts on/yes/off/no and returns a tri-state.
findings.apertar_way: Upstream reads each file one way. Booleans use `== "true" || == "1"` (src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:9486@upstream-1.6.0).
findings.why_it_matters: On a Pi 4 the Controls check and the Boot Config card give different DPI answers for the same file.
findings.rework: The Controls validator takes the DPI lines from bootconf::readState(...) with the detected board. Delete the DPI part of parseConfigTxt. boolFieldValue -> the upstream test.

findings.title: Sensor list lacks IMX283 although the port supports it
findings.port_way: The comment says 'The sensors Core has handling for (CameraController detectSensorFamily: imx577, imx477, imx294, imx585)'. There is no imx283 entry.
findings.apertar_way: Hand-copied option lists must follow the sensor support. The port's detectSensorFamily returns Imx283 (src/camera/CameraController.cpp:2569-2570@cinemate-port), and the imx283 driver ships imx283-overlay.dts.
findings.why_it_matters: Failing input: cam0 `dtoverlay=imx283,cam0`. The card shows an unlisted sensor and cannot switch to IMX585 and back.
findings.rework: Add {"imx283","imx283","IMX283",false,0,0,{}} and fix the comment.

findings.title: Permission error carries install commands; wrong advice when the helper exists without sudoers
findings.port_way: 'Writing config.txt needs root. Install the helper: sudo install -m 0755 ... then sudo install -m 0440 ...'. With the helper installed but sudoers missing: sudo refuses without an 'apertar-boot-config:' line, the install fallback fails on 'password', and the operator gets the same 'Install the helper' advice.
findings.apertar_way: 'Changing the fan mode needs sudo permission.' (src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:3164@upstream-1.6.0); install steps live in the README. Field names in socket errors are upstream style ('set_fan_mode requires value.', src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:10571@upstream-1.6.0), so those stay.
findings.why_it_matters: The operator sees shell commands, and the advice is wrong in the half-installed case.
findings.rework: After F2: 'Writing config.txt needs sudo permission.' rev-App-1 F8.

findings.title: Header essay with Cinemate history, section banners, per-field comments, non-ASCII label glyphs, sh-style helper
findings.port_way: 'Ported from Cinemate's settings-editor config.txt tab (cinemate src/module/app/boot_config.py)'; 'Cinemate's resources/sensors.json: the will127534 IMX585 driver table'. 8 `// ----` banners in BCT and 1 in App. A trailing comment on nearly every field. Labels with U+00B7 and U+2014. The helper uses #!/bin/sh, [ ] and set -u.
findings.apertar_way: Upstream has rare one-line hazard comments, no history of other projects and no banners in App. Scripts use #!/bin/bash + set -euo pipefail (scripts/start-apertar-core.sh@upstream-1.6.0). Upstream App has 2 non-ASCII lines (U+2022, src/ApertarCoreApp.cpp:2366@upstream-1.6.0).
findings.why_it_matters: It reads as ported Cinemate code in its own documentation register.
findings.rework: Header to two lines. Delete the banners and Cinemate references. Keep the hazard comment at BCT:950. ASCII labels. The helper is removed with F2.

findings.title: Host tests for engine and helper
findings.port_way: A plain g++ test with the dev Pi's file as fixture, and an sh test of the helper on a scratch copy. Neither is in CMake.
findings.apertar_way: Upstream Core has no tools/ dir, no tests and no test target.
findings.why_it_matters: New ground. Acceptable only as an owner decision for the port's tools/ as a whole (15 *_test.cpp files).
findings.rework: Keep the C++ test outside the build if tools/*_test.cpp stays for the port. Drop the helper test with F2.
findings.deliberate_evidence: Commits f19b245, dda1713; KB 7.1 lists both tests.

findings.title: README lists socket commands; commits authored Claude with a claude/* merge
findings.port_way: The README ends with a list of socket commands and fields. Six commits are authored 'Claude', and 4581a69 (Patrik) merges claude/cool-volta-y7fiw7.
findings.apertar_way: The upstream README stops at the CLI launch flags. Upstream history is linear, with no claude/* merges.
findings.why_it_matters: Commit and README hygiene for the merge.
findings.rework: Drop the socket-command paragraph. Linearise and re-author in the commit-clarity step.

commits-core-1.summary: 95 linear commits (0 merges in this half; the 10 merges are commits 146-167). About 45 features, about 20 fixes of earlier commits in the same series, 4 reverts or undo pairs, about 15 wording-churn commits and 7 build fixes. All 95 carry Co-Authored-By (Claude Opus 5.5 / Sonnet 5.5) and Tested:. Original Apertar has one release commit with neither. 55 of 95 Tested: lines say desk only or built on the Pi next. Bodies cite 9 SHAs that no longer exist, tutorial numbers (T20..T51, Q2), clip ids and "User, date". Two commits are stated as not building (80ddac1, 438a342) and one probably does not (e16033e). Tests named in Tested: (phase_lock_sim, ModeLadder host test) are not in the tree. The proposed clean series folds the 95 old commits into 34 new ones; 8 old commits need a split. Nothing was rewritten.

findings.title: Commits that do not compile on their own
findings.detail: 80ddac1 declared phaseLockStatus in the libcamera-only private section; 8f7dc39 body: 'is private within this context'. 438a342 put encoder.abandon() in dngWorkerLoop (CdngEncoder has no abandon()); e8bb1b7 body says the build failed. e16033e adds std::vector<double> ladderTops to Types.hpp without the include; 62c1711 adds it (probable break, depends on include order). 80ddac1 and 438a342 say 'not built'. A no-libcamera build hides errors in the #if APERTARCORE_HAS_LIBCAMERA branch.
findings.fix: Fold 8f7dc39 into 80ddac1, e8bb1b7 into 438a342, 62c1711 into e16033e. Build every new commit on the Pi with libcamera on, not only the OFF configuration.

findings.title: Add-then-remove and flip-flop pairs
findings.detail: e58ae40 then fee41e6 is exactly nil (16 b then 16-bit, body 'reverts 5d06b67'). 97adea0 then bcedbe5 is not nil: it leaves fps_max in both state JSONs, losslessMaximumFps/modeMaximumFps/maximumFpsForSettings, and ClearHdrIsoLimits renamed CameraSection (loadCameraSection, cameraSection) although the struct now only holds two ISO maxima (git diff 97adea0^ bcedbe5). Colour rule goes green (e25fd2b), white (15bba86), italic (e58e7e5). FPS coverage bar added in 1ef94fe, removed in b21c76a; red x added in 920beb0/1ef94fe, removed in 8050d56.
findings.fix: Drop 48/49. Fold 43/44 into one 'publish fps_max' commit without the rename. Fold the colour chain into one commit stating the final rule. Drop the coverage bar and red x from the series.

findings.title: Chain of 36 WebUI wording and tweak commits around the Mode Ladder
findings.detail: Commits 58-89 are almost all WebControlPage.cpp, one design iterated live: threshold chip then editable max, Save button then autosave, order rules rewritten three times (b8ee23f, 8bcc5dd, 25f553e), 'rung' to 'resolution' in two commits (a7b6f82, cdf83cd). 1ef94fe alone is +1537/-493 and rewrites the editor from 920beb0. Reviewing this as is means reading each intermediate design.
findings.fix: Fold into three web commits by card (Value Lists, Speed Ramp, Mode Ladder with Activated sensor modes), final design only. See new 27-30 in the report.

findings.title: fsync/writeback experiments committed as a chain
findings.detail: syncfs per second (4ce382e), then per-file sync_file_range (441e42a), then folder fsync instead of syncfs (7d9dd60), then per-file fsync on the sync thread (5b68f1f), then audio raw fsync (b606c4f). Each Why cites a measured run (C0001..C0011) that refutes the previous step. The final design is 441e42a + 7d9dd60 + 5b68f1f + b606c4f; 4ce382e's syncfs is not in it.
findings.fix: One commit 'rec: write the take through to the card once a second'; keep the measurement as numbers in the body, drop clip ids.

findings.title: Media tuning shipped, then switched off; privileged helper has no upstream precedent
findings.detail: 26da30e adds a root helper, sudoers and tmpfiles files plus MediaProfile.hpp and applies tuning on every mount. 0358fcf reverts the exFAT row to Core's pre-profile {4,12,0}. ebdcd08 body: 'T29's root helper is not installed and not needed' and makes it opt-in (APERTAR_MEDIA_TUNE=1). Upstream Core scripts/ holds only start-apertar-core.sh and config/ only apertar-core-capture-priority.conf (confirmed).
findings.fix: Fold 26da30e/0358fcf/ebdcd08 into one media-profile commit; ask the owner whether the helper, sudoers and tmpfiles stay (opt-in) or go.

findings.title: Tutorial numbers and internal ids in subjects and bodies
findings.detail: Subjects carry (T33), (T34), (T47), (T48), (T49). Bodies carry T20..T51, Q2, clip ids C0001..C0106, 'User, 2026-10-28', 'apertar.local', 'on the Mac', a KB path (b5847c7: working/research-30fps-answer.md), 'T27 reference patch, applied unchanged'. Meaningless to the original developer (BRIEF vocabulary). Nine bodies cite SHAs that do not exist in the repo (775083f, 76094a9, 47d44ff, 71487c5, 84081f7, a89a5df, 6c34e8a, 5d06b67, 753f181), so the cross-references cannot be followed.
findings.fix: New subjects without numbers; bodies state what and why in plain words, numbers kept as measurements, no ids, no stale SHAs.

findings.title: Co-Authored-By and Tested: trailers on every commit; Tested: text is a run log
findings.detail: 95/95 have Co-Authored-By (Claude Opus 5.5 on 2-55, Claude Sonnet 5.5 on 1 and 56-95) and Tested:. Upstream history is one commit '1.6.0 Release' with no trailers or body; the fork's 8 earlier commits have no trailers either. 55 Tested: lines say 'desk only', 'built on the Pi next' or 'pi build (see next run)': they describe a later run, not the commit. Tested: also names tests that are not in the tree (phase_lock_sim.cpp in 80ddac1; 'ModeLadder host test 28/28 .. 38 checks' in 88e644d, 0041ba0, a7b6f82, cdf83cd, 3cae990, e16033e): no tools/*ladder* or *phase* file exists at cinemate-port.
findings.fix: Owner decides whether trailers stay. If they stay, Tested: says what was run on that commit. Commit the host tests the messages cite or drop the claims.

findings.title: Mixed-purpose commits
