findings.detail: 438a342 writers + audio + probe + App watcher + WCP, 14 files +810. 0358fcf reverts the exFAT row and the audio ring default in one commit. ebdcd08 joins media-tuning opt-in and the audio drift fit with ';'. 8175273 Clear HDR hold and ISO caps. ac00fb0 speed-ramp block and preset switches. e25fd2b colour, ISO list and ISO lock. b0e90ad value lists, free stepping and flicker-free angles. b5b787e Core auto-ISO rule and WebUI Auto offer. 1ef94fe three cards. 909aaa5 Core and web. 1af26c8 /api/media/frame plus vendored third_party/liblj92 (4 files, ~1400 lines).
findings.fix: Split these along the lines in the report; the plan needs interactive staging for 11, 16, 19, 25, 29, 55, 71, 93.

findings.title: b5b787e reverses a 1.6.0 behaviour inside a mixed commit
findings.detail: b5b787e body: 'Upstream kept lossless on manual ISO (1.6.0)'; enforceLosslessCaptureLimits now keeps auto ISO on IMX585 and the WebUI offers Auto wherever Clear HDR is off. Its Tested: line says 'Unverified: a tuning file with a higher AGC gain would let auto ISO pass the lossless cap'. 2f43ecc raises the lossless ISO cap from 800 to 1600 in a 1-line commit. Both change stock ISO behaviour and are buried in the middle of an unrelated series.
findings.fix: Own commit with a subject that says 'changes lossless ISO behaviour from 1.6.0'; owner confirms.

findings.title: Subjects that do not say what changed, and prefix mismatches
findings.detail: e16033e 'the ladder tells the editor more (T34 UI design)'; 1ef94fe '... per the approved design'; 909aaa5 'the UI timecode and the file timecode are set apart'; 4b04a1d 'one naming pattern for sections and modes'. 3c4f07d is prefixed web: but touches only ApertarCoreApp.cpp; 60645d4 is prefixed hw: but touches only ApertarCoreApp.cpp. ab4cc92 repeats what f91fafa's body already says (list answers from the cache).
findings.fix: New subjects name the setting, field or endpoint and use the prefix of the file that changed.

findings.title: New ground with no Apertar upstream precedent introduced in this half
findings.detail: Core upstream has no third_party/ tree (BRIEF). 1af26c8 adds third_party/liblj92 (lj92.c 1275 lines, LICENSE, README.apertar.md) inside a commit that also adds /api/media/frame. 0b1632f adds CfeHat.hpp (I2C slot bit read, [cfexpress_hat] config) as a header-only util instead of in a hardware class. Pure-logic header-only classes (FramePhaseLock, ModeLadder, MediaProbe, MediaFault, MediaIntent, ClipFrames, ClipProbe, PlaybackHold) have no .cpp counterpart as upstream classes do.
findings.fix: Separate 'build: vendor liblj92' commit for owner approval; document the header-only pure-logic pattern or move hardware reads into the hardware class.

findings.title: Unrelated small commits inside topic chains
findings.detail: 086443c (recording event broadcast) sits inside the media chain; d7ff071 (conform_fps) between speed ramp and ladder; 60645d4 (WB dial) among ISO changes. Each is a clean one-purpose commit but out of place, so git log neighbours suggest a relation that does not exist.
findings.fix: Order the clean series by topic (new 11, 19, 18).

commits-core-2.summary: 92 commits (81 Patrik, 11 authored "Claude", 10 merges). Not one clean series: side branches, hunks swapped between 04bac89/e0fa852, one 12-feature squash (d44b177), 12 subjects with T-numbers, 3 trailer names, cherry-pick trailers to absent commits, and env-knob commits superseded by later ones. Proposed 52 clean commits in 7 blocks (B build fix, N controls/viewer/layout, D drop-frames/media, E boot config, W write path, S sensors, P split clips). d44b177 splits by path only for its new files (about 2000 of 5170 lines); the rest needs git add -p.

findings.title: d44b177 squashes 12 features under a 7-feature subject
findings.detail: One commit, 25 files, +5170 -100, 'Squashed from 19 commits'. Subject names trim, Log, RAM buffer, safety stop, buffer bar, fps max, pre-roll. Body also holds lossless JPEG fps cap lift, speed ramp After-the-take, Clear HDR override of the ladder, WebUI search box, white GPIO dropdowns, Tally card. Body says the pre-roll and Clear HDR override were not compiled or run. Cannot be reviewed or bisected.
findings.fix: Split into D4 fps max, D2 Log, D1 trim, D3 RAM buffer+safety stop+bar, D5 pre-roll, D6-D10. New files split by path (LogCurve.hpp, BufferBudget.hpp, StoragePreroll.hpp, FpsCeiling.hpp, apertar-media-trim, tests: about 2000 lines). ApertarCoreApp.cpp (+881), CameraController.cpp (+882), WebControlPage.cpp (+1422, 97 hunks in one function), Types.hpp, README need git add -p; mixed hunks in buildWebStateJson, settingsBody, the handleCommand record gate, settings persistence. Fallback: keep RAM buffer, pre-roll, ramp, override as one honestly named commit.

findings.title: Message and diff disagree: 04bac89 and e0fa852 carry each other's hunks
findings.detail: 04bac89 says trim after outside delete and after every pre-roll delete; its diff holds only the media-watcher trimMedia('free-space') hunk. e0fa852 says noatime/umask on the re-insert mount; its diff also changes the pre-roll trim to trimMedia('delete'). 766aba8 admits it and says the branch is not rewritten.
findings.fix: In the clean series put the free-space trim and the pre-roll trim in D1 (media trim) and the mount options alone in W3.

findings.title: Tutorial and work-package numbers and 'part N' in subjects
findings.detail: 12 subjects carry T36, T37, T38, T50, T51; 3 more say 'Controls page, part N'. T38 has parts 1,2,3,5. 21 commits carry T/Q/R/design-section numbers in the body. Meaningless to the original developer.
findings.fix: Rewrite subjects in upstream style (core:, web:, media:) saying what changed; move design numbers out; squash part halves into N5-N9.

findings.title: Controls page and gestures rewritten four times; page and Core halves in separate commits
findings.detail: WebControlPage.cpp Controls card written in 110, rewritten in 115, 118, 120 (about +1345 -446 lines); GPIO gestures polled in 114 then replaced by edge events in 116 in the same files; 114, 117, 121, 122 each bundle 3 to 8 features; 96+97, 105+106, 109+110 are page/Core halves.
findings.fix: Squash to final form per feature: N9 Controls card, N11 gestures+edge events, N12 I2C/Hardware card, N13 switches, N14 apply/Listen/history split by hunk. Core and web in the same commit.

findings.title: Merges of side branches hide conflict resolution and one is pure noise
findings.detail: 10 merges. 389f8a7 (author Claude) merges drop-frames into keen-bardeen only to shrink a PR (3187 lines, same content as 4b2eeac). 163 and 164 resolve conflicts in CameraController.cpp and WebControlPage.cpp inside the merge commit. 154-156 carry only 'Merge pull request #N'.
findings.fix: Linearise; drop 389f8a7 and 5e25f69; redo the conflict hunks of a47dc28 and dd00206 by hand and review them as ordinary commits; move build fix 5f5cea2 to the front.

findings.title: Behaviour added then reversed inside the series
findings.detail: 16-bit Clear HDR 25 fps cap added in d44b177 and caa0153, removed in 31d5418 which leaves '(void)settings; (void)sensorFamily;' and a comment naming 'User'. APERTAR_DNG_DONTNEED default writer (0ed07ea) flipped to sync (adac040). IMX585 whitelists (900d282) replaced by tables (caa0153). Hardware template fixed in 4d80a35 and again in 7af9f13.
findings.fix: Fold 31d5418 into D8, adac040/48f8b8c into W4 with final default only, 900d282 into S1 keeping the 3840x2072/1920x1036 migration, 7af9f13 into N6. Remove the dead (void) stubs.

findings.title: Env-knob commits made moot by later commits
findings.detail: APERTAR_RT (139) superseded by APERTAR_RT_CAPTURE_PRIORITY (144); PAYLOAD_COPY, WRITE_ROWS (132) and RAW_POOL_WARM (134) are A/B levers on fixed behaviour; DONTNEED (140) default flipped by 168; the media tune file (170, 171) makes env knobs redundant ('environment variables still win'); APERTAR_MEDIA_TRIM (124) is duplicated by set_media_trim (179); APERTAR_CDNG_FRAMES_PER_FOLDER and APERTAR_STORAGE_PREROLL duplicate hardware-file keys. Confirmed with git grep at cinemate-port.
findings.fix: Drop 139 and 144 (empty after knob removal), strip knobs from W1, W2, W4, P1; keep W5 and W6 only on owner decision; follow verdicts in sweep-knobs.md.

findings.title: Eleven commits authored 'Claude' and three trailer names
findings.detail: 11 of 92 commits have author 'Claude'. Trailers: Co-Authored-By Claude Opus 5.5 x54, Sonnet 5.5 x26, Fable 5.1 x9; 20 Claude-Session URLs. 3 cherry-pick trailers (a344376, 69a700e, 6bd002b) and a body reference to 00f2327 point at commits that are not in this repo. Bodies reference KB paths, 'the campaign branch', 'the temp branch', 'User'.
findings.fix: Re-author under the owner; one trailer form or none; no session URLs; drop cherry-pick lines and KB-only references when the series is rewritten.

findings.title: Subjects that say nothing or use a branch name as prefix
findings.detail: 766aba8 'fixes from the review of the seven commits above'; afa00e8 'wrap the DRM note' without body; f19b245 'config.txt engine'; rows 124-128 use the branch name 'drop-frames:' as prefix and 127/128 are not about dropped frames; fb557e9, 1319967, 9b5ea14 use 'web:' but change Core; 116/117/119 use 'hw:', 129-136 use 'WebUI:', 'Core:', 'README:'.
findings.fix: Use upstream/fork prefixes (core:, web:, camera:, cdng:, media:, rec:, scripts:, build:); 'core, web:' when both change; fold small fixes into their feature.

findings.title: Dead-code and not-run commits in the series
findings.detail: 3526e4b adds the store with 'Nothing in Core calls the new code yet'; f19b245 adds a 1228-line BootConfigText.hpp with no caller until 2955ef8; a37a902 and fa19856 say 'Pi build pending'; d44b177 says part of it was never compiled or run. Intermediate commits are not shown to build or work.
findings.fix: Combine each header with its first caller (N5, E1+E2); take the build check per new commit with the libcamera-off build.

findings.title: Commit bodies hold behaviour changes the subject hides
findings.detail: 916c1dd: 'isoinf and isonan are refused now' inside a refactor; 243fe2c: new action plus label fix; 5395fa4: socket line limit 64 KiB to 1 MiB inside a Config-page commit; dcf09ee: 'Renames: Adafruit rotary 0-3, switch positions' buried after five features; c48e693: Clear HDR cleared before start() when no imx585 is on the bus, inside the IMX283 commit; 131: fan write path rewritten inside get/set_boot_config.
findings.fix: Give each its own commit or name it in the subject.

findings.title: Unrelated features and layout churn placed between others
findings.detail: Timecode rename (113) sits inside the Controls series; Clip browser Loading text (123) after the Controls page; Value Lists move (172) and Modes pane (173) are layout moves; 166 fixes a first-half Mode Ladder page; clip names (127) and audio outline (128) are under 'drop-frames:'.
findings.fix: Order by feature: N10, N17, S5 stand alone or fold into the feature they touch.

findings.title: Tests and A/B data referenced only in bodies
findings.detail: Bodies rely on KB research ids (R2-R8, V/H15, working/dng-chain) and measured dates; the original developer cannot read them. Tests ride inside the feature commits (buffer_budget_test, log_curve_test, ...) which Apertar upstream does not have.
findings.fix: Keep one sentence of measured reason; drop research ids; test files follow the tests decision in the other sweeps.

findings.title: Controls, boot-config and split-clip features are large new ground bundled in drive-test commits
findings.detail: HardwareConfigStore (1617 lines), BootConfigText (1228), TuningTdnStrip (451), ClipMerge worker (796), MediaTune (318) have no upstream precedent. They appear as ordinary feature commits with no note for the original developer.
findings.fix: Keep as separate commits N5, E1, S6, P2, W6 with a decision flag and a short design note in the body; owner decides keep, off by default, or drop.

commits-ui-drivers.summary: UI: 39 commits classify as 18 feature, 1 squash, 6 fix of an earlier one, 4 wording churn, 5 revert, 5 experiment. The four preview experiments and their four drops net to nil: git diff c234d77 c153c33 is empty, CMakeLists and main.cpp included, with no leftover names in src/ or qml/. A ninth knob, APERTAR_UI_PREVIEW_RECORDING_FPS (c234d77), was kept. The UI still caps 4K Clear HDR 16-bit at 25 fps (CameraPage.qml:822) after Core removed that cap in 31d5418. A clean UI series is 15 commits, each paired with its Core commit. imx585 (55 commits) and imx283 (93) are mostly experiment-and-fix steps and need one squashed mode-set commit per driver plus a docs commit. Both drivers: install cinemate-port. imx585 README.md still describes 7 modes under a gone branch name, cinemate-7modes, while APERTAR.md says 187 modes. Neither README links APERTAR.md.

findings.title: Eight preview experiment commits net to nothing but stay in history
findings.detail: git diff c234d77 c153c33 is empty, CMakeLists.txt and main.cpp included. Eight commits add and remove about 1 037 lines. No leftover names (PREVIEW_PLANE, PREVIEW_DIRECT, PREVIEW_PEAKING, uFastPeaking, uOverlayOnly, DrmPreviewPlane) in src/ or qml/ at cinemate-port. The drop commits say 'park it on preview-plane / drop-count'; those branches are not in this clone (whether they exist on GitHub is unconfirmed).
findings.fix: Leave all eight out of the clean series; rebuild the series from c234d77's parent. Keep the parked branches if the experiments matter.

findings.title: Touch UI caps 4K Clear HDR 16-bit at 25 fps; Core removed that cap
findings.detail: CameraPage.qml:822 returns 25.0 for 3840x2160 with Clear HDR at 16-bit, and the comment says 'as in Core's tableMaximumFpsForResolution()'. Core 31d5418 (2026-11-03) removed the 25 cap (4K 30, crops up to 42.4). d1efb67 (10-27) was not revisited. The touch UI offers less than Core and the WebUI allow. The same comment text is copied into ApertarCoreApp.cpp:1386.
findings.fix: Drop d1efb67 from the series. Have maximumSupportedFpsForResolution() follow Core's fps_max from state instead of a hard-coded table. Fix the stale comment in ApertarCoreApp.cpp:1386.

findings.title: UI preview-FPS env knob kept after its eight sibling experiments were dropped
findings.detail: APERTAR_UI_PREVIEW_RECORDING_FPS is a 'desk only' A/B knob like the dropped ones. It is the only APERTAR_* env var the port adds to the UI; the other APERTAR_* names in the UI are original. It mirrors Core's APERTAR_WEB_PREVIEW_RECORDING_FPS.
findings.fix: Decide with the Core knob sweep: drop both, or keep both and document them for the original developer. Keep c234d77 as its own commit either way.

findings.title: UI colour and label churn: green, white, italic; 16-bit, 16 b, 16-bit
findings.detail: The marking of camera-decided values changes three times in one day (green, then white/green, then italic). The resolution label goes '16-bit', '16 b', '16-bit'. Two fixes (b4591dc ISO fallback, 682a186 ISO Auto) correct f1edf96. A reader of the series sees decisions that were reversed.
findings.fix: Squash into one 'Value lists and camera-decided values' commit with the final state (italic, '16-bit').

findings.title: UI commits depend on Core commits and cannot merge alone
findings.detail: 41ff827 sends set_fan_mode and removes the UI's config.txt writer: needs Core 2955ef8 + dda1713 + f19b245 (Boot Config). c9d841f deletes both default hardware-file templates (578 lines): needs Core 4d80a35 and 014fa22, or no hardware file is ever created. 7ea9afc reads part_NNN folders: needs Core d7dd337. 841d0ed needs the drop-frames Core commit d44b177. 160898c needs Core 70e8376 (media_state). The full pairing table is in the report, section 1.1.
findings.fix: Merge each UI commit in the same release as its Core partner, Core first; use the 15-commit clean series in report section 1.6.

findings.title: UI commit bodies carry internal numbers, branch prefixes and 'not built' notes
findings.detail: Subjects and bodies use T33, T38 p4/p5, T31, T45 and the prefix 'drop-frames:' (a branch name, 5 commits). 841d0ed, d1efb67, 2d27c46 say not built or not compiled; c9d841f, 7c41a27 say the Pi build was not yet run. Every commit has a Co-Authored-By Claude line; 15 also a Claude-Session line. None of this means anything to Apertar-Studio.
findings.fix: Rewrite subjects in plain words, without T-numbers or branch prefixes, when building the clean series; build on the Pi before the merge and change the 'Tested' lines to what was tested.

findings.title: imx585 history is experiment-and-fix steps, with WP-585 numbers and 'experimental:' subjects
findings.detail: 55 commits, 4 by Will Whang and 51 by Patrik/Claude. 22 are crop-mode steps, 11 with the subject prefix 'experimental:'. Pure back-and-forth: sub-960 crops removed (234cccb), restored (475c3ea), then dropped (8f508fb); 16-bit binned crops added (b050b7c) and withdrawn (fdd767a); enum order fixed (7061c74) and restored (27c7cb4); crop metadata reported five times (b703f46, 74ed4c6, 951aeee, 24172e6, 97649ba); three README commits on one paragraph (e9d5759, 0af0293, bd57617). 13 subjects carry WP-585-n. No intermediate commit leaves a correct table, so bisect has no value.
findings.fix: Keep Will Whang's 4 commits; one squashed 'imx585: Cinemate mode set'; one tools/ commit; one docs commit (README.md, APERTAR.md). Subjects without WP numbers.

findings.title: imx283 history: one experiment in 11 commits ended by a revert, values flipped back and forth
findings.detail: 93 commits, 84 of them already on origin/cinemate-modes; the last 9 are Claude's fixes and docs. Back-and-forth: 6.12 build fix (24f7bf0), reverted (146d24f), redone in three commits (16de05f, 6f6410d, 5d1c193); active-only frames, two commits with the same subject (4350e3e, 4612d68), 9 fixes, ended by 'revert: restore IMX283 sensor crop window' (a852cfe); MODE_1C window 236, 924, 236, 924 (3c2310e, 812c058, de6693c, cb925e5); 18 fixed crops replaced by the aspect family (773c5bb); mode table rebuilt four times in six days. WP-283-1 to -6 appear in 6 subjects. 'Your Name' is the author of 050e2e3 and 289131a. origin/master lacks the 8 old base commits (probable: it is not Will's current master; git log origin/master -3 would settle it).
findings.fix: Keep the 8 base commits; one squashed 'imx283: Cinemate mode set'; keep 4a1662e (kernel oops fix, reword 'oopsing'), d810aa7, d6ec1c7, 4064e88, 257c9cf as own commits; one docs commit.

findings.title: imx585 README describes 7 modes under a gone branch; READMEs do not link APERTAR.md
findings.detail: Both drivers: install branch cinemate-port (APERTAR.md 'Which branch', README clone -b cinemate-port, Core CameraController.cpp:441-442 and Imx283Modes.hpp:1-2 name it). imx585 README.md:148 has a section 'CineMate branch (cinemate-7modes)' with a 7-mode matrix; APERTAR.md says 187 modes in four families. cinemate-7modes is not a branch in the clone, so cinemate-modes, cinemate-port and cinemate-7modes are three names for the driver. Neither README mentions APERTAR.md. The Apertar-Beta 1.6.0 image ships the old apertar branch, whose 1.85:1 crops (3840x2076, 1920x1038) differ from the 3840x2072 and 1920x1036 Core expects.
findings.fix: Rewrite or delete the cinemate-7modes section in the imx585 README; add 'Apertar users: see APERTAR.md' to both READMEs; state in the handoff that the image build must pull cinemate-port.

knobs.summary: All 19 findings were re-read on both sides. None was dropped. Four were downgraded. X-knobs-5 (the record gate) is now minor: upstream already treats an unmounted root as no media in the library, format and Sound Recorder code. X-knobs-7 (storage switches in the hardware file) is now minor: upstream commands also write single hardware keys (the set_imu_* commands, through Mpu6050RecordingSession). X-knobs-10 (the kernel-tune helper) is now minor: sudo env_reset drops the env path, and pi already has unrestricted sudo -n on upstream. X-knobs-14 (mode_ladder.conf) is now a nit: a separate file per concern has upstream precedent, so only the copied path function remains. X-knobs-1 is now a nit with its template leftover dropped: upstream Core's template has no chip= in [gpio] either, and knownKey only checks edits. X-knobs-9 got one evidence fix: APERTAR_RT was never measured, only judged the wrong shape. X-knobs-4 got a caveat on the fix: it needs a format change to re-run start(), which is probable. X-knobs-15 gained one item: the README names a private UI commit and a local branch. The blocker (X-knobs-2, the display fallback) holds, with its reach corrected: fresh installs and files without [display] keys.

findings.title: The display fallback is the contributor's HDMI rig
findings.detail: In the port, the UI fallback is 1920x1080, landscape_large, hdmi_external_only=true. Upstream it is 720x720, square, false (DisplayConfigBridge.cpp:14-15, :579, :584, :649@upstream-1.6.0). The port's UI no longer writes a default file (c9d841f); upstream wrote one (ensureDefaultHardwareConfigFile, :41, :587@upstream-1.6.0). With hdmi_external_only set, main.cpp:432-433@cinemate-port hides the main window. Who is hit: a fresh install, or any apertar-hardware.conf without [display] keys, shows no touch UI on the stock 720x720 panel. Cameras whose file the upstream UI wrote keep their explicit keys and are not affected. Core's template is only shown when the file is missing, never written (App:6201). Commits: Core 7af9f13, UI 7c41a27.
findings.fix: Put 720, 720, square and false back in the UI constants, in loadConfiguration, in the header members and in Core's defaultHardwareConfigTemplate. The HDMI rig keeps the 1920x1080 / landscape_large / hdmi_external_only=true values in its own [display] section. Whether to restore the first-run file write (c9d841f) is for the UI file reviewer to decide.

findings.title: The storage pre-roll runs by itself (default on)
findings.detail: automaticEnabled returns conf.automatic.value_or(true). Core then records a 2 s take at the sensor's maximum fps and deletes it at every Core start, card insert and format. Upstream has no pre-roll. The KB says 'no measurement exists' and 'the honest default is off for the automatic triggers' (working/dng-chain-answer.md:175, :186). The port's own plan said it would be a setting, 'default off at first', never a hidden step (working/drop-frames/README.md:341).
findings.fix: Change to value_or(false), make the template comment '# preroll=off', and add one README line. The manual storage_preroll command stays.

findings.title: preview_tdn=false also strips temporal denoise from H.264 and ProRes recordings
findings.detail: The strip in the loadablePath lambda does not test the record format. The ProRes colour tuning is derived from the stripped file (makeProresIspTuning(activePath, ...)). For H.264 and ProRes the ISP picture is the recording itself. So after the merge a stock camera records these two formats without temporal denoise, even with a tuning file the user picked. Upstream loads the tuning file as it is. The README mentions DNGs only.
findings.fix: Use: if (!settings.previewTdn && !isProcessedVideoFormat(settings.recordingFormat) && !settings.photoModeEnabled). The helper is at CC:280 and upstream has it too. First check that a format change re-runs start(): setRecordingFormat ends in applySettingsLocked(next, requiresReconfigure) at CC:11390 (probable). The alternative is bool previewTdn = true, which keeps upstream behaviour everywhere.

findings.title: A second bench-tuning mechanism beside upstream's .apertar-tuning
findings.detail: Each write-path knob resolves through four layers: env var, /run/apertar-media/media-tune.override.conf, ~/apertar-media-tune.conf, built-in default. The port adds new key names beside the env names, per-medium sections, a 318-line parser and a 487-line CLI. Upstream already has a mechanism for the same need: tuningOverride(name) reads the environment, then /home/pi/.apertar-tuning with the same APERTAR_* names, and re-reads it at clip open (src/prores/ProresEncoder.cpp:771-813@upstream-1.6.0). In the port, dontneed and writeback are read once per process, so a change still needs a restart. Three texts disagree on when the file is read. MediaTune.hpp:5 names tools/media_tune_test.cpp, which does not exist. The owner asked for this file (2026-11-02), so removing it is his decision.
findings.fix: Move tuningOverride() to src/util/TuningOverride.hpp. Let unsignedEnvValue and boolEnvValue (CC:1341, :1357) call it. Read APERTAR_DNG_DONTNEED and APERTAR_DNG_WRITEBACK per take. Delete MediaTune.hpp, the template, scripts/apertar-tune, the override file and the README section. Keep writerSettingsFor() as the per-medium table. If the owner keeps the file, drop the override layer and the CLI, and document the file for the original developer.

findings.title: Experiment leftovers among the env vars (27 names, RT scheduling, LimitRTPRIO)
findings.detail: 27 of the env vars the port adds are restore switches, reverted experiments or constants nobody ever set (sweep-knobs.md Table A). APERTAR_RT_CAPTURE_PRIORITY was measured with 'no effect' (lessons/hardware-log.md:954). APERTAR_RT was never measured; the KB judges it 'wrong shape, control arm only' (working/dng-chain/F/F3.md:166). LimitRTPRIO=80 now sits under upstream's own comment 'Permit only a bounded, non-real-time boost'. Upstream bench knobs are env-only, read with unsignedEnvValue / boolEnvValue, and absent from the README.
findings.fix: Delete the 27 names listed in Table A, the APERTAR_RT block of the start script and LimitRTPRIO. Make the never-set knobs constants. Keep 15 developer-only knobs in upstream's form.

findings.title: The record gate's opt-out is an undocumented env var
findings.detail: record_start, capture_photo and timelapse_start are refused when the media root is not a mount point or has less than 1024 MiB free. Upstream does not gate recording (App:9090-9110@upstream-1.6.0). But upstream already treats an unmounted root as no media in the library, format and Sound Recorder code (App:7676, :8970, :8351@upstream-1.6.0), so the gate fits upstream's model, and a stock camera with its drive mounted sees no change. The problem is the opt-out: APERTAR_MEDIA_REQUIRE_MOUNT=0 and APERTAR_MEDIA_MIN_FREE_MB are not documented anywhere.
findings.fix: Add a launch option --allow-unmounted-media beside --media (src/main.cpp, ApertarCoreApp::Options, README 'Launch Options'). mediaGateBypassed() returns options_.simulateCamera || options_.allowUnmountedMedia. Add constexpr uint64_t kMinFreeMiB = 1024 and drop both env vars.

findings.title: Storage switches in two stores, edited by App itself
findings.detail: set_buffer_mode, set_frames_per_folder, set_clip_merge and set_storage_preroll write [storage] and [media] keys of apertar-hardware.conf from App. They do it in three copied 25-line blocks, each also writing a .bak file. set_media_trim and set_preview_tdn, from the same port, store in camera_settings.conf. Upstream does write single hardware keys from commands (set_imu_driver, set_imu_orientation, set_imu_sync_offset, via Mpu6050RecordingSession.cpp:1295-1330@upstream-1.6.0), but always through the class that owns the section. No class owns [storage] or [media] here, and one family of recording switches is split across two stores.
findings.fix: Add five CaptureSettings members beside mediaTrimEnabled: bufferRam, framesPerFolder, clipMerge, storagePreroll, storagePrerollSeconds. Save them after media_trim= (CC:976), carry them across formats like mediaTrimEnabled (CC:11348-11367), and set them through setters shaped like setMediaTrimEnabled. Remove parseBufferConf, parsePrerollConf and the [media] section. The RAM numbers and the stop percent stay as env bench knobs.

findings.title: Env twins silently beat a UI switch
findings.detail: APERTAR_CDNG_BUFFER, APERTAR_CDNG_FRAMES_PER_FOLDER, APERTAR_CLIP_MERGE, APERTAR_STORAGE_PREROLL and APERTAR_MEDIA_TRIM each override a setting that also has a command and a UI switch. Four state fields (frames_per_folder_env, clip_merge_env_off, storage_preroll_auto_env, media_trim_env_off) and 8 uses in WCP exist only to explain the override. No upstream env var overrides a setting the UI shows.
findings.fix: Remove the five env vars and the four state fields. A campaign script sends the socket command instead (for example set_clip_merge enabled=false).

findings.title: The kernel-tune root helper chain never ran
findings.detail: The helper is off by default, was never installed on the rig, and the KB lists it as 'not recommended' (working/dng-chain-answer.md 5.3). Its sudoers rule pins the path but not the arguments; upstream's rules list each argument (Apertar-UI/systemd/*.sudoers@upstream-1.6.0). The root-owned tune folder sits inside a pi-owned folder, and save_once writes 'cat > $STATE_DIR/name' as root, so pi could swap the folder or plant a symlink. In practice no privilege is gained: pi already has unrestricted sudo -n, which upstream relies on (App:3157@upstream-1.6.0). APERTAR_MEDIA_RUN_DIR is probably dropped by sudo's env_reset.
findings.fix: Remove the helper, its sudoers file, the tune line of the tmpfiles file, kernel_tune, APERTAR_MEDIA_TUNE and applyMediaTuning. If kernel tuning is ever wanted, it belongs on the image as a sysctl.d file and a udev rule.

findings.title: The eject flag has no reader
findings.detail: Core writes /run/apertar-media/eject/<device> for 'an automounter that honours' it. Nothing in Apertar-UI (src, systemd, scripts) or in Core reads the file.
findings.fix: Either delete the flag functions, the eject line of the tmpfiles file and APERTAR_MEDIA_RUN_DIR, or write the reader in Apertar-UI/src/CfeAutomounter.cpp and document the shared folder.

findings.title: Knobs that do nothing: conform_fps, hold_ms/double_ms, directIo
findings.detail: conform_fps has a setting, a set command, state lines and a preset key, but no consumer and no UI (0 hits in WCP and Apertar-UI). set_controls accepts and writes hold_ms and double_ms, but the gesture times are constexpr. MediaWriterSettings::directIo is commented 'unused'.
findings.fix: Remove conform_fps and cameraConformFps. Take hold_ms and double_ms out of knownKey, or read them into ButtonGesture. Remove directIo and the fourth value of each writerSettingsFor row.

findings.title: Clear HDR ISO caps as a [camera] section of the hardware file
findings.detail: The caps have their own parser, are read once, and have no command and no UI. The values come from the driver's gain codes. Upstream keeps such limits in code (settings.iso = std::min<uint32_t>(settings.iso, 800u), CC:2483@upstream-1.6.0).
findings.fix: Add two constexpr uint32_t beside kLosslessMaxIso (CC:3100). Delete loadCameraSection, the [camera] section and its template lines.

findings.title: README documents bench knobs, install recipes and private references
findings.detail: The README lists 15 env vars in 13 rows with measurements, cites knowledge-base paths, gives three sudo install recipes, and names a private UI commit and local branch ('Apertar-UI 7ea9afc (local branch clip-split)'). The upstream README names no env var (0 'APERTAR_' hits), no measurement log and no sudoers install.
findings.fix: Keep in the README what an operator sets (Boot Config card, trim, preview denoise, split clips), without KB paths or commit refs. Move the knob table to a developer page and the install steps to the image notes.

findings.title: Three write routes for config.txt; new shell helpers in Core
findings.detail: writeBootConfigText tries a direct write, then the apertar-boot-config helper, then sudo -n install. Upstream has only the last route (App:3150-3160@upstream-1.6.0). Trim goes through a second new shell helper. Upstream's root helpers are C++ programs in the UI repo, with sudoers rules that list every argument.
findings.fix: Use one route: sudo -n install, keeping the backup line (App:3595). Run trim as timeout 20s sudo -n fstrim -v <mount>. If a locked-down image is wanted, move both helpers beside the UI's helpers and write the arguments into their rules.

findings.title: IMX283 driver default and Core default cancel each other
findings.detail: The driver turns on an 'experimental, UNMEASURED' per-crop VMAX floor by default (crop_vmax = true; the parameter is not in the driver baseline origin/master). Core then caps the fps at the crop_vmax=0 floor table unless APERTAR_IMX283_PROBE_FPS=1 is set.
findings.fix: Set the driver default to crop_vmax = false. Delete the floorFps cap and the env var. Turn the experiment on in the driver once it is measured.

findings.title: set_controls refuses the GPIO keys [gpio_encoders] shares
findings.detail: The chip setting is back on the Controls card (04fe197). set_controls still refuses chip, active_low, pull, poll_ms and debounce_ms in [gpio_encoders]. The reader does read them there (one shared value, the later line wins), and the upstream UI template wrote them there (DisplayConfigBridge.cpp:172-176@upstream-1.6.0). Only edits are checked (HardwareConfigText.hpp:496), so existing files still load and save. The template part of the original finding is dropped: upstream Core's template has no chip= in [gpio] either. Not tested on a Pi with a second GPIO chip.
findings.fix: Add the five names to the gpio_encoders branch of knownKey. Or keep refusing them with the message: 'Set chip, pull, active_low, poll_ms and debounce_ms in [gpio_buttons]: the encoders share them.'

findings.title: modeLadderPath() copies persistedSettingsPath()
findings.detail: A separate mode_ladder.conf is acceptable. Upstream keeps one file per concern, and its camera_settings.conf holds only the active block and profile.* blocks, written by a snapshot persister (CC:780-791@upstream-1.6.0), so folding the ladder in would add a new kind of block. What remains is the duplication: the two path functions are the same code with a different file name.
findings.fix: Use one helper for the apertar-core config folder (XDG_CONFIG_HOME, then HOME, then the temp fallback) in both functions.

findings.title: Eight UI commits add and drop three env knobs
findings.detail: These commits add and then drop APERTAR_PREVIEW_PLANE, APERTAR_PREVIEW_PEAKING and APERTAR_PREVIEW_DIRECT. The net diff is none. They are 8 of the 39 UI commits.
findings.fix: Leave them out of the merge series.

findings.title: Two boolean spellings in camera_settings.conf
findings.detail: Six port booleans are written as true/false. Upstream writes '<< s.member', which gives 0/1 (CC:749@upstream-1.6.0). The fork's main branch started this with clear_hdr. The reader accepts both.
findings.fix: Write the booleans as '<< s.member' and keep reading both spellings.

board-support.summary: I checked all 16 findings against the port (Core 01f170c, UI 7ea9afc) and against upstream-1.6.0. All 16 survive, 3 with a lower severity. Finding 4 goes from major to minor. Its Pi 2 and Zero W rows are dropped: those SoCs cannot run Apertar's aarch64-only image, so "unknown = Pi 5" only applies to a dev host, and the code comment says that is intended. Upstream's exact SoC list is copied in two headers, not one. The claim that [pi0w] applies to a Zero 2 W is removed because there is no source for it. Finding 7 goes from major to minor: it is an untested risk with a way to switch off each change, and no defect is shown on any board. Finding 11 goes from minor to nit, because stock config.txt files carry [all]. Finding 13 is backed up: Core's own clip writer stores 8-bit DNGs as BitsPerSample=8, which the viewer refuses. The fix for finding 1 (04fe197) is confirmed not to be in cinemate-port. I found nothing new of this kind. The Skeptic and Final findings sections are appended to the notes file.

findings.title: Controls page models only the 40-pin header; chip= is gone from the card
findings.detail: Upstream reads chip/gpiochip/gpio_chip in [gpio_buttons], [gpio_encoders], [trigger_output] and [recording_indicator], with default auto and lines 0..63 (GpioInput.cpp:233, :431-432; TriggerOutput.cpp:311; RecordingIndicatorOutput.cpp:319 @upstream-1.6.0). The port's card has no chip setting and caps lines at 27 (CM:268). It lists free pins as 4..27 whatever the chip (CM:381). Switch pins are limited to 0..27 (HCT:697). Line claims are keyed by line number only, and gpio_i2c1 and gpio_dpi apply to every line <= 27 on any chip (HCT:858-872). The WebUI save sends no force flag (App:8642-8644), and the store refuses any save that adds errors (HardwareConfigStore.cpp:337). Result: a file upstream accepts (buttons on /dev/gpiochip2) is refused on a DPI rig with 5 new errors, and the touch UI shows a Controls warning. The fix commit 04fe197 is on work/improve and origin/claude/awesome-pasteur-qzsiow but not on cinemate-port (checked with merge-base --is-ancestor).
findings.fix: Merge 04fe197. It puts the chip and poll_ms rows back in peripheralSettings, keys claims by chip and line, and applies gpio_i2c1/gpio_dpi only on the header chip. It also raises switch pins to 0..63, lists free pins per chip, and makes the status read the chip the reader actually uses.

findings.title: Display defaults are the owner's HDMI rig; the touch UI is hidden when the key is missing
findings.detail: Upstream falls back to 720x720, layout square and hdmi_external_only=false, and writes a default file through ensureDefaultHardwareConfigFile() (UI DisplayConfigBridge.cpp:14-15, :41, :577-587, :646-649; Core template App:4329 @upstream-1.6.0). The port falls back to 1920x1080, landscape_large and true. It no longer writes a default file, and Core's template says hdmi_external_only=true. main.cpp:432-433 hides the window when the value is true. On a rig with the DPI touch panel and no hardware file, or a file without that key, there is no touch UI.
findings.fix: Restore upstream's four defaults in the bridge, its header and Core's template, and restore the default-file writer. The owner's values belong in his own apertar-hardware.conf.

findings.title: Boot Config card does not see include camera-selection.txt
findings.detail: lineFrom gives a line without '=' no key (BCT:288-289), so an include line is ignored. The test fixture still carries the stock image's comment about the 'include camera-selection.txt' line. Upstream's UI treats that file as the authority for which sensor is fitted (UI DeviceInfoBridge.cpp:213-215 @upstream-1.6.0). On such a file the card shows no sensor. Choosing a sensor adds a second dtoverlay next to the included one, and 'None connected' changes nothing. The read-back agrees with the request because it reads the file the same way. Probable: the stock config.txt is not in this container.
findings.fix: In readState, an uncommented include line that applies adds a warning and makes the camera rows read-only, the same way state.problem and editable work today. Reading the included file is the larger option. Settle the premise with grep -n '^include' /boot/firmware/config.txt on a fresh Apertar-Beta 1.6.0 image.

findings.title: Third board detector, matching by substring, with its own config.txt filter rules
findings.detail: Upstream tells SoCs apart by exact brcm,bcm27xx strings in RecordingCapabilities.hpp:18-35 and DefaultTuningSelection.hpp:18-31, and does not guess on an unknown platform (DefaultTuningSelection.hpp:67 @upstream-1.6.0). The port adds a substring detector with a different list: it adds bcm2710 and lacks bcm2836/bcm2835. It reads no match as a Pi 5. Apertar ships aarch64 only, so on a real board the unknown case is only a dev host, and the comment at BCT:79 says that is intended. The earlier Pi 2 and Zero W rows are dropped for that reason. Zero 2 W: the port applies [pi3] and [pi02] but not [pi0]. Whether the firmware applies [pi3] to a Zero 2 W is unconfirmed (test T5). If it does not, a file with a [pi3] section gets the sensor line where the firmware ignores it, and the read-back still agrees. The stock layout has no [pi3] section, so the card edits [all] and works.
findings.fix: Derive family from upstream's exact SoC strings with one inline helper beside recordingCapabilitiesFromCompatible, used by the card. Keep the Pi 5 reading only for a host without a device tree. Correct the Zero 2 W filters after test T5 on a board.

findings.title: Controls validator reads config.txt as a Pi 5 would
findings.detail: parseConfigTxt counts lines only under [all] or [pi5] (applies = filter == "[all]" || filter == "[pi5]"). DPI overlays under [pi4] or [cm5] are not seen. Under [pi5] they are counted on every board (host run). On a Pi 4 that means either a missing DPI warning, or false gpio_dpi errors that refuse a save. The Boot Config reader already knows the board (BCT:540-553, displayLines). Upstream has no such validator, so this is new ground.
findings.fix: hardwareConfigFacts() takes bootconf::readState(bootconf::parseDocument(text, board), board).displayLines. Remove the filter code from parseConfigTxt.

findings.title: Link-frequency cap exists for family pi4 only
findings.detail: linkOptionsFor caps the list only when family == "pi4". Pi 3 and Zero 2 W get the full Pi 5 list (IMX477 up to 972 MHz, IMX585 up to 1039.5 MHz). The labels say 'fps at 4K' and 'over RP1 spec' on boards that have no RP1. Probable: a rate the driver does not accept means no camera after the reboot.
findings.fix: Apply the cap to every family that is not pi5 and rename pi4MaxHz to match. Drop the fps and RP1 text on boards that are not Pi 5-class.

findings.title: Raw write path changed for every board and was run on one CM5
findings.detail: Four changes are on by default: one request per raw buffer, a copy worker that counts dropped_copy_slot, sync_file_range per DNG with a 1 s fsync, and a storage pre-roll at start. Upstream keeps three requests in flight for four buffers, copies on libcamera's thread, does no sync and no pre-roll, and uses per-family defaults where memory matters (CC:1126, CC:6001-6004 @upstream-1.6.0). Each change has an env or config switch. Nobody ran them on a Pi 4 or CM4. This is an untested risk; no defect is shown. Downgraded from major.
findings.fix: Run tests T1 and T2 on a Pi 4. If no board is available before the merge, default the pre-roll and the per-file sync to off where recordingCapabilities().hardwareH264 is true. That is one line in each function that reads the knobs, in the shape of CC:1126 @upstream-1.6.0.

findings.title: Raw copy pool is kept between takes
findings.detail: Upstream clears rawPool_ at every stop (CC:3486 @upstream-1.6.0). The port keeps min(queue, max(workers+2, 4)) copies, about 100-110 MB at 4K, until the session is configured again. On a 1-2 GB Pi 4 that memory is not returned between takes.
findings.fix: Free the idle pool after 30 s idle, the rule src/playback/DecodeSlots.hpp:9-13 uses, or keep it only when MemTotal allows, read the way BufferBudget.hpp:83-95 reads it.

findings.title: New cards do not follow recording_capabilities
findings.detail: Upstream hides and disables options the board cannot do (WCP:9524-9529 @upstream-1.6.0). The ladder probe goes through sanitizeSettingsForSensor, which clamps the compression, and then compares only fps, bit depth and Clear HDR. On a board without rawCompression, every compression therefore reads as usable with the uncompressed ceiling. The SDR default is lossless_jpeg. A Pi 4 shows Lossless JPEG and records uncompressed, with no sentence saying so. Pi 3 and Zero 2 W are shown raw-only cards.
findings.fix: Set ceilingBy[i] = 0 for i >= 1 when !recordingCapabilities().rawCompression. The caller picks none as the default on such a board. Hide the raw-only cards with recordingFeatureSupported / raw_recording === false (WCP:9488-9496).

findings.title: Media tuning helper sets dirty-page limits in absolute bytes
findings.detail: dirty_bytes is set to 256 MiB-1 GiB whatever the RAM size, after the ratios are set to 0. On a 512 MB-1 GB board that is half of RAM or all of it. Opt-in (APERTAR_MEDIA_TUNE or kernel_tune). Not measured.
findings.fix: Cap both values by MemTotal in the script: dirty_bytes at a quarter of RAM, the background value at half of that.

findings.title: Root helper requires a [pi5], [pi4] or [all] header, and fan mode now goes through it
findings.detail: Upstream installs the fan text with sudo -n install and applies no content rule (App:3127-3165 @upstream-1.6.0). The port's helper refuses text without one of the three headers, and Core does not fall back when the helper says no. Stock Raspberry Pi OS and Apertar files carry [all], so only a hand-written file is hit. Downgraded from minor.
findings.fix: Accept any [section] header, or drop the header rule. Core's textProblem already checks size and NUL bytes.

findings.title: APERTAR_RT=1 pins Core to cores 1 to 3 without checking
findings.detail: With fewer CPUs online (maxcpus=), taskset fails at exec and Core does not start, so systemd restarts it in a loop. Opt-in. Every supported board has four cores today.
findings.fix: Test taskset -c "$RT_CPUS" /bin/true first, the same way chrt is tested at :29.

findings.title: Clip viewer refuses 8-bit DNG that Core itself writes
findings.detail: The viewer accepts only 10, 12 and 16 bits and refuses anything else with 'Unsupported DNG layout'. Core's clip writer stores 8-bit clips as BitsPerSample=8 (src/cdng/CdngEncoder.cpp:149-152, :1206-1209), and the IMX477 has 8-bit modes. An 8-bit IMX477 clip cannot be opened in the WebUI viewer.
findings.fix: Accept bits == 8: one byte per sample in the row size, and one more branch in the row loop.

findings.title: Sensor paths run on a CM5 only
findings.detail: The port drops upstream's IMX585 12-bit crop auto-configuration fallback (CC:5993-5996 @upstream-1.6.0). The mode tables, the Clear HDR buffers (8 x 16.9 MB), the start-up sensor probe and the phase lock were run on PiSP only. Upstream's README lists the IMX585 for Pi 3 and Pi 4 (README.md:143). The per-pipeline hook backendMaximumFps is empty.
findings.fix: No code change. State the tested scope in Core's README and run tests T3-T6 and T8 before claiming more.

findings.title: Preview temporal denoise off by default also changes recorded ISP output
findings.detail: previewTdn=false means the tuning copy without tdn is loaded for every format. On Pi 5-class boards H.264 and ProRes record the ISP output, so probably they lose temporal denoise by default, not only the preview (no frame compared). No effect on VC4. The camera review owns this one.
findings.fix: Default previewTdn = true, or strip tdn only when a raw format records.

findings.title: Drivers need kernel 6.12
findings.detail: <linux/unaligned.h> replaces <asm/unaligned.h> (origin/master), so a 6.6 image cannot build the imx283 module. The Apertar imx585 base already uses that header.
findings.fix: None needed if 6.12 is the image's kernel floor. Say it once in Core's README.

protocol-security.summary: 9 of 10 findings survive, and 4 of those were corrected. Dropped: X-10. Its claim that upstream replies are flat except a short list, with lists sent as strings, is wrong. Upstream settingsBody already carries the exposure_metering_modes array, and replies carry the modes array and the state object. The comma-separated-string rule applies only to commands coming in. Corrected: X-1. The revision check is a stale-write guard, not a security control, so that part moves to X-7. Because the card's Edit-file feature is deliberate, the fix is now a deny-list of boot-chain keys plus removal of the sudo -n install fallback. X-2 is corrected too. eject is removed from the fix, because upstream already allows eject_media from the LAN. Restricting the runner's script paths becomes an optional second step that changes stock behaviour. X-3 goes from minor to nit. Lock appears only while ISO is Auto, so against a 1.6.0 Core it does nothing (not the opposite). The old fix does not work, because upstream sends no iso_actual. X-6 goes from minor to nit. X-4 notes that the next get_state corrects the wrong state. X-9 notes that upstream already calls its own /usr/local/libexec helpers through sudo -n. I found nothing new and serious. The Skeptic and Final findings sections were added to the notes file.

findings.title: Any LAN client can write arbitrary text into /boot/firmware/config.txt as root
findings.detail: set_boot_config text= carries the whole file (the card's Edit file). Core checks only non-empty, <=64 KiB, no NUL (textProblem), applies the card's choices on top (applyRequest), and writes as root through the helper. When the helper is missing or sudo refuses it, Core falls back to sudo -n install (App:3594-3608), which skips even the helper's one content check (a [pi5]/[pi4]/[all] line). Any directive can be written: kernel=, cmdline=, os_prefix=, initramfs, start_file=, dtoverlay=. The LAN controls the boot chain persistently and can at least leave the Pi unbootable. Upstream @upstream-1.6.0: the LAN picks one of the fixed fan modes and Core builds the block (core-upstream App:3142-3157, :10568-10577). Both versions trust the LAN by design (same-origin check only, core-upstream WebServer.cpp:156-170; C1-N10), so the gap is the new reach, not missing authentication. The revision check does not help, because any client can read the revision with get_boot_config first (see X-7). Confirmed in code.
findings.fix: In bootConfigSet, after textProblem, refuse text that changes a boot-chain key (kernel, cmdline, os_prefix, initramfs, start_file, fixup_file, device_tree, overlay_prefix, boot_*), using bootconf::lineChanges against the file on disk: return {400, errorReplyBody(command.id, "config.txt: " + key + " is not changed from the WebUI.", "\"code\":\"refused\"")}. In writeBootConfigText, drop the sudo -n install fallback: no helper means no write, with the existing 'Install the helper' message. Give textProblem the helper's section check so both refuse the same input.

findings.title: test_input lets the LAN run any readable file with bash, without a button press
findings.detail: test_input section=gpio_buttons key=remote0 runs whatever the saved file maps to that key, through handleHardwareInputAction (App:12410). remoteN rows skip the section-on check (App:12404). A LAN client can save [run_script] path1=<file> and [gpio_buttons] remote0=run_script1 through POST /api/config or set_controls. The runner re-reads the path on each request (App:10333). It accepts any absolute, regular, readable file and runs /bin/bash -- <file> as pi, which is root through the stock NOPASSWD: ALL. Combined with X-1, the LAN can fill config.txt with shell lines. Upstream @upstream-1.6.0 has the same runner checks (core-upstream HardwareScriptRunner.cpp:88-89, :238). But there handleHardwareInputAction is called only from the GPIO, NeoRotary and PCF8574 callbacks and from the standby wake (core-upstream App:6786-6792, :8613), so a script ran only on a physical press. Each piece is confirmed in code; the end-to-end chain is probable (not run on a Pi).
findings.fix: In testInputReply, before handleHardwareInputAction, refuse an action list that holds a script action: for (const auto &a : line.actions) if (hardware::scriptActionSlot(a) >= 0) return errorReply(command.id, "Scripts run from a button, not from the WebUI.");. Optional second step, which changes stock runner behaviour and needs the original developer: require the script to be executable and not group- or world-writable.

findings.title: Port UI ISO Lock does nothing against a 1.6.0 Core
findings.detail: Lock is offered only while ISO is Auto (CameraPage.qml:531). It sends set_iso_auto enabled=false. The port Core reads enabled (App:12995-13001). A 1.6.0 Core ignores it and calls setIsoAuto(), so ISO stays auto while the UI reports success and saves settings. Upstream sends no iso_actual, so the UI cannot learn the ISO in use from an old Core. Only a mixed install (new UI, old Core) is affected. Confirmed.
findings.fix: Pass &reply to sendCoreCommand for Lock. If reply.value("iso_auto").toBool() is still true, call setLastError("Lock needs a newer ApertarCore.") and return false. Or offer Lock in CameraPage.qml only when the state carries iso_actual.

findings.title: set_timecode_mode target= is ignored by a 1.6.0 Core
findings.detail: The port UI sends target=ui to change only the screen timecode. A 1.6.0 Core ignores target and changes the file timecode too. The UI keeps m_fileTimecodeMode unchanged until the next get_state corrects it (ApertarControlBridge.cpp:1698-1705). Only a mixed install is affected. Confirmed.
findings.fix: Take the reply and set m_fileTimecodeMode from its timecode_mode, as the state handler at :1698 does, instead of from target.

findings.title: Six commands run before commandMutex_; get_controls is not read-only
findings.detail: get_controls, controls_history, controls_last_input, scan_i2c, list_actions and test_input answer before the lock. Upstream takes the lock on the first line of handleCommand (core-upstream App:9093; C1-S03). There is no data race: controlsErrors_ and controlsWarnings_ are atomics (ApertarCoreApp.hpp:174-175), and pendingUnitSince_ is under controlsWorkerMutex_. But get_controls writes those counters, erases pendingUnitSince_, spawns systemctl show for each pending unit, and parses the same text 8 times (App:12439-12448). scan_i2c checks for a take once, then probes up to 117 addresses without the lock, so a take can start mid-scan. test_input must stay outside the lock, because its actions take the lock themselves.
findings.fix: Move get_controls, controls_history, controls_last_input, list_actions and scan_i2c back into the locked if chain. If the scan is slow, run it as a worker with polled state, like the media speed test (C1-S20). Parse the text once in get_controls (const hwconf::Document doc = hwconf::parse(info.text);). Move the systemctl probe into the controls worker. Keep only test_input before the lock, with its existing comment.

findings.title: get_state emits media_state twice
findings.detail: The get_state reply writes media_state from a fresh mediaSnapshot() at :12944 and again from mediaState at :12961. That is a duplicate JSON key, from two snapshots that can differ. Qt and JS keep the last one, so nothing breaks. Upstream get_state has no media_state key at all. Confirmed.
findings.fix: Delete line 12944.

findings.title: Two doors to set_boot_config with different guards; HTTP route wraps the command parser
findings.detail: POST /api/boot-config splices "cmd":"set_boot_config" into the body, parses it with parseControlCommand, and calls bootConfigSet with browser set when an Origin header is present, so a browser save needs a revision. /api/command reaches the same function with browser=false, so a save without a revision is accepted there, even from the WebUI page itself. The revision is a stale-write guard (the card's reload case), not a security control. Upstream has one command door plus resource routes that do not reuse the command parser (core-upstream App:7392-7500, :7637). Confirmed.
findings.fix: Keep set_boot_config as a plain command behind /api/command and drop the POST /api/boot-config write route. In bootConfigSet, require revision on every non-dry-run save (if (!revision) return the existing 409 old_page reply) and drop the browser parameter.

findings.title: Port UI polls get_state at 1 Hz while auto ISO or auto WB is on
findings.detail: Upstream polls every 30 s (kSteadyStatePollIntervalMs). The port polls every 1 s while auto ISO or auto WB is on, so it can show the value in use. Each get_state takes commandMutex_ and builds the full state, and the HDMI process doubles the rate. Confirmed.
findings.fix: Have Core send the ISO and WB in use with an existing event (the settings event on change), and keep the 30 s poll.

findings.title: sudoers files are new ground and imply a hardening Core does not have
findings.detail: Upstream ships no sudoers file; its config/ folder holds only apertar-core-capture-priority.conf. It relies on the stock NOPASSWD: ALL for pi and calls sudo -n on tools and on its own /usr/local/libexec helpers (core-upstream App:1544, :1549, :3031, :3157, :3205). So the helper pattern is upstream's; only the three narrow rules are new. Core still needs full sudo for the upstream paths, so the rules add nothing on a stock image and do not confine Core.
findings.fix: Say in the handoff that the rules are optional and do not confine Core. Or drop the files and call the helpers with plain sudo -n, as upstream calls apertar-standby-usb.

state-consistency.summary: 13 of 14 findings survive. I dropped X-state-consistency-10: the two timecode keys are deliberate. Commit 909aaa5 splits the UI timecode from the file timecode; set_timecode_mode takes target=ui|files|both. Corrections: 2 lowered to minor, because the reply carries the clamped fps and the display snaps back. 4 narrowed: the IMX477 difference is upstream drift, so only IMX585 100/120 is the port's. 8 lowered to nit: upstream uses the same pattern for wb_actual_*. 9 lowered to nit: hdr_* fields belong to fork main, and upstream also publishes fields no UI reads. 3 gets an upstream-style fix, plus a new detail: the touch list still offers 3840x2076/1920x1038, which Core migrates to sizes the list lacks. 14 widened to media_trim. 1, 5, 6, 7, 11, 12, 13 confirmed as stated. For 6, a script diff shows frameBufferBarEnabled is the only key missing from the WebUI allow-list that upstream did not already miss.

findings.title: Touch UI presets omit every camera setting the port added
findings.detail: The touch UI writes its own preset files. Its camera keys come from cameraPresetSettings, which is byte-identical to ui-upstream (empty diff). Core's buildCurrentPresetPayload (WebUI save) adds cameraFpsSpeedRamp, cameraFpsSpeedRampShutter, cameraFpsSpeedRampAudio, cameraFpsSpeedRampAfter, cameraClipNameTemplate, cameraFpsPhaseLock, cameraTimecodeMode, cameraConformFps, cameraClearHdr, cameraHdrThresholdHigh, cameraHdrThresholdLow, cameraHdrBlend, cameraHdrGainAdder and cameraCdngLog. Upstream precedent: both writers carry the same camera* set. In fork main neither writer had the Clear HDR keys. Operator: a preset saved on the touch screen does not record Clear HDR, Log, speed ramp, phase lock, conform fps, file timecode or clip name template, and loading it leaves the current values in place. The same preset saved from the WebUI restores them. Loading works either way: applyCameraPreset (:1288) forwards every camera* key.
findings.fix: In ApertarControlBridge, keep the missing fields from applyCoreState as members. It already keeps clip_name_template (:664), fps_speed_ramp (:1511), keep_exposure (:1599), clear_hdr (:1681), timecode_mode (:1698) and cdng_log (:2791). Add fps_speed_ramp_stretch_audio/return, fps_phase_lock, conform_fps and hdr_*. Insert them in cameraPresetSettings under Core's keys and value words: angle/exposure, real/stretch, stay/return, free_run/rec_run.

findings.title: Touch UI and hardware buttons ignore fps_take_max during a ladder take
findings.detail: In a ladder take, Core clamps set_fps to fpsTakeMax, the running rung's ceiling, and replies ok. The WebUI cuts its FPS list at fps_take_max when recording && ladder_active. The bridge never reads fps_take_max: fpsCeiling uses fpsMax, and availablePcfFpsOptions (buttons) uses settings.fpsMax. Operator: the touch picker and the FPS buttons offer values above the rung (e.g. 100). The take stays at the rung maximum, and the display snaps back because the reply carries the clamped fps. Severity lowered from major for that reason. New ground (the ladder), so this is an internal inconsistency of the port.
findings.fix: Read fps_take_max in applyCoreState next to fps_max, and expose it as Q_PROPERTY fpsTakeMax on cameraSetValuesChanged. In fpsCeiling, use it when recording && ladderActive && fpsTakeMax > 0, as WCP:7485 does. In availablePcfFpsOptions, use settings.fpsTakeMax when settings.ladderActive and the camera is recording.

findings.title: IMX585 mode table has one source in Core; touch UI keeps the upstream list, the WebUI a hand copy
findings.detail: Commit caa0153 moved Core's IMX585 sizes into per-class tables (s12/s10/h12/h16). The WebUI repeats them as strings (imx585ClassModes), as a fallback until the ladder pool arrives. The touch UI lists at CameraPage.qml:418 and SettingsPage.qml:161 equal ui-upstream. They lack 2880x2160, 2160x2160, 2976x2160, the 2048x* crops, 1440x1080 and 1920x1040. They still offer 3840x2076 and 1920x1038, which Core migrates to 2072/1036 (CC:442-450, :10648). After such a pick, the current value is not in the list. Operator: the touch UI cannot select the 2K crop, 4:3 or 1:1 modes the WebUI offers. Upstream also had per-UI hand lists (core-map 4.5). The port made a single source in Core and left two consumers off it.
findings.fix: Upstream style (flat scalar state, per-UI lists): update the QML imx585 lists to Core's class tables, with bit depth and Clear HDR picking the class as WCP does. In Imx585Modes.hpp, add a comment naming WCP:8915 and CameraPage.qml/SettingsPage.qml as copies. If a shared source is wanted, the bridge calls the port's list_sensor_modes once per sensor, and the QML list stays as the fallback. Document that as new ground.

findings.title: Touch UI built-in FPS list lacks Core's IMX585 100/120
findings.detail: When UI.conf has no fpsSteps, Core uses builtInFpsSteps for the buttons and sends it to the WebUI as ui.fps_steps. For the IMX585 that list is {24,25,30,50,60,100,120}. The touch UI falls back to {24,25,30,50,60} for the IMX585. Operator: on an IMX585 the touch picker lacks 100 and 120, which the WebUI and the buttons offer. The IMX477 difference (QML 27 values vs Core 6) is upstream drift, not the port's: ui-upstream CameraPage.qml:804 vs core-upstream App:1154-1157, and the upstream WebUI fallback fpsPresets (WCP:4039) is also the 27-value list.
findings.fix: Add 100 and 120 to the QML fallback for imx585Detected, with a comment naming App builtInFpsSteps as the source.

findings.title: Old FPS ceiling copies stay beside fps_max
findings.detail: fps_max (maximumFpsForSettings, CC:3495) is the smaller of modeMaximumFps and losslessMaximumFps. modeMaximumFps includes the IMX477 uncompressed table and the IMX585 mode. losslessMaximumFps includes the 4K 30/24 and 2K 60 caps. The WebUI re-applies the IMX477 uncompressed cap and the 4K/2K lossless caps on top of fps_max. QML and App keep the old per-sensor tables as the fallback for a Core without fps_max (the upstream mechanism), and the port still edits that copy: UI d1efb67 added the Clear HDR 16-bit 25 fps cap. Values agree today. core-map 4.5 records that 33/50 fps was once blocked by four separate caps.
findings.fix: Delete the re-application in WCP:7490-7509 when fps_max > 0. Keep the QML and App fallbacks only for an older Core, mark them frozen and stop editing them. Comment next to maximumFpsForSettings that it is the one table.

findings.title: WebUI preset load allow-list drops frameBufferBarEnabled
findings.detail: Commit d44b177 added frameBufferBarEnabled to Core's preset writer and reader, and the touch UI writes and reads it. buildPresetApplyPayload lacks it, although its sibling keys are at :19109. Its only caller is loadPresetFromLibrary (:19155). A script diff shows every other key missing from the allow-list is missing upstream too (core-map 4.4). Operator: a preset loaded through the WebUI library leaves the buffer bar unchanged.
findings.fix: Add "frameBufferBarEnabled" next to "recordingFrameEnabled" at WCP:19109.

findings.title: settingsBody carries 14 hardware-file keys the settings event lacks
findings.detail: Upstream settingsBody (core-upstream App:167-216) holds the CaptureSettings fields only, the same set as settingsEvent. The port appends bufferSettingMembers(): buffer_setting, buffer_note, buffer_safety_stop, buffer_stop_percent, buffer_flush_discarded, storage_preroll_active/auto/auto_env/fps/last, frames_per_folder(_env), clip_merge_enabled and clip_merge_env_off. So every set_* reply carries [storage] state while the settings event does not. The buffer event and the web state carry these keys anyway, via bufferMembers.
findings.fix: Remove bufferSettingMembers() from settingsBody and append it in get_state's body only.

findings.title: settings event always sends iso_actual 0
findings.detail: isoMeasured is filled only on the copy that settings() returns. emitSettingsEventLocked serialises settings_, so the event's iso_actual is always 0. The touch UI treats 0 as unknown and keeps its last value (ApertarControlBridge.cpp:1602-1603), so no UI shows a wrong value. Upstream does the same for wb_measured / wb_actual_* (core-upstream CC:159, :8572), so the port follows upstream's pattern. Lowered to nit.
findings.fix: Leave iso_actual out of settingsEvent, so the live value comes from get_state only. Or fill the measured ISO and WB in emitSettingsEventLocked, as settings() does.

findings.title: Published port state fields with no reader in either UI
findings.detail: Apertar-UI src/qml and WCP have no reader for conform_fps, ladder_override, fps_phase_lock_active/err_us/dur_us/pushes/saturated, tuning_file_active, media_device/fstype/class/profile, recording_fault, sensor_binning/_source or sensor_crop. Only the KB test rig reads them. Upstream also has unread fields (wb_measured, wb_actual_*), so diagnostic fields are not foreign. The hdr_* knobs come from fork main (core-main App:202-205), not the port, and are dropped from this finding. conform_fps is the one with an operator effect: it is a setting with no control in either UI, and a preset can change it without anything showing it.
findings.fix: List the diagnostic fields as diagnostic in Core's README state section. For conform_fps, add a WebUI control or document it as set by socket or preset only.

findings.title: get_state emits media_state twice
findings.detail: get_state writes media_state from mediaSnapshot() at :12944 and again from mediaState at :12961: a duplicate JSON key from two reads of the watcher. Both lines are port-new; upstream has no media_state.
findings.fix: Delete :12944 and keep the line next to media_alive.

findings.title: Two array serialisers print ladder_tops with different precision
findings.detail: The settings event uses ladderTopsJson (default precision, 6 significant digits). settingsBody and the web state use jsonNumberArray (precision 10). The output differs only past 6 significant digits, e.g. 119.880119.
findings.fix: Put one helper in a shared header next to escapeJson and use it in both places.

findings.title: help list lacks test_input
findings.detail: test_input is dispatched (:12565). Its pair test_output (:12745) is in the help list; test_input is not. Upstream's list already lacks 12 commands (core-map 2.1), so this extends existing drift.
findings.fix: Add "test_input" next to "test_output" in the help list.

findings.title: preview_tdn and media_trim persisted but not in presets
findings.detail: preview_tdn and media_trim are both camera_settings.conf keys, kept as camera-wide switches across format changes. Neither is in any preset copy, while cameraCdngPreviewColorProfile (upstream) is. Whether a preset should restore them is a product decision.
findings.fix: Add cameraPreviewTdn (and cameraMediaTrim if wanted) to the writer, the reader and the WCP allow-list, or comment in the writer that they are deliberately not preset fields.

slop.summary: Scanned the added lines of Core, UI, imx585 and imx283 (about 42,600 lines). Internal references are the main problem: 272 lines carry tutorial, work-package, request, critic, design or kb ids. 79 more carry names, dates, clip numbers or "test night". 126 mention Cinemate or cinepi. 78 narrate history. No AI residue was found (no Claude, Codex or similar, no emoji). No TODO, commented-out code or debug prints in port-authored code. The only TODO and commented-out code are in vendored lj92.c. The build log shows 5 warnings, none from the port. Comment density is the largest issue. Upstream handwritten Core src is 7 comment lines per 1000. The port is 21 to 54 in the big .cpp files and 117 in its 38 new src files. CameraController.hpp is 185 against 7. WebControlPage.cpp has 21 against 0. Operator-facing text has the right tone, with 5 hints over 160 characters and 5 "CineMate Log" strings that leak into the journal and clip metadata. The report holds the per-file table (144 rows), the density table, and 69 replacement entries.

findings.title: Tutorial and work-package ids in Core comments
findings.detail: Comments carry T31, T33, T34, T37, T39, T40, T42, T43, T47, T48, T50, T51, Q10, Q23, R1, R2, R4, O1, O4, 'request 13/19/24/25', 'critic S11/Y11', 'design §2.7/§4.3', 'kb working/dng-chain'. Upstream comments name no work items (core-upstream src has none, ApertarCoreApp.cpp 5 comment lines per 1000). T34 is also inside the string written to mode_ladder.conf (ModeLadder.hpp:319), so it reaches the operator's file. Confirmed. Replacement text for 31 of these is in the report, section F rows 1-31, 32-46.
findings.fix: Delete the tag, keep the sentence: '// T47: may playback read the card now? ...' becomes '// May playback read the card now? ...'. Drop '(critic Y11). Per-format floors are the next step.' entirely. Change the ladder file header to '# Apertar mode ladder. Core writes this file; edit it in the WebUI (Settings > Record > Mode Ladder).'

findings.title: Pointers to the private KB, critics and design sketch
findings.detail: About 40 lines point to 'kb working/dng-chain', 'working/drop-frames/...', 'KB trap 7', 'KB rule M5', 'critic M4/B2/m14', 'operator P1/P19', 'design sketch v2 (not in any repository)', 'reference for the tutorial; not in any repository until you type it', 'the host test is working/tools/playback/frames_test.cpp' (path does not exist in the repo). The original developer has no apertar-kb, no critic list, no design sketch. Confirmed (grep).
findings.fix: Remove the pointer and keep the reason it supports. Replace each playback header block by one line saying what the file is, e.g. '// The frame list of one clip folder, and the map from time to frame.' Replacements in report section F rows 50-51, 58.

findings.title: Names, dates and clip numbers of test runs in comments
findings.detail: Comments say "Patrik's rule (2026-10-28, after the temp build)", "(User, 2026-11-03)", "(temp 753f181, 2026-10-27 ... C0013 peak 2/24)", "(C0005, 2026-10-26)", "On Patrik's exFAT card", "for Patrik to run", "the owner's examples", "test night", "NVMe campaign's A/B and collect step". Rules are justified by a person and a night instead of by what the code does. Confirmed. Upstream has no person, date or clip id in any comment.
findings.fix: State the rule and the technical reason; drop person, date, clip id, commit id. Example: '// Clear HDR records uncompressed cDNG and SDR lossless, however the mode is switched: lossless overflows the write queue in Clear HDR 16-bit.' Replacement text in report section F rows 33-45, 47-49, 54-58, 62-63. Test names 'owner example: dashes' become 'dashed template'.

findings.title: Cinemate-branded strings reach the journal, clip metadata and operator-readable files
findings.detail: The feature is labelled 'Log' in the WebUI (WebControlPage.cpp:4915) but called 'CineMate Log' in stderr lines, LogCurve::describe() and as a comment. The camera_settings.conf template written by Core says '(CineMate style)' and '(CineMate's warm-up)'. WebUI search keywords include 'cinemate'. The original developer reads these as a foreign brand inside Apertar. Confirmed.
findings.fix: Rename to 'Log' in the five strings; reword the two template lines ('sized from the free memory at the start of a take', 'a short test take ... deleted at once'); drop 'cinemate' from data-search and the CSS comment.

findings.title: Cinemate used as justification and commit hashes of another project in comments
findings.detail: About 60 comments say 'as Cinemate does', 'like Cinemate', 'counted like Cinemate (ButtonGesture)', 'Cinemate f01b6cd', '5021ba3', '58fc7c2', '888093c', 'ff59dd8', 'c8f06c9', or cite cinemate source files (boot_config.py, gpio_input.py, playback.py:57-62). Upstream never cites a sibling project. A one-line provenance in the header of a ported file is acceptable; mid-code references and hashes are not. Confirmed.
findings.fix: Keep at most one provenance line per ported file (BootConfigText.hpp, ButtonGesture.hpp, LogCurve.hpp). Delete the others and the hashes, keeping the reason. Replace 'counted like Cinemate (ButtonGesture)' by 'counted by ButtonGesture'.

findings.title: Comment density far above upstream
where: 38 new src files (117 vs upstream mean 7)

highest: src/playback/PlaybackHold.hpp 359, PlaybackFrames.hpp 341, HardwareConfigStore.hpp 326, GpioChipInfo.hpp 306, FramePhaseLock.hpp 289, ClipFrames.hpp 254, FramePath.hpp 238, FpsCeiling.hpp 229
findings.detail: Upstream comments are one short line above a function or field (65 handwritten Core src files: 7 per 1000, upstream WebControlPage.cpp has 3 comment lines in 11 619). The port writes 3 to 7 line paragraphs with measurements and test ids, about one comment line per 8 to 20 code lines in the big files and per 9 in new files. Reader effort and merge noise follow. Confirmed (script, section D of the report). Whether deliberate is unknown; the style is consistent across the port, so it looks like a house habit of the author or the tool.
findings.fix: Rewrite to upstream shape: one line per function or field, what it does now. Cut measurement narrative (section X-slop-7). Target under 30 per 1000 for new files, under 15 for the big .cpp. About 1 500 comment lines go.

findings.title: Comments that narrate history or a debugging story
findings.detail: Examples: 'the whole-take drift figure went from +1339 to -201 ppm between a 30 s and a 3 min take (2026-10-26)', '782 queue drops in 3 min (C0005)', 'a 16.6 MB zero-fill under it held that thread up', 'the old model assumed 12-bit packed', '64 KiB used to drop the client without a word', 'HISTORY, kept so nobody repeats it', 'v1 checked it after samples.resize()'. They say what was wrong, not what the code does. Confirmed.
findings.fix: Replace by the present-tense rule: '// Once a second the raw capture goes to the card with its size, so a pulled card keeps it.' Put measurements in the commit message that introduced the rule. Rows 38-41, 43, 54, 7, 49 in report section F.

findings.title: Work-package ids and dated test results in the imx585 driver
findings.detail: The driver baseline (origin/apertar) is the developer's own code; the port adds 3 637 lines of which a large part is comment: 'WP-585-8 (2026-09-21) found every windowed 2x2 RAW16 crop returns the OB pedestal', 'see D1 in INVESTIGATION.md' (file not in the branch), 'This table has broken in four independent ways in one day of history'. Confirmed.
findings.fix: State the rule and the measured result without id or date: 'Windowed 2x2 RAW16 is absent: it returns the OB pedestal on hardware.' Rename the gate README title to 'Clear HDR windowed-crop gate'. Replacements in report rows 66-67, 69.

findings.title: Dated debugging history and clip names in the imx283 driver
findings.detail: imx283.c has 1 723 added lines, comment density 333 per 1000 against baseline 109. It names a test clip 'CINEPI_26-09-27_035947_F07', 'operator, 2026-09-27', commit ids (de6693c, 335781d, cb925e5) and a private path 'development/imx283-active-size/REBUILD.md'. Docs refer to branches 'cinemate-modes', 'cinemate-dev', 'experimental-crop-modes planning tree'. EXPERIMENTAL_CROPS.md documents 18 crops that 'no longer exist'. Confirmed.
findings.fix: One statement per value or macro. Delete EXPERIMENTAL_CROPS.md history or reduce to the list of crops that exist. Branch names: describe by content. Text for rows 68-69 needs checking against the driver before writing.

findings.title: Banner comments in Core
findings.detail: 40 added '// ---- Title ---' banner lines, several with a tutorial id in the title ('---- Speed ramping (T31) ----', '---- Mode ladder (T34) ----'). Upstream Core src/*.cpp has none (prores and lossydng files have some). Upstream CameraPage.qml has 19, so QML banners match upstream. Confirmed.
findings.fix: Remove the banners in Core .cpp/.hpp, or reduce to '// Mode ladder' without the rule line and id. Leave QML as is.

findings.title: Dead field that says it is unused
findings.detail: 'bool directIo = false;   // for T24's direct I/O, which this fork does not carry; unused'. A dead field with a tutorial id in the comment. Confirmed (read). Build warnings (no libcamera and libcamera builds): 5, none from the port; the unused-function and unused-parameter ones are #if-guarded upstream code.
findings.fix: Delete the field and its comment, and any initialiser in the profile tables.

findings.title: Over-long operator hints in the WebUI
findings.detail: Upstream card hints: mean 60 chars, max 140, none over 160. Port: mean 80, max 305, 5 over 160. Error replies match upstream length (33 chars mean) and shape. Tone is otherwise the same imperative style. Confirmed (regex sample of 57 vs 45 hints).
findings.fix: Cut each to two sentences of at most 140 characters; move the 'how it works' paragraph to the README.

findings.title: Private branch names and provenance in the driver docs and README
findings.detail: Docs tell the reader to 'use cinemate-port', refer to 'cinemate-modes', 'cinemate-7modes', 'CineMate's sensor detection', and Core's README carries dated measurements ('measured 2026-11-04, probable'), 'test night', 'NVMe campaign'. Needs the owner to decide the branch naming before merge. Confirmed (read); branch naming is a decision, not a defect.
findings.fix: Describe branches by content, remove dates from README tables, replace 'test night' by 'a trial' and 'NVMe campaign' by 'the split-clip A/B'.

stock-behaviour.summary: All 13 findings checked against the code on both sides, at cinemate-port (Core 01f170c, UI 7ea9afc) and at upstream-1.6.0. Every finding survives. Three are corrected. Finding 2: the WebUI hardware editor serves Core's template when the file is missing (App:6201), so the user does have something to edit, and the first save writes finding 1's HDMI layout. Finding 10: the dial already offered Auto in lossless on IMX477 in 1.6.0, then undid it. What is new is auto ISO kept in IMX585 lossless, and Auto offered in the WebUI and touch UI. Finding 11 drops from minor to nit: nothing is trimmed and only the switch misleads. Its skip branch also leaves media_trim_last_result empty. Finding 6 is extended: the stripping also applies to a tuning file the user picked, against the comment at CC:7302. The blocker (finding 1) is confirmed. It hits a fresh install, which has no hardware file, and a file written before 1.6.0. A D1 that already ran 1.6.0 has hdmi_external_only=false in its file and is safe. A "## Skeptic" section with verdicts and a "## Final findings" section were appended to the report.

findings.title: Display fallback is the HDMI rig: touch UI hidden on a stock camera with no hardware file
findings.detail: Port fallback: 1920x1080, landscape_large, hdmi_external_only=true (UI 7c41a27). Core's template has the same values (7af9f13). 1.6.0: 720x720, square, false (DisplayConfigBridge.cpp:14-15,:579,:584,:649@upstream-1.6.0; App:4320-4329@upstream-1.6.0). With true, main.cpp:432-433 hides the window. A fresh install has no file (finding 2), so a stock D1 boots with no touch UI (confirmed in code). A file written before 1.6.0, without the key, does the same (probable). A D1 that already ran 1.6.0 has false in its file and is safe.
