The first WebUI Config save on a camera without a file writes the HDMI layout. Overlaps X-knobs-2.
findings.fix: Put back 720, 720, "square" and false in DisplayConfigBridge.cpp:11-12, :289, :294, :357, in .hpp:52-59 and in defaultHardwareConfigTemplate() App:5089-5098. The HDMI rig keeps its [display] values in its own apertar-hardware.conf.

findings.title: No first-run hardware file is written any more
findings.detail: 1.6.0: the UI writes its template when /home/pi/apertar-hardware.conf is missing (DisplayConfigBridge.cpp:41,:587@upstream-1.6.0). Port c9d841f removed both writers because a file moved away came back as the template. The store now detects that case (014fa22). On a fresh camera no file appears. The WebUI editor shows Core's template (App:6201), and its first save writes it with the HDMI values of finding 1. Until that save, the UI runs on its compiled fallback.
findings.fix: One first-run writer in Core, the file's single writer: when no candidate path has a file and the store has no last-written copy, write defaultHardwareConfigTemplate() through HardwareConfigStore. Keep the replaced-file check for every later start.

findings.title: FPS ceilings come from the probe alone and the IMX585 lossless 30 fps cap is gone
findings.detail: 1.6.0: the table caps IMX585 4K at 30 (CC:2671@upstream-1.6.0), and lossless is capped at 30 (CC:2485-2486@upstream-1.6.0). Fork main used min(table, probe). Port d44b177 uses the probe alone. APERTAR_FPS_LIMIT=table and APERTAR_LOSSLESS_FPS_LIMIT restore the caps. The port comment (CC:3132-3133) calls 30 a policy, since the lossless encoder measured about 69 fps. A stock D1 offers and accepts 4K at the driver's figure (about 60, probable). The dials, the pickers and the storage pre-roll follow it. IMX477 ceilings become whatever its driver reports instead of Apertar's measured table.
findings.fix: Default resolveSensorMaxFps to min(table, probe), as on fork main. Put the probe-only ceiling behind an opt-in (APERTAR_FPS_LIMIT=probe or a [camera] key). Default the IMX585 lossless cap back to 30, and let APERTAR_LOSSLESS_FPS_LIMIT raise it.

findings.title: IMX585 1.85:1 crop sizes of the cinemate-port driver forced on the stock driver
findings.detail: The port moves 3840x2076 and 1920x1038 to 3840x2072 and 1920x1036 in settings, presets, ladder rungs and set_resolution (900d282). It also drops the auto sensor-config fallback for colour IMX585 crops (caa0153). 1.6.0 had that fallback at CC:5993-5996@upstream-1.6.0. The stock driver (imx585 origin/apertar e5b74d3, imx585.c:586,:667,:817-830) has only the old sizes. A D1 saved at 1.85:1 is moved to a size its driver lacks, and the explicit configure has no fallback, so configureAndStart fails at boot. This is probable; it is settled by putting resolution=3840x2076 in camera_settings.conf on a stock-driver Pi. The 1.85:1 crop also disappears from the offers.
findings.fix: Let the probe decide. Migrate a size only when probedSensorModes has the new transport size and lacks the old one. Keep 2076/1038 valid for a driver that advertises them. Restore the auto-config fallback for a table size the probe did not confirm. Name the driver requirement in the README.

findings.title: Storage pre-roll runs by itself at start, insert and format
findings.detail: 1.6.0 has no pre-roll. Port: automaticEnabled() returns conf.automatic.value_or(true). At every Core start, card insert and format, a stock D1 records a 2 s take at the mode's highest fps and deletes it (0.7-1.5 GB written per run). While it runs, record, photo, format, eject and standby are refused (App:12588-12591). Overlaps X-knobs-3.
findings.fix: Use value_or(false) and the template line '# preroll=off'. The storage_preroll command stays.

findings.title: Preview temporal denoise off by default also strips TDN from H.264 and ProRes recordings
findings.detail: 1.6.0 loads the tuning file as it is. Port e625c68: previewTdn=false strips rpi.denoise tdn for every record format (CC:7311). The ProRes ISP tuning is built from the stripped file (CC:7412). For H.264 and ProRes the ISP output is the recording, so a stock D1 records them without temporal denoise. The port also strips a tuning file the user picked, although the comment at CC:7302 says a picked file is used as given. Overlaps X-knobs-4.
findings.fix: Strip only when the format records raw frames: if (!settings.previewTdn && recordsRawFrames(settings.recordingFormat)). Or default previewTdn = true.

findings.title: Default APERTAR_DNG_DONTNEED=sync removes 1.6.0's per-file page-cache drop from Lossy DNG
findings.detail: 1.6.0 calls posix_fadvise DONTNEED after every Lossy DNG file (LossyDngEncoder.cpp:82@upstream-1.6.0). The port drops pages only in writer mode, and the default is now sync (adac040). Lossy files never reach the sync thread: noteWrittenFile is called only in the cDNG branch (CC:5293). A stock Lossy DNG take therefore keeps every frame in the page cache, the kswapd pattern adac040 blames for lost frames. Confirmed in code.
findings.fix: In LossyDngEncoder.cpp: if (dngPageCacheDrop() != DngPageCacheDrop::Off) ::posix_fadvise(fd, 0, 0, POSIX_FADV_DONTNEED); with the comment 'lossy takes have no sync thread: drop here'.

findings.title: Touch-UI timecode tap and Settings Mode no longer change the files' timecode
findings.detail: 1.6.0: the tap (CameraPage.qml:1714@upstream-1.6.0) and Settings Mode (SettingsPage.qml:3778@upstream-1.6.0) send no target, so one mode applies to screens and files. Port UI 7029db1: both send target "ui", and for "ui" Core skips camera_.setTimecodeMode (App:13290). An operator who taps to Rec Run sees Rec Run on screen while DNG, MLV, ProRes, H.264 and WAV keep Free Run. Core's default target stays both (909aaa5).
findings.fix: Send "both" from the tap and the first Settings row while the UI and file modes are equal. Send "ui" only after the operator has set them apart in the File timecode row.

findings.title: Lossless cDNG ISO cap raised to 1600 on every sensor
findings.detail: 1.6.0 caps lossless ISO at 800 on every sensor (CC:2483@upstream-1.6.0). Port 2f43ecc raises it to 1600, measured on the IMX585 only. IMX477 4K/2K lossless now also reaches 1600, where lossless JPEG slows as noise grows.
findings.fix: Use a per-sensor cap: 1600 for SensorFamily::Imx585, 800 for the rest, in enforceLosslessCaptureLimits and maximumIsoForSettings.

findings.title: Auto ISO kept in IMX585 lossless and offered in every UI; Core undoes it on other sensors
findings.detail: 1.6.0 forces manual ISO in lossless on every sensor (CC:2484@upstream-1.6.0). Its dial already offered Auto (App:8789-8797@upstream-1.6.0), so the dial offering Auto on IMX477 and Core undoing it is not new. New in the port: Core keeps auto ISO in IMX585 lossless, bounded only by the default tuning's AGC limit (b5b787e: 'Unverified' for other tunings). The WebUI and touch UI now offer Auto wherever Clear HDR is off, and Core undoes it in IMX477 lossless.
findings.fix: Core publishes iso_auto_allowed in the state from the sanitiser's own rule, and the three UIs read it. On the IMX585 with a user-picked tuning, keep 1.6.0's manual ISO in lossless.

findings.title: Media trim switch shows on when the root helper is not installed
findings.detail: mediaTrimEnabled defaults to true. A stock image has neither /usr/local/libexec/apertar-media-trim nor its sudoers rule. The worker logs once and continues without calling finish(), so media_trim_last_result stays empty while the state and the WebUI Performance card say on. Nothing is trimmed; only the switch misleads. Upstream has no trim.
findings.fix: Call finish("not-installed", 0, 0) in the skip branch, or add media_trim_available (helper exists and is executable) to the state. The WebUI greys the switch and shows the install line when it is false.

findings.title: HDMI monitor timecode turns red during takes by default
findings.detail: In 1.6.0 the HDMI timecode stays white during takes. UI da2a9b5: recordingRedTimecodeEnabled defaults to true and 'HDMI now follows it too' (ExternalMonitorWindow.qml:1208).
findings.fix: The HDMI monitor follows the switch only when recordingRedTimecodeEnabled is set in UI.conf. Or use a separate HDMI key that defaults to off.

findings.title: Audio meter red outline on by default
findings.detail: New indicator (UI 5697b54), default true. A stock D1 shows a red outline on the audio meter during takes with sound. The neighbouring indicators, the recording frame and the buffer bar (:368-369), default to false.
findings.fix: Default audioRecordedOutlineEnabled to false.
